articles.body:
Wealth Asuquo is an Abuja-based Afrobeats singer and performer whose rise has been powered by consistency, confidence, and an unmistakable connection to live audiences. 







While many emerging artists focus on digital virality first, Wealth has built her foundation where it matters most—the stage.



Rooted in Nigerian culture and shaped by performance, she represents a new wave of female artists who balance authenticity with ambition, delivering music that feels both grounded and scalable.



Musical Identity & Sound



At her core, Wealth Asuquo makes pure Afrobeats—rhythmic, melodic, and driven by groove. Her sound leans into chant-ready structures, infectious hooks, and records designed to move bodies before they impress algorithms.









Rather than overcomplicating her music, she prioritizes clarity and energy. Each song is built to translate effortlessly from headphones to packed venues, a strategy that aligns perfectly with her strengths as a live performer.



Latest Release: “Ayan Wodowo”



Wealth Asuquo’s most recent single, “Ayan Wodowo,” marks a pivotal moment in her journey.



The title comes from Akwa Ibom slang, loosely translating to “you wan kill person?”—a phrase used to describe something overwhelmingly hot or mind-blowing. The record lives up to its name. It’s bold, catchy, and unapologetically confident.









Produced by Shiiro, the song rides on clean, chant-like production that makes it instantly memorable. Musically, “Ayan Wodowo” sits comfortably as a melodic Afrobeats chant—simple in structure, powerful in execution, and engineered for repeat listens and live crowd interaction.



Beyond the sound, the single acts as a cultural bridge. It ties Wealth back to her roots in Uyo while resonating strongly with Abuja’s urban Afrobeats scene and wider Nigerian audiences. It’s a record that celebrates identity without limiting reach.



Performance Power & Stage Dominance



Where Wealth Asuquo truly separates herself is on stage.



Known for her commanding presence and crowd control, she has built a reputation as one of the strongest live performers in Abuja. In a standout run, she performed on over 15 stages in less than 30 days, a pace that speaks to both demand and discipline.




        View this post on Instagram            




A major career highlight came when she opened for Davido during the 5IVE Alive Tour – Abuja, performing in front of over 10,000 people. It was a defining moment—proof that her energy, confidence, and vocal presence scale effortlessly to massive crowds.



This live credibility feeds directly back into her recordings, giving her music a sense of urgency and readiness that many studio-only artists lack.



Cultural Roots & Artistic Direction



Wealth Asuquo’s artistry is deeply connected to culture. Whether through language, rhythm, or performance style, she consistently reflects her background while engaging a modern Afrobeats audience.




        View this post on Instagram            




Her music doesn’t chase trends blindly. Instead, it leans into identity, repetition, and rhythm—elements that have always driven African popular music. This approach positions her well for longevity, not just momentary attention.



Growth, Momentum & Audience Connection



With a rapidly expanding fan base and a growing reputation within Abuja’s music ecosystem, Wealth Asuquo is moving with intention. Each release builds on the last, and every performance expands her reach.



“Ayan Wodowo” in particular feels like a consolidation record—one that captures her momentum and reinforces her brand as an artist who delivers energy, culture, and performance-ready music.



The Road Ahead



Wealth Asuquo is no longer operating in potential alone—she’s operating in proof. Proof of audience connection. Proof of stage dominance. Proof of artistic clarity.







As she continues to release music and expand her footprint, she is positioning herself as one of Abuja’s most promising female Afrobeats acts, with clear crossover potential beyond the city.



If the recent run is any indication, Wealth Asuquo isn’t warming up anymore.



She’s already on fire—and “Ayan Wodowo” is the sound of her stepping fully into that moment.

Born Ilupeju Fawaz Tomiwa and raised in Lagos, Nigeria, ICLOUD FZ represents a new kind of Nigerian artist—one shaped by street reality, cultural heritage, and digital ambition. 







His music exists at the intersection of trap, Afrofusion, and alternative hip-hop, merging gritty energy with emotional depth and coded storytelling. More than a stage name, ICLOUD FZ is a statement.



“The cloud you can’t touch.” Elusive, elevated, and constantly evolving.



MUSICAL IDENTITY & CREATIVE DIRECTION



ICLOUD FZ’s sound is defined by contrast. Hard drums meet introspective lyrics. Yoruba inflections blend with global trap cadences. Street grit exists alongside atmospheric, almost cinematic moods. This balance has become his signature—music that speaks to both the hustle of Lagos and the mindset of a generation navigating pressure, ambition, and identity.









Rather than chasing trends, ICLOUD FZ bends genres to fit his reality. His writing often leans coded and reflective, allowing listeners to read between the lines while still feeling the energy on first listen. It’s this duality—raw but thoughtful, aggressive yet emotional—that sets him apart.



DISCOGRAPHY & CAREER PROGRESSION



ICLOUD FZ’s catalog reflects steady growth and artistic curiosity, spanning solo releases, projects, and notable collaborations.









Key Projects & Releases:




Trap Not a Genre In My Country (EP) — a defining early project that established his genre-bending mindset and trap-centric foundation.



FLOWERS & DEATH (EP) — a more introspective body of work exploring vulnerability, loss, hope, and emotional complexity.




Notable Singles:




KA$hAMADUPE — one of his most streamed releases, showcasing his blend of confidence, cultural coding, and modern trap influence.



ASTRO BOY — expanding his sonic range with spacey textures and melodic ambition.



Birthday & Sacrifice (feat. Ferra Ys) — an emotionally charged record that highlighted his reflective songwriting.




Collaborations & Features:




Inside / There’s Still Hopë / Dēath (feat. Tamiee) — collaborative moments that added depth to his artistic narrative.



“ON TOP” (with Zilla Oaks) — dropping December 10, 2025, marking one of the most important collaborations of his career so far.




“ON TOP” WITH ZILLA OAKS: A CAREER-DEFINING MOMENT



The upcoming release of “ON TOP” with respected rapper Zilla Oaks signals a major step forward for ICLOUD FZ. The collaboration pairs his melodic sharpness and hunger-driven delivery with Zilla Oaks’ seasoned lyricism, bridging the gap between emerging energy and established credibility.









Built around themes of growth, elevation, pressure, and relentless ambition, “ON TOP” positions ICLOUD FZ within a broader national conversation—expanding his reach beyond Lagos while reinforcing his presence in Abuja’s alternative and rap ecosystem. It’s not just a feature; it’s a statement of readiness.



CULTURAL RELEVANCE & AUDIENCE CONNECTION



ICLOUD FZ resonates with listeners who see themselves in the in-between—those balancing street reality with dreams of elevation. His music speaks to young Nigerians navigating identity, hustle culture, emotional weight, and the desire to rise without losing themselves.







Fans often describe his aura as enigmatic, unpredictable, and intentional. His visual direction, branding, and sound choices suggest an artist who understands that longevity comes from identity, not noise.



WHY ICLOUD FZ MATTERS NOW



As Nigerian music continues to diversify beyond traditional Afrobeats, artists like ICLOUD FZ are defining the next chapter—where trap, alté, hip-hop, and cultural storytelling coexist. His steady catalog growth, increasing collaborations, and evolving sound point to an artist building for the long term.



With “ON TOP” closing out the year and more releases expected ahead, ICLOUD FZ is no longer just emerging—he’s positioning.



LOOKING AHEAD



ICLOUD FZ is still ascending, but the foundation is clear:



a distinct sound, a grounded identity, and a vision aimed at the future.



He isn’t chasing the cloud.



He is the cloud you can’t touch.

Abuja’s drill and hip-hop scene just gained a major boost as 3PMF, formerly known as MoMoney MoFame, officially releases his comeback single “EYEZ ON DE BENJI$” featuring Silv4boy. 







After five years away from the spotlight, the battle-tested rapper re-enters the culture with renewed focus and the same raw edge that once earned him respect in Nigeria’s underground rap circles.



The release lands at a crucial moment for Abuja—now widely recognized as one of Nigeria’s fastest-growing rap hubs. For 3PMF, this is not simply a new song; it’s a reintroduction into a movement he helped shape long before drill became a national conversation.



SONG OVERVIEW









“EYEZ ON DE BENJI$” is built on heavy drill percussion, dark basslines, and a relentless tempo that mirrors the urgency of street ambition. 3PMF delivers hardened, motivational bars with clarity and conviction, reflecting themes of hustle, survival, ambition, and tunnel-vision focus.



Silv4boy brings balance to the record with an Afrobeats-influenced hook that adds melody, emotion, and replay value. Together, both artists create a sound that feels gritty yet accessible—rooted in drill culture but open enough to travel across playlists and audiences.



Lyrically, “Benji$” becomes more than money—it represents discipline, sacrifice, and the determination to rise regardless of circumstance. The production merges UK drill patterns with Abuja’s street pulse, giving the record a sound that feels both global and local.



CULTURAL & INDUSTRY IMPACT




        View this post on Instagram            




With this release, 3PMF positions himself firmly within Abuja’s evolving rap identity. The city has become a breeding ground for raw, unapologetic hip-hop, and “EYEZ ON DE BENJI$” fits seamlessly into that narrative—while also standing out due to 3PMF’s lived experience and long-standing credibility.



His return reconnects listeners with a foundation built on earlier underground releases such as “GHOST,” “Savage,” and “Kiki”, reminding fans that today’s movement didn’t appear overnight. Instead, it was shaped by voices like his—artists who carried the culture before it gained national traction.



The collaboration with Silv4boy also reflects a broader trend in Abuja’s scene: synergy between seasoned street voices and newer melodic talents pushing drill into wider spaces.




Stream EYEZ ON DE BENJI$




Since its release, “EYEZ ON DE BENJI$” has sparked conversation within Abuja’s grassroots rap communities, with listeners praising its hunger, authenticity, and focused delivery.

ICLOUD FZ and Zilla Oaks come together on “ON TOP,” a fierce, high‑drive collaboration that blends ambition, sharp lyricism, and raw hunger. 







The release positions both artists as pivotal voices in Nigeria’s evolving hip-hop scene, offering a record packed with fire, replay value, and undeniable chemistry. With bold storytelling and polished production, “ON TOP” arrives as one of the standout rap moments closing out the year.







A Statement Release From Two Dynamic Voices



Released December 10, 2025, “ON TOP” marks a major moment for rising artist ICLOUD FZ as he joins forces with celebrated rapper Zilla Oaks for a record that captures the urgency and competition fueling today’s rap movement.



ICLOUD FZ’s upward trajectory has been one to watch, defined by versatility and a confident sonic identity. Zilla Oaks, known for anchoring Abuja’s modern rap wave, brings seasoned presence and lyrical precision.



Together, they deliver a release that feels intentional: a declaration of momentum, dominance, and elevation.









The Sound & Story — A Fusion of Drive, Precision, and Chemistry



“ON TOP” thrives on the dynamic interplay between both artists.



ICLOUD FZ charges through the track with relentless energy and a tone shaped by ambition and grind. His verses carry the urgency of an artist carving out a definitive place in the industry.




        View this post on Instagram            




Zilla Oaks counters with polished confidence — tight bars, sharp diction, and a steady composure that reinforces the track’s message of rising above obstacles.



It’s the kind of record that fuels playlists, workouts, late-night drives, and personal grind moments.



Cultural Impact & Industry Relevance — A Release That Reflects the Times



“ON TOP” fits directly into the larger shifts happening in Nigerian hip-hop. The scene is expanding, maturing, and embracing collaborations that bridge perspectives and amplify artistic growth.



For ICLOUD FZ, this release marks a powerful step forward — an alignment with an established figure that underscores his rising influence. For Zilla Oaks, it’s another reminder of his role as a connector between new voices and the broader rap community.



“ON TOP” doesn’t just sit within these trends — it strengthens them.







Audience & Reception Potential — Built for Engagement and Replay



With the release now live, early listeners are connecting with its confidence and intensity.



Its message of ambition is widely relatable, especially among young audiences navigating their own growth stories.



“ON TOP” arrives with the energy of a record built to travel — across regions, subcultures, and platforms.



A Charge Into the Future



Now officially out, “ON TOP” stands as a powerful marker for both ICLOUD FZ and Zilla Oaks.



It’s motivational, high‑impact, and sonically sharp — a release that celebrates ambition while showcasing the evolution of two artists shaping their own momentum.




Stream ON TOP




As the year closes, this collaboration sets the tone for what’s coming next: higher stakes, higher creativity, and higher elevation.

MBBSZN—Kelechukwu Anyanwu to origin but a genre-warper by destiny—belongs to the lineage of artists who thrive in the margins where genres blur and identities expand. 







Born in Imo State and creatively grounded in Abuja, his style has always defied convention. He blends alté’s atmospheric freedom with hip-hop’s edge and Afro-fusion’s warmth, building a sonic identity that feels emotional, cinematic, and deeply human.



Pause If You Must but Don’t Stop. is the clearest expression of that identity to date.



A PROJECT WITH PURPOSE AND DIRECTION



A mantra for the moment, and a bridge to the right audience









The title of the EP is both a confession and a strategy. It acknowledges the weight of life while reminding you that momentum is still possible. But there’s a second layer—one the casual listener might miss:



This project is intentionally built for a specific kind of listener.



The community that loves soul-heavy Afro-fusion.



The people still spinning Blackmagic’s “Repete.”



The Ajebutter22 loyalists who appreciate wit, smoothness, and cultural reflection.



The OT waveheads who found a home in Odunsi, Tay Iwar, BOJ, and the soft-grit universe of alté.



The fans searching for the textured depth of Burna Boy’s “Ye”—music that feels both global and intimately Nigerian.



MBBSZN knows exactly where his sound belongs, and this EP is his handshake to that tribe.



SONIC LANDSCAPE OF THE EP



A study in emotion, groove, and controlled experimentation



Karma



A contemplative record that carries the emotional weight of someone who has tasted life on both sides of grace. The Afro-fusion bounce is subtle but persistent, giving his introspection movement. It’s the kind of track Blackmagic fans would instantly recognize—melodic, honest, spiritually gritty.



Ojuju









A rhythmic standout designed for the Ajebutter/Afro-alté audience. The groove is warm, the delivery is charismatic, and the vulnerability is wrapped in swagger. It’s addictive in that understated, deceptively calm way that “Ye” also mastered—songs that don’t shout but stay with you.



The Full Experience



Across the entire project, you hear an artist shaping atmosphere with intention. The beats breathe. The vocals float. The emotions feel lived-in. The production leans toward minimalism, giving each lyric space to resonate.



This restraint is exactly why fans of Afrofusion and alté gravitate toward artists like Ajebutter22 and Odunsi.



And it’s why they will gravitate toward MBBSZN.



A STORY WITH REAL ROOTS



Life, pressure, culture, and the quiet moments in between



MBBSZN writes like someone who has sat with his own shadows long enough to understand their shape. His verses explore ambition, fear, cultural roots, relationships, and that quiet ache of wanting something bigger for yourself. There’s no performative toughness—just sincerity.



This is the emotional architecture that defines the new wave of Nigerian alternative music.



And MBBSZN fits perfectly into that lineage without sounding like anyone else.



WHY THIS PROJECT IS AN OPPORTUNITY



Strategic positioning for fanbase growth



This EP isn’t simply a release—it’s a market entry strategy.



By aligning his sonic identity with the listener segments orbiting Blackmagic, Ajebutter22, Burna Boy (the deeper cuts), BOJ, Odunsi, and the broader alté/Afro-fusion cosmos, MBBSZN is tapping into:



• an audience that values lyricism



• a fanbase that prioritizes songwriting over hype



• listeners who appreciate texture, emotion, and replay value



• global curators watching the Nigerian alté space closely



This is the exact pocket where long-term cult fanbases form.



The fans who stay.



The fans who evangelize.



The fans who grow with the artist.



CULTURAL & EMOTIONAL RELEVANCE



Why this project resonates beyond sound



Nigeria is a country where pausing feels dangerous—where slowing down looks like failure.







Yet here comes MBBSZN with a contrary thesis:



Rest is part of the process. Survival requires rhythm.



That message aligns with the generation navigating pressure from every direction.



It’s music therapy disguised as Afro-fusion.



It’s cultural commentary disguised as vibe.



It’s motivation whispered instead of screamed.



And that subtlety is exactly what makes it powerful.



MBBSZN IS POSITIONING HIMSELF FOR A CULT FOLLOWING

A fresh voice is rising from Nigeria’s evolving soundscape as Liseh—born Onu Olisaemeka—releases his highly anticipated debut EP, “ReadyUhNot”. The Port Harcourt–raised, Anambra-born singer has been quietly gaining attention for his ability to fuse Afrobeat rhythms, alternative soundscapes, rap cadences, and emotionally charged writing. 







With this 5-track project, Liseh marks a bold entry into Nigeria’s contemporary music conversation, offering a deeply introspective sound that feels authentic, soulful, and strikingly relatable.



“ReadyUhNot” arrives at a moment when young listeners crave honesty, vulnerability, and storytelling they can see themselves in—and Liseh delivers exactly that.



PROJECT OVERVIEW



At its core, “ReadyUhNot” is an emotional exploration of the tension between hesitation and action. It reflects the internal conflict many young adults face—the fear of not being fully prepared, and the courage it takes to step forward anyway.



According to Liseh,



“It reflects my journey of breaking free from perfectionism and trusting the process. Progress speaks louder than perfection, and growth begins the moment you take your first step.”









Across the EP’s five tracks, Liseh blends haunting melodies with gritty undertones and introspective storytelling, balancing heaviness with softness in a way that feels both cinematic and deeply personal. His voice carries a quiet vulnerability—honest but controlled, reflective but forward-moving.



Themes throughout the EP include:



• fear of failure



• self-doubt vs. ambition



• heartbreak and isolation



• pressure to evolve



• courage, movement, and inner growth



From track to track, “ReadyUhNot” builds a world where private battles become art, and uncertainty becomes creative fuel.



CULTURAL & INDUSTRY IMPACT



Liseh stands out because his sound is not built on trends but on texture, emotion, and lived reality. Raised on a mix of traditional African rhythms, global pop, and R&B influences, his sonic identity feels both familiar and refreshingly experimental.



His emergence reflects a growing shift in Nigeria’s youth culture—a movement toward vulnerability, self-awareness, and intentional artistry.




        View this post on Instagram            




Even before the EP dropped, Liseh’s ability to create soulful, atmospheric, and introspective records earned him early admiration from listeners who describe him as “enigmatic,” “unpredictable,” and “deeply intentional.”



Visually and creatively, he brings a quiet aura that pulls audiences in rather than overwhelming them. His brand choices and storytelling suggest a rising star who understands identity, narrative, and emotional resonance—skills crucial to long-term industry relevance.



As “ReadyUhNot” begins circulating across digital platforms, playlists, and growing fan communities, it positions Liseh as a new voice worth watching—one capable of speaking to a generation that battles heartbreak, pressure, ambition, and the desperate need to keep going.



AUDIENCE & RECEPTION



Listeners have begun gravitating toward Liseh’s raw honesty and cinematic sound. His music resonates with people who navigate emotional turbulence behind closed doors—young adults carrying the weight of expectations, dreams, and silent struggles.




Stream ReadyUhNot




With his distinct sound and introspective edge, Liseh is poised to gain support from both mainstream listeners and niche communities seeking meaning-driven music.

Abuja is stepping into a new creative era, and at the center of this rising movement stands Capitol Film Fest 3.0, returning on December 14, 2025, as the city’s biggest annual gathering for filmmakers, artists, storytellers, and culture-shapers. 







In just three years, the festival has evolved into the North’s most vibrant celebration of film and contemporary arts—an immersive convergence of cinema, music, community, and innovation hosted by The Greatest Collective, one of Abuja’s leading creative communities.



A Festival Born From Vision and Community



Capitol Film Fest began as a dream shared by young creators who wanted more than just screenings—they wanted a space where Abuja’s creative identity could thrive. From its humble beginnings as an indie showcase to its current status as a regional cultural phenomenon, the festival has retained its heartbeat: authenticity, collaboration, and a deep belief in storytelling.

















































Today, Capitol Film Fest is widely recognized as the event that has revived the culture of film appreciation in the North. Each edition welcomes a growing crowd of filmmakers, actors, directors, musicians, screenwriters, photographers, cinephiles, and curious newcomers eager to witness the future of cinema from their own city.



What Makes the 2025 Edition Special



This year’s edition promises to be Capitol Film Fest’s most expansive and immersive experience yet. Built around a fusion of independent film screenings, live musical performances, creative showcases, industry conversations, and community activities, the event aims to push the boundaries of what a film festival can be.







Attendees can expect:



• A powerful line-up of new and emerging indie films from Abuja and across Nigeria.




        View this post on Instagram            




• A synchronized live concert featuring some of Abuja’s finest performers.




        View this post on Instagram            




• Interactive discussions and panel sessions with industry professionals.




        View this post on Instagram            




• A vibrant marketplace of creatives, including pop-up vendors, merch stands, artists, and makers.




        View this post on Instagram            




• A red carpet and photo experience designed for creators, brands, and guests.




        View this post on Instagram            




• A growing community space where filmmakers can connect, collaborate, and build future projects.




        View this post on Instagram            




Capitol Film Fest 3.0 stands at the intersection of culture and creativity—equal parts cinematic expression, youth culture, and city identity.



A Platform That Inspires the Next Generation



For filmmakers, Capitol Film Fest has become a launchpad—a place to share new work, meet collaborators, build networks, and find fresh audiences. For emerging talents across music, visual arts, and storytelling, it offers a rare stage that values originality and artistic courage. And for the city’s broader creative ecosystem, the festival serves as a beacon of possibility, proving that world-class culture can thrive in Abuja—not as an imitation of other cities, but as a unique expression of its own creative spirit.




        View this post on Instagram            




Capitol Film Fest 3.0 is not just a date on the calendar; it is a moment of cultural convergence. A celebration of young creators who refuse to wait for permission. A gathering built by community, for community. And a testament to what becomes possible when vision meets relentless passion.




Get Your Tickets




On December 14, 2025, Abuja becomes the Capital of Creativity once again—alive, electric, and ready for the world to watch.

Northern Nigeria’s creative wave is rising fast, and leading that charge is Kaduna’s own Skilon—the Afro-fusion artist and saxophonist whose sound blends soul, rhythm, and cinematic storytelling. On December 13, 2025, Skilon will host OWL FEST (Owl Invasion Abuja) at 3J’s Hotels & Apartments, an immersive live experience projected to pull in more than 800 fans from across the country. More than a show, OWL FEST is shaping up to be a cultural announcement—a moment where Northern artistry claims its place at the center of contemporary African music.







For an artist who calls himself “the dead but not allowed to die,” this concert is both a victory lap and a rebirth.



The Sound of the New North Takes the Stage



Skilon has spent years building a reputation for music that feels honest, layered, and deeply connected to lived experiences. 







His Afro-fusion sound—rooted in Afrobeat, jazz, R&B, and soul—has set him apart as a storyteller with a unique Northern voice. Singles like “Act Like You Know Me” and “Inside” (feat. Millano) have cemented his relevance in digital spaces, with rising streams across Lagos, Abuja, Accra, Nairobi, and Port Harcourt.



But where Skilon truly shines is on stage.



His performances—from intimate Kaduna showcases to thousands of fans at the sold-out Glass House Concert (2023) and the high-energy Owl Fest 2024—have earned him a loyal, organic fanbase built on emotional connection, not hype. With each show, he proves that Northern talent isn’t just catching up—it’s setting a new standard.



OWL FEST 2025 is the next evolution of that standard.



Owl Invasion Abuja: More Than a Concert—A Movement







This year’s edition of OWL FEST represents Skilon’s most ambitious offering yet. Set in Abuja, the cultural capital of Northern entertainment, the event aims to merge live instrumentation, storytelling, and immersive performance art into an unforgettable night.



Fans can expect:



• A full live band experience built around Skilon’s signature saxophone



• New unreleased music revealing his next artistic chapter



• High-energy rearrangements of fan favorites



• Cinematic stagecraft inspired by jazz lounges, Northern culture, and Afro-fusion aesthetics



• A vibrant community atmosphere celebrating the New North’s creative spirit



For first-time attendees, OWL FEST offers a rare chance to witness Skilon’s emotional range up close. For long-time supporters, it is a homecoming—a moment to celebrate how far both the artist and the Northern scene have come.



Why This Night Matters



OWL FEST isn’t just another stop on a performance calendar. It represents something much bigger: the emergence of Northern Nigeria as a rising powerhouse in modern African music. Skilon is not only performing—he is hosting a cultural declaration.





























He is proving that Northern artists can headline their own movements, fill venues, lead communities, and create moments that resonate across borders.



Abuja will become more than a backdrop; it will be the birthplace of a new chapter in Northern sound.



A Personal Invitation From Skilon to His Tribe



At the heart of Skilon’s artistry is connection. His music exists to uplift, to resonate, and to reflect the stories of real people navigating real emotions. His saxophone, his voice, his writing—everything he creates is meant to reach someone who needs it.



OWL FEST is his invitation to you.



Whether you’ve followed him since the Kaduna days or discovered his music yesterday, this night promises to be a shared experience of rhythm, emotion, and pure Northern brilliance.



December 13th Is More Than a Date — It’s a Moment







Skilon isn’t just performing.



He’s building culture.



He’s rewriting perception.



He’s showcasing the power of a Northern voice ready for the global stage.



OWL FEST: Owl Invasion Abuja



Date: December 13, 2025



Venue: 3J’s Hotels & Apartments, Abuja



Capacity: 800+ fans



Experience: Live band • Saxophone magic • New music • Cultural celebration



Mark your calendar. Bring your crew. Come witness the rise of a movement.



Skilon is ready.



Abuja is ready.



The North is rising.

His performances—from intimate Kaduna showcases to thousands of fans at the sold-out Glass House Concert (2023) and the high-energy Owl Fest 2024—have earned him a loyal, organic fanbase built on emotional connection, not hype. With each show, he proves that Northern talent isn’t just catching up—it’s setting a new standard.

OWL FEST 2025 is the next evolution of that standard.

Owl Invasion Abuja: More Than a Concert—A Movement

This year’s edition of OWL FEST represents Skilon’s most ambitious offering yet. Set in Abuja, the cultural capital of Northern entertainment, the event aims to merge live instrumentation, storytelling, and immersive performance art into an unforgettable night.

Fans can expect:

• A full live band experience built around Skilon’s signature saxophone

• New unreleased music revealing his next artistic chapter

• High-energy rearrangements of fan favorites

• Cinematic stagecraft inspired by jazz lounges, Northern culture, and Afro-fusion aesthetics

• A vibrant community atmosphere celebrating the New North’s creative spirit

For first-time attendees, OWL FEST offers a rare chance to witness Skilon’s emotional range up close. For long-time supporters, it is a homecoming—a moment to celebrate how far both the artist and the Northern scene have come.

Why This Night Matters

OWL FEST isn’t just another stop on a performance calendar. It represents something much bigger: the emergence of Northern Nigeria as a rising powerhouse in modern African music. Skilon is not only performing—he is hosting a cultural declaration.

He is proving that Northern artists can headline their own movements, fill venues, lead communities, and create moments that resonate across borders.

Abuja will become more than a backdrop; it will be the birthplace of a new chapter in Northern sound.

A Personal Invitation From Skilon to His Tribe

At the heart of Skilon’s artistry is connection. His music exists to uplift, to resonate, and to reflect the stories of real people navigating real emotions. His saxophone, his voice, his writing—everything he creates is meant to reach someone who needs it.

OWL FEST is his invitation to you.

Whether you’ve followed him since the Kaduna days or discovered his music yesterday, this night promises to be a shared experience of rhythm, emotion, and pure Northern brilliance.

December 13th Is More Than a Date — It’s a Moment

Skilon isn’t just performing.

He’s building culture.

He’s rewriting perception.

He’s showcasing the power of a Northern voice ready for the global stage.

OWL FEST: Owl Invasion Abuja

Date: December 13, 2025

Venue: 3J’s Hotels & Apartments, Abuja

Capacity: 800+ fans

Experience: Live band • Saxophone magic • New music • Cultural celebration

Mark your calendar. Bring your crew. Come witness the rise of a movement.

Skilon is ready.

Abuja is ready.

The North is rising.

Kendol is stepping into his most defining moment yet. The Benin-born Afro-fusion artist has built a reputation for blending rhythm, soul, and street charisma into a sound that feels electric and emotional in equal measure. With his debut EP Get Down Groove, released under Robust Records and produced entirely by Chief Dave D Beat Wizard, Kendol finally presents the full picture of who he is and who he’s becoming. 







The project arrives on a wave of anticipation fueled by viral freestyles, breakout singles, and the confidence of an artist carving his lane with precision.



A New Chapter Built on Vibes, Emotion, and Pure Groove



Get Down Groove marks Kendol’s first fully curated body of work — a six-track experience shaped by the duality that defines him. He’s the lover with a soft, soulful center, and he’s the performer who thrives on energy, rhythm, and dance-floor heat. This EP captures both sides without losing balance. 









Pulling from Afrobeat, Afro-Soul, dancehall, and hip-hop, the project leans into warm melodies, smooth percussion, and that signature street-wise bounce his fans have grown to love.



Kendol describes the project best in his own words:



“Every song I create carries a piece of where I come from and where I’m going.” 



The Story Behind the Sound: A Journey From Benin City to Viral Spotlights



Kendol’s roots run deep. Born and raised in Benin City, Edo State, he absorbed the heart of Afrobeat and the soul of modern rhythm long before the spotlight found him. His sound today reflects that mix of foundation and evolution — emotional, street-savvy, and globally relevant. 







His journey took a sharp upward turn following the success of his viral moments:



• Chris Brown Residual Challenge



• Teni Freestyle Challenge



• GoodGirl LA “Good Girl” cover



Each one showcased a different layer of his artistry — versatility, control, and a fearless approach to performance. 



Singles like “Bunda” and “Fine Face” expanded his reach even further, proving that Kendol had the consistency and charisma to compete among Afro-fusion’s most promising voices. 



The Sonic Architect: Chief Dave D Beat Wizard



A project is only as strong as its production, and Get Down Groove thrives because of its synergy between Kendol and long-time collaborator Chief Dave D Beat Wizard. Credited on every track, the producer delivers lush soundscapes that match Kendol’s emotional cadence, allowing the EP to feel cohesive and deeply intentional. 



Afro-fusion is expanding rapidly, and Kendol is one of the artists stretching the genre with authenticity rather than imitation. His appeal lies in his contrast — street energy wrapped in soulful storytelling — a combination that resonates strongly with a new generation of listeners. 







This EP is a turning point for three reasons:




It presents Kendol’s identity in full detail.Not just vibes. Not just groove. Real emotion, real rhythm, and intentional writing.



It elevates Afro-fusion with a fresh Benin perspective.Kendol stays grounded in where he comes from while shaping a sound built for global stages.



It positions him as one of the genre’s next wave leaders.The consistency behind the singles, virality, and storytelling hints at an artist ready for the long run.




The Verdict: A Must-Listen Milestone for Afro-Fusion Fans



Get Down Groove isn’t just a debut — it’s a declaration. Kendol steps into the center of his sound with confidence, clarity, and a creative spirit that refuses to be boxed in.







It’s the kind of project that connects instantly, but grows deeper with every replay.



Whether you’re drawn to the soulful storytelling, the infectious bounce, or the cultural grounding, this EP delivers on every front.




Stream Now




Kendol is no longer emerging — he’s establishing.

When Walker Mallow steps into a new release cycle, the air shifts a little. The Ghanaian singer and rapper has cultivated a reputation for delivering music that blends emotional depth with modern trap finesse, and his latest single “OBAA” continues that tradition with refined confidence. 







Now available on all digital platforms, the track positions Mallow at a pivotal moment in his creative evolution — one where vulnerability, cultural grounding, and sonic innovation meet seamlessly.



A Song Rooted in Meaning: What “OBAA” Represents



In the Akan language, Obaa means woman, and Walker Mallow leans into that meaning with striking sincerity. “OBAA” is more than admiration set to melody — it is a tribute to the quiet power and natural grace a woman carries without effort. Through warm, intentional writing, the song paints a portrait of instant connection, the kind that disarms and inspires in equal measure.









Rather than chasing fleeting sonic trends, Mallow slows the tempo down — emotionally and musically — offering listeners a breath of calm in an era where most trap-infused records sprint toward virality. Here, he chooses softness as strength.



SAMBII TSB Behind The Boards — A Production Built on Space and Clarity



Produced by Ghana’s own SAMBII TSB, “OBAA” merges hip-hop drum patterns with smooth trap textures, resulting in a soundscape that feels both polished and purposefully restrained. The beat creates room for the story to breathe. No clutter. No noise. Just intention.



Mallow uses that space wisely. His delivery is clean, direct, and emotionally transparent — a rarity in a soundscape often layered with effects and heavy metaphors. That simplicity becomes the song’s superpower.




        View this post on Instagram            




In his own words:



“OBAA is appreciation not just attraction. It’s about the calm someone can bring into your life without even speaking.”



If music had a deep breath, this would be it.



A Steady Climb: Walker Mallow’s Artistic Blueprint



Walker Mallow is far from a newcomer. With more than 12 singles and a full studio album, he has carved out a distinct lane in Ghana’s rising music ecosystem. His style — a fusion of African storytelling, trap sensibilities, and afro-fusion tones — continues to build a signature that listeners can instantly recognize.







Under WALKMUXIC INC, Mallow has mastered the art of experimentation without losing cultural authenticity. Every release feels like a page in a diary, as he refines his voice while pushing Ghanaian music into fresh, global-ready spaces.



A New Era Begins — Out Now Everywhere



With “OBAA” now officially streaming worldwide, Walker Mallow enters a new chapter marked by deeper storytelling and refined sonic direction. Fans can expect visuals, performance cuts, and follow-up records that explore love, evolution, and emotional maturity.




Stream OBAA




Walker Mallow stands at the forefront of Ghana’s new wave — an artist balancing heart and ambition with effortless control. “OBAA” is not just another release; it’s a statement of intention.

articles.body:
County has officially unlocked his newest Afrofusion record, “Fried Rice,” a vibrant, flavour-packed single that expands his artistic universe and cements him as one of the most intriguing new voices in the diaspora music space. 







Following the emotional success of “64 Kids,” County returns with a record that celebrates culture, connection, and the joy woven into the everyday Nigerian experience.



A sonic feast built for replay value



“Fried Rice” isn’t just a song — it’s an atmosphere. County blends warm Afrobeat rhythms with soulful melodies, percussive bounce, and his signature calm, resonant vocal tone. The track feels festive yet intimate, mixing nostalgic Lagos energy with a modern Afrofusion blueprint designed for global ears.









The symbolism is deliberate. In the same way fried rice brings people together at celebrations, County uses the track to highlight unity, gratitude, and the vibrant simplicity of life.



County’s cultural duality on full display



Born in Lagos and shaped further in the UK, County channels his cross-cultural identity with confidence. Where “64 Kids” explored love and vulnerability, “Fried Rice” shifts the lens to joy, community, and the richness of shared experience. It’s proof of his range — the ability to pivot from reflective storytelling to groove-driven Afro rhythms without losing emotional authenticity.







Built for playlists, parties, and personal moments



With its polished production and easily addictive groove, “Fried Rice” positions County squarely in the conversation of next-generation Afrofusion artists pushing the sound forward. This is the kind of record that fits effortlessly into mood playlists, late-night drives, living-room dance sessions, and global Afrobeats rotations.




Stream Fried Rice

Daniel Strongman has built his career on a simple but powerful value proposition: authenticity scales. The Lagos-born, Atlanta-grounded Afrobeats artist continues to elevate that narrative with “Never Change,” his most intimate and emotionally intelligent release to date. 







Known for blending soulful African rhythms with hip-hop grit, Strongman carries the confidence of the streets and the lived experience of someone who has walked through every lyric he delivers. “Never Change” signals a strategic evolution—one that strengthens his brand equity while deepening his storytelling capability.



From “On Me” to Breakout Moments—A Discography Built on Growth



Strongman entered the ecosystem in 2022 with “On Me,” but his defining entry point came a year later with “Big Brudda,” an Afro hip-hop anthem that echoed through Atlanta, Lagos, and diaspora communities hungry for a hybrid sound. By 2024, he doubled down with “Handle It,” a high-octane release born from the adrenaline of one of his most electrifying performance nights. Later that year he expanded his sonic palette with “PREE,” a textured, flute-driven record rooted in honest introspection. This catalogue has positioned him as one of the new-wave voices building cultural bridges between West Africa and the U.S.



Introducing “Never Change” — A Vulnerable, Cinematic Pivot



“Never Change” marks a shift from raw bravado to emotional depth. The record blends Afro-R&B warmth, mellow AfroSwing bounce, Yoruba melodies, and atmospheric Afro-Pop sensibilities. 









It’s a love letter to strong brown-skin women—the ones who stay consistent through storms, ego, and distance. The songwriting carries a softness that reveals a new layer of Strongman’s artistry, balancing vulnerability with the melodic confidence his audience already connects with.



The rollout itself is deliberately crafted: candle-lit scenes, narrations styled like vintage love letters, and visuals inspired by the 1700s–1900s romantic era. It’s a strategic brand moment—one that expands his visual language and positions him for lifestyle, fashion, and cinematic partnerships.







Cultural Footprint, Creative Community, and Rising Influence



Strongman’s presence extends well beyond the booth. He has graced major Atlanta Afrobeat platforms like MyAfrobeat Nights and has built relationships with respected creatives including Kelvin Boj, Praiz, and Niphkeys. 




        View this post on Instagram            




His ecosystem spans music, visual art, and fashion—anchored in a personal philosophy that “Dreams Shape Men.” This multi-disciplinary branding gives him a competitive advantage as Afro-fusion continues its global acceleration.




Stream NEVER CHANGE

After a breakout year that firmly put Abuja’s blossoming Afro-fusion ecosystem on the national radar, Mamuzo is closing 2025 with a statement release: two brand-new singles, “Go Pay” and “3D Level,” dropping Friday, November 21. Known for blending Afrobeat, highlife, and modern alté textures into a sound that’s unmistakably his, Mamuzo has become one of the most intriguing young voices rising out of the capital.







This new double drop is more than another release cycle — it’s the culmination of a year defined by growth metrics, fan engagement, creative leaps, and a sharpening artistic identity.



Momentum Built on Milestones



2025 has been a year of strategic output and steady audience expansion for Mamuzo. He kicked off the year with “Jazzman,” a high-energy collaboration with Tehn10, Soundboi BME, and DJ Obidi that fused jazz-inflected riffs with a percussive Afrobeat backbone. The record travelled fast within Abuja’s scene and became an early signal that Mamuzo was engineering a distinctive lane.



By July, he followed up with “Madmoiselle,” a multilingual, melody-rich anthem centered on love, loyalty, hustle, and emotional sincerity. Sung in a seamless mix of Pidgin English and his native dialect, the track highlighted his storytelling ability and expanded his resonance with listeners across demographics. Audiences gravitated toward the song’s groove, and the numbers reflected it.



Across the catalogue, Mamuzo’s streams have continued to climb through the year, with his broader discography crossing the 20,000+ mark on key platforms. New listeners keep entering the funnel with every release, and his live performances across Abuja have consistently drawn larger crowds. BlaqRose arrives with 3 Of Life, and what he delivers is more than a project—it’s a deeply human experience crafted for anyone who has ever fought, doubted, prayed, or dreamed. It’s intimate, raw, spiritual, and unmistakably his. But most importantly, it’s a gift to the fans who have watched his evolution in real time.







This release stands as a full-circle moment in his eight-year grind. BlaqRose doesn’t just make music here—he bares his soul, opens his scars, and builds a bridge straight to anyone who knows what it means to rise from nothing.



A PROJECT WITH A PULSE



The cover alone announces that this is no ordinary body of work: a radiant woman before the Tree of Life, crowned in light, surrounded by black roses blooming through broken ground. She represents all of us—the vessel, the journey, the pain, the rebirth. Behind her, the Tree rises like BlaqRose himself: roots in North Bank, branches stretching into new worlds.



Every element echoes one idea:



your story matters, your pain has purpose, and your growth is sacred.









That’s the heart of 3 Of Life—a project built on the threefold nature of existence:



Body, Soul, Spirit. Birth, Becoming, Bloom. Roots, Rise, Fruit.



These are not abstract themes; they’re the emotional coordinates of BlaqRose’s life. And he translates those coordinates into sound.



TRACKS REVIEW: WHERE FANS MEET HIS TRUTH









PERSONAL JOURNEY



A confessional opener that invites listeners into the reality behind the music. The track feels like a mirror—everyone who’s ever struggled will hear themselves inside it. The chorus becomes a mantra: free your mind, let your light keep burning. Fans will feel the weight of that line because it’s a daily reminder to hold on.



ONE DREAM



This one hits the fans directly. It’s a track that celebrates those who kept streaming, sharing, cheering—even when the world doubted. When he sings, “Na my music them dey stream,” it feels like a thank-you note disguised as an anthem.



BADMANROSE



A gritty portrait of the boy before the artist. Fans who’ve followed him from the trenches will hear familiar echoes—North Bank, Lafia Junction, broken boundaries, and divine survival. This track is street poetry with spiritual undertones, a reminder that greatness can rise from overlooked places.



FREEDOM



A moment of clarity for anyone fighting internal battles. BlaqRose asks the questions we avoid: Does your freedom give you peace? The track becomes a space of reflection—a sanctuary inside the album where listeners can breathe.



E TOO SURE



The emotional peak of the project. It’s the sound of someone who almost quit, almost fell, almost faded—but didn’t. The inclusion of his mother’s prayer transforms the song into something sacred. Fans will feel the sincerity, the weight, and the gratitude. It’s one of those rare songs that stays with you long after the project ends.



WHY THIS PROJECT CONNECTS



3 Of Life resonates because it refuses to pretend. It honours the pain people carry quietly. It honours the dreams fans chase silently. It honours the faith many hold onto privately.









BlaqRose doesn’t position himself above his listeners—he stands with them.



He makes music like someone who has lived inside the struggle, not written about it from afar.



And that authenticity is what fans have always loved about him.



A SOUND UNAFRAID OF TRUTH



Sonically, BlaqRose blends Afro-fusion, melodic rap, and grounded storytelling. But beneath the production lies a deeper resonance: every line sounds lived-in, every word earned. The project carries the weight of someone who has walked through storms and found his way home.







A MESSAGE FOR THE FANS



3 Of Life reminds every listener that:



You can rise from anything. You can bloom from scars. Your story is still being written. Your pain can become prophecy.




Stream 3 OF LIFE




BlaqRose isn’t just sharing his journey—he’s lighting a path for anyone still fighting through theirs.

Fast-rising Nigerian artist Khaliberry has just unveiled his latest single “Nice To Know You” — a smooth, soul-tinged Afrobeats record featuring the vibrant VJ Skinny. The song represents a pivotal moment in Khaliberry’s journey, merging rhythm and raw emotion to tell a story that feels both personal and universal. 







Released on November 7, 2025, the record is now streaming on all major platforms via Dvpper Music.



THE ARTIST: KHALIBERRY’S RISE TO RECOGNITION



Born Alfa Enemona Calistus, Khaliberry hails from Kogi State but was raised in Abuja, Nigeria, where his love for music began to take root. Drawing inspiration from icons like Fela Kuti, Bob Marley, Wizkid, Burna Boy, and Rema, his style fuses the essence of Afrobeats, Pop, and Dancehall into a unique sound that’s both refreshing and deeply relatable.







Khaliberry made his professional debut in 2019 with the single “Body”, marking the start of a journey defined by passion, growth, and authenticity. Over the years, he has built a loyal audience that connects to his sincerity and creative evolution — a testament to his commitment to excellence and his city’s buzzing entertainment scene.



THE RECORD: “NICE TO KNOW YOU” – A STORY OF FEELINGS AND FREEDOM



“Nice To Know You” is more than just a feel-good Afrobeats jam — it’s a reflection of modern emotional struggles and self-awareness. Khaliberry describes the song as being “built out of a situation,” capturing the reality of navigating relationships in a world where personal desires often outweigh true emotions.









“The lyrics tell a story of someone’s journey through life with the female gender,” Khaliberry shares. “Society has made people place their needs above emotions and true feelings. As a badman, I’d rather let it go than try to prove a point.”



Sonically, the record thrives on its simplicity — clean percussion, mellow guitar riffs, and melodic vocals that glide effortlessly across the beat. It’s a mood-setter, a late-night anthem, and a perfect balance between reflection and rhythm.



THE COLLABORATION: VJ SKINNY’S VIBRANT TOUCH



The inclusion of VJ Skinny elevates “Nice To Know You” into a full-bodied collaboration. His smooth delivery and magnetic presence add color and depth to the song’s emotional undertones. Together, Khaliberry and VJ Skinny strike a delicate balance — blending vulnerability with charisma and melody with message.




        View this post on Instagram            




“This record marks an exciting new chapter for me,” Khaliberry explains. “I wanted to experiment with a different sound and direction, and VJ Skinny brought exactly the kind of energy that made the song come alive.”



Their chemistry is undeniable — it’s a collaboration that feels organic, like two creatives aligning their energies for a shared purpose.



THE MESSAGE: GROWTH, VERSATILITY, AND REALITY



“Nice To Know You” stands as a bold declaration of artistic growth and emotional maturity. Khaliberry uses this song to explore his evolving sound, stretching beyond the boundaries of his earlier work while maintaining his signature authenticity. It’s both a reflection of his current mindset and a preview of what’s to come.



The track reveals an artist not afraid to be real — to show the cracks and complexities that make human connections messy, meaningful, and memorable.



THE NEXT CHAPTER FOR KHALIBERRY



“Nice To Know You” is more than a collaboration — it’s a milestone in Khaliberry’s evolution as an artist. With its heartfelt lyrics, infectious rhythm, and impeccable production, the single proves that he’s ready to push beyond limits and claim his space in the Afrobeats scene.




Stream Nice To Know You




Available now on all streaming platforms, “Nice To Know You” is a must-listen for anyone who loves honest storytelling wrapped in irresistible melody.

Today marks a defining moment for Nigerian rising star Fav4 (real name Onwusor Chukwuemeka Favour) as he officially releases his debut self-titled EP, FAV4.







Born in Owerri and now based in Lagos, Fav4 delivers a refreshing Afro-fusion experience that bridges spirituality, hustle, and street energy into one powerful body of work. The seven-track project introduces him as a dynamic voice — confident in delivery, grounded in faith, and fluent in the languages of English, Igbo, and Pidgin.



The EP: A Sonic Balance of Faith and Fire



FAV4 features crisp, melodic production from BigProm, with additional input from Spiritual Beat and Scopenero, resulting in a sound that’s polished, soulful, and deeply rooted in African rhythm.



From the jubilant praise of “Hallelujah” to the sultry flow of “Aquafina”, each song reflects Fav4’s multi-dimensional artistry:










“Hallelujah” – A vibrant Afro-pop anthem celebrating gratitude and spiritual victory.



“Hustle & Bustle” – A motivational ode to resilience and street ambition.



“Tambourine” – A playful, rhythmic Afrobeat groove built for dancefloors.



“Trabaye” – A bold, energetic street anthem fueled by confidence and charisma.



“Gangster Love” – A gritty yet heartfelt story of love and loyalty.



“Aquafina” – A smooth, late-night Afrobeat track laced with warmth and seduction.



“She” – The emotional closer — tender, sincere, and soul-rich.




Fav4’s Arrival



FAV4 is more than a debut — it’s a declaration. It introduces an artist who embodies the duality of the modern African youth: faithful yet fierce, spiritual yet street-smart. His music captures both the reflective calm of devotion and the fiery rhythm of ambition.




Stream Fav4

Nigerian hitmaker Giftty sets the tone for the festive season with his electrifying new single “Jaye”, featuring one of Nigeria’s sharpest lyricists, Dandizzy. The collaboration delivers a seamless blend of Afrobeats groove and hip-hop precision, creating a sound that’s as soulful as it is contagious.







“Jaye,” a Yoruba expression meaning enjoy life, captures the spirit of youthful freedom, ambition, and joy. It’s not just a song — it’s a mantra for those who’ve fought through struggle and still choose to dance. Giftty’s smooth vocals and irresistible melody make the hook unforgettable, while Dandizzy’s razor-sharp bars inject a dose of grit and lyrical finesse that speaks to every hustler chasing their dream.









With its vibrant percussion, catchy chants, and feel-good rhythm, “Jaye” is built for the dancefloor yet carries an emotional undercurrent — a reminder that joy is an act of defiance in a world that constantly tests our resolve. Giftty channels that defiance into something bold and inspiring, marking a fresh era in his artistry.

articles.body:
After charming listeners with the soulful storytelling of “64 Kids”, UK-based Nigerian artist County returns with a bold and flavorful new single, “Fried Rice.” 







Dropping November 5th, the song promises a vibrant blend of Afrobeat rhythm, Afrofusion groove, and County’s signature emotional depth — a sound built to move both heart and body.



A FLAVORFUL SOUNDTRACK TO MODERN AFROBEAT



“Fried Rice” takes its name from one of Nigeria’s most beloved dishes, turning the everyday meal into a metaphor for connection, culture, and joy. County serves up a sonic feast — layered percussion, rhythmic guitars, and lush melodies simmer beneath his smooth, heartfelt vocals. The track moves effortlessly between high-energy Afrobeat and mellow soul textures, showing how fusion can still sound organic and deeply rooted.







“Music should feel like a meal,” County says. “You should taste it, share it, and remember it.”



A CROSS-CULTURAL VOICE WITH GLOBAL REACH



Following the acclaim of “64 Kids,” which introduced him as a rising voice of emotional honesty in Afrobeat, County continues his evolution with “Fried Rice.” Born in Lagos and based in the UK, his artistry bridges two worlds — African rhythm and Western refinement — with effortless synergy. The result is a track that feels timeless and global, yet unmistakably Nigerian at its core.







Where “64 Kids” explored love and vulnerability, “Fried Rice” celebrates life, gratitude, and the small things that make community powerful. It’s County’s way of saying: even in chaos, there’s something beautiful to savor.




Presave Fried Rice




Fans can pre-save “Fried Rice” now on all streaming platforms ahead of its release tomorrow. Expect a rich Afrofusion anthem that balances celebration with sentiment — a record that could easily soundtrack both your kitchen and your dance floor.

The Orange Flame Meets the Purple Militant



In a clash of sound, energy, and identity, Jos-bred Afrofusion powerhouse Asound teams up with rising Afrobeat talent Xaint Jhaypee for “Carnivorous Animal” — a bold new record that tears through convention with raw emotion, street realism, and spiritual undertones.







The track is more than a song — it’s a mirror held up to the chaos of survival. Built around sharp lyricism and a hauntingly groovy beat, “Carnivorous Animal” exposes the predatory nature of the modern hustle, where morality and ambition wrestle for dominance in a world that demands both faith and ferocity.



The Sound of Survival



From the first line, “Wetin me see that day no be joker / Spiritually speaking I been koker,” the record dives into a world where darkness and divine purpose coexist.









The narrative feels cinematic — a spiritual battleground painted with the vivid realism of street life. The hook, “Carnivorous Animal / Street is getting cold with no cardigan,” sums up the hunger, the cold ambition, and the loneliness of the chase.



Asound, known for blending melodic warmth with emotional gravity, uses this track to flex his versatility — merging soulful Afrofusion energy with gritty urban storytelling. Meanwhile, Xaint Jhaypee’s verse injects a raw youthful defiance, balancing vulnerability with swagger: “Goal is getting money and be filthy rich / Pull up in Aston Martin with six bitches.”




        View this post on Instagram            




It’s unfiltered, it’s bold, and it captures the modern artist’s paradox — chasing light in a world ruled by shadows.



Asound: The Orange Prophet



For Asound (Aaron Nenliah Mike), music has always been a divine calling. Born in Jos, Nigeria, his journey began with a surreal moment — a flock of birds circling as he sang in high school — a sign he still credits as proof of purpose. Since then, his artistry has been built on faith, fearlessness, and the color orange — symbolizing warmth, confidence, and creative fire.







His catalog, from “Love Karma” to “Perilous Pack,” reflects a consistent evolution: deeply emotional yet sonically global. The Orange Family — his ever-growing fan community — represents not just listeners but believers in self-expression, unity, and bold authenticity.



With “Carnivorous Animal,” Asound expands that mission — tackling the grit of street realities while still championing spiritual awareness.



Xaint Jhaypee: The Purple Militant



Born in Enugu and raised in Jos, Xaint Jhaypee (Joseph N. Patrick) represents a new breed of Afrobeat visionaries — deeply rooted in rhythm but unafraid to speak uncomfortable truths. His sound is an intoxicating mix of Afrobeats, R&B, and melodic storytelling — a space where vulnerability meets dominance.







Songs like “Sweet Temptation” and “Love Don’t Lie” showed his emotional range, but on “Carnivorous Animal,” he steps into darker terrain. His “Purple Militant” persona shines through — reflective of power, royalty, and rebellion. His verse doesn’t just complement Asound’s energy; it completes it, turning the track into a duet of hunger and hope.



The Message Behind the Madness



Despite its gritty tone, “Carnivorous Animal” is a layered record. Beneath the flashy bars and hard-hitting rhythm lies a warning — the streets are getting colder, and survival now demands instinct.



The “carnivorous” metaphor speaks to the moral erosion of modern hustle culture, where everyone’s fighting to eat, and only those who stay spiritually grounded survive with their soul intact.




Stream Carnivorous Animal




It’s both a banger and a sermon. A song you can vibe to, yet think about long after it fades out.

OG Armani returns with “Zoned Out”, a sonic journey that blends introspection, rhythm, and psychedelic allure into one immersive experience. 







Featuring the distinct vocals of Bolt LSG — short for Lyrical Sound God — this record captures a creative partnership built on authenticity and effortless chemistry. Together, they transport listeners into a state of self-awareness and calm rebellion — the kind where silence feels loud, and peace feels earned.The Sound: Where Psychedelia Meets Alte EnergyFrom the very first note, “Zoned Out” thrives on its hypnotic, layered production — a canvas of lush synths, deep percussion, and subtle trippy effects that instantly pull you into Armani’s creative mind. His lyrical delivery sits perfectly between poetic reflection and street realism, embodying the Hip-Hop/Alte fusion that defines the modern African soundscape.









Bolt LSG complements this energy with his signature baritone, providing warmth and gravity to the track. His presence isn’t just featured — it’s essential. The synergy between the two artists feels organic, like two frequencies aligning to form one continuous pulse.The Message: Self-Expression Through IsolationIn Armani’s words, “Zoned Out means being in your own space (zone), not bothered about anything or anyone, and ultimately landing in a euphoric state.”It’s a record about peace in solitude — the kind of mindset artists, dreamers, and visionaries often find themselves chasing. There’s a subtle rebellion in the tone — not the loud defiance of chaos, but the quiet discipline of focus. It’s a reminder that zoning out isn’t about escape; it’s about returning to yourself.




        View this post on Instagram            




The Creators: OG Armani & Bolt LSGOG Armani continues to evolve as one of the most genuine new voices in Hip-Hop and Alte. Known for his ability to fuse meaningful lyricism with dynamic production, Armani’s storytelling resonates with those who crave both substance and rhythm in equal measure. His sound is emotionally textured — every bar feels lived, every line intentional.Bolt LSG, whose name translates to Lyrical Sound God, embodies vocal mastery with his smooth baritone and intuitive storytelling. His presence on “Zoned Out” elevates the record into something timeless — a moment of musical reflection you can feel as much as you hear.

articles.body:
MBBSZN has officially returned — and this time, he’s not narrating survival; he’s celebrating seduction. His brand-new single “Ojuju” featuring Defa OF is a feverish cocktail of rhythm, wit, and raw attraction. It’s a record that fuses the grit of the streets with the gloss of Afrofusion nightlife, transforming temptation into sound.







Where “Ya Diba” told stories of hustle and scars, “Ojuju” invites listeners into the after-hours — where pleasure, danger, and self-confidence collide. The shift feels deliberate: MBBSZN is shedding old skin and embracing an evolved sound defined by bass-heavy percussion, teasing vocals, and swagger that sticks.



The Chemistry That Defines a Generation



The synergy between MBBSZN and Defa OF is immediate — effortless, fiery, and addictive. Their verses bounce like a conversation between confidence and control: MBBSZN’s rugged charisma finds perfect balance in Defa OF’s measured delivery.









Lines like “Defa OF A+ / I no dey fw C-” echo a playful bravado that gives the record its charm, while the infectious hook “Baby just dance for me…” turns vulnerability into command. It’s two artists flexing chemistry without ego — just rhythm and intent.



“Ojuju” — From Calabar to the World



Lyrically, Ojuju is an ode to sensual chaos. MBBSZN’s muse — a Calabar beauty — becomes the symbol of irresistible temptation. His words are mischievous, full of exaggeration and humor: “I no fit carry her nyash / E be like 10 girls own combined.” Yet beneath the banter lies a sharp understanding of modern romance — fast, digital, and dangerously charming.



The track’s sonic palette leans into Afrobeat percussion layered with R&B texture and club-ready bounce. The result is a record that can light up dancefloors while keeping lyric-heads nodding in approval.



From “Ya Diba” to “Ojuju” — The Artist Evolves



MBBSZN’s storytelling has always been personal. In “Ya Diba,” he rapped about pain, hustle, and the struggle to rise. With “Ojuju,” he’s choosing joy — not as denial, but as proof of survival. It’s the energy of an artist who’s learned to enjoy the light after walking through long nights.




        View this post on Instagram            




This duality — grit and groove, pain and play — defines the new MBBSZN. He’s no longer the underdog; he’s the man at the center of the dancefloor, owning his story with rhythm instead of rage.



Defa OF — The Catalyst of Cool



Defa OF doesn’t just feature; he amplifies. His verse slides in with confident restraint, creating the contrast that makes Ojuju so dynamic. Together, they bridge two sonic worlds — the lyrical edge of conscious street music and the polished feel of Afro-lounge sophistication.




        View this post on Instagram            




This collaboration signals a new creative chemistry in the Nigerian scene — one driven by intention, artistry, and cultural wit.



A Celebration of Sound and Freedom



Ojuju is more than a record; it’s a statement of freedom — from pressure, from perception, from the weight of “proving something.” It’s MBBSZN’s most confident sound yet, the type of music made when an artist stops chasing approval and starts building his own legend.




Stream “OJUJU”

Following the momentum of his breakout single “K K K”, Teegha DapluG, also known as BiG 7, steps back into the spotlight with a highly anticipated new release titled “Come 2 Me.” The Northern-born rapper, songwriter, and creative visionary is once again proving why he’s one of the most promising forces in Nigeria’s alternative hip-hop scene.



Screenshot



Known for his deep, resonant voice and unapologetic storytelling, Teegha doesn’t just rap—he communicates. With “Come 2 Me,” he peels back another layer of his artistry, offering listeners a sound that’s both intimate and explosive, personal yet deeply relatable.



A New Era for DapluG RepubliK

A New Dawn for Alternative Soul



Today marks a defining moment for Nigeria’s alternative R&B and soul scene as Zipowei unveils her long-awaited project, “Echoes of Zi.” The project captures the core of who she is — raw, soulful, and unafraid. More than a collection of songs, it feels like a letter to herself and to every listener learning to stand in their truth.







Zipowei, known for her delicate balance of emotional storytelling and cultural fusion, offers a soundscape that bridges Nigeria’s rhythmic pulse with the global soul movement. Her music doesn’t chase trends; it invites intimacy. “Echoes of Zi” arrives as a breath of clarity in a world of chaos.




“I wanted this project to feel like reflection — like standing still long enough to hear your own thoughts echo back,” Zipowei says.




Behind the Sound: Crafting “Echoes of Zi”



The journey to “Echoes of Zi” was deeply personal. Recorded between Abuja and Lagos, the EP took shape over quiet nights of introspection, experimentation, and truth-telling. Zipowei collaborated with select producers and instrumentalists who understood her vision for a sonic experience rooted in both stillness and emotion.









Each track tells its own story — “Bloom” explores self-growth, “Crave” dives into desire and vulnerability, while “Vulnerability Games” showcases her lyrical honesty. The sound is lush yet minimal, blending live instrumentation, moody synths, and her unmistakable velvet voice.



This is not an artist following a formula; it’s one carving her lane with intention.



The Vision: Building the “Gen Zi” Movement



At the heart of Zipowei’s creative philosophy is her community — Gen Zi. What started as a name for her fanbase has grown into a cultural collective that celebrates authenticity, emotional growth, and self-expression.



Through Gen Zi, Zipowei creates a safe space for people to embrace their own complexities. Her audience doesn’t just listen to her music; they see themselves in it. Every lyric, post, and visual release strengthens that connection.




“I’ve always wanted my music to feel like a conversation — not performance,” she says. “Gen Zi is about that connection, about finding people who feel too much and realizing that’s a gift.”




Aesthetic Identity: The Visual Story of Zi



Visually, “Echoes of Zi” mirrors the sound — cinematic, minimal, and ethereal. Her aesthetic draws from her Nigerian roots while borrowing textures from neo-soul and indie visual cultures. Flowing fabrics, warm tones, and symbolic imagery define the project’s rollout, communicating a soft but powerful statement: vulnerability is strength.




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by zi (@zipowei)




Her upcoming visuals promise storytelling that is equally introspective — a mix of surreal imagery, natural elements, and spiritual undertones that paint her journey from self-doubt to self-acceptance.



The Message: Healing Through Sound



What makes “Echoes of Zi” stand out isn’t just its production or vocal delivery — it’s the emotion. Zipowei doesn’t sing to impress; she sings to heal. Each song feels like a confession whispered through melody, a safe space for hearts that crave understanding.



In her world, music is therapy. Her stories touch on love, identity, growth, and the quiet moments of becoming — all framed through her Nigerian heritage and her global soundscape.



This blend of honesty and innovation positions Zipowei as one of the most promising voices shaping Africa’s alternative future.



A Movement, Not a Moment



“Echoes of Zi” is not the end — it’s the beginning of a movement. Zipowei is redefining what it means to be a soulful artist in today’s digital world: emotionally intelligent, culturally grounded, and globally resonant.




Stream Echoes of Zi




As the EP hits streaming platforms today, the world gets to experience what her growing fanbase already knows — Zipowei isn’t just making music; she’s building a legacy of truth.

THE DUALITY OF “RHYTHM AND RAGE”



Nigerian-born, Istanbul-based artist Vuga Kvngz returns with a compelling new project titled Rhythm and Rage — an emotionally charged body of work that explores the fragile intersection between passion and pain.







Renowned for his genre-defying artistry, Vuga masterfully weaves together elements of Hip-Hop, R&B, Afrobeats, and Alternative sounds to create his signature sonic identity known as Vuga Vibes. With Rhythm and Rage, he delivers his most personal and vulnerable expression yet — a bold exploration of human emotion, inner conflict, and artistic evolution.



This project is not just music; it’s a confession — unfiltered, soulful, and unapologetically raw.



A TRACKLIST THAT TELLS A STORY



Every track on Rhythm and Rage unfolds a different layer of Vuga Kvngz’s psyche, reflecting his journey through self-discovery, ambition, and emotional intensity.









Buss It Down — a high-octane opener that asserts confidence, drive, and ambition. Jigga ft Ralph — a vibrant collaboration fusing trap energy with Afro-fusion melody. My Way — a reflective anthem celebrating independence and self-assurance. Road Man Gist ft Reeplay — gritty and grounded, capturing the rhythm of the streets and the hustle within. Stuck in My Ways — intimate storytelling that balances pride with vulnerability. Trap Work — a hustler’s chronicle layered with cinematic production and focused lyricism. Blicky Talk ft Mister B — an explosive finale that embodies strength, survival, and sonic dominance.




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Vuga Kvngz (@vugakvngzofficial)




Collectively, the seven tracks chart an emotional journey — from Rhythm to rage, serenity to chaos — the dual forces that continue to shape Vuga’s creative spirit.



FROM IMO STATE TO ISTANBUL — A GLOBAL VOICE IN MOTION



Hailing from Imo State, Nigeria, Vuga Kvngz (real name Chiedozie Eze Walter) began his musical pursuit after earning a degree in Political Science. His move to Istanbul, Turkey, not only broadened his worldview but reignited his passion for music — inspiring him to craft a sound that bridges continents.







Through his imprint World Boyz Entertainment, co-founded with his cousin Cheng, Vuga has become a key figure in the growing African creative scene abroad. The collective’s event series Worldly Activities and its fashion-forward extension, World Boyz Collective, serve as cultural platforms that merge music, art, and fashion — cultivating a vibrant community of creatives in Istanbul.



Rhythm and Rage stands as the latest manifestation of this ecosystem — a project that’s globally inspired yet deeply rooted in African rhythm and soul.




STREAM “RHYTHM AND RAGE”




Rhythm and Rage by Vuga Kvngz is officially out now on all major streaming platforms including Spotify, Apple Music, Audiomack, and Boomplay.
