THE CAPITAL’S SOUND IS GETTING LOUDER



Abuja’s music circuit has become a living frequency — a blend of grit, luxury, humor, and ambition vibrating through clubs, street corners, and streaming platforms. This week’s Top100 Abuja Charts captures that energy perfectly: two major Odumodublvck records lead the pack while emerging talents like FirstKlaz, SoundboiBme, and Nunu Eluma redefine the soundscape from the ground up.







The collaboration between The GrillHype, RADARCharts by REM, and Abuja’s leading cultural platforms signals a new era of data-driven music journalism. Together, they’re not just ranking songs — they’re documenting a city’s rhythm.

















#1 — “BIG TIME” (feat. Wizkid) by ODUMODUBLVCK & Wizkid



When street rap meets silky Afrobeats precision, sparks fly. BIG TIME stands tall for its confident swagger, powered by ODUMODUBLVCK’s unflinching delivery and Wizkid’s effortless global cool. The record topped both Apple Music Nigeria and Audiomack Abuja charts, confirming that Odumodu’s signature rawness can thrive in polished spaces.









Critics have hailed it as “the sound of Abuja confidence” — a city that’s tired of playing catch-up and ready to lead.



#2 — “Lili” by FirstKlaz  & Iliya Entertainment Music



If BIG TIME is a roar, Lili is a whisper that travels far. FirstKlaz’s heartfelt delivery sits on a smooth Afro-fusion groove, balancing melancholy with melody. The track has gained momentum through social media storytelling — short videos and user-generated covers spreading its message of resilience and soft strength.



It’s a defining moment for Iliya Entertainment, signaling a north-meets-capital crossover in the mainstream scene.



#3 — “Howfar” by SoundboiBme, OBA DDJ45



Raw. Honest. Relatable. Howfar speaks the language of every Abuja hustler. SoundboiBme and OBA DDJ45 blend street cadence with digital finesse, creating a track that feels both gritty and futuristic. The pair’s chemistry is magnetic — echoing the underground’s growing power in shaping Abuja’s pop future.



#4 — “GROOVING” (feat. Davido & Seun Kuti) by ODUMODUBLVCK, Davido & Seun Kuti



The capital’s anthem of collaboration. Three generations of Nigerian sound — Seun Kuti’s brass legacy, Davido’s hitmaking instinct, and Odumodu’s street fire — combine into a pulsating hybrid that’s both nostalgic and new. It’s political, cultural, and proudly chaotic.



#5 — “100 Meters” by Shagba



Fast-paced and motivational, 100 Meters sprints through motivational rap verses and catchy hooks. Shagba’s breakout track is finding its footing on TikTok with fitness and hustle-themed edits.



#6 — “RUFF” by Geezyshore



Port Harcourt grit meets Abuja confidence. RUFF is unapologetically street, fusing patois, pidgin, and mid-tempo rhythm. It’s an anthem for those who see survival as a sport.



#7 — “No Chicken Na Kpomo” by Sativa Boy



Sativa Boy brings humor to highlife bounce. No Chicken Na Kpomo proves that virality doesn’t need a label deal — just attitude and relatability. DJs across the capital are spinning it for its pure comic relief energy.



#8 — “Just You and I” by Nunu Eluma



Soft, heartfelt, and mature. Nunu Eluma’s presence at #8 reflects the increasing visibility of Abuja’s female voices. Just You and I is a radio-ready ballad, smooth and cinematic — love songs still have a place in the chaos.



#9 — “Mother Confessor” by Lysense Slim



Dark, poetic, and unapologetically experimental. Lysense Slim’s Mother Confessor weaves spiritual imagery and Afro-trap ambience. It’s less a song and more a confession booth in stereo — proving Abuja’s underground scene has artistic depth beyond the party.



#10 — “Alaye” by Boylikevilla



Alaye closes the week’s Top 10 with the hunger of youth energy. Boylikevilla embodies the “no label, no limit” generation — young, raw, and buzzing off grassroots streams. Clubs in Wuse and Gwarinpa are already chanting along.









TRENDS — THE PULSE OF ABUJA



The Odumodu Era: Two tracks in the Top 5 prove his cultural command. New Balance Between Street & Soft: The coexistence of Lili, Howfar, and No Chicken Na Kpomo shows a shift toward emotional openness, humor, and individuality. Women Rising: Nunu Eluma’s Top 10 debut reminds the industry that female voices in Abuja are ready for spotlight rotation. Indie Power: Five of the Top 10 come from independent or regional imprints — the DIY movement is alive.

The pair’s chemistry is magnetic — echoing the underground’s growing power in shaping Abuja’s pop future.

#4 — “GROOVING” (feat. Davido & Seun Kuti) by ODUMODUBLVCK, Davido & Seun Kuti

The capital’s anthem of collaboration. Three generations of Nigerian sound — Seun Kuti’s brass legacy, Davido’s hitmaking instinct, and Odumodu’s street fire — combine into a pulsating hybrid that’s both nostalgic and new. It’s political, cultural, and proudly chaotic.

#5 — “100 Meters” by Shagba

Fast-paced and motivational, 100 Meters sprints through motivational rap verses and catchy hooks. Shagba’s breakout track is finding its footing on TikTok with fitness and hustle-themed edits.

#6 — “RUFF” by Geezyshore

Port Harcourt grit meets Abuja confidence. RUFF is unapologetically street, fusing patois, pidgin, and mid-tempo rhythm. It’s an anthem for those who see survival as a sport.

#7 — “No Chicken Na Kpomo” by Sativa Boy

Sativa Boy brings humor to highlife bounce. No Chicken Na Kpomo proves that virality doesn’t need a label deal — just attitude and relatability. DJs across the capital are spinning it for its pure comic relief energy.

#8 — “Just You and I” by Nunu Eluma

Soft, heartfelt, and mature. Nunu Eluma’s presence at #8 reflects the increasing visibility of Abuja’s female voices. Just You and I is a radio-ready ballad, smooth and cinematic — love songs still have a place in the chaos.

#9 — “Mother Confessor” by Lysense Slim

Dark, poetic, and unapologetically experimental. Lysense Slim’s Mother Confessor weaves spiritual imagery and Afro-trap ambience. It’s less a song and more a confession booth in stereo — proving Abuja’s underground scene has artistic depth beyond the party.

#10 — “Alaye” by Boylikevilla

Alaye closes the week’s Top 10 with the hunger of youth energy. Boylikevilla embodies the “no label, no limit” generation — young, raw, and buzzing off grassroots streams. Clubs in Wuse and Gwarinpa are already chanting along.

TRENDS — THE PULSE OF ABUJA

The Odumodu Era: Two tracks in the Top 5 prove his cultural command. New Balance Between Street & Soft: The coexistence of Lili, Howfar, and No Chicken Na Kpomo shows a shift toward emotional openness, humor, and individuality. Women Rising: Nunu Eluma’s Top 10 debut reminds the industry that female voices in Abuja are ready for spotlight rotation. Indie Power: Five of the Top 10 come from independent or regional imprints — the DIY movement is alive.

FAN REACTIONS

Across X and TikTok, the hashtags #Top100Abuja and #RADARCharts are trending locally. One fan calls BIG TIME “the anthem of FCT nightlife.” Another tags Lili as “music that hits the spirit.” Memes built around No Chicken Na Kpomo are spreading faster than press releases.

THE SOUND: “DOC STYLE” — A SONIC IDENTITY OF THE NORTH



In the heart of Abuja’s creative wave stands Dr. Kozzo, a genre-bending artist whose signature sound — “Doc Style” — fuses soulful rhythm, street energy, and deep lyrical storytelling. His music is a seamless blend of Hausa and Pidgin, wrapped in authenticity and emotion. “Doc Style” isn’t just a genre; it’s a philosophy.







 It reflects his roots, his reality, and his refusal to conform to musical stereotypes. Every track carries the pulse of Northern Nigeria while reaching for universal resonance — a blend that’s as grounded as it is global.



THE JOURNEY: FROM JOS TO THE WORLD



Born Nasiru Ali in Jos, Plateau State, Dr. Kozzo’s creative spark was lit early. From playing the tenor drum during morning assemblies in primary school to leading chapel choruses at St. John’s College, Jos, music has always been part of his DNA. His leadership as President of the Art Club and his later studies in Mass Communication at Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria, deepened his connection to storytelling and visual expression.




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Luka Gudah | GEN Z TAFAWA BALEWA (@jericanonthegram)




That passion evolved into a multifaceted creative career — music, photography, and filmmaking — all woven together by his sharp eye for detail and narrative. Kozzo co-founded Vogue Music Group with producer T-Shayne, later establishing his own imprint, OMG (One Man Gang) Recordings, under his broader creative collective, Normalife Camp.



THE PROJECTS: A GROWING DISCOGRAPHY WITH DEPTH



Dr. Kozzo’s catalog is rich with projects that highlight his range and message. Tracks like La’Ila, Ki Zabe Ni, and Reconcile display his poetic edge and rhythmic versatility. His collaborative EPs — The Lord’s Army with BOC Madaki, and Ready or North with Langtang Mafia — further cement his influence in Northern Nigeria’s evolving music scene.




https://spotify.link/VSjhq1bqJXb




His debut EP, “Doc Style,” serves as both an introduction and a declaration — a sonic prescription blending soul, grit, and wisdom. Each record feels deliberate, shaped by life experiences and a relentless drive to tell the Northern story through music that heals, provokes, and unites.



THE VISUAL ARTIST: KOZZOGRAPHY IN MOTION



Beyond sound, Dr. Kozzo thrives in the visual arts. As an award-winning travel photographer and filmmaker, known globally as Kozzographa, he documents Nigeria and the world through a bold, cinematic lens. His photography captures the raw pulse of humanity — landscapes, people, and stories that embody the modern Northern Nigerian identity.







 Through both visuals and sound, Kozzo’s artistry converges into one clear mission: to redefine creative expression from the North.



THE MESSAGE: ORIGINALITY AS CULTURE



Dr. Kozzo is more than an artist — he’s a movement. His work embodies resilience, faith, and creative excellence. Whether behind the mic or the camera, he represents a generation of Northern Nigerian creatives who are unafraid to be different. His journey reflects a belief that art, in all its forms, is a tool for transformation and truth.




Follow Dr.Kozzo




With “Doc Style,” Dr. Kozzo doesn’t just perform — he prescribes. His artistry bridges music, image, and emotion, marking him as one of the most compelling voices redefining the future of Nigerian creativity.

articles.body:
Wesse Gucci continues his impressive streak of impactful releases with Aje — a spirited Afro-fusion record featuring Kosere and ATEGUN IMG, set to drop on October 31, 2025.







Following the success of Need Somebody featuring Blac Lion and the reflective Playstation, Aje feels like the evolution of an artist who understands both sound and substance. It’s a rhythmic statement of gratitude, resilience, and belief — the soundtrack of anyone grinding toward purpose.



From the opening line, “Oluwa lon sho mi,” Wesse Gucci commands attention with conviction and calm power. His verses are grounded in lived experience, while Kosere and ATEGUN IMG inject the record with a raw street pulse, creating a synergy that bridges reflection and energy. The production captures the rhythm of Lagos hustle — fierce, alive, and hopeful — transforming Aje into more than a record; it’s a prayer in motion.




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Critic Circle | Entertainment & Pop Culture (@thecriticcircle)




As anticipation builds across streaming platforms and social channels, Aje stands as another defining entry in Wesse Gucci’s expanding catalog — proof that he’s not just making music for the moment but building a legacy rooted in authenticity, gratitude, and growth.



About Wesse Gucci



Wesse Gucci (pronounced Wei-sei Gucci) embodies calm confidence and cultural depth. Born and raised in Ajegunle — the melting pot of grit and dreams — his sound is shaped by both the chaos and charisma of Lagos streets.







His musical journey began with a simple spark: a cousin’s lyrics booklet filled with verses from Bob Marley, 2Pac, Jay-Z, Fela Kuti, and Biggie. What started as mimicry evolved into mastery as Wesse found his own rhythm, building a voice that now resonates across Nigeria’s new sound movement.



The name “Wesse” is drawn from the Edo phrase Uwese, meaning “thank you,” while “Gucci” adds a touch of flair — together forming the mantra “Thank you, I’m good.” This balance of gratitude and confidence defines both his music and his identity.



Influenced by legends like Daddy Showkey and Dagrin, Wesse blends Afrobeat’s bounce with Hip-Hop’s storytelling edge. His delivery is smooth but deliberate — every lyric a reflection of faith, focus, and experience.







Beyond the music, Wesse Gucci is a mindset. His brand pillars — Too Unruly and YN (Young & Noble) — reflect resilience, ambition, and youth-driven empowerment. His creative movement merges lifestyle, street fashion, and social impact, symbolizing a generation that dares to dream differently.



For Wesse, style is strategy. Music is purpose. Every move is intentional — like chess. And with Aje, he’s making his next move boldly, reminding the streets that success isn’t luck; it’s alignment.



Aje by Wesse Gucci featuring Kosere & ATEGUN IMG drops October 31, 2025, on all major streaming platforms.

Ahead of his upcoming two-single release, “Grey Area: Scene 1 & Scene 2,” and his next EP, RADARCharts caught up with Treeps for an exclusive TALK TO US session — a deep dive into his roots, his rise, and his next move.







WHERE HE COMES FROM



You started your solo journey officially in 2019 with Wicked Whyne. How did your early beginnings and upbringing shape the artist we know today as Treeps?




Growing up in ojuelegba, surulere, from an early age, I was surrounded by the sounds of the streets Fuji, Highlife, R&B, Afrobeats, the daily hustle, the traffic, the distant calls of hawkers, all of that was music to me. But beyond the sound, it was the spirit of survival and creativity in unlikely places that formed the foundation of Treeps. There’s a beauty in simplicity, in struggle, in making something out of almost nothing, and that’s where my artistry was born.




Afro-fusion is such a broad and evolving sound. Who were the biggest influences that helped shape your sonic direction in the early stages of your career?




There are quite a number of them talking about Duncan mighty, ABBA, ASA, Bright chimezie, and djniee. Just to mention a few








You’ve worked with names like Sesan, Barobeatz, and opened for Ayra Starr and Cheque at Beat Naija FM’s concert. What did those early experiences teach you about stage presence and musical identity?




Those early experiences taught me how to command attention, stay authentic on stage, and define my sound. Opening for big names pushed me to connect with the crowd and sharpen my musical identity under pressure. Now i can say i’m better at it




You’ve described music as “an escape route” in your Guardian interview. Can you expand on that — what does music help you express or release that words alone can’t?




Sure, when I called music an “escape route,” I meant that it let me express things I can’t always say with words. Sometimes emotions are too big, too messy, or too layered to explain, but music makes room for all of that.




Each of your songs — from Craze to Deception — feels emotionally charged and rhythmically layered. How do you approach storytelling through your songwriting?




To be honest, I won’t necessarily say there’s a template, i just follow what the SPIRITs whisper to me. 








Nigeria’s music scene is incredibly competitive. What challenges did you face breaking through as an independent Afro-fusion artist, and how did you overcome them?




As an independent artist, I don’t have the luxury of a big PR machine or massive funding. I am building my audience one person at a time, and we’ll get there with my current partnership with Music Dome Ent.  Expect so much more than before. 




Before we jump into what’s next, give a special shoutout or prayer to your supporters who’ve been on this journey with you from day one.




  I don’t take any stream, post, or share for granted. Genuinely, it means everything to me because it draws me closer to the goal, and i’m ever grateful about that. 




WHERE HE’S GOING TO



Your upcoming double single, Grey Area: Scene 1 & Scene 2, sounds like a conceptual project. Can you tell us what inspired it and what story it aims to tell?




Grey Area: Scene 1 & Scene 2 is definitely a conceptual project. It was inspired by that emotional in-between space the “grey area” where things aren’t black or white, right or wrong, love or hate. It’s about the moments when you’re stuck between decisions, emotions, or people, and nothing feels certain. I call it the introduction into the new SOUNDSCAPE. 










You’ve consistently evolved sonically from Wicked Whyne to No Yawa and OMF (The Convrstn). What’s your creative process like when experimenting with new sounds?




For me, I would say I engage my core sounds, which is afrobeats, highlife, i call the combination ( Hiplife) lol, R&B & soul, and moods that inspire me in the moment. I collaborate with producers, play around with melodies, and let the vibe guide the direction. It’s all about staying open, experimenting, and letting the music grow naturally.




You’ve performed alongside giants like Wande Coal and Tiwa Savage. How do collaborations and live experiences shape your vision for future projects?




Performing alongside legends like Wande Coal and Tiwa Savage has been a masterclass in artistry. Finally, drop a heartfelt message for your fans — what does this new era of Treeps stand for, and what can they look forward to as you continue your journey?

To my Day Ones, my New Ones, and everyone in between — thank you. Thank you for riding with me from when this was just a dream to now, when it’s becoming a movement.
This new era of Treeps isn’t just about making bigger music — it’s about putting more soul into every beat, every lyric, every performance. It’s about purpose now.
Please stay with me — na beg I dey beg — because soon, we’ll witness the epiphany together. I love y’all, I promise.

The Rise of a Northern Powerhouse



From the bustling streets of Kano to the cultural rhythm of Abuja, Teegha DapluG—born Temitope and popularly known as BiG 7—is steadily emerging as one of the most distinctive and fearless voices in Nigeria’s evolving hip-hop scene. As the founder and creative head of DapluG RepubliK, Teegha represents the new generation of Northern creatives fusing grit, melody, and purpose into something deeply original.







Since stepping into the music industry in 2018, Teegha has continuously refined his sound and identity, building momentum through persistence, experimentation, and a rare kind of self-awareness. What began as a personal escape for a naturally introverted artist has evolved into a movement connecting fans across regions and cultures.



The Sound: Afro-Drill Meets Conscious Rap



Teegha DapluG’s artistry thrives at the crossroads of Hip-Hop, Afro-Drill, Trap, and Alternative music—a genre fusion that reflects both his urban influences and his Northern heritage. His voice, deep and commanding, serves as an instrument on its own, instantly recognizable for its tone and presence.









Each verse is more than just a rhyme—it’s a reflection of lived experience. He raps about everyday life, community, ambition, and the unspoken stories of his environment. What makes Teegha stand out is his ability to blend street realism with emotional vulnerability, delivering hard-hitting bars laced with melody and humor. His freestyles, often spontaneous and insightful, have made him a fan favorite both online and in local music circles.



The DapluG RepubliK Movement



Beyond the music, Teegha has built a movement—DapluG RepubliK—which he describes as a “family of listeners who understand his truth.” It’s more than a fanbase; it’s a community bound by authenticity and shared struggle. For Teegha, music is a medium of communication, a way to speak to those who feel unseen or misunderstood.



Through his brand, he’s creating a creative ecosystem that celebrates individuality, regional diversity, and artistic freedom. This vision mirrors a growing wave of independent artists in Nigeria who are reclaiming control of their narratives and reshaping the country’s hip-hop map from the ground up.



The Breakthrough: ‘K K K’ and Beyond



Teegha’s breakout came in 2024 with his debut single “K K K”, a record that quickly gained traction across the North and spread organically through word-of-mouth and social media. The track showcased his signature flow—raw, witty, and rhythmically precise—and positioned him as an emerging force with both street credibility and mainstream potential.









The success of “K K K” marked more than a hit song; it was a signal that Teegha’s moment had arrived. Listeners were drawn to his authenticity and the way he turned regional slang and cultural expression into universal art.



Personality and Purpose



While he describes himself as naturally introverted, Teegha’s stage presence tells a different story—animated, hilarious, and magnetic. He channels his humor and sharp observations into performance, making every live show feel personal and unpredictable.







His creative philosophy centers on truth and evolution. He sees every song as a step toward growth—both as an artist and as a person. By using his platform to narrate his journey, he continues to inspire young dreamers from the North who see in him a mirror of their own aspirations.



The Vision Ahead



For Teegha DapluG, music is both mission and ministry. He envisions DapluG RepubliK as more than a label—it’s a legacy, a bridge connecting Nigerian hip-hop’s next frontier. As he continues to explore new sonic territories and collaborations, Teegha’s ambition remains the same: to elevate his art, represent his roots, and redefine the narrative of Northern artists on the national and global stage.



With his unique voice, versatile flow, and relentless drive, Teegha DapluG is not just rising—he’s leading a cultural shift that proves real artistry doesn’t chase the spotlight; it commands it as he sets to drop his next hit titled ‘Come 2 Me’








Presave Now




Teegha DapluG is not just making music—he’s building a republic of believers in his sound, his story, and his vision. The world is only beginning to tune in.

articles.body:
Dǎlu Osǎdebe stands at the intersection of tradition and innovation—a self-made artist redefining what modern Afrobeats can sound like. Since his emergence in 2019, he’s been building a sound that doesn’t just entertain but expands the boundaries of African music.







Blending traditional African percussion with trap-inspired textures and global rhythms, Dǎlu has crafted a sonic identity that’s as unpredictable as it is magnetic. His music speaks to both the dancefloor and the mind—equal parts groove and grit. Whether he’s layering log drums with synth basslines or merging soulful vocals with punchy 808s, Dǎlu’s artistry feels like a conversation between cultures, one that bridges the ancestral and the futuristic.



The Architect of His Own Sound



What separates Dǎlu from most of his peers is his independence—not just as an artist, but as a producer, mix engineer, and sonic architect. Every beat, vocal texture, and frequency in his catalog bears his personal fingerprint. A self-produced artist, he controls every stage of his creative process—from recording to mixing to mastering—ensuring his vision remains untouched.




https://open.spotify.com/artist/0ngHnug5tOwCrBcEBBJqHx?si=5GSdg_cIT3CPfXONR_nWvQ




This meticulous approach gives his music a rare coherence and identity. His tracks sound alive, layered with emotional depth and technical precision. It’s not just about control; it’s about authenticity. For Dǎlu, creating music is both a craft and a calling—an art form that demands patience, experimentation, and integrity.



The Sound: Where Afrobeats Meets Trap Energy



At the core of Dǎlu’s sound is Afro-fusion—but not the kind that fits comfortably in one category. His productions weave together Afrobeats rhythms, trap percussion, and melodic rap cadences, creating a hybrid energy that feels both local and global. Drawing inspiration from the emotion-driven approach of trap and the communal rhythm of Afrobeats, he’s building a bridge between worlds—between Lagos and Atlanta, between tradition and technology. The result is a refreshing, futuristic Afro-trap sound that’s as experimental as it is accessible.




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by DǍLU OSǍDEBE (@dalu_osadebe)




Scholar and Soundsmith



Beyond the music, Dǎlu embodies the discipline of a scholar and the creativity of a craftsman. Holding a Doctor of Pharmacy (Pharm.D) degree from Hungary, he balances intellect with instinct—a rare duality that mirrors his approach to music. His academic background has instilled in him a methodical mindset. In the studio, he operates like a scientist in a lab—testing, refining, and perfecting until the music feels both scientifically precise and emotionally resonant. It’s this balance of art and analysis that gives his sound its depth and distinction.







Vision and Evolution



Dǎlu Osǎdebe represents a new class of African artists: self-sufficient, global-minded, and sonically fearless. His mission isn’t to fit into the mainstream—it’s to reshape it. By merging genres and cultures, he’s helping define what the next era of African music could be: experimental, hybrid, and proudly original. With every release, Dǎlu pushes the limits of sound design and storytelling, positioning himself not just as a performer but as a visionary engineer of his own musical universe. His growing catalog is proof that the future of Afrobeats doesn’t belong to one sound—it belongs to innovators like him who dare to mix tradition with tomorrow.

Nigerian rap powerhouse SUBZIRO is setting the tone for a new generation of street ambition with his latest single, “BILLIONAIRE MINDED”, officially dropping Friday, October 24th, 2025 on all major streaming platforms.








Presave Now




A New Chapter for Nigerian Street Rap



Emerging from the vibrant streets of Enugu, SUBZIRO — real name Collins Chisom Ugwuonah — continues to shape his legacy as one of the most authentic and determined new voices in Nigeria’s ever-evolving hip-hop scene. Following the success of his debut single “Ni’Me Ogbe”, SUBZIRO returns with a project that’s more than just music — it’s a declaration of intent, a mindset, and a movement.



The Message Behind “BILLIONAIRE MINDED”




“BILLIONAIRE MINDED is not just about money,” SUBZIRO explains. “It’s about the mentality — the discipline, the hunger, the self-belief. It’s about knowing your worth and working like your dreams depend on it.”




The song serves as an anthem for dreamers, hustlers, and go-getters — those who turn challenges into motivation and see opportunity where others see struggle. SUBZIRO channels that raw determination through every bar, delivering a track that feels both personal and universal.




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by 𝐒𝐮𝐛𝐳𝐢𝐫𝐨 🥷🏿 (@iam_subziro)




A Bold Sound Rooted in Afro-Drill and Street Energy



Built on a fusion of Afro-drill and trap-infused street rhythms, “BILLIONAIRE MINDED” captures the pulse of modern hustle culture. Its production is gritty yet aspirational — a soundscape that mirrors SUBZIRO’s lyrical grit and unapologetic authenticity.



His confident flow and commanding delivery reflect the essence of Nigeria’s street rap renaissance: sharp, fearless, and purpose-driven.



Kucci World Records: The Vision and the Movement



Under Kucci World Records, SUBZIRO is positioning himself as more than an artist — he’s becoming a voice for Nigeria’s new generation of self-made leaders. “BILLIONAIRE MINDED” reinforces his mission to inspire youth who are building wealth not just in currency, but in character and conviction.



The single marks another major step in his growing influence under the Kucci World banner, a label that continues to spotlight emerging voices redefining Afro-street music.



About SUBZIRO



Born on May 27th, 1995, in Enugu State, Nigeria, SUBZIRO (Collins Chisom Ugwuonah) is a graduate of Enugu State University of Science and Technology (ESUT) with a degree in Material and Metallurgical Engineering.







Formerly known as King Sly during his university days, he rebranded as SUBZIRO in 2024 — marking a pivotal evolution in his artistry. His music blends Afrobeats, Drill, and Street Rap, reflecting his journey, struggles, and vision of greatness.

Genre: Afro-Drill / Afro-Fusion




A Collaboration Born from Vibe and Vision



There are songs that sound good — and then there are songs that feel like something new is happening. Let You Go by Mosa Temple featuring VJ Skinny lands squarely in that second category. 







It’s a hypnotic mix of Afro-Drill rhythm, Afrobeats warmth, and raw emotion, wrapped in a story that speaks to the heart while shaking up the floor.



Mosa Temple, known for his haunting vocals and grounded lyrics, locks in effortlessly with VJ Skinny — a street-certified lyricist with a flair for drill and trap-infused flows. Together, they create a sonic moment that bridges love and loyalty, intimacy and intensity.



The Sound: Love Meets Grit



From the opening line —




“If I ever let you go, oh my shawty, make water carry me dey go” —





you can feel the ache and honesty. Mosa Temple sings like a man lost in devotion, while VJ Skinny cuts through the melody with clever precision, making it both street and soulful.








The record pulses with layered drums, dark synths, and melodic ad-libs that nod to both London drill and Lagos nightlife. It’s that perfect middle ground where Afro emotion meets drill energy — a balance few artists pull off naturally.



Meet the Voices Behind the Wave



Mosa Temple has been building a quiet storm. From his Abuja radio tour with 88Godspeed Records and RADRCharts by REM to his genre-fluid sound that merges spirituality and swagger, he’s proving to be one of Nigeria’s most promising alternative voices. His songwriting is reflective, deeply personal, and tailor-made for replay.







VJ Skinny, on the other hand, brings the fire. His signature drill flow, sharp wordplay, and storytelling edge have made him a name in Nigeria’s new school movement. Whether performing on stage or behind the mic, Skinny embodies the confident chaos of this generation’s sound.




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by MOSA TEMPLE (@nonelikemosatemple)




Together, they’re not just collaborating — they’re building a new lane.



The Message Behind the Music



“Let You Go” dives into the tension between commitment and temptation — a story that feels both universal and personal. It’s for the lover who’s loyal yet restless, and for the streets that understand love isn’t always soft.







When Mosa Temple sings, “Spiritually, physically, mentally, mo wà pẹ̀lú rẹ,” it’s devotion. When VJ Skinny raps, “I swear I lie if I tell you say, I go waka alone,” it’s vulnerability dressed in confidence. The contrast makes the song human — honest, imperfect, real.



A New Chapter in Afro-Drill



Nigeria’s music landscape is evolving, and Afro-Drill is no longer underground — it’s a movement. Let You Go positions Mosa Temple and VJ Skinny as frontrunners in this next wave, showing how African artists can bend global genres without losing their cultural pulse.



Pre-Save and Join the Vibe



Fans can now pre-save “Let You Go” ahead of its official release on October 24 across all major streaming platforms. Pre-saving ensures you’re the first to catch the drop — and helps both artists gain algorithmic traction for playlist placements and early visibility.

“Let You Go” dives into the tension between commitment and temptation — a story that feels both universal and personal. It’s for the lover who’s loyal yet restless, and for the streets that understand love isn’t always soft.

When Mosa Temple sings, “Spiritually, physically, mentally, mo wà pẹ̀lú rẹ,” it’s devotion. When VJ Skinny raps, “I swear I lie if I tell you say, I go waka alone,” it’s vulnerability dressed in confidence. The contrast makes the song human — honest, imperfect, real.

Nigeria’s music landscape is evolving, and Afro-Drill is no longer underground — it’s a movement. Let You Go positions Mosa Temple and VJ Skinny as frontrunners in this next wave, showing how African artists can bend global genres without losing their cultural pulse.

THE SOUND: WHERE ROOTS MEET RESONANCE



Zipowei is one of those rare artists whose music feels like both a confession and a celebration. Her sound is a refined fusion of alternative R&B, soul, and Afrobeat, shaped by her Nigerian roots and a global ear for rhythm and emotion. 







Every song she crafts carries a pulse of vulnerability — music that doesn’t just entertain, but speaks directly to the listener’s inner world. Zipowei’s ability to blend warm, soulful melodies with cultural nuance positions her as one of the most promising voices in the evolving soul scene.



THE EP: “ECHOES OF ZI” — AN ANTICIPATED REBIRTH



Zipowei is set to make a grand return with her upcoming EP, “Echoes of Zi.” The project promises to be a soulful exploration of identity, healing, and transformation — a mirror reflecting the artist’s own evolution. Built on themes of love, loss, and renewal, Echoes of Zi is expected to showcase Zipowei’s most intimate storytelling yet. 




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by zi (@zipowei)





Pre-Save ‘ECHOES OF ZI’




THE MOVEMENT: GEN ZI AND THE POWER OF COMMUNITY



At the core of Zipowei’s artistry lies “Gen Zi” — a movement and safe space for those who value truth, growth, and authenticity. It’s more than a fanbase; it’s a collective of listeners who find comfort in Zipowei’s message of self-acceptance and emotional transparency. Through Gen Zi, she’s building a culture around empowerment — encouraging people to embrace their real stories, their imperfections, and their evolution.







THE MESSAGE: MUSIC AS HEALING ENERGY



Zipowei’s music reminds us that vulnerability is not weakness — it’s the essence of connection. Her lyrical honesty, combined with soulful instrumentation, makes her work both deeply personal and universally relatable. She stands for an era of artists redefining what it means to make music: not just to perform, but to heal. Each song is a gentle reminder that we are all works in progress, echoing through time in search of truth.

Abuja, Nigeria — Fast-rising Afro-fusion artist Mosa Temple has made a bold statement ahead of his upcoming single, embarking on an extensive Abuja radio tour that touched down at four of the city’s biggest stations — Love FM, Beats FM, Kiss FM, and Voice of the People 96.1 FM.







The tour featured dynamic appearances with some of the capital’s most recognizable on-air personalities: Mr. Sugar Sugar of Love FM, Victor Velmo of Beats FM, Victor Jerry of Kiss FM, and Darababy of Voice of the People FM. Powered by 88Godspeed Records and RADRCharts by REM, the media run was managed and executed by The iNDUSTRY MESSiAH, serving as an early prelude to what’s shaping up to be one of Abuja’s most anticipated collaborations of the year.



BUILDING MOMENTUM THROUGH MEDIA CONNECTION



Mosa’s radio presence was more than a promotional routine — it was a strategic rollout, designed to deepen his connection with Abuja’s music audience while reinforcing his growing influence in the Afro-fusion scene. Known for his soulful melodies and layered songwriting, Mosa used these interviews to discuss his artistic evolution, tease upcoming projects, and share his vision for Nigerian contemporary music.




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Sugar Sugar (@mrsugarsugar)




Each stop provided an intimate look into the artist’s personality — from heartfelt reflections with Mr. Sugar Sugar on Love FM, to vibrant banter with Victor Velmo on Beats FM. On Kiss FM, Mosa’s conversation with Victor Jerry touched on the realities of staying authentic in a rapidly evolving industry, while Darababy’s Voice of the People segment highlighted his journey from emerging talent to a fast-rising voice on the Abuja creative radar.



A NEW ERA ON THE HORIZON



The buzz surrounding the tour centers on Mosa’s upcoming single, set to drop next week. The track features a well-known Abuja-based artist — a “son of the soil”, whose identity remains undisclosed pending official confirmation from management. Early insiders describe the collaboration as a “cultural moment,” expected to bridge homegrown energy with Mosa’s smooth Afro-fusion aesthetic.




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by MOSA TEMPLE (@nonelikemosatemple)




Mosa’s team, led by The iNDUSTRY MESSiAH and 88 Anonymous, has described the rollout as “an intentional positioning move” — one that reintroduces Mosa not just as a promising act, but as a serious creative force with a deep understanding of audience building and storytelling through sound.



THE EMERGING FACE OF AFRO-FUSION



Since the release of his “Second Chance” EP, Mosa has steadily carved a lane defined by emotive storytelling, genre-blending production, and a confident embrace of his Nigerian identity. Critics and fans alike have praised his ability to fuse rhythm, introspection, and originality — a blend that makes his forthcoming release one to watch.







With a grounded media presence and an ambitious rollout strategy, Mosa Temple is setting the tone for a powerful new chapter in his career. As anticipation builds across Abuja and beyond, one thing is clear: this tour wasn’t just about airplay — it was about staking his claim as one of the next major voices in Afro-fusion.



Follow Mosa Temple for real-time updates and release news via his official channels.

LilTee is making waves. A story of grit, fusion, and raw storytelling, his musical voice merges passion with purpose — from Auchi roots (Edo State) through the bustle of Abuja’s music scene. 







For fans seeking authenticity in Afro-fusion and Hip-hop, LilTee offers more than tracks: he offers truth.



Origins & Early Musical Steps



LilTee hails from Auchi, Edo State, and today is based in Nigeria’s capital, Abuja. His youth was steeped in the rhythms of street life, struggle, and dreaming big — experiences that became fuel for his lyricism.









Sound, Style & Themes



LilTee’s style is a mix-and-match of genres with a purpose. He draws on:



Afrobeats & Afro-fusion for feel-good hooks, dance-able grooves, melodic choruses Hip-hop / Rap for street narratives, sharp verses, and lyrical honesty R&B inflections when exploring vulnerability — love, doubt, dreams




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Omoigberai Testimony (@_meetliltee_mdl)




The recurring themes in his music: love in its many forms, the hustle to transcend one’s beginnings, self-belief despite setbacks, and the everyday stories of those who dream. He doesn’t hide scars — he wears them in his voice.



Strengths & What Makes Him Stand Out



Authentic storytelling: LilTee doesn’t lean heavy on glitz or hyperbole; he paints his truth — which helps him connect.



Genre fluidity: Rather than sticking strictly to one lane, he roams across Afro-rhythms, street-rap, melody. That gives him flexibility in both creative expression and audience reach.



Emotionality: His tracks resonate not just because of catchy beats but because there’s feeling behind them. When an artist can make you nod and reflect, that’s powerful.







Forward Motion



If LilTee continues on this path, some likely next steps: A follow-up EP or album that leans into more polished production while preserving raw honesty. Live performances in Abuja and perhaps regional venues — building a strong live reputation helps solidify fanbase. Possibly pushing for visibility outside Nigeria — West African circuits, streaming playlists, or global Afro-fusion spaces as he’s currently rocking the waves with his new release ‘Personalize’



Why LilTee Matters 



Artists like LilTee are essential because they bridge gaps: between the street and the studio, between dreams and reality. They show that music is more than production values or hype — it’s voice, struggle, hope. In a landscape of fast fame and polish, LilTee represents perseverance, authenticity, and incremental growth. Those kinds of stories often outlast trends.




Stream ‘Personalize’

There’s a quiet confidence that radiates from JohnBlackMusic, a Lagos-based artist whose sound balances between trap’s raw emotion and R&B’s tender groove. Born Gyang John Danjuma in Jos, Plateau State, he carries the soul of the Berom hills into the pulse of the city—bridging old roots and new rhythms with ease.







From humble beginnings freestyling in church as a teenager to building a professional sound shaped by years in the studio, JohnBlack has crafted something rare: music that doesn’t just entertain, but speaks directly to the heart.



From Jos to Lagos: The Journey of a True Believer



JohnBlack’s musical story began in 2007, long before he had a microphone of his own. Alongside his friend Nenzee, he formed a group called NJ Young Stars, inspired by local producer Mandela, who gave them beats to freestyle on. Those early days in Jos were raw—handmade beats, choir rehearsals, and endless experimentation—but they laid the foundation for a lifelong commitment to sound.



He recalls, “I discovered I had a special voice back in SS1. From then, I started hearing melodies in my head every day.”



That innate connection to melody has never left him. Even now, in Lagos’ creative sprawl, JohnBlack’s process remains simple: freestyle until something real surfaces, then build the song from there.



A Sound Built on Soul, Trap, and Truth



At his core, JohnBlackMusic is a storyteller. His sound floats between trap, R&B, and Afro-fusion—genres he bends effortlessly into one emotional experience. The influence of Akon’s smooth melodies, the bounce of Afrobeats, and the energy of modern trap all find a place in his catalog.









His lyrics often explore love, lifestyle, and the struggles that shape everyday life. But beyond themes, it’s the feeling that defines his music. Whether it’s the vulnerability in “Make Me Better” or the smooth confidence of “Roll With Me,” JohnBlack’s voice becomes a vessel—equal parts spiritual and streetwise.



His listeners cut across borders, religions, and age groups. “I make music for everyone,” he says. “For lovers, kids, Muslims, Christians. Anybody with a heart that feels something.”



The Independent Hustle



Behind the stage name is a determined entrepreneur. When he’s not in the studio, JohnBlack runs his own business—selling cars, e-bikes, and phone gadgets—funding his music and staying self-reliant. His independence isn’t just a status; it’s a philosophy.



He’s the type of artist who builds from the ground up—recording with close collaborators Slash Beat and Bobbery, pushing every release by himself, and treating every show like a chance to convert new believers.



“Doing different jobs to support my music hasn’t been easy,” he admits, “but it keeps me grounded. It makes the dream




        View this post on Instagram            




Vision Beyond the Music



JohnBlack’s ambition is crystal clear. Within a year, he aims to lock in a global audience. Within five, he wants to be recognized as one of Africa’s most distinctive voices—a multi-genre powerhouse who can move from amapiano to R&B to dancehall without missing a beat.



His dream collaborations tell you everything you need to know about his range: Nasty C and Chris Brown. Two artists who, like him, live at the intersection of melody and movement.







Long-term, he hopes to build a legacy as “the artist who could sing, rap, fuse Afro sounds, and still make it feel spiritual.”



A New Chapter Begins



With two official singles—“Make Me Better” and “Roll With Me”—already streaming across platforms, and an upcoming EP in the works, 2025 marks the start of a new chapter for JohnBlackMusic.



His story is no longer just about where he came from; it’s about the message he carries: that simplicity, humility, and authenticity still matter in music.



In a world obsessed with noise, JohnBlackMusic offers calm. In a scene racing for clout, he’s focused on connection. His voice—smooth, deliberate, and deeply human—reminds us that true art is timeless.




Follow JohnBlackMusic

JohnBlack isn’t here to blend in — he’s here to become the voice of a new sound rising from Nigeria’s underground to its global stage.

From the heart of Jos to the pulse of Abuja, JohnBlackMusic is rewriting the soundbook of modern Afro-Fusion. His music is raw, emotional, and purpose-driven — a fusion of Trap, R&B, and African rhythm that speaks to the soul while keeping heads nodding.
With songs like Make Me Better and With Me, JohnBlack opens a window into his world — one built on grind, faith, and authenticity. Every lyric feels lived, every melody intentional. He’s not just making hits; he’s building a message for dreamers, believers, and the ones still fighting their way up.
JohnBlack isn’t here to blend in — he’s here to become the voice of a new sound rising from Nigeria’s underground to its global stage.
articles.title: ARTIST SPOTLIGHT: JohnBlackMusic — The Voice that Moves Between Worlds

At just 19, Astrumm stands as one of the most electrifying new forces in Nigerian hip-hop—a rare blend of intellect, raw energy, and divine confidence. Born in Anambra and raised in Lagos, her journey began not on a stage, but on paper. By the age of seven, she was already writing poetry, shaping words into rhythm long before she realized those verses would become her weapon in music.







By eleven, she had found her voice as a singer, but at fourteen, hip-hop claimed her heart for good—thanks to her older brother, whose love for the genre lit her own creative fire. Since then, Astrumm has forged a path that’s uniquely hers: a sound defined by depth, rhythm, and authority. Every bar feels intentional, every verse grounded in the authenticity of a young woman who knows she’s meant to lead.



Currently in her final year studying Biochemistry, Astrumm is living proof that art and ambition can coexist. Her discipline in academics mirrors her precision as an artist—a balance that speaks to her drive and purpose. Her name, Astrumm—Latin for “a heavy body”—isn’t just poetic; it’s prophetic. She carries herself with gravity, her presence impossible to ignore.




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Tthe Prophecy (@the_astrumm)




Her rise hasn’t gone unnoticed. With co-signs from Spyro, Qing Madi, Dandizzy, and Ayra Starr, Astrumm is already being recognized by some of the most respected names in the game. Her Showoff AKTIVATED session revealed a lyricist with both edge and elegance, while her performance at Lagos Gidi Cypher 2025 stamped her authority as a leader of the next generation.



Astrumm calls herself The Prophecy, and it’s not just a name—it’s a statement of intent. She’s not waiting for a seat at the table; she’s building her own throne. In a genre often dominated by bravado and competition, Astrumm brings something different: truth, power, and artistry wrapped in purpose.




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Tthe Prophecy (@the_astrumm)




Her reign has only just begun, but the signs are clear—Astrumm isn’t here to participate. She’s here to rule.



Career Highlights



• Featured on Showoff AKTIVATED Session



• Co-signed by Spyro, Qing Madi, Dandizzy, and Ayra Starr



• Performed at Lagos Gidi Cypher 2025



• Began writing poetry at age 7, embraced rap at 14



• Final-year Biochemistry student balancing academics and artistry



• Known for her distinct, powerful, and authentic sound







Astrumm represents the evolution of Nigerian hip-hop—lyrically sharp, creatively fearless, and spiritually grounded. The prophecy is unfolding, and she’s writing it in real time.

Abuja’s fast-rising Afrobeats artist Boylikevilla has officially released his latest single, “Alaye”, now available on all major streaming platforms. 







The track, which dropped October 10th, captures a deeply personal story of betrayal, divine elevation, and resilience, offering listeners both a groove and a message.



A TRUE STORY TURNED INTO SOUND



Born Elias David Birdling, the Abuja-based artist from Adamawa State transforms a real-life moment of betrayal into a motivational anthem. In “Alaye”, Boylikevilla recounts how someone close to him tried to take credit for his work. Instead of letting pain define him, he channeled it into a powerful reminder of self-belief and gratitude to God.









Over crisp Afrobeats production and a rhythm that stays stuck in your head, Boylikevilla’s street-honed delivery gives the song a raw, emotional edge.




“Alaye you wan steal my maye,



my nigga pass me the jay,



I wan still puff rosé.”




That lyric says it all—hurt turned into strength, pressure turned into purpose.



THE SOUND OF THE STREETS, THE SPIRIT OF GROWTH



“Alaye” blends authentic Afrobeats percussion with Villa’s unfiltered street energy. It’s both danceable and reflective, connecting deeply with fans who know what it means to face envy, stay grateful, and keep pushing forward.









Speaking about the release, Boylikevilla shared:




“‘Alaye’ came from a real place. It’s about turning that betrayal into motivation and just thanking God for how far I’ve come.”




The single reinforces his growing reputation as one of Abuja’s most relatable new voices, bridging street culture and soulful introspection.



BUZZ ACROSS SOCIAL MEDIA



Ahead of the release, Boylikevilla built strong anticipation online, teasing snippets and behind-the-scenes clips on TikTok and Instagram, where he commands a loyal and growing fanbase.



45,000+ TikTok followers 1 million+ total likes Videos consistently reaching 200,000+ views



His previous viral moment—the “Abracadabra Challenge” for his single “Magician” (feat. TeeBlqc+)—proved his instinct for connecting with fans. That challenge, where fans danced in towels for a ₦100,000 prize, became one of Abuja’s most talked-about online moments.



A CONSISTENT RISE IN THE ABUJA MUSIC SCENE



On streaming platforms, Boylikevilla’s numbers continue to grow steadily, averaging 20,000 streams per track and more than 1,000 monthly listeners. His commitment to authenticity and relatable storytelling sets him apart from the crowd.







He’s built a foundation from the ground up—bridging the trenches and the urban districts, often seen collaborating with other rising Abuja acts such as EESKAY.



“ALAYE” — MORE THAN A NAME



“Alaye” is both personal and universal—a song for anyone who’s been wronged but chose growth over grudges.




Stream Now

Born and raised in Aba, Abia State, Dotar is a fast-rising Afro-fusion artist whose sound carries the depth of her roots and the confidence of her evolution. Growing up surrounded by rhythm, storytelling, and community, she developed a natural sensitivity to sound and emotion—an instinct that would later define her artistry.







Her musical journey began in the Catholic Church, where she sang as an opera vocalist in the choir. It was there she learned the power of harmony, vulnerability, and spiritual resonance in music—qualities that remain present in her songs today.



A Leap of Faith and Purpose



After completing her HND in Nursing, Dotar made a bold move to Abuja in 2023 to pursue music full-time. This decision marked the true beginning of her creative journey—a leap of faith that fused her love for humanity with her passion for storytelling through sound.



Her artistry is shaped by this duality: emotional honesty and purposeful creation. Every track reflects her belief that music should heal, uplift, and connect people to something deeper than the surface.









Breakthrough and Recognition



In 2024, Dotar introduced herself to the world with her debut single “Mon Bébé”, a smooth Afro-dancehall anthem that showcased her tender yet confident voice. The song positioned her as a rising storyteller with a gift for balancing melody and message.



Her momentum grew with the release of “Reasons” featuring Kingeorge, an Afro-fusion masterpiece that explores heartbreak and healing. The single achieved impressive success—landing on over 200 Spotify playlists and gaining 10,000+ streams within two weeks of release. More importantly, it resonated with listeners who found their own stories reflected in her words.









A Distinct Voice in Afro-Fusion



Dotar’s sound is a rich blend of Afro-dancehall rhythms, emotive soul, and introspective storytelling. Her voice moves effortlessly between softness and power, carrying a sense of truth that draws the listener in.



She stands out for her ability to turn personal experiences into universal expressions, crafting songs that feel intimate yet globally relatable. Each release expands her sonic identity while reinforcing her message of resilience and authenticity.



Building “The Realms” and Beyond



As an independent artist, Dotar is steadily building her community of supporters known as The Realms—a space for fans who connect with her message of truth, soul, and growth. She sees her music as a bridge between worlds, merging tradition with modernity, vulnerability with strength, and melody with meaning.







Through every performance, post, and lyric, Dotar continues to establish herself as a voice of honesty and hope in Nigeria’s new wave of Afro-fusion talent.



A Rising Storyteller to Watch



Dotar represents the next chapter of African music—introspective, genre-fluid, and deeply human. From her early beginnings in Aba to her blossoming career in Abuja, she embodies the courage of an artist willing to take risks in pursuit of purpose.



With her heart in her voice and her faith in her journey, Dotar is not just creating songs; she’s crafting experiences that remind listeners that vulnerability is strength—and that music, at its core, is truth set to rhythm.

articles.body:
A Rising Star from the Heart of Abuja



From the vibrant rhythm of Nigeria’s capital, Abdulmalik “SoKoGa” Haruna has emerged as one of the most exciting new voices in the Afrofusion space. Based in Abuja, SoKoGa has been redefining modern African sound since officially stepping into the professional music scene in 2019. 







His music—an intoxicating blend of Afrobeats, dancehall, alté, and worldwide influences—is both bold and melodic, a reflection of his deep emotional expression and creative versatility.



The Journey from Covers to Viral Hits



SoKoGa began his journey by performing covers and sharing snippets of his original songs across social media. His talent and charisma quickly drew attention, building a growing fanbase both in Nigeria and abroad. Over the years, his evolution as an artist has been marked by viral moments and consistent output. Tracks like “Dangote,” “Oh Marayana,” and “Parte After Dawn” captured audiences with their infectious rhythms and lyrical honesty. These songs not only showcased his songwriting skill but also cemented his ability to create music that connects across cultures and moods.



The “Blue Roses” Era — A Defining Debut









In 2021, SoKoGa released his debut EP, “Blue Roses”, a body of work that introduced the world to his genre-bending style and emotional depth. The project stood out for its vulnerability and range, effortlessly weaving between soulful melodies, vibrant Afro rhythms, and introspective lyricism. “Blue Roses” was more than just a debut—it was a statement of intent. It announced SoKoGa as an artist who could bridge mainstream energy with alternative artistry, a combination that would soon define his signature sound.



Collaborations and Community









One of SoKoGa’s greatest strengths lies in his collaborative spirit. His musical chemistry with Realmaj, seen on records like “Let Go” and the “Gangster Living” pack, showcases a synergy that elevates both artists. Beyond that, SoKoGa’s catalog includes standout collaborations such as “Corner Corner” (with Eugene Dolph and Mannie Tseayo) and “Sneaky Link” (featuring Geezyshore and Mannie Tseayo). Each track reinforces his ability to adapt across styles while maintaining his unmistakable vocal identity. In Abuja’s growing music scene, SoKoGa has also made waves through his partnership with AfroSelecta-BBK, delivering standout hits like “Roadman,” “Wonder,” “Hallelujah,” and “Giant Killer.” These collaborations highlight his commitment to community-driven creativity and his role in shaping the city’s new sound.



A Sonic Explorer with Global Vision



SoKoGa’s music lives at the crossroads of rhythm and experimentation. He continues to explore genre-bending sounds, drawing inspiration from dancehall, trap soul, Afrobeats, and other global genres. Each new release expands his musical palette, proving that his artistry is not confined by borders or labels. His smooth vocal delivery, coupled with infectious hooks and innovative production, makes every song a distinct experience—crafted to resonate, move, and inspire.







A Name Poised for the World Stage



With every project, SoKoGa continues to solidify his reputation as one of Abuja’s most dynamic Afrofusion acts. His journey from social media performances to viral tracks and acclaimed collaborations reflects the evolution of an artist with vision, discipline, and global ambition. SoKoGa represents the modern African artist: genre-fluid, emotionally open, and unafraid to experiment. As he continues to evolve, his sound promises to travel far beyond Abuja, carrying with it the heartbeat of a new generation of Afrofusion.

An Innovative Voice Rising from Ibadan



The city of Ibadan is becoming a creative hotspot for Nigeria’s evolving music scene, and at the center of this wave is Syntax, The Creator—a visionary Afrofusion artist redefining the sonic possibilities of African music. 







His sound is both familiar and refreshingly unexpected, drawing from deep cultural roots while fearlessly exploring new frontiers.



Bending Genres, Building Experiences



Syntax thrives on genre-bending experimentation, blending the pulsating rhythms of Afrobeats with lush orchestral textures and global soundscapes. The result is music that feels cinematic, layered, and emotionally immersive.



Each track is crafted as a sonic journey rather than just a song. Syntax builds sound worlds where drums converse with strings, traditional grooves meet modern synths, and the listener is transported beyond genre labels into an entirely new experience.



Innovation Anchored in African Soul



While Syntax explores global sounds, his music remains deeply anchored in African rhythm and soul. He understands the essence of traditional grooves—the heartbeat that powers Afrobeats—and uses it as a foundation for creative expansion.









This balance between authentic cultural grounding and fearless innovation gives his music a rare duality: it speaks intimately to local audiences while resonating powerfully with international ears.



A Distinct Signature in Afrofusion



Syntax’s artistry stands out for its meticulous sound design and inventive production. His beats are constructed with precision, weaving layers of instruments and textures to create rich, atmospheric compositions. This distinctive fingerprint sets him apart in a genre that’s rapidly evolving, positioning him as one of Ibadan’s most promising musical innovators.



Redefining Afrofusion for a Global Stage



For Syntax, music is more than entertainment—it’s a medium of cultural expression and global connection. By merging orchestral grandeur with African rhythms, he challenges conventional boundaries and reimagines Afrofusion for the modern era.









His work reflects the mindset of a new generation of African creators—artists who are not just participating in global conversations but shaping them.

The creative heartbeat of Abuja is fast becoming a breeding ground for new talent, and at the center of this wave is Ihcego — a multi-genre artist whose work transcends musical boundaries.







Over the past nine years, Ihcego has quietly and consistently carved out a space for herself, blending raw emotion, authentic narratives, and bold experimentation into a sound that resonates deeply with listeners both locally and internationally.



Multi-Genre Expression Rooted in Emotion



Ihcego’s artistry thrives on versatility. She navigates different musical genres effortlessly, allowing her voice and message to dictate the production rather than the other way around. Her songs explore universal themes such as love, hustle, personal growth, and social behavior—delivered through emotionally vulnerable storytelling that connects with audiences on a human level.









Whether it’s a slow-burning ballad that tugs at the heartstrings or an upbeat anthem that commands a crowd, Ihcego approaches each track with a clear intention: to communicate truth and evoke feeling.



The “Bare” Era: A Career Turning Point



Her journey gained momentum with the release of her debut EP “Bare”, a body of work that introduced listeners to her unique voice and lyrical depth. The project set the stage for a career built on authenticity.



Since then, Ihcego has expanded her reach through consistent social media presence, live performances, and a growing footprint on streaming platforms, steadily drawing in a loyal fan base. Her sound reflects influences from celebrated artists like Asa and Teni, yet she maintains a distinct aura that positions her as a standout in Nigeria’s evolving music scene.









Purpose Beyond the Music



Ihcego’s influence extends beyond her melodies. She’s an outspoken advocate for positive societal change, with a focus on spotlighting women in music, raising mental health awareness, and community building. For Ihcego, music functions as more than entertainment—it’s a tool for healing, dialogue, and development. This commitment to social impact is woven into her creative identity, giving her music an added layer of depth and purpose.



New Releases and Expanding Horizons



Ihcego continues to build momentum with powerful singles like “Human Being,” “Pleasing People,” and her latest track “Bad Character.” Each release demonstrates her growth as an artist, combining compelling songwriting with fresh sonic choices.









These records mark a strategic push toward reaching a wider global audience, while staying true to the roots, experiences, and values that shaped her.



A Future Defined by Authenticity



As Ihcego steps further into the spotlight, she embodies a new generation of Nigerian artists—those who merge musical innovation with cultural consciousness. Her journey is a testament to perseverance, vision, and unwavering authenticity.







From Abuja to the world, Ihcego is more than an artist; she’s a voice for change, a storyteller for her generation, and a rising force poised to leave a lasting imprint on the music landscape.

articles.body:
In the ever-evolving tapestry of Nigerian hip-hop, new voices emerge to challenge boundaries, rekindle regional identities, and push the genre’s idioms forward. Rhymino—hailing from the Eastern corridors of Nigeria—is one of those voices. His six-track EP, Awaga Movement, stakes a bold claim: this is not just a mixtape, it’s a mission statement.







The Context: Igbo Rap in Resurgence



Igbo rap is no niche side act. It has grown from its late-1990s roots into a vibrant force—blending indigenous language, Afrobeats textures, highlife sensibilities, and rap swagger.  In the last few years, the genre has seen a surge of energy as newer acts interweave local slang, vernacular flows, and street narratives into mainstream consciousness. In that milieu, Awaga Movement is Rhymino’s entrance into a broader conversation: about ambition, regional pride, and the evolving identity of Nigerian rap.



Rhymino doesn’t emerge in a vacuum. Comparisons are being whispered online: “Rhymino is one of the few young Igbo rappers who can attempt to replicate Phyno’s success.”  That’s high expectation, but Awaga Movement demonstrates he’s staking his claim—with style.



Featured Voices & Strategic Pairings



Rhymino does not walk alone on this EP. He brings in collaborators whose flavors help diversify and deepen the project:









Zyno TopBoy joins him on Lungu, a drill-inflected anthem that injects aggressive energy and street grit into the body of the EP. Evado and Beepee the Rapper join forces on Ego, pushing introspection and emotional tension. Quincy Raph appears on Update, lending additional texture and contrast.



These features are savvy: they maintain cohesion (all within the new wave of Igbo / Nigerian rap) while opening spaces for contrast.









The Sound & Themes: Ambition, Hustle, Identity



At the heart of Awaga Movement lie themes that are familiar to rap’s pantheon—but especially resonant in the Eastern/Nigerian context: ambition, striving against constraints, the hunger for wealth, and the quest for legacy. Rhymino weaves these with vernacular lyricism, metaphor, and cadence that root firmly in Igbo rap’s lineage.



Some standout tracks:



Prison — A visceral opener. Whether literal or metaphorical, the theme of confinement highlights the internal struggles of ambition. Mmeri — (Igbo for “victory”) This track leans into resilience, turning the EP’s tension into a release. Money Won Talk — A swaggering number: talk is cheap, but money speaks louder. With assertive bars and confident delivery, this becomes a statement track.




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Rhymino Awaga-Boy (@rhymino_awagaboy)




Each song lands with force. As soon as the listener presses play, Rhymino demands attention.



Strengths, Risks & What the EP Signals



Strengths:



Cohesive vision. Despite diverse features, the EP holds together as a unit—there’s tonal consistency and narrative flow. Lyrical dexterity. Rhymino shows command of metaphor, cadence, vernacular punchlines, and emotional texture. Strategic collaborations. The features are well-chosen, strengthening rather than overshadowing the host. Cultural anchoring. He is not merely appropriating styles—he’s embedding himself in the Igbo rap project, asserting linguistic and geographic identity.




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Rhymino Awaga-Boy (@rhymino_awagaboy)




Risks / challenges:



Comparisons loom large. For new artists in Igbo rap, comparisons to luminaries like Phyno are inevitable. Rhymino must carve his distinct lane. Market balance. The tension between street authenticity and broader commercial appeal is delicate—lean too niche and limit reach; lean too mainstream and dilute identity.







What Awaga Movement signals is a coming-of-age for Rhymino. It communicates: “I am ready for the next tier.” It says to audiences and industry alike: “I can anchor a body of work, deliver consistency, and carry features without being carried.”




Stream ‘Awaga’

UkBoy Raaeli’s journey begins in the bustling capital city of Abuja, Nigeria—a place where every corner hums with rhythm, movement, and vibrant energy. Growing up surrounded by the soundscape of street vendors, public transport, and nightlife, music became more than just entertainment for him; it became a language, a way to express his reality.







Unlike many who discover their sound later in life, UkBoy Raaeli’s musical instincts were sharpened early. His environment acted as both classroom and inspiration, infusing his artistry with authenticity and a deep cultural pulse. This foundation gave rise to a distinctive style that merges the grit of Hip-Hop with the infectious grooves of Afrobeats, resulting in a voice that is as rooted as it is forward-looking.



The Birth of “NIGHT LIFE”



UkBoy Raaeli’s new EP, NIGHT LIFE, represents the next phase of his evolution as an artist. The three-track project is more than a collection of songs—it’s a carefully curated sonic experience designed to reflect the relentless rhythm of urban hustle and the search for balance within it.









Featuring guest appearances from Zilla Oaks and Major X, the EP strategically blends Hip-Hop/Drill, AfroPop, and Afro/Amapiano, offering listeners a journey through different moods and soundscapes while maintaining a cohesive narrative.



The title NIGHT LIFE captures the essence of ambition. It symbolizes those late hours when dreams are built, when streets come alive with both temptation and opportunity, and when personal battles are fought away from the public eye.



A Fusion of Genres and Perspectives



UkBoy Raaeli refuses to be boxed into a single genre. On NIGHT LIFE, he effortlessly moves between sounds that reflect the multifaceted nature of modern African youth culture:







Hip-Hop/Drill: The opening track channels gritty flows and raw lyricism, showcasing his ability to dominate hard-hitting beats with precision and intent. AfroPop: The second track lightens the mood with melodic hooks and relatable storytelling, capturing the joy and vulnerability of everyday life. 



Afro/Amapiano: The closing record dives into the pulsating rhythms of Amapiano—a South African-born sound that has swept across the continent—infused with UkBoy’s Nigerian swagger, creating a vibe tailor-made for the dancefloor.



This intentional blend underscores his versatility and positions him as a genre-bending innovator capable of appealing to diverse audiences.



Themes of Hustle, Peace, and Purpose



At its core, NIGHT LIFE explores the duality of modern hustle—the grind and the glory, the chaos and the calm. UkBoy Raaeli uses his lyrics to highlight the struggles that every dreamer faces: the late nights, the sacrifices, and the moments of doubt.




https://videopress.com/v/uV9npV89?resizeToParent=true&cover=true&preloadContent=metadata&useAverageColor=true




Beyond glorifying the hustle, he emphasizes the need for balance and inner peace, urging listeners to find stillness amid ambition. This mature thematic direction sets him apart from many emerging acts, showing a depth that reflects both personal experience and cultural awareness.



Collaborations that Elevate the Sound



Zilla Oaks and Major X are not just featured artists—they are collaborators who add layers of perspective and energy to the EP. Zilla Oaks brings his trademark lyrical sharpness, while Major X adds melodic flair, creating a dynamic interplay that elevates the project beyond a solo effort.




https://videopress.com/v/kFL8wFsO?resizeToParent=true&cover=true&preloadContent=metadata&useAverageColor=true




These collaborations also highlight UkBoy Raaeli’s strategic approach to growth—aligning with respected voices in the scene while maintaining his unique identity.



A Rising Force in the Nigerian Music Scene



With NIGHT LIFE, UkBoy Raaeli isn’t just releasing music; he’s staking a claim in Nigeria’s rapidly evolving music landscape. His ability to merge genres, tell authentic stories, and deliver with confidence places him among the new generation of artists pushing the sound forward.



As Afrobeats continues to dominate the global stage and Drill carves out its place in African cities, artists like UkBoy Raaeli are at the forefront of creating a hybrid sound that is unmistakably local yet globally resonant.




Stream ‘NIGHTLIFE’

Juice Coal is steadily rising as one of Nigeria’s most promising voices, blending Afrobeats energy with alternative hip hop storytelling. 







With his latest single “Oh No” (released September 17, 2025), the Enugu-born, Lagos-based artist delivers a victory anthem that captures both his journey and his resilience.



Early Foundations



Juice Coal began carving out his identity in 2022 with the release of “Antidote,” a confessional, funk-inspired hip hop record produced by Eraps. Written by Sidney Nzekwe, the track revealed his unfiltered honesty: “I thought I needed love but it turns out it was the studio calling.” From the very start, Juice Coal established himself as more than just another Afrobeats newcomer—he was an artist determined to tell his story, even without the polish of a full studio setup.







From Enugu to Lagos



Hailing from Enugu, Juice Coal’s decision to move to Lagos was a turning point. The city, often described as the heartbeat of Nigeria’s music scene, became the stage where he could transform ambition into action. That migration wasn’t without obstacles—financial strain, industry gatekeeping, and personal challenges—but those very experiences now shape his sound.



The Power of “Oh No”



“Oh No” is the sound of triumph. Built on infectious Afrobeats grooves and laced with funk-inspired rhythms, the track is a bold rejection of doubt and defeat.




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Dope Boy (@juicecoal)




“‘Oh No’ is a victory song. There’s this certainty that I’ll pass this stage and reach where I want to be. It’s a song I play to celebrate triumph,” says Juice Coal.



The track is more than just celebratory—it’s motivational, a soundtrack for anyone defying the odds. With its anthemic hooks and spirited beat, “Oh No” positions Juice Coal as both a storyteller and a motivator.









Style & Influence



Drawing from alternative hip hop and Afrobeats, Juice Coal creates music that resonates across boundaries. His sound blends raw lyricism with rhythms designed for dance floors, while his message connects with listeners chasing their own victories.



What’s Next for Juice Coal



With “Oh No” signaling his breakthrough, Juice Coal is gearing up for more. Fans can expect new music, live performances in Lagos and beyond, and deeper explorations of the themes that define him—resilience, ambition, and triumph.

Juice Coal began carving out his identity in 2022 with the release of “Antidote,” a confessional, funk-inspired hip hop record produced by Eraps. Written by Sidney Nzekwe, the track revealed his unfiltered honesty: “I thought I needed love but it turns out it was the studio calling.” From the very start, Juice Coal established himself as more than just another Afrobeats newcomer—he was an artist determined to tell his story, even without the polish of a full studio setup.

From Enugu to Lagos

Hailing from Enugu, Juice Coal’s decision to move to Lagos was a turning point. The city, often described as the heartbeat of Nigeria’s music scene, became the stage where he could transform ambition into action. That migration wasn’t without obstacles—financial strain, industry gatekeeping, and personal challenges—but those very experiences now shape his sound.

The Power of “Oh No”

“Oh No” is the sound of triumph. Built on infectious Afrobeats grooves and laced with funk-inspired rhythms, the track is a bold rejection of doubt and defeat.

“‘Oh No’ is a victory song. There’s this certainty that I’ll pass this stage and reach where I want to be. It’s a song I play to celebrate triumph,” says Juice Coal.

The track is more than just celebratory—it’s motivational, a soundtrack for anyone defying the odds. With its anthemic hooks and spirited beat, “Oh No” positions Juice Coal as both a storyteller and a motivator.

Style & Influence

Drawing from alternative hip hop and Afrobeats, Juice Coal creates music that resonates across boundaries. His sound blends raw lyricism with rhythms designed for dance floors, while his message connects with listeners chasing their own victories.

What’s Next for Juice Coal

With “Oh No” signaling his breakthrough, Juice Coal is gearing up for more. Fans can expect new music, live performances in Lagos and beyond, and deeper explorations of the themes that define him—resilience, ambition, and triumph.

A fresh wave is rising in Nigeria’s ever-evolving music landscape, and leading this charge is King Tedi — a dynamic Afro-Trap artist blending cultural depth with raw creative energy to deliver a sound that’s both familiar and refreshingly unique.







Born Daniel Iorfa in Benue State and now based in Abuja, King Tedi represents a new generation of artists fearlessly merging the infectious rhythms of Afrobeats with the grit and emotion of Trap. His music is a masterful fusion of emotive storytelling, heavy-hitting drums, and melodic flows, creating a sonic experience that speaks directly to the struggles, ambitions, and spirit of young Africans.



A Journey Fueled by Passion



King Tedi’s musical journey began in 2014, sparked by freestyle sessions and unfiltered self-expression. By 2018, he transitioned from experimenting to recording in the studio — not in pursuit of fame, but driven by a deep passion for the craft. Drawing inspiration from global icons such as Drake, Playboi Carti, Wizkid, and Burna Boy, he has steadily refined his sound, developing a distinct Afro-Trap identity that stands out in today’s crowded music scene.







Early Milestones and Versatility



From the soulful “Delilah” (produced by Goldmain and featuring Patey), to the vibrant “Tonight” alongside 90djbasemedia, and a standout performance at the Benue State University Cypher hosted by Prime Wave, King Tedi has consistently displayed versatility. Moving fluidly between Afropop, Trap, and Rap, each release has revealed new layers of his artistry, hinting at the rise of a future star.




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Hybrid (@kingtedi_ng)




“3AM” — A Defining Moment



With the release of his latest single, “3AM”, King Tedi steps firmly into the spotlight as one of Afro-Trap’s most exciting emerging voices. The track explores themes of loyalty, hustle, love, and purpose — resonating powerfully with a generation navigating real-life challenges while chasing their dreams.










“This is just the beginning,” King Tedi shares. “My goal is to create music that connects deeply with people, while pushing the boundaries of what Afro-Trap can be.”




Armed with a clear vision, a growing fan base, and a sound built for global stages, King Tedi is set to make a lasting impact on the Nigerian music scene and beyond.




Listen to “3AM”
