Kene Himself is not your typical artist—he’s the full package. Born in Port Harcourt and now based in Abuja, he grew up in a home filled with instruments and endless music. 







While exposed to different sounds, it was the raw energy of Hip-Hop that captured his heart. By age 11, he was writing rhymes; by university, he was producing beats; and with the founding of Tunehouse Records, he established himself as both a creator and an innovator in Nigeria’s fast-growing music scene.



A Career Built on Experimentation



Over the years, Kene has released projects that highlight his fearless approach to music. His experimental tapes This is Totally Xperimental and Outlet pushed sonic boundaries, while singles like Village People, Bad Boy from Port Harcourt, Ogbono, and Runaway bridged Hip-Hop grit with Afropop smoothness. His single Runaway caught international attention on CNN’s African Voices, while The Guardian Nigeria profiled him as one of the artists reshaping the future of African sound.



The New Single: We Don’t Have Fun Anymore (WDHFA)









With his latest release, We Don’t Have Fun Anymore (WDHFA), Kene Himself blends raw honesty with his signature playful creativity. The track captures a mix of groove and introspection, resonating with anyone navigating modern-day realities. It’s the kind of music that both moves the body and stirs the soul—an emblem of Kene’s ability to balance depth with accessibility.




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Kene Himself (@kenehimself)




An Artist Who Does It All



Kene Himself is more than a performer—he’s a rapper, singer, producer, engineer, and visual creative rolled into one. His independence fuels his artistry, allowing him to craft music that is authentic, experimental, and unmistakably his own. With every release, he reinforces why his name is a perfect fit: there’s truly nobody like Kene Himself.




Stream ‘WDHFA’

Today, we sit down with a rising force in South African hip-hop whose music is as spiritual as it is lyrical. Hailing from the Eastern Cape and now making waves across Cape Town and beyond, Pro CHxLD has carved out a lane that blends isiXhosa storytelling with contemporary rap rhythms. His artistry is not just about beats and bars—it’s about revival, community, and carrying a message that transcends borders. Checkout his latest Album and celebrate this Episode with him👊🏾









WHERE HE COMES FROM



Pro CHxLD, your journey began in the Eastern Cape before you moved to Cape Town’s buzzing hip-hop scene. How did your upbringing and roots shape the artist we see today?




I was born and bred in the Eastern Cape by my grandmother. She taught me love and respect, and she raised me with prayer and the church. That foundation shaped me from the very beginning. Becoming an artist didn’t change who I am, it just taught me even more about how to work with people.




You’re known for blending isiXhosa with contemporary rap, creating a sound that feels both authentic and global. Why was it important for you to carry your language and culture into your music?




In isiXhosa I find it easier to paint and create a clear picture of my story than when I’m using other languages. I only use other languages as additionals.




Your debut album Watch My Changes turned heads and Uyesu EP was described as “food for the mind, body, and spirit.” When you look back, what do you think set those projects apart in the industry?




I wrote Watch My Changes after a few years of losing my father. I was doing my last high school grades and I was blessed with a daughter, so that was a project where I was noticing the changes to my life and things that were happening around me. Basically, it was me looking back to where I’m coming from and the current living situation. On Uyesu, it was me tapping into other sounds, blending them with my sound, and obviously introducing and establishing myself to the new hip-hop audience.




Hip-hop in South Africa has evolved with unique sub-genres and voices. Who were some of your biggest influences when you first picked up the mic in 2014, and who motivates you now?




Coming to Cape Town from the Eastern Cape in 2014, I thought I was going to do reggae music, because that’s what I was mostly listening to at the time. I had done a few performances at my previous schools, but everything changed when I was exposed to Spaza music and the whole hip hop movement happening back then. Artists like Nqikilitye, AKA, and Maggz were buzzing. To be honest, I wasn’t inspired by specific names—it was the movement itself that made me feel at home.




Beyond music, you’ve been deeply involved with community work—whether through high school tours, your signature Imvuselelo noPro CHxLD show, or serving as a brand ambassador. How important is that humanitarian side of your artistry?




The humanitarian side of my artistry is deeply important, as it forms the heart of my music and public presence. My work goes beyond entertainment—it’s rooted in uplifting, healing, and creating meaningful spaces for spiritual and social revival, making my impact both artistic and transformative.




You’ve already performed with notable names like iFani, Anela Jahmena, and collaborated with Flash Ikumkani. Looking back at these milestones, which moment still feels surreal to you?




Every moment has been special, but watching Anela Jahmena perform still feels surreal to me. Her presence and energy are on another level. But honestly, what surprises me the most is the impact of Imvuselelo noPro CHxLD. Every time we host it, the way people show up, the energy, the healing—it reminds me why I do this. It’s more than just a show; it’s a spiritual experience. Seeing how the music connects with people like that always humbles me.




Before we move forward, could you give a shoutout or even a prayer to the people who have carried Pro CHxLD this far—your fans, your community, and your family?




First and foremost, I want to give all glory to God—without His grace, none of this would be possible. To my family, my day ones, and the community that raised me: thank you for believing in me, even when I was still finding myself. You carried me with your prayers, your love, your patience, and your presence.





        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Pro CHxLD (@prochxld_za)





To my fans, every single person who streamed a song, came to a show, shared a post, or spoke life into me—you’re not just supporters, you’re part of this mission. Your energy keeps me going when the weight gets heavy.




Let me pray this over all of you:




“Yanga uThixo anganikhusela, aniqhubele ezindleleni ezinilungeleyo, andise. Yanga angandisa kuthando enindinika lina alibuyise emakhayeni eni, kwiintliziyo zenu, nakumaphupha enu. May you rise, may you heal, and may you walk in the fullness of your calling. Amen.”




Where He’s Going T

Where He’s Going To

Your upcoming project, Thamsanaqa, is set to drop on 14 September 2025. What does the title mean to you, and how does this project build on your past work?

The project was moved to 11th September due to unforeseen circumstances. Moving to your question, the whole album is dedicated to my late father and his name was Thamsanqa. I named my project after him. The project came after a lot of meditations and dreams that made me tap in and think deeply on how great he was. It’s also part of my healing.

In this project, I’ve worked with Wavely.

In your profiling, we saw highlights like being in studio with Black Coffee and working on the USA/SA versions of Nkosi Sikelela. Should fans expect surprises of that magnitude on Thamsanaqa?

No, you can maybe expect those in future. As for Nkosi Sikelela, it was a song made for UMAMA Monument which was happening in USB, and it was for their exhibitions.

Your music is already charting on Trace Urban and Trace Africa, and your sound is reaching beyond borders. Do you see yourself as a cultural bridge between South Africa and the global hip-hop scene?

Yes, I do see myself as a cultural bridge between South Africa and the global hip-hop scene. I bring my roots, my language, and my faith into every beat and bar. My music carries the rhythm and soul of Xhosa identity, while still speaking the universal language of hip-hop.

I’m not here to copy what the world is doing, I’m here to contribute something real from this side of the world. By blending local truth with a global sound, I’m building a connection. I want people to hear not just the beat, but the message… the revival. I believe that’s what makes my work a bridge not just between cultures, but between purpose and sound.

Hip-hop is not just sound—it’s a movement. With your spiritual rap and storytelling, what impact do you hope Thamsanaqa will have on the younger generation coming after you?

They must appreciate their fathers and learn the good from them while they are still alive, because I’ve witnessed later that I had a very smart and loving father that I think I could’ve learnt a lot from. It also gives you hope to believe in yourself and not live by societal standards because people will always talk, whether you’re doing good or bad.

You’re also plugged into fashion, culture, and brand ambassadorships. Do you see Pro CHxLD evolving into a multi-industry figure, and how do you balance music with these other ventures?

Yes! I see music as the core of everything, but fashion, culture, and brand partnerships are natural extensions of who I am and what I represent. They’re just different languages I use to express the same message: purpose, authenticity, and revival.

Balancing it all comes down to alignment. I don’t step into any space just for visibility—it has to connect with the story I’m telling through my music. Whether it’s on stage, in a campaign, or behind a clothing brand, I’m showing up as the same vessel.

So as I evolve into a multi-industry figure, I stay grounded by keeping music at the center, and I let every other venture flow from that source. If it doesn’t add to the mission, I leave it. If it does, I build with it.

Five years from now, what’s the vision? Do you see yourself headlining global stages, launching your own label, or something even bigger?

Yes! Having my own label would be a dream come true. Headlining global stages would be cherry on top.

Finally, with Thamsanaqa on the horizon, what is your heartfelt message to the fans waiting for this body of work?

To everyone who’s been riding with me, I just want to say thank you. Thamsanqa is more than just an album. It’s a testimony, a journey through pain, purpose, and praise. Every song carries a piece of my truth, and I poured my soul into this body of work so that you could feel seen, lifted, and reminded that blessings are real even in the dark.

To my supporters (Ibandla): this one is for you. When it drops, please stream it, share it, and let it live in your hearts. Thamsanqa will be available on all digital platforms, and your support means everything.

I’m also fully open for bookings and performances both in South Africa and globally. Let’s bring this message to your city, your stage, your people. Revival doesn’t stop at the studio, it moves with us.

Much love, and may the blessings find you.

Emerging from the heart of Nigeria’s vibrant music scene, EL Nayaan is proving to be more than just another rising voice — he’s an artist whose sound and story are rooted in resilience, transformation, and a fearless sense of self-expression.







Born on January 22, 2000, EL Nayaan began shaping his craft in Kaduna, where studios like Audio City Studios, Futuremusiq, and KD World Records gave him his earliest platforms. His artistic journey deepened when he moved to Abuja, a shift that opened doors to mentorship at YesAcademyNigeria and collaborations at Elytron, where he was granted studio space that became a foundation for his unique sound.



Blending Afro-dancehall, Afro-swing, and Afropop, Nayaan crafts music that’s as rhythmic as it is purposeful — a sound that speaks to community, healing, and strength.



Rising Through Setbacks



Nayaan’s story is not without its challenges. After an accident that left him with a fractured hand, he could have paused his career — but instead, he chose to turn his pain into fuel. “I don’t like to just submit to what life throws at me,” he says. “Instead, I flip it. I’d rather say, I’m showing life what I can do, instead of, life is showing me something.”









That grit and determination shine through his catalog, which already includes standout singles like “No Competition,” “Talk,” “Mandela,” “Addicted,” and the official theme song for Nigeria’s basketball teams at the 2021 Olympics — proof that his artistry is already crossing boundaries of sound and culture.



The Next Chapter: YOLO & All My Life



Now shuttling between Abuja and Lagos, EL Nayaan is gearing up for one of his most personal and anticipated projects yet: a dual release of “YOLO” and “All My Life.”







The project, born out of a dark moment, captures the duality of acceptance and defiance, pain and joy, freedom and destiny. “Before, it was just vibes, vibes,” Nayaan admits. “But now, I really want to write about the things people don’t like about me — because those same things are what some people love about me too. That duality is part of the story.”




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by EL Nayaan (@el_nayaan_)




That honesty threads through the music, making the upcoming release not just a collection of songs, but a statement of identity.

Emerging from the heart of Nigeria’s vibrant music scene, EL Nayaan is proving to be more than just another rising voice — he’s an artist whose sound and story are rooted in resilience, transformation, and a fearless sense of self-expression.

Born on January 22, 2000, EL Nayaan began shaping his craft in Kaduna, where studios like Audio City Studios, Futuremusiq, and KD World Records gave him his earliest platforms. His artistic journey deepened when he moved to Abuja, a shift that opened doors to mentorship at YesAcademyNigeria and collaborations at Elytron, where he was granted studio space that became a foundation for his unique sound.

Blending Afro-dancehall, Afro-swing, and Afropop, Nayaan crafts music that’s as rhythmic as it is purposeful — a sound that speaks to community, healing, and strength.

Rising Through Setbacks

Nayaan’s story is not without its challenges. After an accident that left him with a fractured hand, he could have paused his career — but instead, he chose to turn his pain into fuel. “I don’t like to just submit to what life throws at me,” he says. “Instead, I flip it. I’d rather say, I’m showing life what I can do, instead of, life is showing me something.”

That grit and determination shine through his catalog, which already includes standout singles like “No Competition,” “Talk,” “Mandela,” “Addicted,” and the official theme song for Nigeria’s basketball teams at the 2021 Olympics — proof that his artistry is already crossing boundaries of sound and culture.

The Next Chapter: YOLO & All My Life

Now shuttling between Abuja and Lagos, EL Nayaan is gearing up for one of his most personal and anticipated projects yet: a dual release of “YOLO” and “All My Life.”

The project, born out of a dark moment, captures the duality of acceptance and defiance, pain and joy, freedom and destiny. “Before, it was just vibes, vibes,” Nayaan admits. “But now, I really want to write about the things people don’t like about me — because those same things are what some people love about me too. That duality is part of the story.”

That honesty threads through the music, making the upcoming release not just a collection of songs, but a statement of identity.

Rising Nigerian Afrobeat artist Kelly Mayami is gearing up for the release of his much-anticipated single, JUMOKE, set to drop this Friday on September 26, 2025 across all major digital platforms.







With the launch of the official pre-save campaign, fans and music lovers can now be among the first to experience what is already being described as Kelly’s most defining record to date.



A Story of Love, Told in Rhythm



JUMOKE is an amapiano-inspired Afro-fusion track that explores the timeless theme of love and devotion. Inspired by the narrative power of Afrobeat and modern sonic trends, the single blends heartfelt lyrics with infectious percussion and melodies designed to move both hearts and dancefloors. Kelly paints a picture of relentless pursuit and commitment, making JUMOKE not just a song, but a story every listener can connect to.







A Strategic Moment for Kelly Mayami



Since making his debut in 2022, Kelly Mayami (born Duza Yunusa) has built a reputation for crafting music that resonates with both passion and authenticity. Drawing influence from the legendary Fela Kuti, Kelly’s artistry fuses socially conscious energy with deeply personal storytelling. His breakout track Isale Eko set the tone, but JUMOKE marks a bold new chapter—one that positions him as a rising voice in the ever-evolving African music scene.



Visuals and Rollout







Alongside the audio release, Kelly Mayami is set to deliver a cinematic visual experience directed by @sickdirector. With creative direction from @crosswordz and striking imagery by @jpegsfromdave, the project is supported by a robust content rollout curated by RADARCharts by REM, ensuring maximum visibility across DSPs, social platforms, and media outlets.



Pre-Save JUMOKE

Featuring Anointeen & D4Donzii



Emerging talent Skeng We$ has officially released his latest body of work, an EP titled “IS THIS WHAT YOU WANT?” — a daring, forward-thinking project that blurs the lines between alternative rap and the infectious grooves of Afrobeats.







With contributions from Anointeen and D4Donzii, the EP offers a fresh listening experience that balances raw lyricism, vibrant rhythms, and experimental soundscapes. Skeng We$ demonstrates his ability to craft music that resonates beyond borders, appealing to fans of both underground hip-hop and the global Afrobeats wave.



A Thematic Exploration of Authenticity



At its core, “IS THIS WHAT YOU WANT?” wrestles with a crucial artistic question: how does a creator stay true to themselves in a music industry that often prioritizes trends and commercial appeal?




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by We$ (@skengwes)




Skeng We$ approaches this tension with lyrical honesty and sonic boldness. The EP isn’t just a collection of tracks — it’s a reflection of the artist’s internal dialogue, his push to remain authentic while still delivering music that captivates.



The Power of the Title



The project’s title itself, “IS THIS WHAT YOU WANT?”, is more than a name — it’s a provocation and a dialogue. It challenges listeners to consider what they seek in music and culture, while simultaneously asserting Skeng We$’s own creative voice. By asking this question, he invites fans into his artistic journey, making them active participants in the conversation.




Stream ITWYW

articles.author: RADARCharts by REM
articles.body:
In an era where Afrobeats continues to dominate global charts, a fresh and fearless voice is rising—Mosa Temple. 







Born Enetule Temple Anu, the Nigerian singer-songwriter is quickly carving out a place for himself as a leading force in the Afro-fusion movement. Backed by Royal Empire Management, Mosa Temple represents the next generation of artists unafraid to blend cultural heritage with global influences.



Rooted in Heritage, Shaped by Innovation



Mosa Temple’s artistry is firmly grounded in the rhythms and traditions of Africa, but his sound goes beyond borders. Drawing inspiration from Afrobeat, Afro-pop, R&B, and soul, he creates sonic landscapes that balance familiarity with freshness. 









This balance allows his music to appeal not only to African audiences but also to listeners worldwide who crave authenticity paired with modern energy.



The Stories Behind the Sound



What sets Mosa apart is his ability to tell stories that resonate. His lyrics explore themes of love, identity, struggle, and self-discovery—stories both intimate and universal. From the ecstasy of romance to the pain of betrayal, Mosa Temple doesn’t just sing; he translates real-life emotions into music that feels personal for every listener. His artistry reflects vulnerability, courage, and an understanding of the human experience.









From Lagos Streets to Global Streams



Raised in Lagos and working between Lagos and Abuja, Mosa Temple carries the vibrancy of Nigerian cities in his music. His breakout track has already begun reaching audiences on streaming platforms, gaining traction with listeners who recognize his distinctive blend of honesty and rhythm. For many fans, his music is not just something to dance to—it’s something to feel.



A Generation’s Soundtrack



Mosa Temple’s music speaks directly to today’s generation—a generation that values authenticity, creativity, and emotion. With only a short time active (since 2024), his trajectory already hints at long-term impact. His sound is not just Afro-fusion; it’s a cultural bridge, bringing together tradition and the global stage in a way that feels organic and effortless.







What’s Next for Mosa Temple?



As his journey unfolds, Mosa Temple is set to expand his footprint across Africa and beyond. With his strong sense of identity, genre-bending sound, and a growing community of listeners, the future looks bright. For fans of Afrobeats who want to discover the next big name before the world catches on—Mosa Temple is that artist.

Lagos, Nigeria – September 5, 2025 – Today marks the official release of Mr. Bady’s (Uchenna Richard) latest dual single project, featuring “Up To Something” and “Sho Ti Gbo”. 







The rising Afrobeat star is set to captivate fans worldwide with this fresh collection, available now on all major streaming platforms.



A Dual Release That Shows Versatility



Mr. Bady’s new singles demonstrate his unique ability to balance high-energy, modern Afrobeat with deep cultural storytelling.









“Up To Something” channels ambition and unstoppable energy, perfect for fans looking for a motivational anthem. 









“Sho Ti Gbo” dives into Mr. Bady’s roots, blending Afrobeat with Highlife and reggae influences to create a sound that feels both nostalgic and contemporary.









This dual release reflects where Mr. Bady is as an artist: evolving, versatile, and committed to bringing Afrobeat to a global audience.



Building Momentum: From Stage to Studio



Since his debut project MR BADY DEH HERE XO earlier this year, Mr. Bady has been steadily making waves. His singles “OJEMBA” and “ACHALUGO” have already captured the attention of local and international audiences.



Live performances have further cemented his rising profile:




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Mr. Bady (@mrbadyofficial)




He electrified fans at Jeriq The Husla’s Stadium Homecoming Concert. Currently, he is touring Russia, performing alongside Afrobeat heavyweights like Ruger, expanding his global footprint.



The Artist Behind the Music



Born in Anambra and raised in Onitsha, Mr. Bady draws from a rich musical heritage, influenced by legends such as Fela Kuti, as well as Highlife and reggae sounds. Since his official debut in January 2025, he has been carving out a unique space in the Afrobeat scene, blending tradition with modern rhythms that resonate across borders.







He describes his new release as “a celebration of Afrobeat and how far it has come,” highlighting both his personal growth and the genre’s evolution.




Stream Now

articles.body:
There’s a familiar feeling when you meet a great new artist: like discovering a friend’s playlist on repeat, or stumbling into a small venue where everyone knows the chorus before the second bar. 







RADARCharts feels like that kind of discovery — friendly, local, and stubbornly real — but built with the tools and reach today’s independent artists need. More than a chart or a website, it’s a creative workshop that helps music meet story, and songs become careers.



Where it started (and why it feels different)



RADARCharts grew out of Royal Empire Management (REM), a talent-first outfit rooted in Abuja rather than the usual Lagos glare. That origin matters. Instead of copying the major-label playbook, RADARCharts pairs editorial storytelling, grassroots showcases and practical services — distribution, playlist pitching, radio support, visuals — into one ecosystem. Think of it like a neighbourhood studio that also happens to have a publicist, a magazine, and a small record shop attached.







Because it’s born of a community mindset, RADARCharts doesn’t chase hype for hype’s sake. It scouts artists where attention is still tender — regional scenes, local cyphers, experimental pockets of sound — and gives them a clear runway to grow. That makes the platform feel relatable to artists and audiences alike: artists see a team that understands the grind; listeners find context that makes music stick.



What RADARCharts actually does



RADARCharts operates across a few interlocking tracks:



Editorial & storytelling: Features, interviews and deep-dive pieces that let artists tell why they make music, not just what they made. These aren’t press releases — they read like conversations you’d have after a long soundcheck. RADARMusic & RADARStore: Practical artist services — distribution, EPKs, playlist pitching, campaign support — packaged for independents who want professional results without losing ownership. Live & community projects: From curated shows to cyphers and recording camps, RADARCharts converts local energy into digital and commercial visibility. Curated charts and lists: Top-25 features and playlists that help audiences find music outside the usual algorithmic loop.







The combination is potent because it treats artists as people with stories and needs, not just content to be monetized.



MOTHERLand: identity, heritage, and a louder voice



One of the platform’s most human parts is MOTHERLand — an editorial vertical and programming space that centers heritage, identity, and the voices of women in West African music. MOTHERLand doesn’t just spotlight female artists as another checkbox; it frames their music within lineage, language, and lived experience. Features under this banner often highlight indigenous rap, soul-laced storytelling, and creative producers who marry tradition with contemporary production.







For listeners, MOTHERLand feels like getting a friend’s recommendation: “You have to hear this — she flips Igbo rhythms into something that sounds like yesterday and tomorrow at once.” For artists, it’s validation — a space that respects cultural roots while translating them for wider audiences.



Why RADARCharts matters to West Africa’s music scene



There are three big reasons RADARCharts is becoming essential to the regional ecosystem:



Decentralization. Not every great artist in Nigeria is in Lagos. By investing in scenes across Abuja, Enugu and beyond, RADARCharts helps diversify what the wider Afrobeats conversation sounds like. Narrative-first discovery. Today’s listeners want to feel involved. Editorial features and contextualized playlists create emotional hooks — people don’t just stream a song, they follow a story. Real services for real artists. Distribution, PR, and playlist pitching can feel opaque; RADARCharts packages them in ways that make sense for independent careers, not just headline-grabbing launches.



Put simply: the platform makes it easier for artists to turn attention into momentum and for listeners to find music that actually matters to them.



Face of the movement and community wins



RADARCharts amplifies artists who match its values. The “RADARMan” concept — a figurehead who embodies the brand’s spirit — and projects like city cyphers or producer-led camps show that the platform is both a curator and a community-builder. Those projects turn local buzz into things people can stream, share, and book gigs with.



Partnerships with streaming and discovery platforms also show RADARCharts can scale without losing its curatorial edge: local work that gets amplified globally, not repackaged into generic playlists.



The clearest challenge (and the biggest opportunity)



Scaling while staying authentic is the tightrope. If RADARCharts leans too hard into commercial partnerships, it risks losing the trust of the underground scenes that fed it. But if it stays too small, its artists miss opportunities. The sweet spot is measurable pipe

Partnerships with streaming and discovery platforms also show RADARCharts can scale without losing its curatorial edge: local work that gets amplified globally, not repackaged into generic playlists.

The clearest challenge (and the biggest opportunity)

Scaling while staying authentic is the tightrope. If RADARCharts leans too hard into commercial partnerships, it risks losing the trust of the underground scenes that fed it. But if it stays too small, its artists miss opportunities. The sweet spot is measurable pipelines: predictable playlist slots, radio rotations, sync opportunities, and live showcases that convert discovery into sustainable income.

If RADARCharts keeps investing in those mechanics while protecting its editorial soul, it will be a model for how regional tastemakers grow — not by imitating major players, but by building honest, artist-first infrastructure.

Why a listener or artist should care

If you’re a listener, RADARCharts is a friend who hands you the next song you’ll replay — not a feed that buries human context beneath trends. If you’re an artist, it’s a practical partner that knows how to tell your story and get it heard, without asking you to lose yourself.

At a moment when Afrobeats is both global and deeply local, RADARCharts offers a middle path: rooted curation that connects to real business outcomes. That’s how scenes grow, songs travel, and artists build careers that last.

South African hip-hop continues to thrive on voices that dare to stand out, and Pro CHxLD is leading the charge. The Cape Town-based rapper, known for his rich storytelling, spiritual lyricism, and fearless fusion of isiXhosa with contemporary hip-hop, is gearing up to drop his highly anticipated project, Thamsanqa, on September 11, 2025.







The project, already building anticipation ahead of its release, features the powerful lead single “Ukelemile” with rising star Leo Brenin, a track that’s quickly become a fan favorite and a strong introduction to the project’s vision.



A Story-Driven Body of Work



Pro CHxLD has built his reputation on authenticity. His music is deeply rooted in his Eastern Cape upbringing and shaped by his rise through Cape Town’s creative scene. With Thamsanqa—a name meaning “Blessing” in isiXhosa—he promises a project that blends spirituality, grit, and innovation.









“This project is not just music; it’s a journey of faith, resilience, and inspiration for those who listen,” Pro CHxLD shared. “I want people to feel seen and uplifted, while also knowing that South African hip-hop is evolving into something global and powerful.”



“Ukelemile” ft. Leo Brenin: A Breakout Anthem



The project’s lead single, “Ukelemile,” featuring Leo Brenin, is a bold, melodic anthem that’s already capturing ears across the continent. Its seamless mix of soulful hooks and hard-hitting verses offers a clear glimpse into what Thamsanqa has in store—music that’s grounded in South African culture but elevated for an international audience.




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Pro CHxLD (@prochxld_za)




With streaming numbers rising and strong radio traction, this single positions Pro CHxLD as one of the most dynamic voices shaping hip-hop’s future.



A Star with Momentum



From his critically acclaimed debut Watch My Changes to the spiritually charged Uyesu EP, Pro CHxLD has consistently delivered music that challenges norms and inspires listeners. His music video for “Thu” held the #1 spot on Trace Urban’s SA Hip-Hop Chart for three consecutive weeks, proving his ability to connect with audiences on a large scale.







Off-stage, Pro CHxLD’s influence extends into culture and community: he’s a Too Much WiFi brand ambassador, a member of the Bridges Academy development team, and a dedicated advocate for inspiring youth through his tours and shows.



RADARViewers: Mark Your Calendars



While fans anticipate the official release of Thamsanqa on September 11, 2025, the excitement doesn’t stop there. RADARViewers should tune in to his exclusive TALK TO US interview dropping this Sunday on RADARCharts. In the episode, Pro CHxLD opens up about his creative process, collaborations, and the deeper meaning behind Thamsanqa, giving fans a rare behind-the-scenes look at one of South Africa’s most exciting hip-hop talents.




Presave ‘Thamsanqa’

In a music scene constantly hungry for authentic sound, Nigerian Afrobeat sensation Kelly Mayami is setting the stage for a breakout moment. Known for his rich blend of Afrobeat rhythms, soulful melodies, and socially conscious lyrics, Kelly is preparing to drop what industry insiders are already calling his most defining work yet — “Jumoke.”







With a style inspired by Afrobeat legend Fela Kuti and a drive shaped by his modest beginnings, Kelly Mayami has been steadily carving a lane for himself since his debut in 2022. His breakout track “Isale Eko” introduced him as a voice to watch, showcasing his lyrical depth and ability to marry storytelling with Afro-fusion grooves. Now, Kelly is hinting that “Jumoke” is more than just a single — it’s a cultural moment in the making.



Speaking on the track, Kelly teased that “Jumoke” embodies everything he has worked for as an artist: authenticity, storytelling, and a sonic experience designed to resonate across borders. The song is expected to feature lush instrumentation, catchy but meaningful lyrics, and a vibe that celebrates Afrobeat’s global influence while staying true to its Nigerian roots.









To amplify excitement, Kelly’s team has rolled out a cinematic official trailer, viral cut clips, and a stunning visual campaign, setting the stage for what promises to be one of the hottest Afrobeat releases of the season. Early teasers on social media have sparked anticipation among fans, with many praising Kelly’s attention to artistry and branding as he prepares for this monumental drop.



“Jumoke” also marks a new chapter for Kelly as he continues his evolution from an underground talent to a rising Afrobeat powerhouse. With his rebrand in motion and a carefully planned rollout strategy, this release isn’t just about dropping a song — it’s about cementing his place as one of Nigeria’s next big musical exports.







Fans can expect “Jumoke” to officially drop this month, accompanied by a striking music video and an engaging social media campaign designed to bring Kelly closer to his audience. With his team working tirelessly behind the scenes and a wave of anticipation building, “Jumoke” is poised to be a career-defining moment for the rising star.

Kaduna-born, Abuja-based artist 3yga Ali (Caleb Aliyu) is carving his name into Nigeria’s growing alternative rap and afrodrill scene. Known for his fluid rap delivery, gritty storytelling, and fearless energy, 3yga Ali has evolved from dominating online battle rap groups and dropping viral freestyles in 2017 to becoming one of the country’s most promising drill voices.







His breakout moment came in 2023 with Shine featuring Zilla Oaks, a hard-hitting single that earned a coveted spot on Spotify’s official Naija Drill playlist, solidifying his place among a new wave of artists shaping the genre’s future. Now, with his debut EP 3YGA WARNING (2025), 3yga Ali delivers a powerful statement of intent. The project blends unapologetic braggadocio, melodic hooks, and street-conscious bars, featuring heavyweights like Eeskay, Terry Tha Rapman, BiG OG, and Moefasa.









3YGA WARNING is more than a debut—it’s a manifesto. Each track channels 3yga Ali’s hunger and resilience, offering a raw look into the streets while embracing afro-influenced rhythms and alternative rap textures. With this release, he firmly establishes himself as a rising force, spearheading the next era of Nigerian drill and alternative rap.



As afrodrill continues to evolve, 3yga Ali is setting the pace—one bar at a time.




Stream ‘3YGA WARNING’

Nigerian hip-hop trailblazer Rhapstar OTP is back, and this time he’s making a bold statement. His latest release, “Secure The Bag,” featuring rap powerhouse King Rapsodi and lyrical preacher IPreach Gospel, is a hard-hitting anthem that blends motivational energy, raw lyricism, and undeniable street credibility.







“Secure The Bag” is more than just a song — it’s a declaration of ambition and perseverance. Backed by a gritty, bass-heavy beat layered with Afro-fusion elements, the track captures the hustle spirit of today’s generation while showcasing the unique artistry of each collaborator. Rhapstar OTP delivers razor-sharp verses with his signature smooth flow, while King Rapsodi brings a punchy, confident edge. IPreach Gospel rounds out the track with a thought-provoking and spiritually charged delivery, offering a powerful message about grinding with purpose.









This collaboration marks a significant moment in Rhapstar OTP’s career, as it bridges different voices and styles to create a record that resonates across hip-hop, gospel-rap, and Afro-fusion audiences. The chemistry between all three artists is undeniable, resulting in a track that feels fresh, authentic, and anthemic.



For Rhapstar OTP, “Secure The Bag” is a testament to his growth as both an artist and CEO of Only The People Involved Entertainment (OTPIE). The song reflects his commitment to telling real stories, uplifting his community, and inspiring listeners to chase their dreams relentlessly.



“‘Secure The Bag’ is for every dreamer, every hustler, every believer,” Rhapstar OTP explains. “It’s about fighting for your purpose, staying focused, and never giving up on what’s yours.”



With its infectious hook, crisp production, and dynamic lyrical performance, “Secure The Bag” is primed to become a playlist favorite and a motivational anthem for fans worldwide.




Stream ‘Secure The Bag’

On this episode, we’re excited to chat with CAMEO HUZLA, an original talent bringing his unique sound from the East. You won’t want to miss it! Be sure to check out his latest project “LOST BUT FOUND” in the meantime to get a taste of his incredible style. We can’t wait for you to hear this one!







WHERE HE COMES FROM



Can you take us back to the beginning—what was life like growing up in Enugu Ezike, and how did your environment shape your music?




Growing up in Enugu Ezike was raw and real. It’s a place where culture isn’t just tradition—it’s the rhythm of everyday life. I remember hearing ogene sounds at community gatherings, gospel echoes from early morning prayers, and street chants from local hustlers. Life wasn’t easy, but that mix of struggle, resilience, and celebration shaped how I hear and feel music today. Every beat I make has a bit of home in it—whether it’s the storytelling from our elders or the energy from the streets. My environment didn’t just inspire me; it gave me a reason to keep pushing and a sound that’s authentically mine.




What made you first pick up a mic and start expressing yourself through music?




For me, music wasn’t a choice—it was a calling. I grew up surrounded by sounds that spoke to my soul, but I also had a lot I wanted to say about my life, my dreams, and my reality. The first time I picked up a mic, it was less about performing and more about finally giving my thoughts a voice. I realised music could carry my struggles, my wins, and my culture to the world. From that moment, I knew this was more than a hobby—it was my way of living and connecting.








Your sound is distinct and deeply personal. Who are the major influences that helped you shape your style?




My biggest influence isn’t a specific artist—it’s life itself. The things I’ve been through, the things I’m still going through, my moods, emotions, scars, and stories—they all shape my sound. When I create, I’m pulling from real moments—both the pain and the joy—and translating them into music people can feel. That’s why my sound is so personal, because it’s not borrowed from anyone else; it’s my life in rhythm and melody.




What challenges have you faced as an independent artist, and how have they made you stronger?




Being an independent artist means every step is on you—funding your projects, building your audience, and knocking on doors that sometimes don’t even open. I’ve faced times where resources were low, support was scarce, and it felt like I was shouting into the wind. But those challenges taught me resilience and creativity. They forced me to learn every side of the game—from production to promotion—and to keep believing in my vision even when no one else did. Now, every win feels earned, and every setback just makes me hungrier.




You’ve dropped projects like Tested, Strength, and Devil’s Passage. What do these titles mean to you personally?




Each of those titles is a chapter in my story. Tested represents the trials I’ve faced—life situations that pushed me to my limits and proved how much I could endure. Strength is about the inner power I had to build to keep moving forward, even when things felt impossible. And Devil’s Passage is the darker chapter—fighting through temptations, setbacks, and moments where it felt like the odds were against me. Together, they’re not just projects; they’re reflections of my journey, my battles, and my growth.








How has the response from your community and fans shaped your journey so far?




The love from my community and fans has been like fuel. Coming from where I come from, every stream, every message, every shout-out feels personal. It’s proof that my story is connecting. Their support reminds me that I’m not just making music for myself; I’m speaking for people who relate to the struggle, the hustle, and the dream. Even in tough moments, knowing they’re listening and rooting for me keeps me going and pushes me to aim higher.




Drop a prayer or shout-out to everyone who’s been riding with you since day one.




To everyone who’s been with me since day one—may your hustle never be in vain, may your dreams never run out of breath, and may your blessings overflow. You’ve carried me with your love, your energy, and your belief when I had nothing but a vision. I pray the same light you’ve poured into me comes back to you a hundredfold. We’re in this together—forever HU$$LE GANG.










WHERE HE’S GOING TO



What’s next for Cameo Huzla? Any new drops, visuals, or collaborations we should watch out for?




The journey’s just getting started. I’ve got new music on the way that’s even more personal and raw, visuals that bring my stories to life, and some collaborations that will surprise a lot of people. I won’t give away too much, but just know everything coming next is bigger, bolder, and built to hit you right in the heart. Stay tuned—Cameo Huzla season is here.

The first time I picked up a mic, it was less about performing and more about finally giving my thoughts a voice. I realised music could carry my struggles, my wins, and my culture to the world. From that moment, I knew this was more than a hobby—it was my way of living and connecting.

Your sound is distinct and deeply personal. Who are the major influences that helped you shape your style?

My biggest influence isn’t a specific artist—it’s life itself. The things I’ve been through, the things I’m still going through, my moods, emotions, scars, and stories—they all shape my sound. When I create, I’m pulling from real moments—both the pain and the joy—and translating them into music people can feel. That’s why my sound is so personal, because it’s not borrowed from anyone else; it’s my life in rhythm and melody.

What challenges have you faced as an independent artist, and how have they made you stronger?

Being an independent artist means every step is on you—funding your projects, building your audience, and knocking on doors that sometimes don’t even open. I’ve faced times where resources were low, support was scarce, and it felt like I was shouting into the wind. But those challenges taught me resilience and creativity. They forced me to learn every side of the game—from production to promotion—and to keep believing in my vision even when no one else did. Now, every win feels earned, and every setback just makes me hungrier.

You’ve dropped projects like Tested, Strength, and Devil’s Passage. What do these titles mean to you personally?

Each of those titles is a chapter in my story. Tested represents the trials I’ve faced—life situations that pushed me to my limits and proved how much I could endure. Strength is about the inner power I had to build to keep moving forward, even when things felt impossible. And Devil’s Passage is the darker chapter—fighting through temptations, setbacks, and moments where it felt like the odds were against me. Together, they’re not just projects; they’re reflections of my journey, my battles, and my growth.

How has the response from your community and fans shaped your journey so far?

The love from my community and fans has been like fuel. Coming from where I come from, every stream, every message, every shout-out feels personal. It’s proof that my story is connecting. Their support reminds me that I’m not just making music for myself; I’m speaking for people who relate to the struggle, the hustle, and the dream. Even in tough moments, knowing they’re listening and rooting for me keeps me going and pushes me to aim higher.

Drop a prayer or shout-out to everyone who’s been riding with you since day one.

To everyone who’s been with me since day one—may your hustle never be in vain, may your dreams never run out of breath, and may your blessings overflow. You’ve carried me with your love, your energy, and your belief when I had nothing but a vision. I pray the same light you’ve poured into me comes back to you a hundredfold. We’re in this together—forever HU$$LE GANG.

WHERE HE’S GOING TO

What’s next for Cameo Huzla? Any new drops, visuals, or collaborations we should watch out for?

The journey’s just getting started. I’ve got new music on the way that’s even more personal and raw, visuals that bring my stories to life, and some collaborations that will surprise a lot of people. I won’t give away too much, but just know everything coming next is bigger, bolder, and built to hit you right in the heart. Stay tuned—Cameo Huzla season is here.

As the founder of Hussle Gang Records and Huzla Place, how do you plan to use those platforms to impact the industry?

For me, Hussle Gang Records and Huzla Place are more than just brands—they’re platforms to give a voice to raw, undiscovered talent and to create a movement. I want to build spaces where artists don’t have to compromise their truth to be heard, where hustle is respected, and where culture is celebrated. My goal is to set a standard in the industry—quality music, real stories, and a family-like network that grows together. It’s not just about my journey; it’s about creating lanes for the next wave of hustlers to shine.

What does success look like to you right now, beyond numbers and awards?

For me right now, success is peace of mind—waking up every day knowing I’m living my purpose and touching lives through my music. It’s hearing someone say a song of mine helped them through a hard time, or seeing a fan in a faraway place connect to my story. Numbers and awards are great, but the real win is growth—becoming a better artist, a better man, and making sure the people who believe in me feel proud to say they’ve been part of the journey.

What’s your take on the current state of Nigerian hip-hop, and where do you see it heading?

Nigerian hip-hop is in an interesting place right now—it’s evolving. Afrobeats has taken the spotlight globally, but hip-hop here is quietly building a new wave. Artists are blending our local rhythms, languages, and street stories into rap, making it uniquely Nigerian. I see it heading towards a space where it’s not just respected at home but making real noise internationally. And I want to be part of that wave—bringing authenticity, storytelling, and that raw hustle energy to push the culture forward.

How do you balance your street roots with commercial appeal as you grow?

For me, the streets are my foundation—that’s where my truth comes from. But as I grow, I’ve learned how to package that truth so it can connect with a wider audience without losing its soul. It’s about keeping the raw energy, the slang, the grit—but presenting it in a way that even someone who’s never been to my hood can feel it. I’m not trying to water down who I am; I’m building a bridge between where I come from and where the world is going.

What dream collaborations or stages are on your radar right now?

I’ve got a list in my head of artists I’d love to connect with—people whose energy and storytelling match mine. On the home front, I’d like to work with some of the heavyweights pushing Nigerian rap and Afrobeats forward. Globally, I want to work with artists who inspire me with their honesty and stage presence. As for stages—think global festivals like Rolling Loud, Afro Nation, or even Coachella. I see myself taking the sound from Enugu Ezike to the world, and those stages are just stepping stones.

To wrap up, send a message straight from your heart to your fans and those just discovering Cameo Huzla.

To everyone who’s been riding with me, and to those just finding out about Cameo Huzla—thank you. Every stream, every share, every word of encouragement keeps me going more than you know. My music is my life, my scars, my dreams—and if you connect with it, you’re already part of my story. Keep believing in your hustle, keep chasing your light, and never let anyone tell you it’s impossible. We’re building this together—HU$$LE GANG for life.

In the thriving soundscape of Nigeria’s music scene, few voices cut through with as much grit and grace as Timi Kei. Born Kei Ndutimi Inedouye in Bayelsa State and based in Port Harcourt, Timi Kei is more than a musician — he is a messenger. 







His music, an Afro-Urban fusion of Hip-Hop, Soul, Afrobeats, and Gospel, resonates with authenticity, weaving together the raw honesty of street experiences and the enduring hope of faith.



From Struggle to Sound



Timi Kei’s journey is one of transformation. Having risen from a past of addiction into a life renewed by grace, his artistry carries the weight of lived experience. His songs are not just verses and hooks; they are testimonies of redemption, resilience, and survival. Every bar echoes the struggle of real-life battles, while every chorus lifts with the unshakeable assurance of God’s love.









Accolades & Recognition



Timi Kei’s rise hasn’t gone unnoticed. His breakthrough project Soulsoup earned him a spot on Pulse.ng’s Top 10 Hip-Hop Albums of 2019, solidifying his reputation as one of Nigeria’s most compelling new voices. He has been featured on platforms like MTV Base Cypher (2020) and took the stage as 2nd Runner-Up at Airtel One Mic (2014) and 1st Runner-Up at Monster Verse (2020). Each milestone is proof of a craft sharpened by dedication and fueled by vision.







As The Chrd Mag once described him, he’s “a musical alchemist, a lyrical master, blending genres with the precision of a seasoned chef.” Native Mag echoes this, noting that he “raps like he’s walking on water.”



The Sound of a Storyteller



At his core, Timi Kei is a storyteller. His discography — spanning albums, EPs, and singles — carries listeners through deeply personal yet universally relatable journeys. Tracks pulse with Afro rhythms while maintaining the lyrical sharpness of Hip-Hop and the soaring soul of Gospel. It’s music that speaks to both the street and the sanctuary, bridging divides with honesty and hope.









The Brand & The Vision



Timi Kei’s artistry is anchored in a bold, vibrant brand. With his signature colors — white, black, and orange — he reflects purity, depth, and fire. His performances and visuals are not just entertainment but an experience of gratitude, faith, and upliftment.









Follow Timi Kei

articles.body:
In a rapidly evolving Nigerian music scene where Afrobeat dominates the global conversation, one artist is carving a lane that feels both revolutionary and deeply rooted in culture. Meet Rhapstar OTP — born Junior Kingsley Ebose, also known as Jhay Banks — a dynamic hip-hop and Afro-fusion artist whose name is quickly becoming synonymous with authenticity, innovation, and ambition.







Hailing from Uromi, Edo State, Rhapstar OTP brings a raw, unfiltered perspective to his craft. His music is a bold fusion of hip-hop grit, Afro-fusion melodies, and deeply introspective lyricism that reflects both his personal journey and the stories of his community. He is not just a musician but a cultural narrator, delivering art that resonates with listeners from the streets of Nigeria to audiences abroad.



A Breakthrough in the Making



2023 marked a defining year for Rhapstar OTP. His debut singles, “Future Message” and “I Miss You”, introduced him as an artist who isn’t afraid to explore vulnerability while maintaining a cutting-edge sound. The tracks showcased his ability to blend emotive storytelling with sharp production — a skill that has positioned him as a fresh voice in Nigeria’s hip-hop landscape.









Critics and fans alike have praised Rhapstar OTP’s unique sonic identity, describing his music as “unapologetically authentic” and “deeply resonant.” This rising momentum signals the arrival of an artist determined to leave a lasting mark on African music culture.



CEO, Visionary, and Movement Builder



Beyond his artistry, Rhapstar OTP is a creative entrepreneur. He is the founder and CEO of Only The People Involved Entertainment (OTPIE), an independent label and cultural movement dedicated to amplifying voices from underrepresented communities. The label’s name reflects his ethos: music is not just a product but a platform for unity, empowerment, and cultural pride.







His growing fanbase, affectionately known as “Only The People,” has been integral to his journey. Through social media, grassroots support, and streaming platforms, his audience has transformed his music from a personal pursuit into a movement that inspires young creatives and fans alike.



A Global Vision with Local Roots



While his music is deeply tied to his Edo State roots, Rhapstar OTP’s artistic vision is global. With Afro-fusion and hip-hop taking center stage internationally, he is focused on positioning himself as one of Africa’s leading genre-blenders. His ability to weave street narratives, motivational themes, and cross-cultural sounds sets him apart as a truly versatile artist.









As he works on expanding his catalog, Rhapstar OTP remains laser-focused on growth, creativity, and global influence. His ultimate goal is to create timeless music that speaks to the struggles and triumphs of his generation while inspiring those who come after him.

In an industry where sound and identity evolve daily, few emerging artists manage to strike a balance between raw authenticity and futuristic vision. TEEDASHI (born Abraham Yusuf, also known as Renji) is one of those rare voices. With a bold, cinematic sound that blends Afrobeats, trap, and alternative influences, TEEDASHI is carving out a lane that’s distinctly his own — one that reflects his Nigerian roots while speaking to a global generation.







Born in Gwarinpa, Abuja, and now based in Kaduna, TEEDASHI’s musical journey started in childhood, nurtured by his father’s love for legends like Akon, Lauryn Hill, and Michael Jackson. By his teenage years, he had discovered hip-hop through artists like Ice Prince and Olamide, sparking a passion for storytelling through music. By JSS3, he recorded his first local hit — a defining moment that ignited his relentless pursuit of artistry.




“Music has always been my voice,” he says. “It’s how I tell my story, how I connect with people who feel unseen. Every track I make is a reflection of that connection.”




A Sound That Pushes Boundaries



TEEDASHI’s music is as versatile as it is intentional. He seamlessly switches between singing and rapping, creating songs that are both deeply emotional and sonically adventurous. His production choices — often leaning toward Afro-fusion, Afro-trap, and melodic, cinematic beats — reflect a futuristic vision for Afrobeats. Influenced by Yung6ix, Dice Ailes, and GMK, TEEDASHI’s sound isn’t bound by trends; it’s a bold exploration of culture, identity, and ambition.









His lyrics explore themes like self-discovery, rebellion, love, and the hustle — themes that resonate deeply with his growing audience of young creatives, students, and trendsetters in Nigeria, Ghana, South Africa, and beyond.



Nigeria to the World



TEEDASHI is more than just a musician; he’s a movement. His brand and artistry represent a new generation of African talent unafraid to blend cultural heritage with global soundscapes. With music distributed through UnitedMasters and a clear vision for growth, TEEDASHI is positioning himself as a cultural force ready for international stages.









What’s Next for TEEDASHI



With unreleased singles in the pipeline, collaborations on the horizon, and plans for immersive visuals and performances, TEEDASHI is gearing up to make his mark in 2025 and beyond. His focus is clear: build a brand that extends beyond music — into fashion, visuals, and storytelling — while using his platform to inspire and connect with his fans.



“Afrobeats is global now, but there’s still so much room to innovate,” TEEDASHI explains. “I want to bring my own twist — something that makes people feel proud of where we come from but also excited about where we’re going.”



For TEEDASHI, the mission is simple:




“I want people to hear my music and feel powerful, emotional, and part of something bigger. My sound is for the culture, but it’s also for the world.”

Nigerian rap talent and RADARCharts’ official ambassador, TELMAN, has officially released his brand-new single “IF NOT GOD”, now available on all major streaming platforms.







Written during his final university exams, the song is rooted in TELMAN’s personal journey of resilience, near-death experiences, and unwavering gratitude. Over hard-hitting drill percussion and a haunting flute line, TELMAN delivers a gripping testimony of faith and survival, declaring with conviction:



“IF NOT FOR GOD / WHO KNOWS WHAT MY LIFE WOULD BE.”



“IF NOT GOD” stands out for its unique balance of grit and grace — a track that is danceable yet reflective, spiritual yet raw, bridging gospel and drill in a way that speaks to both the streets and the spirit. TELMAN’s storytelling and flow bring authenticity, while his message of thanksgiving connects universally.









As RADARCharts’ ambassador and RADARMan, TELMAN continues to represent the brand’s mission of spotlighting talent with depth, vision, and impact. 



With this release, TELMAN offers more than just music — he delivers a reminder to count blessings over losses and to hold onto faith through adversity.




Stream “IF NOT GOD”

In the ever-evolving landscape of the UK music scene, rising Afro-fusion sensation TRENCHVIBE is poised to make a significant impact with the release of their highly anticipated EP, “Midnight in London.”







This bold new project is a masterful fusion of UK Drill, Hip-Hop, Afrobeat, and Dancehall, creating a soundscape that is as vibrant and multifaceted as the city that inspired it.



A Sonic Journey Through London’s After-Hours

Emerging from Abuja’s thriving cultural scene, Dirichi Mark Eche-Ejikeme, widely known as Deerichi, is a multi-dimensional artist reshaping the Nigerian creative landscape. 







A rapper, singer, sound engineer, model, and law student from Anambra State, Deerichi blends music, fashion, and culture into a fearless artistic identity that resonates beyond borders.



Crafting the Sound of GBEDU



Deerichi’s latest single, “GBEDU,” has quickly become a vibrant anthem of joy and movement. Produced by Adie, the track pulses with a unique rhythm that feels both experimental and universal.









Sharing insight into his process, Deerichi reflects:




“When I was creating GBEDU, my only mission was to make something that gets people moving no matter where they’re from. The beat was produced by Adie, who told me it was the most unique beat he has ever made and I knew right away it had that magic. I wanted the rhythm to feel like pure energy, the kind that pulls you to the dancefloor before you even realize it. The process was all about capturing that summer feeling—late nights with friends, laughter, and moments where nothing else matters but the music. I kept the lyrics light and fun, letting the beat lead the way. For me, GBEDU is more than just a song—it’s a celebration of joy, connection, and the power of music to unite people across cultures.”




With this track, Deerichi reaffirms his place as one of Abuja’s most exciting new voices, capable of creating music that is both deeply personal and universally relatable.



From At Midnight to Now



Deerichi first gained recognition with his debut EP, At Midnight (September 2023), which peaked at #16 on Nigeria’s Top Alternative Albums Chart and crossed 30,000 streams—an impressive feat for an independent release. 









The project showcased his ability to fuse Afro Fusion, Afro Swing, Rap, and Experimental sounds, while establishing him as a boundary-pushing creative unafraid to explore new sonic landscapes.



Beyond the Music – A Style Visionary



Deerichi’s artistry extends seamlessly into fashion, where he has modeled for brands like MBARI CLUB, embodying a distinctive style that merges African cultural depth with global runway influence. His ability to balance music and fashion creates a holistic brand identity that sets him apart as both an artist and tastemaker.



The Rising Wave



On the Abuja scene, Deerichi has earned a reputation as one of the hardest rappers, praised for his raw energy and originality. At the same time, his versatility as a singer, engineer, and model underscores a commitment to creative excellence across disciplines.




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by DEE💲 (@deerichi)




With GBEDU capturing new audiences and his artistic footprint expanding, Deerichi is quickly emerging as part of the next wave of Nigerian creatives shaping the future of music, culture, and style.

In a world where authenticity is often overshadowed by fleeting trends, Sativa Boy emerges with Grime Vs Love, a bold and emotionally charged project that captures the raw essence of life, love, trust, betrayal, and socio-economic realities. 







The Portharcourt-born artist delivers an unapologetic body of work that cements his place as one of the most authentic and dynamic voices in the Nigerian music scene.



A Blend of Grit and Soul



From the very first track, Grime Vs Love pulls listeners into an immersive experience. Sativa Boy’s signature gritty punchlines collide with smooth, soulful flows, creating a soundscape that feels both urgent and timeless. 









Every lyric drips with intention, and every beat seems carefully chosen to match the project’s emotional weight. Fans of his earlier work will recognize his unmistakable vocal tone and sharp storytelling, while new listeners will be captivated by the vulnerability and honesty woven throughout the tape.



Themes That Hit Home



The heart of Grime Vs Love lies in its relatable themes. Sativa Boy navigates the delicate balance between ambition and affection, hope and hardship, love and loss. He paints vivid pictures of the hustle, the heartbreak, and the resilience required to survive in an unforgiving world. Whether it’s the reflective moments that make you pause or the hard-hitting verses that ignite a fire, this project is designed to resonate deeply.







A No-Skip Experience



What makes Grime Vs Love stand out is its seamless listening journey. From the intro’s emotional pull to the closing track’s lingering impact, there are no fillers here. Each song feels like a crucial chapter in a larger story — one that invites you to not just listen but feel every word and note.









About Sativa Boy



Hailing from Portharcourt, Nigeria, Sativa Boy is a versatile artist who fuses Alte and Afrobeats with unmatched authenticity. With a growing discography available on major digital streaming platforms, he’s steadily building a loyal fan base through both solo projects and underground collaborations. His ability to connect with audiences — blending cultural depth with modern sounds — is a testament to his artistry and dedication to the craft.




Stream ‘Grime vs Love’

On this episode, we’re excited to chat with MOELOGO, an original talent bringing his unique sound called ‘Afro Healing’. You won’t want to miss it! Be sure to check out his track “SORRY YOU COULDN’T LOVE ME” in the meantime to get a taste of his incredible style. We can’t wait for you to hear this one!







WHERE HE COMES FROM



From Lagos to London, your journey spans continents and cultures. What are some of your earliest memories tied to music, and how did your Nigerian roots shape your sound?




Some of my earliest memories of music are from Lagos, church choirs, street sounds, family parties with Fuji and Highlife blaring through the speakers. Yoruba music, especially, was always in the air. When I moved to London, I carried those sounds with me. My roots gave me rhythm, soul, and storytelling. They’re the reason why no matter how far I go, the spirit of Naija is in everything I create




You’ve often been described as “a healer” through music. What moment in your early career made you realize music could be more than entertainment—it could be medicine?




When I dropped Ireti, I got messages from people telling me how songs like “Penkele” and others helped them through depression, heartbreak, and even loss. That shook me. I realised then – it’s deeper than vibes. Music can hold people up when they feel like falling. That’s when I knew I wasn’t just an artist – I was a vessel.








You’ve written for some of the biggest names in music—Tiwa Savage, Adekunle Gold, Kelly Rowland, and more. What does your writing process look like when creating for others versus for yourself?




Writing for others is like tailoring – you’re stitching their truth with your fabric. I tap into their emotions, their vision, and what they want to say. When I write for myself, it’s more raw, sometimes even spiritual. There’s less filter. I let my ancestors, pain, joy, and faith speak freely.




Emotion seems to be your true language. Who or what taught you to be so in tune with feeling, and how do you channel that into your music?




Life. I’ve felt pain that forced me to listen to silence. I’ve loved deeply, lost people, and prayed my way out of dark places. Growing up in two cultures taught me sensitivity – to people, to energy. When I sing, I don’t just want to sound good- I want you to feel seen. That’s where the healing begins. 




You’ve been nominated and awarded by respected platforms like the Headies and MOBOs. How do these accolades connect with your personal definition of success?




 I appreciate them, for real- they’re recognition from the world. But success to me is impact. If one person listens to a song and decides not to give up, that’s a bigger win. Awards come and go, but the lives you touch? That stays.








Collaboration has been a huge part of your journey. What’s one unforgettable studio experience that reminded you of the power of creative connection?




One session with Adekunle Gold still gives me chills. We weren’t even trying to make a hit- we were just speaking truth and vibing. The synergy, the laughter, the depth… it reminded me that when the energy is right, music writes itself. It’s a spiritual exchange, not just a business move.




Navigating the UK music industry as a Nigerian artist must’ve had its highs and challenges. How has this dual identity shaped you musically and personally?




It made me a bridge. I’ve learned to stand strong in my identity while navigating a system that didn’t always understand it. Being Nigerian in the UK taught me resilience, and being in the UK made me understand versatility. I’ve become more fearless and more intentional because of that balance.










WHERE HE’S GOING TO



“Music as medicine” is a powerful mission. How do you stay spiritually and emotionally grounded while creating healing sounds for others?




I protect my peace. I pray, I journal, I take time off when I need to. I’m constantly checking in with myself. Because to heal others, I have to first stay aligned. I don’t rush music. I let it come through me when the time is right.










You’ve grown from singer-songwriter to sonic therapist. What’s next for you—more music, mentorship, or something beyond the music itself?




All of the above. Music will always be my core, but I want to mentor young creatives, build safe spaces for artists to heal and express. I’m even exploring sound therapy and Yoruba spiritual teachings. The goal is wholeness, not just hits.




Are there any personal stories or untouched themes you’re eager to explore in your upcoming projects?




Definitely. My next body of work will dive deeper into ancestral memory, healing generational wounds, and the power of vulnerability – especially for men. There’s so much we bottle up. I want to break those walls gently, with melody.








With over 120 million streams and a truly global fanbase, how do you plan to deepen that connection in this next chapt

I protect my peace. I pray, I journal, I take time off when I need to. I’m constantly checking in with myself. Because to heal others, I have to first stay aligned. I don’t rush music. I let it come through me when the time is right.

You’ve grown from singer-songwriter to sonic therapist. What’s next for you—more music, mentorship, or something beyond the music itself?

All of the above. Music will always be my core, but I want to mentor young creatives, build safe spaces for artists to heal and express. I’m even exploring sound therapy and Yoruba spiritual teachings. The goal is wholeness, not just hits.

Are there any personal stories or untouched themes you’re eager to explore in your upcoming projects?

Definitely. My next body of work will dive deeper into ancestral memory, healing generational wounds, and the power of vulnerability – especially for men. There’s so much we bottle up. I want to break those walls gently, with melody.

With over 120 million streams and a truly global fanbase, how do you plan to deepen that connection in this next chapter of your journey?

By being even more intentional. I’m sharing more of my story visually, through documentaries, live shows with cultural elements, and deeper engagement on platforms like TikTok and IG. I want people to not just hear me but understand my essence.

What role does Yoruba culture still play in your sound today, especially as you push global boundaries?

It’s the heartbeat. The proverbs, the drums, the chants, the spirituality- it’s all Yoruba. Even when I sing in English, the cadence is Yoruba. I carry my heritage like a crown. It’s not just inspiration; it’s identity.

If you could collaborate with any artist—dead or alive—for a soul-stirring record, who would it be and why?

Fela. No question. His boldness, his message, the way he used music to shake systems- that’s power. A record with him would’ve been revolutionary. It still inspires me to use my voice for more than entertainment.

 What message do you want every listener to take from your music in 2025 and beyond?

That you are not alone. That your pain has purpose. That healing is possible. My music is your mirror, your medicine, your reminder that even in your brokenness, you are whole.

Saint Petersburg’s own Ben Stunner has officially raised the bar with the release of his highly anticipated project, Legacy of Benjamin. Known for his razor-sharp lyricism and genre-defining artistry, the Russian-born rapper once again proves why he’s a force in the contemporary hip-hop scene.







Blending the raw grit of classic hip-hop with cutting-edge production, Legacy of Benjamin is a sonic journey that captures both the urgency of the present and the timelessness of true storytelling. Each track carries Stunner’s signature energy — hypnotic beats layered beneath clever wordplay, thought-provoking themes, and an undeniable emotional depth.



A Reflection of Life, Culture, and LegacyBen Stunner has long been celebrated for his ability to connect with listeners on a personal level, and this project is no exception. Drawing from his experiences in Saint Petersburg’s vibrant streets and the challenges of navigating a rapidly evolving industry, Legacy of Benjamin dives into themes of perseverance, ambition, and self-identity. From hard-hitting anthems that exude confidence to introspective cuts that pull back the curtain on his personal journey, the album feels both intimate and universal.







The Craft Behind the SoundBehind the scenes, Stunner approached Legacy of Benjamin with meticulous precision. The beats are diverse — some dripping with the heavy bass and boom-bap nostalgia of hip-hop’s golden era, others infused with modern trap influences and melodic layers. His lyrical delivery remains sharp and versatile, shifting effortlessly between rapid-fire flows and deliberate, poetic pacing.









Speaking on his process, Ben Stunner describes the project as more than music:




“This is about immortalizing my truth. Legacy of Benjamin is not just an album — it’s a statement of who I am, where I’ve been, and where I’m going.”




Solidifying a Global Hip-Hop PresenceWhat makes Ben Stunner stand out is his ability to transcend language and location. While rooted in Russian culture, his music speaks to a global audience — a testament to hip-hop’s power as a universal language. With Legacy of Benjamin, Stunner cements his position as an artist who’s not only shaping the sound of Russian hip-hop but also contributing to the genre’s global narrative.




Stream LEGACY OF BENJAMIN

In the vibrant landscape of contemporary music, Pearl emerges as a formidable force—a guitarist, producer, and sonic architect whose innovative approach transcends traditional genre confines. 







With over a decade of experience in live instrumentation, she masterfully intertwines the organic warmth of her guitar with the expansive textures of electronic soundscapes, crafting a unique auditory experience that resonates deeply with listeners.



An Eclectic Influence



Pearl’s musical style is a rich tapestry woven from diverse influences. Drawing inspiration from the narrative depth of Country music, the electrifying energy of EDM, the entrancing grooves of House, and the emotional resonance of R&B, her sound is both evocative and atmospheric. This distinctive fusion results in a signature style that not only captivates but also invites listeners to embark on an emotional journey.




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Pearl (@pearl_rocker)




Breaking Barriers in Music Production



In an industry where female producers remain underrepresented, Pearl stands out as a beacon of innovation and resilience. Her fearless approach to music production challenges conventional norms, seamlessly merging genres that may seem disparate at first glance. With each composition, she not only creates music but also imbues it with a fresh perspective—one that celebrates boldness and encourages experimentation.



Anticipation for Her Debut EP



As she channels her creativity into her highly anticipated debut EP, set to release later this year, Pearl promises a collection of work that is profoundly personal and sonically rich. This project aims to encapsulate the emotional essence for which she is known while venturing into new artistic territories. Each track is designed to forge connections, inspire reflection, and leave an indelible mark on the listener’s heart.







Fostering Community Through Music



Beyond her studio endeavors, Pearl is the visionary behind the Pearl Acoustic Sessions—a curated live event series that nurtures a community of music enthusiasts. These intimate gatherings strip music back to its core, fostering an environment where sound and emotion converge without pretense. Such spaces allow for genuine connection, encouraging attendees to experience music in a profoundly personal way.



The Essence of Her Artistry



Whether commanding the stage with her guitar, meticulously sculpting sound in the studio, or creating environments for authentic musical discourse, Pearl remains steadfast in her mission: to produce music that resonates on a deep emotional level. Her artistry transcends mere auditory pleasure; it evokes feelings, sparks conversations, and invites listeners to explore the depths of their own emotions.







As the release of her debut EP approaches and her influence within the music community continues to expand, Pearl is carving out a space where genre boundaries dissolve, emotions flow freely, and creativity flourishes without limitations. In a world that often seeks to categorize, Pearl’s work stands as a testament to the beauty of musical exploration and the power of heartfelt expression.



Stay tuned for the unfolding of Pearl’s artistic journey—an odyssey that promises to be as inspiring as it is transformative.
