In 2025’s vibrant music landscape, the fusion of car culture and sonic innovation has become a growing trend, with tracks like Escaladizzy paving the way. Now, Afro-Drill trailblazer EESKAY takes the wheel with his latest release, Lamb Truck—a track that doesn’t just follow the movement but redefines it.







Rather than chasing formulas, EESKAY crafts a bold narrative, using the “Lamb Truck” as a metaphor for ambition, resilience, and the relentless pursuit of greatness. It’s more than an automotive nod—it’s a declaration of motion, movement, and momentum.









From the first chest-rattling 808 to the last echoing bar, Lamb Truck hits like a victory lap. EESKAY’s gritty yet melodic delivery blends seamlessly with the sleek, hard-hitting production of Wana Sn and Tubase, creating a soundscape as exhilarating as a V12 engine tearing through city streets. The result? A track engineered for summer domination—fit for festival main stages, high-energy road trips, and packed dance floors.




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by EESKAY DEM (@disrespectthe_gram)





“This isn’t just music; this is motion,” EESKAY declares. “When you hear it, you’re in the driver’s seat. You feel the power, the hunger to win.”




Already climbing playlists and sparking conversation across social media, early listeners have crowned Lamb Truck as a frontrunner for “Song of Summer 2025.” Its infectious hook and undeniable drive capture the spirit of Afro-Drill at its most ambitious—raw, triumphant, and unshakably confident.




Listen to Lamb Truck




With Lamb Truck, EESKAY doesn’t just release a single—he sets a pace for the season. This is the sound of victory in motion, an anthem that invites fans to not just listen, but ride along in the fast lane of Afro-Drill’s next chapter.

Afro-fusion artist Jayslite continues to captivate audiences with “Hero”, the second track off his compelling Pack of Life single pack. 







Released under Arabthings Records, “Hero” delivers a deeply personal, soulful message dedicated to the quiet warriors of life — the people whose strength, love, and faith often go unnoticed.



A Song Beyond Sound – The Message Behind “Hero”



In “Hero”, Jayslite translates his own reflections on faith, time, and purpose into a timeless ballad. The track serves as an ode to those who persevere without fanfare, highlighting the sacrifices made in silence. His intention was to speak to anyone who has ever felt unseen yet continues to give, love, and show up for others.









As Jayslite explains, “This is my tribute to the silent fighters — the ones holding up the world in the background. You may not always get the applause, but you are someone’s hero.”



Critical Acclaim – A Supporter’s Review



Music producer and curator Claudemir Tavares describes “Hero” as a track that “carries a spiritual and emotional depth that goes beyond the music itself.” He praised Jayslite’s ability to “translate connections between time, faith, purpose, and the Creator”, calling it a form of “artistic and human commitment that deserves to be valued.”









Tavares further commended the well-balanced mix and master, the soft harmonic base that gives the voice space to deliver truth and intensity, and Jayslite’s full and emotive vocal performance.



The Craft – Production and Sound



“Hero” is an elegant blend of Afro-fusion and soul, built on a warm, harmonic foundation that allows Jayslite’s voice to take center stage. The arrangement is intentionally uncluttered, giving each lyric room to breathe while subtle instrumentation keeps the track engaging from start to finish.







While the song’s minimalism is one of its strengths, Tavares suggests that future projects could explore “more subtle instrumental layers or dynamic variations” to further enhance the sensory experience — a testament to the potential he sees in Jayslite’s evolving artistry.



The Pack of Life Journey



Pack of Life is not just a music release — it’s a statement of purpose. Comprising two tracks, “Duro” and “Hero”, the single pack showcases Jayslite’s dual approach to storytelling: one rooted in movement and perseverance (Duro) and the other in quiet strength and devotion (Hero). Together, they create a sonic reflection of life’s resilience and hope.




Stream ‘Pack of Life’

Emerging from the gritty yet culturally rich streets of Port Harcourt, Nigeria, AC$ENT is not just another voice in the growing world of Afro-influenced hip-hop — he’s a movement in the making. 







Blending Afrotrap, grime, and raw street energy, AC$ENT is carving out a distinct sound that captures the reality of his environment while pushing the boundaries of Nigeria’s underground music scene.



ROOTED IN THE STREETS



With his roots deeply embedded in the heartbeat of Port Harcourt, AC$ENT’s music is a reflection of lived experience. His verses are steeped in the slang, hustle, and chaos of his environment — delivered in a mix of English, pidgin, and native tongue that feels both intimate and universal. His ability to infuse street storytelling with infectious rhythm is turning heads and building a cult-like fanbase that resonates with his authenticity.









SONIC IDENTITY: GRIME MEETS NAIJA TRAP



What sets AC$ENT apart is his genre-fluid approach. His soundscape is a dynamic collision of Afrotrap, grime, Afrostatic, and fusion, with hard-hitting beats and emotionally charged delivery. Inspired by icons like Skepta, Lancey Foux, and Wizkid, he’s unafraid to experiment — creating music that’s honest, instinctive, and unfiltered. His artistry thrives on freestyle creation, allowing emotions to guide the flow rather than formula.



NEW RELEASE: WEREY – CHAOS IN VERSE



His latest single, WEREY, is a street anthem wrapped in rhythm and realism. A vivid portrayal of life’s madness and the characters that come with it, WEREY is both a warning and a mantra — urging listeners to stay sharp and dodge negative energy. The record is built on hypnotic beats and raw vocal performance, capturing the essence of his fast-paced city life and the unpredictability it brings.




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by AC$ENT (@_capalotszn)





“WEREY is the kind of track that doesn’t just get played — it gets felt.”




A visual for the track is on the way, promising a gritty, cinematic interpretation of the song’s message — further cementing AC$ENT’s vision as both a storyteller and cultural observer.



WHAT’S NEXT?



With more music dropping this summer, AC$ENT isn’t slowing down. He’s setting his sights on a larger audience while staying rooted in his identity. His focus remains on consistency, growth, and impact — building a legacy that represents Port Harcourt’s new wave of hip-hop rebels. He’s not just making music; he’s documenting a lifestyle.







As AC$ENT continues to rise, he represents more than just a genre — he represents a generation unafraid to speak their truth, on their own terms.

Set for release on August 8th, The Glance is the highly anticipated sonic offering from Nigerian genre-blending artist Ánesi. Known for her bold fusion of African acapella, gospel, alté, Afrobeats, R&B, and experimental soul, Ánesi presents The Glance as a meditative, forward-facing project — one that sees music as not only expression but medicine.







Each track is crafted to evoke stillness, spiritual depth, and personal revelation. This is a project for listeners who crave meaning in music — who seek both rhythm and restoration.



Ánesi: Where Tradition Meets Technology



Born Comfort Ogbonnaya, Ánesi began her journey in music at the age of five. By 12, she had released her debut gospel album The Genesis, selling over 1,000 copies independently and earning her first million. She later trained at ABBA Music School, where she mastered vocal performance and music theory, before founding AX: Acapella Xpression, an ensemble rooted in harmonic African traditions.







Her career took a digital turn in 2023, when she launched Trapiano (her first NFT), performed in the metaverse, and began crafting AI-assisted music. As a software engineer and data analyst, Ánesi brings a rare technical perspective into the artistry of sound — blurring the lines between the spiritual and the synthetic.



A Standout Track: Stargaze



        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Ánesi (@anesi_empire)
//www.instagram.com/embed.js



The EP’s highlight, “Stargaze,” is a dreamy, immersive track that blends poetic introspection with celestial production. It’s a moment of escape — and a call to look higher, dream deeper, and trust the unseen.








Presave ‘The GLANCE’

Rising R&B/alt-soul artist GMGBABY dives headfirst into emotional territory with his new single “What Are We”, now streaming on all platforms. 







The song captures one of the most vulnerable and relatable moments in modern relationships — that unspoken question hanging between two people when feelings deepen but definitions remain blurry.



The Sound of Emotional Bravery



GMGBABY continues to solidify his space in the alternative R&B soundscape with a moody, melodic track that blends his signature smooth vocal delivery with atmospheric production. “What Are We” isn’t just a song — it’s an internal dialogue externalized, a late-night text turned into melody, a quiet storm of longing and uncertainty.










“This song is about that moment where you’re brave enough to ask what’s really going on — when you care enough to risk it,” says GMGBABY. “I wanted to give voice to what so many of us feel but don’t say.”




Between Friendship and Forever



“What Are We” paints the emotional grey space between platonic connection and romantic commitment — the space where hopes hang, silence screams, and vulnerability can either birth love or heartbreak. With lyrical honesty and restrained confidence, GMGBABY manages to turn a personal question into a collective confession.




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by GRAY (@gmgbabyy)




Whether you’ve been on the asking or receiving end of “What are we?”, this track gives you a soundtrack for both the courage and the chaos.



Introducing GMGFM: A New Era Begins



The release of “What Are We” also marks the beginning of a new chapter. GMGBABY has teased that GMGFM is the working title of his forthcoming body of work — a project expected to expand his sonic universe and deliver even more intimate stories through soul-tinged soundscapes.



Stay tuned. The airwaves are only just starting to hear what GMGBABY has to say.



About GMGBABY



GMGBABY is an emerging voice in contemporary R&B and alternative soul, known for emotionally charged songwriting and immersive sonic textures. With a growing catalogue of genre-blending releases, his music merges vulnerability with vibe — offering listeners a raw, relatable experience with every track.




Stream “What Are We”

Lagos, Nigeria – July 30, 2025 — Rising Afro-fusion artist Mosa Temple has officially entered the spotlight with his gripping new single, “Love and Felony” — a provocative anthem that redefines the boundaries of Afrobeat with passion, tension, and soul.







Built on pulsating drums, haunting melodies, and razor-sharp lyricism, Love and Felony explores the duality of a love that feels both euphoric and dangerous. It’s a modern-day tale of desire and deception, laced with rich African grooves and contemporary sonic layers.










“This song is about the kind of love that consumes you,” says Mosa. “It’s beautiful, it’s toxic, and at times it feels criminal. But you stay… because it’s real.”




Produced with a bold sonic palette that blends Afrobeat, soul, and experimental percussion, Love and Felony immediately grips the listener. Mosa’s delivery is both vulnerable and commanding — his voice rising and falling with the emotional tide of the story. It’s a performance that doesn’t just entertain; it connects.



A STAR ON THE RISE



Mosa Temple has quickly become one of the most intriguing new voices in Nigeria’s fast-evolving music scene. Known for his ability to fuse lyrical storytelling with culturally grounded rhythms, his music reflects a new era of African creativity — one that’s emotionally intelligent, sonically daring, and globally resonant.




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by MOSA TEMPLE (@nonelikemosatemple)




With Love and Felony, Mosa proves he’s not just here to make hits — he’s here to leave a mark.



FOR FANS OF AUTHENTIC AFRO-FUSION



If you’re drawn to artists like Burna Boy, Tems, or Tay Iwar, Mosa Temple brings a refreshing yet familiar energy to your playlist. Love and Felony isn’t just a song — it’s an experience. The kind that lingers in your chest long after the beat drops.



As Mosa Temple prepares for more releases and performances in the coming months, Love and Felony sets a bold tone for what’s to come: an artist with purpose, passion, and presence.




Stream ‘LOVE & FELONY

Nigerian trap artist and streetwear mogul Obuduboi is stepping into a new emotional terrain with the release of his latest single, “YOU”, out today across all major streaming platforms. 







Known for his gritty storytelling and relentless hustle, the self-proclaimed Voice of Obudu trades bravado for vulnerability, offering fans a softer, more introspective chapter in his journey.



A Shift in Tone, A Statement of Growth



“YOU” is not just another love song—it’s a bold shift from Obuduboi’s usual hard-edged sound to something more melodic, intimate, and soulful. The track is built around reflective verses and heartfelt melodies, detailing how one person’s presence can bring peace to a life built on struggle and survival. It’s romantic, yes—but not idealized. It’s grounded in real-life chaos, late-night thoughts, and the healing power of emotional connection.










“This isn’t about fairy tales,” Obuduboi says. “It’s about finding calm in the storm—and the kind of love that doesn’t ask you to change, but meets you where you are.”




Produced with minimalist trap beats, lush chords, and an emotionally rich vocal delivery, “YOU” is the kind of song that reveals more with each listen. It’s tender without being weak, and honest without sounding rehearsed—showing that even the hardest hearts can have soft centers.



From Obudu to Onitsha to Everywhere



Obuduboi was born in Obudu, Cross River State, and raised in the commercial city of Onitsha, Anambra—two places that taught him to hustle early and dream bigger. That duality—grit and grace—has been the core of his brand from the beginning. As founder of the independent fashion label Husslecraft Luxury, he’s made a name for himself not just as a rapper, but as a multi-hyphenate entrepreneur with a clear vision and street-savvy aesthetic.







With past singles like “Halle” and two independent projects under his belt, Obuduboi has steadily built a cult following, earning respect as one of the most promising new voices from Nigeria’s underground trap movement. “YOU” adds a new layer to that voice—more melodic, more intentional, and deeply personal.



Final Thoughts: A Love Song for the Real Ones



In a music scene that often celebrates the surface, “YOU” goes deeper. It’s not just about romance—it’s about redemption, restoration, and recognizing the kind of love that doesn’t save you but strengthens you. Obuduboi might still be rising, but songs like “YOU” show he’s already found his voice.




Stream ‘YOU’

On July 25, 2025, Fav4 released his highly anticipated single “Tambourine”, a provocative Afrobeat record that explores sensuality and male confidence with an effortless touch. The song, produced by BigProm, is a hypnotic fusion of percussion-driven rhythm, vivid lyricism, and Fav4’s signature melodic style.









With “Tambourine,” Fav4 doesn’t just enter the Afrobeat scene — he commands it. The track leans into a late-night mood, offering listeners a sultry, immersive sound that feels both intimate and danceable. From the production’s smoky groove to Fav4’s smooth delivery, every element is crafted with intent.



Lyricism That Balances Playfulness and Passion



Sung in a blend of English and Igbo, “Tambourine” explores themes of physical desire and romantic tension through poetic metaphor. Lyrics like “Cabernet Sauvignon,” “gasoline,” and “tangerine” signal a bold, almost cinematic level of imagery — Fav4 doesn’t just sing about love, he paints it.



The standout line, “Tambourine, you go blow your trumpet – Paranranran,” is cheeky yet impactful, transforming flirtation into an infectious hook that lingers long after the beat fades. This kind of writing reflects an artist confident in his expression, rooted in cultural nuance yet wide open to global ears.



The Sound of a Star in Ascent



Fav4, born Onwusor Chukwuemeka Favour, is part of a new generation of Afrobeat artists redefining the genre’s sound and emotional palette. His past releases — including “Nwanyi Oma,” “Kill A Man,” and “Winnerman” — have established him as a smooth vocalist with an ear for melody and a gift for storytelling.







With over 50 unreleased songs and a debut EP on the horizon, “Tambourine” signals Fav4’s transition from underground buzz to serious contender. His vocal performance on the track is measured and magnetic, laying bare his range and refining his identity in a genre often dominated by larger-than-life personalities.



Cultural Roots, Global Intentions



While “Tambourine” is clearly crafted for a mainstream Afrobeat audience, it doesn’t shy away from Fav4’s Igbo heritage. The linguistic blend adds texture to the song, allowing it to resonate locally while standing tall in the global Afro-fusion space. His influences — from Fela Kuti to Wizkid, Burna Boy, and Chris Brown — are evident, but never overpowering.

Fav4’s appeal lies in his ability to feel familiar while offering something fresh. His voice is soft but grounded. His tone is warm yet commanding. His style is laid-back but intentional. All these layers come together to form a distinct sonic identity.



“Tambourine” may be the spark, but it’s clear Fav4 has much more fire in store.

Hailing from the culturally rich city of Ilorin and currently making waves between Ilorin and Lagos, Dapalmusic is an emerging force in the Afrobeat and Afropop scene. 







Born Mubarak Oluwapelumi Ayinde in 2003, Dapalmusic represents a new generation of Nigerian creatives—blending rhythm, emotion, and ambition to craft a sound that speaks to both the streets and the soul.



Early Life & Musical Roots



Raised in Ilorin, Dapalmusic’s musical journey began in his formative years, nurtured by a deep connection to storytelling, percussion, and the powerful influence of Nigerian pop culture. His passion for music evolved into a full-fledged mission during his time at Kwara State University, Malete, where he balanced academics with a growing reputation as a singer, songwriter, and producer.



Sound & Style



Dapalmusic’s sound is a unique fusion of Afrobeats and Afropop, with catchy melodies, vibrant rhythms, and emotionally charged lyrics that reflect real-life experiences. As a self-producing artist, he takes pride in crafting his records from scratch—writing, composing, and overseeing production to ensure every song reflects his signature sound and message.









Whether he’s serenading listeners with smooth romantic tunes or delivering streetwise anthems, Dapalmusic’s music is always rooted in authenticity and rhythm.



The Mission



More than just an artist, Dapalmusic sees himself as a messenger—using music to tell stories of resilience, youth empowerment, and love. For him, Afrobeat is not just a genre; it’s a movement, and he’s here to be part of its global evolution.









As he continues to grow his audience both locally and digitally, Dapalmusic is building a legacy grounded in consistency, sound innovation, and cultural pride.



What’s Next for Dapalmusic



With upcoming releases in the pipeline and plans to expand his reach across Lagos and beyond, Dapalmusic is focused on pushing his craft to new heights. Whether performing on stage, producing in his dorm studio, or writing verses that resonate with his generation, he remains committed to making timeless music.

Straight out of Port Harcourt and now shaping waves from Lagos, Tup Dugg is not your typical newcomer. He’s a street-rooted poet, a spiritual realist, and a rising star in Nigeria’s evolving hip-hop ecosystem. With a genre-defying blend of hip-hop, grime, and street soul, Tup Dugg brings a rare kind of authenticity—raw, reflective, and intensely focused.







In a scene increasingly dominated by flashy aesthetics and short-lived hype, Tup Dugg offers depth and direction, using his music as both a mirror and a map for the overlooked and the ambitious.



Musical Identity: Bars with Purpose



At the core of Tup Dugg’s artistry is intention. His lyrics are sharp, deliberate, and often deeply personal. Influenced by J. Cole, Kendrick Lamar, and OdumoduBlvck, Tup Dugg’s sound captures the hunger of the streets while echoing spiritual themes of elevation, purpose, and inner peace.









Whether over gritty grime-inflected beats or Afro-fusion instrumentals, he delivers messages that resonate with a generation trying to rise above noise, pressure, and poverty. His tone is firm, his stories are real, and his message is clear: Stay locked in or fall off.



Latest Single: “Locked In”



Released under the management of Owl Universal, Tup Dugg’s latest single “Locked In” is more than just a song—it’s a statement. Set over atmospheric production and hypnotic drum patterns, the track showcases his lyrical precision and unwavering focus.



“Locked In” paints the portrait of a man tunnel-visioned on self-growth, free from distractions, and unapologetically dedicated to his craft. It reflects his mental state as an artist—disciplined, spiritual, and unshaken by the noise of the outside world.










“I’m not just rapping, I’m documenting my journey—and hopefully lighting someone else’s path,” he shared during a recent press briefing.




The Vision: Beyond the Music



Tup Dugg’s movement goes beyond beats and bars. Backed by Owl Universal Management, his long-term vision includes inspiring youth across Africa’s inner cities and global diaspora through creative leadership and lifestyle alignment. His brand represents resilience, discipline, and elevation—three qualities often overlooked in today’s mainstream narrative.









Through music, visuals, and community engagement, Tup Dugg is building a platform where stories from the streets aren’t just heard—they’re understood, celebrated, and transformed into legacies.



Why Tup Dugg is Next



In an era where style often overshadows substance, Tup Dugg is a reminder of hip-hop’s original function: storytelling, resistance, and revelation. With each verse, he breaks the silence around real struggles and speaks life into the dreams of those “locked in” on their goals.



As Nigeria continues to dominate the global music map, artists like Tup Dugg ensure that rap, in its purest form, remains part of that story.

Nigerian rapper Snowfella has built a reputation for crafting music that blends lyrical sharpness with emotional depth. Known for his authenticity and storytelling, he stands apart from the hype-driven noise of today’s rap scene. 







With his latest single Judas Purse, Snowfella takes a darker, more introspective route — pushing his pen into real-life betrayals, survival instincts, and the sacredness of loyalty.



The Meaning Behind Judas Purse



The title Judas Purse is a layered metaphor referencing the biblical Judas who betrayed Jesus for silver. For Snowfella, the “purse” represents what people gain when they sell you out. But this isn’t just a song about pain. It’s also a salute to the real ones: the friends who stood firm, the brothers who didn’t fold. It’s both a warning and a tribute — a sonic letter to the fake and the faithful.



“Took 10 shots for my brother man.



Dem shots shall not befall my brother man.”



These lyrics capture the raw sentiment behind the record — the price of loyalty and the scars left by betrayal.









The Sound: Grit, Ghosts, and Gospel Undertones



Produced by Mhyno (Miracle Chimdindu Njoku), the beat is dark, cinematic, and atmospheric. The track opens with eerie melodies that immediately set the tone — haunted, cautious, but focused. Gritty drums lay the foundation while Snowfella alternates between rap cadences and ghost-like melodic backing vocals, almost like a conversation between his pain and his purpose.



The production pulls influences from J. Cole, Kendrick Lamar, and $NOT, yet remains distinctly Snowfella — personal, Nigerian, unapologetic. There’s tension in the flow, weight in the voice, and subtle spirituality in the undertones.







Not Just Bars — A Story Unfolds



Judas Purse doesn’t chase commercial formulas. It isn’t designed for clubs or trends. It’s the kind of track you listen to alone — in your car at night, or with headphones while reflecting on who’s really in your circle.



Snowfella’s storytelling cuts deep, unpacking not just betrayal but the emotional armor one builds after being hurt. The lines “When I pull up in a white CLA, my bro gon pull up in a black Lambo” show that beyond the pain, there’s still ambition, unity, and a future worth fighting for — together.




Presave ‘Judas Purse’

In a time when African music is storming global charts with soulful rhythms and deeply rooted narratives, Frequencie and Terry Apala have delivered a track that transcends just sound—it’s a movement. Their collaborative special version of “Sapa” isn’t just a remix; it’s a reimagined anthem for the everyday hustler, wrapped in Afrofusion, Dancehall, and Amapiano textures. Originally released last year, this song is now returning to the spotlight—and for good reason: the world needs to hear it.









“Sapa”, the Nigerian slang for utter financial lack, becomes more than a meme in this track—it becomes a lived reality, transformed into music that empowers instead of depresses. With Frequencie’s signature Afro-rock influence and Terry Apala’s gritty Apala-Hip-Hop vocals, the remix is a genre-bending masterclass. Their synergy reflects a fusion of two distinct worlds: Frequencie’s activist-minded storytelling and Apala’s street-rooted grit. What you get is a sound that resonates across Lagos streets, diaspora clubs, and international playlists alike.



A Soundtrack for Struggle, Strength, and Survival



The magic of Sapa (Special) lies not just in its production but in its purpose. As inflation grips economies, unemployment spikes, and mental health challenges deepen, this song doesn’t shy away from the truth. Instead, it leans into it—boldly voicing what many feel but can’t express.







Frequencie, long known as Ilorin’s creative powerhouse and a torchbearer for grassroots musicianship, builds a sonic stage where the pain of poverty becomes a battle cry for dignity. With dancehall bounce, amapiano percussion, and raw Afro-fusion energy, Sapa (Special) becomes both cathartic and irresistible. It’s the kind of record that gets the body moving while speaking to the soul.







Terry Apala brings the perfect edge to the track—his unmistakable tone and Yoruba-laced delivery remind listeners of the importance of cultural continuity in modern Afro sounds. Together, they elevate “Sapa” from a street slang into an international narrative.



Why This Song Cannot Be Missed



In the chaos of streaming algorithms and fast-content culture, some songs cut through not just because they’re sonically rich, but because they matter. Sapa (Special) is one of those songs. As Africa’s creative renaissance gains global attention—from Burna Boy’s Grammy stages to Tems’ soul-bearing anthems—tracks like this one hold the emotional and cultural charge that push the movement forward.







With a renewed rollout strategy, updated visuals, targeted DSP pushes, and fresh grassroots campaigns led by Frequencie’s Abuja-based FREQIE SPACE, this remix is being positioned for the recognition it was always destined to achieve. It’s not a comeback. It’s a takeover.



The Mission: Turn a Moment into a Movement



Frequencie and Terry Apala aren’t just collaborators—they’re cultural conduits. By breathing new life into Sapa, they’re building a bridge between sonic innovation and social truth. The goal is clear: to give the world a sound that is undeniably African, universally relatable, and spiritually charged.




STREAM ‘SAPA’

Emerging Nigerian talent Yng Ryme is poised to expand his sonic universe with the release of his latest single, SPICE, arriving on July 31st. 







Known for his hypnotic blend of Afrobeat, riddim culture, and ambient soundscapes, Yng Ryme isn’t chasing the mainstream — he’s crafting his own lane. And with SPICE, he’s delivering a track that doesn’t just sound good — it feels good.



A New Chapter in the Afro Haze Movement



Since his debut in 2024 with the standout track Joromi, Chidera Chimamkpa Smart, better known as Yng Ryme, has shown a relentless dedication to innovation. From his textured melodies to his minimalist storytelling, he brings something undeniably fresh to the Afrobeat conversation. His recent collaborative project Mendez & Boss with rapper Snow Fella proved that he isn’t afraid to experiment — and now with SPICE, he’s doubling down on his signature style: Afro Haze.



Afro Haze, a genre coined by Ryme himself, blends Afro-fusion’s smooth rhythmic sensibilities with the soulful stillness of ambient Caribbean riddims. It’s not music for the loudest room — it’s for the most intimate vibe.



What SPICE Feels Like



SPICE is not your typical Afrobeat anthem. It doesn’t ask for your attention with heavy drops or punchy lyrics. Instead, it seduces — slowly. Built on warm basslines, soft percussive patterns, and airy vocal textures, the song moves like a breeze at midnight. The rhythm doesn’t demand movement; it invites it — slow, intentional, and confident.







“This one isn’t about telling a story in words,” says Yng Ryme. “It’s about mood, air, rhythm. It’s that chemistry between the beat and the body — no pressure, no overthinking.”



There’s no traditional verse-chorus formula here. The song is structured like a wave — ebbing, flowing, building tension, then releasing it. The repetition becomes hypnotic. The vocals drift between chant, whisper, and soulful hums, enhancing the trance-like feel.



Who Is SPICE For?



This is a track for the slow movers and late-night lovers — for the ones who care more about atmosphere than algorithms. If you gravitate toward Wizkid’s “True Love,” Burna Boy’s “Ye,” or Rema’s “Calm Down”, you’ll find SPICE right at home in your rotation.



No Trends. Just Vibes.



In a time when so many songs chase virality, Yng Ryme leans into vibe as identity. He’s not following trends — he’s setting a tone. And while SPICE may be soft in delivery, its impact is undeniable. It proves that Yng Ryme isn’t just making tracks — he’s building a soundscape, a feeling, and a movement.



“I want people to remember how it made them feel,” he says. “Not the words, not the hook. Just that temperature it left behind.”




PRESAVE ‘SPICE’

Tifah Runaah isn’t just a rapper — she’s a movement. Born Latifah Harunah on April 23rd in the heart of Abuja, Nigeria, Tifah represents a new era of bold, boundary-pushing African female voices unafraid to stand tall in the male-dominated world of hip hop.







From pen to mic, runway to stage, she weaves together a tapestry of talents grounded in raw ambition and lived experiences.



Her sound? Undeniably hers.



Her message? Undoubtedly real.



A Journey from Blogger to Bold Voice









Long before she ever dropped a bar on wax, Tifah was already making her mark in the culture. As a curious and passionate teenager, she launched her blog Latifahandherpenn, where she conducted sharp, soulful interviews with some of Nigeria’s top talents — L.A.X, Ycee, Vector, and others. Her gift for storytelling, empathy, and keen cultural insight helped shape her voice — not just as a writer, but as an artist in the making.



Her blog wasn’t just content. It was a classroom.



From Fashion Queen to Mic Fiend



In 2018, she launched her fashion label, NUVOGUE (SABALI) — an edgy, expressive brand that quickly caught the eyes of Nigeria’s street style elite. From Rahman Jago to Zlatan and DJ Consequence, Tifah styled some of the most influential tastemakers in the scene.







But behind the glam was a burning creative fire. Her deep relationships in the music industry and fashion world gave her the tools — and confidence — to finally step forward with her own voice. And when she did, she came out swinging.



A Sound That Transcends — Rooted in Hip Hop



Tifah Runaah doesn’t box herself in. She thrives in the fusion. While her core is Afro Hip Hop, she boldly experiments across sounds and cultures. Whether she’s dropping introspective lyrics over drill beats or Afro-infused rhythms, Tifah makes music that reflects the chaos, colors, and courage of chasing dreams as a young woman in modern Nigeria.




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by LATIFAH🥷🏽 (@tifah.runaah)




Her influences speak volumes:



2Pac. Meek Mill. Kendrick Lamar. Burna Boy. Young M.A. Kanye West.



Each has shaped her sonic universe — from lyrical depth to swagger, activism to art.



The Mission: Live. Learn. Create.



“My music is a product of my daily experience as a female dream chaser,” she says.







It’s more than a quote — it’s a manifesto. Tifah believes you must live to create, and every lyric, verse, and project she touches stems from real life: the struggles, the wins, the growth, the losses.



Why She Matters



In a world where female rappers are still fighting for space in Africa’s mainstream soundscape, Tifah Runaah is rewriting the narrative — unapologetically. She represents possibility. Not just for Abuja, not just for women, but for anyone daring to take the long way home in pursuit of greatness.

Lagos-based Afrobeat sensation Fav4 is back and ready to take listeners on a steamy ride with his forthcoming single, “Tambourine.” Slated for release on July 25, 2025, the track is already generating buzz across the Nigerian underground for its hypnotic groove, suggestive storytelling, and confident delivery.







Produced by BigProm, Tambourine is a bold expression of passion and male sensuality, driven by slow-burning percussion, sultry melodies, and Fav4’s unmistakable blend of English and Igbo lyricism. It’s not just a song—it’s an experience.



A Bedroom Anthem with an Afrobeat Twist



“Tambourine” isn’t afraid to get intimate. Fav4 explores romantic desire with vivid metaphors like “Cabernet Sauvignon,” “tangerine,” and “gasoline,” painting a picture that’s both seductive and playful.



With standout lines like



“Tambourine, you go blow your trumpet – Paranranran,”



The Official Artwork for ‘Tambourine’ by Fav4



Fav4 turns flirtation into fireworks, delivering a performance that’s equal parts confident and catchy.



It’s the kind of song made for candle-lit nights, slow dances, and speakers turned up just loud enough to feel the bass in your bones.



Rooted in Igbo Soul, Crafted for Global Stages



Fav4 (real name Onwusor Chukwuemeka Favour) is quickly rising through Nigeria’s vibrant Afrobeat scene with his signature sound: unique, soothing, and vibey. Influenced by icons like Wizkid, Fela, Burna Boy, and Chris Brown, he fuses rich Afro rhythms with pop sensibility and raw storytelling.



Based in Lagos but rooted in his Igbo heritage, Fav4 brings authenticity and soul to every track. With Tambourine, he’s not just dropping a hit—he’s creating a cultural moment.



Building Momentum: From Stage to Stream



Fav4’s performance history includes major platforms like Miss Tourism Nigeria, and his discography—featuring songs like “Kill A Man,” “Nwanyi Oma,” and “Winnerman”—has already proven his ability to move crowds and win hearts.



With over 50 unreleased tracks in the vault and his debut EP on the way, Fav4 is more than ready for the spotlight.




Presave ‘Tambourine’

Mamuzo Unveils “Madmoiselle” — A Multilingual Ode to Love, Loyalty, and Hustle



Mamuzo officially releases his highly anticipated single “Madmoiselle” today — and it’s every bit the soulful, rhythmic, and emotionally-layered anthem fans were waiting for. Blending lush Afrobeat percussion with alté-inspired melodies, the song explores love, loyalty, and the emotional weight of hustle in a rapidly changing world.







From the opening lyric, “Madmoiselle, on my radar, I no send, ah ju go fade ah,” Mamuzo invites listeners into a narrative that is both personal and universal. Sung in a seamless mix of Pidgin, Native tongue, “Madmoiselle” captures the complexities of romantic connection while navigating ambition and uncertainty.



A Soundtrack for Today’s Generation



“Madmoiselle” is more than just a vibe — it’s a reflection of the modern African youth experience. The production is subtle but infectious — with smooth drums, airy synths, and a hypnotic hook that lingers long after the first listen. Mamuzo delivers his vocals with clarity and control, striking a balance between melody and raw expression. It’s a record that’s relatable for anyone caught between soft feelings and hard realities.









Whether you’re in love, on the grind, or caught somewhere in between, “Madmoiselle” is the kind of track that finds its place in both emotional playlists and everyday moments.



What’s Next for Mamuzo?



With “Madmoiselle”, Mamuzo proves he’s more than a rising act — he’s an emerging voice for a new generation of Afro-fusion listeners. 




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Mamuzo Eni Diamond (@baddestmamuzo)




His ability to blend cultural languages and emotional nuance within a commercially appealing sound positions him for real growth in today’s global music landscape.




Stream Now

Today marks a defining moment for Eastsidealien, one of the fastest-rising stars in Nigeria’s underground hip-hop scene, as he officially drops his spiritually charged new single “Amarachukwu” featuring the soulful Choo and veteran lyricist Beepee D RapGod.







A beautiful collision of Afro-Adura, Highlife strings, and hard-hitting Igbo bars, Amarachukwu isn’t just a track—it’s a testimony.



ROOTED IN REALITY, LIFTED BY FAITH



Born and raised in Nsukka, Eastsidealien has always used his music to speak on struggle, street life, and survival. On Amarachukwu, he takes a more spiritual route, giving thanksgiving to God for the grace, growth, and grit that has shaped his journey.









From rapping in tight Nsukka corners to gaining national recognition, Eastsidealien’s rise is the stuff of divine orchestration—and this record is his way of saying “I see what You’re doing, Lord.”



CHOO & BEEPEE: THE PERFECT FEATURES



Choo delivers a smooth Afro-fusion performance that balances introspective lyrics with soul-healing melodies. Known for his genre-bending style, he paints sonic pictures that linger long after the beat fades.



Beepee D RapGod, aka The Igbotic Tupac, adds a legendary touch with his razor-sharp rhymes and deeply rooted Igbo flows. With over a decade in the game, Beepee brings weight, wisdom, and wild wordplay to the mic.



Together, these three artists create an unforgettable moment.



WHY “AMARACHUKWU” HITS DIFFERENT




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by REAL LIFE TRAP 👽 (@eastsidealien_)




Message: Uplifting, spiritual, and relatable to every dreamer on a grind.



Sound: A hybrid of Eastern highlife chords, drill bounce, and street gospel energy.



Vibe: For the streets, the church, and every soul in between.



Whether you’re hustling through life or having a quiet moment of reflection, Amarachukwu is that record that reminds you: you’re here by grace.



EASTSIDEALIEN SPEAKS



“I made this song as a thank you—to God, to my supporters, and to my journey. Amarachukwu is not just about religion—it’s about realizing where you started from and giving glory to who brought you this far.”




Stream Amara Chukwu

A Sound of Gratitude, Faith & Street Gospel Set to Shake the Scene



Fast-rising Eastern rap talent EASTSIDEALIEN is gearing up to release a powerful new track titled “Amarachukwu” on July 15—a high-energy fusion of Afro-Adura, Highlife, and Hip-Hop featuring standout collaborators Choo and Beepee D RapGod.







Rooted in faith and gratitude, Amarachukwu (meaning Grace of God in Igbo) is a heartfelt thanksgiving anthem that celebrates divine favor and the undeniable role of grace in Eastsidealien’s journey from Nsukka’s gritty streets to Nigeria’s rising music charts.



EASTSIDEALIEN: THE VOICE FROM THE EAST



Born and raised in Nsukka, Enugu State, Eastsidealien has carved out a bold space in Nigeria’s hip-hop scene with a sound that blends Grime, Drill, and conscious rap. Inspired by global rap icon 21 Savage, he began his musical journey in 2019 and gained widespread attention with his 2023 single Hypocrites.







Now, with millions of streams and co-signs across the East, he’s back—stronger, sharper, and more spiritually charged. For Eastsidealien, music is more than a hustle—it’s a lifelong profession driven by the dream of generational wealth and legacy.



MEET THE FEATURED ARTISTS



CHOOA new school Afro-fusion artist with a taste for psychedelic soundscapes, Choo creates music that lives between alternative, pop, and afrobeats. Influenced by artists like Post Malone, Jon Bellion, Damian Marley, and LÁBÁJA, he brings emotional depth and sonic elegance to every verse. His contribution to Amarachukwu promises to elevate the song’s vibe with soul and style.



BEEPEE D RAPGODNicknamed The Beast from the East and The Igbotic Tupac, Beepee is a veteran rapper known for his hard-hitting Igbo bars and cultural storytelling. With a music career stretching back to 2007, Beepee has long been a pillar of Eastern rap excellence. His lyrical presence on Amarachukwu is not just a feature—it’s a cultural statement.



WHAT TO EXPECT FROM “AMARACHUKWU”



Amarachukwu is more than a song—it’s a prayer, a testimony, and a celebration of growth. With bouncing rhythms, indigenous melodies, and raw lyricism, the track merges street consciousness with spiritual gratitude. Each artist brings a unique energy, creating a record that speaks to the soul of every hustler who knows they’re only here by grace.

Nigerian rapper-singer-songwriter Agunna returns with a refreshing twist to his ever-evolving artistry, delivering an Afro-alte-inspired jam titled “Omoge Meta Shere.” This new single sees the genre-bending performer serenade listeners with a sultry, romantic number that leans into his softer side, affirming his readiness to go all in for love—emotionally and financially.







With bouncy melodies layered over a vibrant blend of Afrobeat, R&B, and alte textures, “Omoge Meta Shere” is more than a love song; it’s a vibe-laden commitment anthem that shows Agunna’s willingness to take care of his woman, no matter the cost. Whether you’re vibing alone or dancing with your own “omoge,” the track effortlessly positions itself as a playlist essential for fans of smooth, modern Afrofusion.



THE MAKING OF A GANGSTAR HERO



For those just tuning in, Agunna isn’t new to the scene—he’s a foundational voice in Abuja’s underground music evolution. Since breaking out in 2017 under the Blvcksheep collective, alongside names like ODUMODUBLVCK, Agunna has consistently pushed the creative boundaries of Nigerian hip-hop, Afro-fusion, and alternative music. Their joint project, @T.A.B.S (TO ALL Blvcksheep), produced standout moments like “Farabale,” a street anthem that shook the capital city and signaled the rise of a new generation of lyrical innovators.









FROM COLLECTIVE GENIUS TO PERSONAL GROWTH



In 2018, Agunna and his team took things up a notch, merging forces with Abuja heavyweights Izzgaju—comprising Reeplay, Cross, and Fatboy E—to form the powerful supergroup Antiworld Gangstars. Their debut album Gang Business quickly became a cult favorite, praised for its lyrical depth, sonic diversity, and bold experimentation. It wasn’t just an album—it was a blueprint for unity and creativity in the FCT’s bustling music scene.







While pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Agunna didn’t lose sight of his craft. His 2021 collection, Live in Owa, kept fans tuned in, offering introspective takes and personal reflections. Then came December 2024, and with it, the long-awaited Antiworld Gangstars album NOTHING CHANGED—a triumphant return that soared to the top of the hip-hop charts and cemented their place as icons in Abuja’s sonic story.



“OMOGE META SHERE” – A SOFT REINTRODUCTION



With “Omoge Meta Shere,” Agunna strips away the bravado for a moment of clarity and connection. It’s a sound that speaks to growth—not just musically, but emotionally. 









The record glides between Afro-swing and alte aesthetics while maintaining his lyrical authenticity, making it a standout release in a market that often prizes noise over nuance.



Agunna proves once again that his artistry cannot—and will not—be boxed in.




Stream Now

Emerging Nigerian artist Erigothi returns with a bold declaration in the form of his brand-new single, “Flex On, featuring JayPoppin” officially out today on all major streaming platforms. The record is a fearless, high-octane anthem that reflects Erigothi’s growing reputation for crafting genre-fluid music that’s both unfiltered and impactful.







The Sound: Sharp Production Meets Intentional Energy



Produced by the fast-rising Orheezyx, “Flex On” is designed to hit hard. Built on a foundation of thunderous drums, wild synth textures, and a hook that sticks on the first listen, the track delivers a sonic punch without trying too hard.









The instrumental moves with intensity, giving Erigothi space to rap and ride the beat with controlled swagger, pushing his unique sound even further into the mainstream without compromising creativity.



The Message: Presence Without Apology



At its core, “Flex On” isn’t just about bragging—it’s about unshakable self-belief. Rather than focusing on struggle or comparison, Erigothi taps into a headspace where confidence is quiet, purposeful, and magnetic.








“Flex On is that energy you need when you know who you are and don’t need to prove it,” Erigothi explains. “It’s about standing firm and moving in your own lane, no matter who’s watching.”




In a time where many artists chase trends, Erigothi doubles down on individuality, offering a refreshing reminder that authenticity always wins.



The Artist: Erigothi’s Evolution Continues



Born out of Nigeria’s creative undercurrent, Erigothi is carving his path with intention. Known for his genre-defying approach, his music blends alternative rap, afro-influences, and experimental energy into something distinctly his own.







“Flex On” builds on the momentum of previous releases while setting the tone for his forthcoming project, Coldest II—a body of work expected to showcase his growing versatility and unfiltered truth.



This release confirms what early fans already know: Erigothi isn’t just making music—he’s building a legacy rooted in confidence, craft, and cultural relevance.




Stream ‘Flex On’

Emerging from the cold winds of Abuja’s underground with a warm, introspective fire, Toocoldbaby—formerly known as ZaddyTC—delivers his latest sonic entry, “I,” a powerful track of self-awareness, emotional tension, and bold proclamation.







Born Okoro Chigosim Praise in Jos, Nigeria, Toocoldbaby is not just an artist to watch—he’s an evolving storyteller crafting his own lane in a hybrid sound he’s named Afro-glacier music. On “I,” TC invites listeners into a reflective headspace that balances vulnerability with grit, wrapping his signature melodic flows around themes of love, identity, pressure, and transformation.



A Letter to Self, A Vibe for the Streets



“I” is more than just a track—it’s a personal journal entry wrapped in harmonies and head-nodding production. Over a mellow, ambient beat that gives space for introspection, Toocoldbaby meditates on growth, emotional suppression, relationship friction, and spiritual strength. It’s soul-searching without the self-pity. Every line hits with a sense of lived experience:










“I’m just tryna change my life / Tryna change my life for my wife and my babies…”




It’s not often that vulnerability is paired with swag, but that’s exactly the energy Toocoldbaby brings to this record.



Lyrical Healing, Abuja-Style



Coming from a background deeply rooted in church choirs and inter-school competitions, TC is no stranger to vocal performance. But on “I,” we see his lyrical pen take center stage. The lyrics read like a confession and a prayer rolled into one, offering insight into his emotional evolution:










“I pray you find peace / I pray you find peace…”




This final chant-like section turns the track into an offering—not just to a romantic muse, but to his fans, his past, and his future. It’s meditative. It’s honest. It’s real.



Global Ambitions



As one of the rising voices in Nigeria’s fast-evolving alt and Afro-fusion space, Toocoldbaby is proving that he’s more than just a cool name. He’s building a brand rooted in emotion, authenticity, and community. His unique ability to fuse Afrobeats cadences with hip-hop sensibilities gives him a cutting edge that resonates with both traditional and digital-era listeners.



With each release, he continues to grow his fanbase, performing and recording with the hunger of someone determined to write his own story. “I” is just another chapter in what promises to be a long and genre-shaping journey.

Today marks the official arrival of “All For You”, the heartfelt new single from Nigerian artists Fancey Dyce and Veeboiski—two rising voices with a shared mission to express love, truth, and vulnerability through music. 









Released as the lead single from their upcoming joint project Beat of My Heart, All For You is a stunning sonic offering packed with emotional weight and lyrical resonance.



A Soundtrack for Real Ones



Built on smooth Afro-fusion textures, street-infused rhythms, and melodic finesse, All For You captures the feeling of laying your heart bare for someone who truly matters. It’s a confession of loyalty. A tribute to real love. And a reminder that music, when done right, can still speak directly to the soul.



“We wanted to keep it honest. This song is about giving everything—to someone who deserves everything,” Veeboiski says.

RADARCharts’ official ambassador TELMAN returns with a striking new single titled “MOOV DIFFERENT”—a genre-bending Afro-Drill statement that signals the start of his most defining artistic chapter yet.







This isn’t just a comeback. It’s a declaration.



Following the viral impact of his gospel-drill anthem ‘Awesome God’ in 2024, ‘Besting EP’ in 2024, reclaimed his status with ‘Rebirth’ this year, TELMAN now reintroduces himself under a bold new identity: The RADARMan—a symbol of creative evolution, spiritual alignment, and visionary thinking proclaiming the tag CFA – Can’t Fall Again. Released under RADARMusic and managed by Royal Empire Management, “MOOV DIFFERENT” sets a powerful tone for what’s to come.



The Sound: Afro-Fusion Meets Drill Realness



Built on a smooth yet gritty production bed, “MOOV DIFFERENT” blends the street energy of UK Drill with the emotional resonance of Afro-fusion. TELMAN floats effortlessly through laidback percussions and bass-heavy textures, delivering melodic cadences and sharp storytelling with a tone that’s both reflective and quietly confident.









Think NSG meets Odumodublvck—with a spiritual twist.



His lyrical finesse shines through Afro-laced lingo and street-smart UK slang, serving up a message rooted in personal growth, silent elevation, and the art of moving with intention. It’s music for the ones walking in purpose—even when no one’s watching.



Key Themes: Growth, Stillness, and Self-Belief



At its core, “MOOV DIFFERENT” speaks to every creative, dreamer, and hustler who chooses the high road over the loud one. TELMAN doesn’t chase virality—he builds legacy. His lyrics reflect a season of discipline, quiet wins, and spiritual recalibration.









Lines like “You pray for a Benz, man, I work for Bugatti” speak directly to a generation choosing value over volume.



Cultural Pulse: A Movement in Motion



With over 6 million+ streams, a Shazam count north of 112K, and an ever-expanding fanbase stretching from Nigeria to the UK, South Africa, and the U.S., TELMAN is no longer just an artist to watch—he’s a cultural force in formation.







As the face of RADARCharts’ creative movement, he embodies the platform’s mission: to spotlight next-gen talent built on substance, strategy, and global vision.



“MOOV DIFFERENT” isn’t just a track—it’s an entry point into TELMAN’s next era, a soundscape crafted for playlists, reels, underground freestyles, and everything in between.



Stream Now: The RADARMan Has Arrived



“MOOV DIFFERENT” is available now on all major streaming platforms.




Stream ‘MOOV DIFFERENT’

articles.body:
ABUJA, NIGERIA – July 2025 — Rising rap force REEPLAY has officially debuted on the Top100 Abuja Charts with his explosive new track “Akpor”, featuring an all-star lineup including Odumodublvck, Portable, and Magnito.









Curated weekly by The Grillhype in collaboration with RADARCharts, Nothing Bad Happens on a Friday, Untamed Music, Hot New Afro, and Abuja Gist, the Top100 Abuja Charts celebrate originality, sonic excellence, and the voices shaping the city’s music identity.



RAW. EVOLVED. LOUD: Who Is REEPLAY?



REEPLAY—an acronym for Raw Evolved Energy Playing Loud All Year—is no stranger to Abuja’s music scene. Known for his gripping storytelling, intricate wordplay, and high-octane performances, Reeplay has earned a reputation as one of the capital’s most dynamic rap artists.









A core member of the Antiworld Gangstars Collective, Reeplay also delivered standout verses and hooks on their seminal 2019 project Gang Business.



“AKPOR”: A Statement Record



“Akpor” isn’t just a song—it’s a statement. Featuring three heavyweight collaborators, each bringing a distinct energy:









Odumodublvck: The genre-fusing rap maverick known for his cinematic flows and cultural sharpness.



 Magnito: A veteran wordsmith with an unmatched knack for punchlines and storytelling. 



Portable: The unpredictable, street-certified Zeh Nation boss whose chaotic charisma commands attention.



Reeplay serves as the anchor, holding the track together with his signature clarity and punch, proving once again that he’s not just a local act, but a national contender.



A Win for Abuja Music



Reeplay’s debut on the Top100 Abuja Charts with Akpor is a win not just for him but for the entire Abuja music ecosystem. It’s a reminder that the FCT has a thriving sound, a loyal community, and rappers capable of going toe-to-toe with the biggest names in Nigerian music.







Stream “AKPOR” now on all platforms. Follow @radarcharts and @grillhype for weekly chart updates and breaking new sounds from the capital.

articles.body:
Nigerian rising star Emiwizzy is back—and this time, he’s bringing the fire with “JAIYE”, a vibrant, high-octane Afrobeat single that speaks directly to the soul of the everyday dreamer, the nighttime dancer, and anyone in need of an unapologetic celebration of life.







A SOUNDTRACK FOR JOYFUL SURVIVAL



“JAIYE” is more than just a song—it’s an energy. Laced with percussive Afrobeat grooves, bright melodic hooks, and Emiwizzy’s confident vocal delivery, the track champions joy, resilience, and movement. It’s a rallying cry for those choosing light over limits, motion over stagnation.









From the first beat, Emiwizzy pulls listeners into a feel-good zone—a space where problems are parked, and pleasure takes the wheel. Whether you’re dancing with friends, riding solo, or vibing on a rooftop, “JAIYE” sets the tone for a moment worth remembering.



EMIWIZZY: THE VOICE OF YOUTHFUL FIRE



Known for his vibrant stage presence and genre-blending style, Emiwizzy continues to solidify his place in the Afrobeat and street-pop soundscape. With “JAIYE”, he builds on his growing catalogue of motivational and energetic bangers, offering a sound that’s both relatable and refreshing.







“JAIYE,” which means “enjoy life” in Yoruba, captures the heart of Emiwizzy’s artistry—music that motivates people to keep going, keep dancing, and keep believing in better days.



A CALL TO MOVE DIFFERENT



In an era weighed down by uncertainty, Emiwizzy’s “JAIYE” offers a necessary escape and a reminder: joy is a form of resistance. As the chorus chants echo over rhythmic drums and addictive synths, one thing becomes clear—this isn’t just a record, it’s a movement.




Stream ‘Jaiye’




Follow Emiwizzy 









Instagram

articles.body:
Emerging as one of the most original voices from Nigeria’s thriving hip-hop scene, TELMAN—the UK-raised, Nigeria-born wordsmith—is gearing up to shake the table with his upcoming single, “MOOV DIFFERENT.” After a pause with his ‘BLACK N WHITE’ release ‘MOOV DIFFERENT’ is slated for release under the RADARMusic imprint, the track represents a sonic rebirth for an artist already admired for his vulnerability, poetic intensity, and spiritual edge.







As a proud representative of Royal Empire Management and a flagship artist under RADARCharts, TELMAN—now known as The RADARMan—announces this next step with full confidence and creative precision. Following a viral gospel-drill moment with Holy Drill’s “Awesome God” and an accumulated 6M+ streams, this new release is set to reposition him on the global music map.



Sound Breakdown: Afro-Drill Fusion That Hits Different



“MOOV DIFFERENT” is more than a title—it’s a manifesto. The song merges UK Drill’s bass-heavy bounce with the rhythmic soul of Afro-fusion, resulting in a genre-fluid track that will resonate with both London streets and Lagos rooftops.









Drawing sonic inspiration from the likes of JAE5 and NSG’s “Spin Da Block,” TELMAN takes this blend further with a grounded, introspective lyrical style. It’s this rare combo—vibey yet deeply lyrical—that makes TELMAN a stand-out among Gen Z’s new wave of storytellers.



Lyrical Energy: The Calm Power of Confidence



The essence of “MOOV DIFFERENT” is one of confidence without arrogance. TELMAN raps about lifestyle shifts, quiet wins, and creative freedom. His lyrics echo a deeply personal transition—emerging from obscurity into self-alignment, without needing external validation.



“I’ve been doing my stuff in a different way.” — TELMAN



This bar isn’t just catchy—it’s autobiographical. It captures the silent transformation of an artist refining his craft, redefining his environment, and rewriting his rules.



Audience Connection: Culture Shifters & Truth Seekers



TELMAN’s fan base spans Nigeria, the United Kingdom, the U.S., Canada, Kenya, and South Africa—driven by Gen Z music heads who gravitate towards cultural storytelling, vulnerability, and drill-infused authenticity. He speaks directly to the “real ones”—those quietly building, evolving, and refusing to conform.



“MOOV DIFFERENT” is TELMAN’s offering to these cultural shifters—a reminder that elevation often begins in silence.



Presave the Shift



Now officially aligned with RADARCharts and Royal Empire Management, TELMAN is ready to deliver his most personal and polished work to date.




Presave ‘MOOV DIFFERENT’



Visit ‘TELMAN’

articles.body:
In a smooth shift from his signature Afro-fusion and Hip-Hop foundation, Nigerian-born, Istanbul-based artist Vuga Kvngz steps into new sonic territory with his latest release — Come Through, a sensual and melodic Afrosoul/R&B track that captures vulnerability, late-night desire, and musical maturity.







This release is more than just a song — it’s a statement of evolution. Vuga Kvngz, born Chiedozie Eze Walter, has continuously defied expectations with his genre-blending artistry. Known for fusing influences from Afrobeats, Hip-Hop, Reggae, and Alternative sounds under his self-styled genre, Vuga Vibes, the artist now introduces a new layer of depth and soul to his catalog.



A NEW SOUND, SAME SPIRIT



Come Through is stripped-back yet emotionally rich — showcasing Vuga’s growth not only as a vocalist but also as a storyteller. The song’s moody production and tender lyrics invite the listener into a world of longing and intimacy. It’s a sonic invitation, one that highlights a softer, more reflective side of the artist.









Yet, even within this new direction, Vuga’s creative DNA is ever-present. His ability to draw from lived experience, to inject fiction from his poetry roots, and to infuse global influences — from Burnaboy and Prettyboy DO, to Drake and Jay Z — is what makes his music distinct and memorable.



FROM IMO TO ISTANBUL: THE WORLD BOY JOURNEY



Originally from Imo State, Nigeria, Vuga’s musical journey began after completing a degree in Political Science. After a few years in Nigeria’s music scene, he relocated to Istanbul, Turkey, where he pursued his Master’s degree and reignited his passion for music.




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Vuga Kvngz (@vugakvngzofficial)




Since then, he’s carved a niche for himself in the Turkish scene, pushing African soundscapes into global spaces with tracks like Take Over — a powerful anthem about ambition and resilience.



Through his co-founded label World Boyz Entertainment, Vuga Kvngz has created more than music — he’s building a movement. From curating Worldly Activities, a concert series that amplifies African and global voices in Istanbul, to designing fashion and merch through World Boyz Collective, Vuga is shaping culture both in sound and style.



VUGA VIBES REIMAGINED



With Come Through, Vuga invites fans into an emotionally honest experience. It’s a love letter written with smooth vocals and textured Afro/R&B (Afrosoul) production — one that shows his readiness to explore deeper, more intimate territories without losing his roots.







The single is a warm-up to what’s next — possibly another full project or an expanded chapter of Vuga Vibes.




Stream ‘Come Through’

Come Through is stripped-back yet emotionally rich — showcasing Vuga’s growth not only as a vocalist but also as a storyteller. The song’s moody production and tender lyrics invite the listener into a world of longing and intimacy. It’s a sonic invitation, one that highlights a softer, more reflective side of the artist.

Yet, even within this new direction, Vuga’s creative DNA is ever-present. His ability to draw from lived experience, to inject fiction from his poetry roots, and to infuse global influences — from Burnaboy and Prettyboy DO, to Drake and Jay Z — is what makes his music distinct and memorable.

FROM IMO TO ISTANBUL: THE WORLD BOY JOURNEY

Originally from Imo State, Nigeria, Vuga’s musical journey began after completing a degree in Political Science. After a few years in Nigeria’s music scene, he relocated to Istanbul, Turkey, where he pursued his Master’s degree and reignited his passion for music.

Since then, he’s carved a niche for himself in the Turkish scene, pushing African soundscapes into global spaces with tracks like Take Over — a powerful anthem about ambition and resilience.

Through his co-founded label World Boyz Entertainment, Vuga Kvngz has created more than music — he’s building a movement. From curating Worldly Activities, a concert series that amplifies African and global voices in Istanbul, to designing fashion and merch through World Boyz Collective, Vuga is shaping culture both in sound and style.

VUGA VIBES REIMAGINED

With Come Through, Vuga invites fans into an emotionally honest experience. It’s a love letter written with smooth vocals and textured Afro/R&B (Afrosoul) production — one that shows his readiness to explore deeper, more intimate territories without losing his roots.

The single is a warm-up to what’s next — possibly another full project or an expanded chapter of Vuga Vibes.

In the vibrant and ever-evolving landscape of Nigerian music, a new voice is emerging—gentle yet powerful, personal yet universal. 







That voice belongs to Fwfeyi, the Lagos-bred, Ondo-rooted Afro-fusion and soul artist redefining what it means to feel music.



WHO IS FWFeyi?



Born Omowa Feyisayo on May 11th, 2000, Fwfeyi grew up in the heart of Lagos, Nigeria’s bustling cultural capital. While the streets of Lagos shaped his hustle, his roots in Ondo State gave him the spiritual grounding that breathes through every note he sings. A self-taught multi-instrumentalist who began his musical journey on the saxophone, Fwfeyi didn’t just stop at playing—he began producing music at just 17 years old, setting the stage for a unique sound that bridges modern Afrobeat with soul-searching intimacy.



SOUND & STYLE: Where Afro Fusion Meets Soulful Honesty



Fwfeyi operates within a lush sonic world that blends Afro Fusion, Afro Soul, and Contemporary R&B—but genres are mere containers for the depth of his emotion. His music serves as a journal through life’s chapters: love, heartbreak, healing, and self-awareness. You don’t just hear a Fwfeyi record—you feel it.









His songs evoke the quiet ache of a broken heart, the calm of inner reflection, and the warmth of self-love. But even more than his melodies, it’s his honesty that sets him apart. Every lyric carries weight because it’s lived experience—real stories told through rhythm and soul.



ARTISTRY ROOTED IN AUTHENTICITY



What makes Fwfeyi magnetic is his vulnerability. In an era where many artists chase trends, he leans into truth and storytelling. His production is intricate yet airy, often layered with warm harmonies, mellow percussion, and a strong sense of place. He’s not afraid to show pain. He’s not afraid to be gentle. And in doing so, he opens the door for others to be real too.




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by FLYESTFW🎖️ (@fwfeyi)




“My music is a mirror. I make what I feel—and hope people feel seen in it too.” – Fwfeyi



THE VISION AHEAD



While still on the rise, Fwfeyi is already carving his own lane. He represents a new generation of Nigerian creatives—those unafraid to be soft, to be spiritual, to break molds. With each release, he continues to expand his emotional vocabulary and sonic palette.







Fans and critics alike are starting to notice his potential, not just as a singer or producer, but as a storyteller who connects deeply with his audience. He’s not trying to be the loudest in the room—he’s trying to be the realest.



WHY FWFeyi MATTERS



In a time when Afrobeat is taking over the world, artists like Fwfeyi are showing that there’s more to the sound than club anthems. There’s depth, poetry, and healing. He’s part of the soul movement within Afrobeats—a movement that whispers where others shout, but leaves just as deep a mark.



As he continues to shape his identity and expand his sound, FWFEYI stands as an artist to watch, to feel, and to believe in. He’s not just made in Lagos—he’s making music for the world to feel.

After building a reputation in underground circles under the name Kill Teedashii, the Nigerian-born artist has turned a fresh page, reintroducing himself to the world as Tidashii. This isn’t just a name change — it’s a total creative rebirth.








“I changed my name because I wanted to reflect growth, clarity, and purpose. Tidashii is still me, just with more intention. I’m not here to destroy — I’m here to build.” — Tidashii




With this new identity comes his most important release yet: Made In Africa, a four-track debut EP that fuses melodic rap, Afro-fusion, and raw emotion into a sound that feels as fearless as it does familiar.



Behind the Sound: A Story from the Heart of the Continent



Crafted in the heart of Abuja and shaped by late-night studio sessions, Made In Africa is a deeply personal offering. According to Tidashii, the EP started with a vision — to blend alternative sounds with Afrobeat in a way that felt raw, emotional, and real.








“I wasn’t trying to copy what’s already out there. I wanted to build something that sounded like me,” Tidashii says.




He let life guide the music. Sometimes freestyling. Sometimes writing line-by-line. Every track, from the emotional vulnerability of “who needs love” to the global bounce of “Foreign” featuring Madisin!, pulses with sincerity. And beyond the music, he directed all visuals himself, ensuring every image mirrored the authenticity of his message — unfiltered and honest.



Made in Africa — The Birth of a Movement



Made In Africa isn’t just an EP title. It’s the name of Tidashii’s independent studio and the engine behind his creative mission. The project also marks the official launch of Disturbing Africa — a fashion and lifestyle brand designed to empower and inspire a new generation of African youth.




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Tee Dashii (@teedashii)




This debut is more than music — it’s a manifesto. It challenges norms, celebrates identity, and invites listeners to break molds unapologetically. For Tidashii, this is the beginning of something greater than himself.



From Abuja to the World



Tidashii is a rising force in alternative Afrobeats — fusing culture, story, and sound. With Made In Africa, he steps forward not just as an artist, but as a leader of a movement rooted in truth and future-driven creativity.



Formerly Kill Teedashii, now fully Tidashii — he’s not here to blend in. He’s here to build a legacy. Made In Africa drops on all platforms July 5th, 2025.

articles.body:
The Voice of Experience Returns



After back-to-back drops of No Pressure (2022) and No Pressure, Vol. 2 (2023), Nigerian rapper and lyrical craftsman Bobbo Esko is back — more introspective, more fearless, and more seasoned than ever.







His latest offering, FEAR WHAT YOU DON’T KNOW (FWYDK), drops this Saturday, July 5th, 2025, and it promises to be a defining moment in the artist’s journey from Asata to acclaim.



Born Chukwuebuka ThankGod, the Enugu-raised rapper is no stranger to complexity. A professional Doctor of Physiotherapy by degree and a poet by instinct, Bobbo’s new album reflects the tensions between intellect and instinct, fear and ambition — and most of all, what it means to navigate the unknown as a black man with dreams that stretch beyond borders.



A Collaborative Alchemy with Icebeatzz



The entire album is produced by Icebeatzz (Chidera Egbo), Bobbo’s long-time collaborator and trusted creative partner. Their bond is built on years of mutual understanding and trust, which shines throughout FWYDK.







The project was born from “a remarkable chemistry and shared vision for creating exceptional music,” according to Bobbo, and it’s clear that this wasn’t just about making tracks — it was about telling a story.



From the fierce Afro-hop rhythm of “BLACK KING” to the soulful trap energy of “MY FAULT,” Icebeatzz provides a rich and versatile backdrop that allows Bobbo to float, punch, confess, and celebrate all in one breath.



A Sound Built on Contrast



The album is an intentional blend of hip-hop’s grit, Afrobeat’s bounce, and R&B’s vulnerability.



FWYDK isn’t just about flexing skills — it’s a sonic meditation on power, fear, and legacy.



Each feature brings a new layer to the story:




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by FWYDK🦁 (@bobbo_esko)




Marc Swagz delivers smooth gravitas Miickey Metro fires off politically charged flows Stakexx & Fozter bring high-octane energy to the street anthem “BIG BAG”



In Bobbo’s Own Words




“This tape is about what happens when we confront the things we don’t understand — fear, ambition, pain, pride.



We didn’t want to just make a project, we wanted to make an experience.



Icebeatzz and I built every beat, every transition, every hook like a step through that dark tunnel.



And what you find on the other side? That’s up to you.”




About the Artist: Bobbo Esko



Hailing from Enugu State, Bobbo Esko is a multifaceted artist who merges lyrical depth with streetwise storytelling.







A trained physiotherapist and the last of four siblings, his music explores identity, heritage, pressure, and perseverance.



After rising to local fame with tracks like MALAGA and OYEGO, he has since evolved into a force within Nigeria’s indie hip-hop landscape.









Bobbo’s blend of Afro-infused rap and emotionally charged lyricism sets him apart as a rare voice in the scene.

On the evening of Sunday, June 30th, 2025, the city of Owerri became the stage for something far greater than a musical performance. What transpired was not just a concert — it was a rite of passage, a communal awakening, and a deeply spiritual invocation. 







Titled Anyafulugo: Lost in the Cave, the live special marked the debut showcase of Mark Anthony Obumneme Osuchukwu, professionally known as Anyafulugo, and a defining moment for his self-styled genre, Afro-Agwu.



A Journey, Not Just a Show



To those already acquainted with Anyafulugo’s artistry, the event came as a confirmation of his creative depth. For newcomers, it was an initiation. With roots deeply anchored in Igbo spiritual traditions, ancestral memory, and mythic storytelling, the evening’s performance unfolded like a ceremonial journey — each song a new rite, each transition a crossing of thresholds.









From the very first note, it was evident that Lost in the Cave was more than a poetic title. It was a metaphor for personal solitude, artistic metamorphosis, and the spiritual discipline of a man who has chosen to create in silence and emerge only when his voice became a vessel.




“The cave is where I went to disappear,” Anyafulugo later shared. “But I came back with fire.”




Sound as Spirit: The Setlist as Scripture



The performance was divided into ten chapters, with each song serving as a ritual moment in the narrative arc. It began with “Uzo” — the symbolic opening of the cave, an initiation chant that set the mood for everything that followed. “Chukwu Ekwena” came next, a thunderous plea for divine protection that stirred the room into spiritual alertness.









Then came “Ngwo Ngwo” and “Chekeleke” — rhythmic, ancestral, playful — evoking memories of village life, moonlit tales, and pouring libation into the earth. These tracks showed Anyafulugo at his most folkloric, echoing the pulse of indigenous Igbo ceremonies.









At the emotional midpoint, “Walk Alone” brought silence into the room. It was a meditation on solitude — not as isolation, but as necessary stillness. The vulnerability in his voice made the cave feel real, not just symbolic.



Collaboration in Communion



Breaking that stillness, Anyafulugo called on collaborators who further expanded the spiritual spectrum of the night. M’Joey joined him on “Many Things”, a standout performance where both artists reflected on the burdens and blessings of life, offering poetry drenched in lived experience.







Later, Jerryvic stepped in for “The Game”, turning the stage into a lyrical battlefield. The duo traded verses with gripping urgency, weaving together charisma, resistance, and raw emotion.



Tenderness, Closure, and the Fire to Come



The night’s final movement came with “Omalicha” and “Ndeli” — songs of healing and remembrance, carried on melodies that felt like lullabies from the ancestors. Then, as if pulling the audience back from their trance, Anyafulugo closed with “Vladimir” — a dark, mysterious finale that served both as resolution and prelude to what lies ahead.









It was the cliffhanger of the night. And yet, its intention was clear: the journey isn’t over.



Afro-Agwu: Music as Memory, Genre as Gospel



What sets Anyafulugo apart isn’t just his performance. It’s his purpose. Afro-Agwu is more than a sound — it’s a philosophical statement. A reclamation of spiritual heritage, rooted in Igbo mysticism, oral storytelling, and musical experimentation. Lost in the Cave was the genre’s full manifestation — a cultural communion that called both the young and the old into remembrance and rebirth.









In a time when modernity often drowns indigenous expression, Anyafulugo is lighting a torch. And in Owerri that night, the flame caught.



A Moment Marked, A Movement Born



As the final chants dissolved and the applause surged like a wave, there was a shared understanding among those present: they hadn’t just watched a performance — they had witnessed a spiritual return. The cave, for Anyafulugo, was never a place of fear. It was the womb of becoming.



And now, reborn and resounding, he walks among us — not just as an artist, but as a messenger of sound, spirit, and ancestral truth.




Follow the journey

Breaking that stillness, Anyafulugo called on collaborators who further expanded the spiritual spectrum of the night. M’Joey joined him on “Many Things”, a standout performance where both artists reflected on the burdens and blessings of life, offering poetry drenched in lived experience.

Later, Jerryvic stepped in for “The Game”, turning the stage into a lyrical battlefield. The duo traded verses with gripping urgency, weaving together charisma, resistance, and raw emotion.

Tenderness, Closure, and the Fire to Come

The night’s final movement came with “Omalicha” and “Ndeli” — songs of healing and remembrance, carried on melodies that felt like lullabies from the ancestors. Then, as if pulling the audience back from their trance, Anyafulugo closed with “Vladimir” — a dark, mysterious finale that served both as resolution and prelude to what lies ahead.

It was the cliffhanger of the night. And yet, its intention was clear: the journey isn’t over.

Afro-Agwu: Music as Memory, Genre as Gospel

What sets Anyafulugo apart isn’t just his performance. It’s his purpose. Afro-Agwu is more than a sound — it’s a philosophical statement. A reclamation of spiritual heritage, rooted in Igbo mysticism, oral storytelling, and musical experimentation. Lost in the Cave was the genre’s full manifestation — a cultural communion that called both the young and the old into remembrance and rebirth.

In a time when modernity often drowns indigenous expression, Anyafulugo is lighting a torch. And in Owerri that night, the flame caught.

A Moment Marked, A Movement Born

As the final chants dissolved and the applause surged like a wave, there was a shared understanding among those present: they hadn’t just watched a performance — they had witnessed a spiritual return. The cave, for Anyafulugo, was never a place of fear. It was the womb of becoming.

And now, reborn and resounding, he walks among us — not just as an artist, but as a messenger of sound, spirit, and ancestral truth.

Follow the journey
