Emerging Nigerian artist OÒSHÀ has made a remarkable entrance into the music world with the release of his debut single, “Salvation”, an Afro-fusion anthem that captures the depth of human vulnerability and spiritual awakening. With a voice as sincere as his story, OÒSHÀ introduces himself not just as an artist—but as a vessel of truth.







A Prophetic Beginning: The Story Behind “Salvation”



OÒSHÀ, whose real name is Adegoke Habeeb, didn’t just write a song—he lived it. The idea for “Salvation” came in the early hours of the morning, following a vivid dream in which he narrowly escaped a fatal accident.



“I woke up feeling grateful and saved, so I recorded the song that same morning—at dawn. It was a pivotal moment.” – OÒSHÀ









The record, written, performed, and recorded by OÒSHÀ himself, carries a potent message:



“Ego must die for elevation.”



This mantra anchors the track and sets the tone for a musical journey rooted in humility, consciousness, and growth.



Meet OÒSHÀ: The Oracle Behind the Music



Formerly known in earlier circles as Bucho DeGo, OÒSHÀ has been making music since 2015. After surviving challenges both personal and professional—including the end of a record deal in 2017—he found rebirth in music, faith, and self-reliance.



The name OÒSHÀ (meaning “Oracle”) was born from his trials and transformations:



“It’s about self-realization. The name represents my journey, the grace that’s kept me afloat, and the divine gift of music that I believe I was given.”







Drawing inspiration from a spectrum of genres like Dancehall, Reggae, R&B, and Highlife, OÒSHÀ’s sound is a refined fusion that speaks to a pan-African generation—restless, spiritual, and hungry for truth.



Inside the Sound: Afro-Fusion with Depth



“Salvation” is not your typical Afrobeats single. It leans into Afro-fusion in the purest sense—layering melodic percussion, introspective lyrics, and soulful vocal runs with minimalist yet moving production.



The chorus hits like a meditation while the verses tell stories of struggle, transformation, and divine intervention. It’s a bold artistic choice for a debut—one that instantly distinguishes OÒSHÀ from his peers.



The Independent Push



Released independently and distributed via CNC Distro, “Salvation” is backed by grassroots effort and a growing community of believers in OÒSHÀ’s sound and story. From building his own home studio to recording his full-length project OOSHATIDE, the artist has demonstrated not just talent—but tenacity.









Despite facing family doubts, industry setbacks, and moments of discouragement, he never considered quitting:



“Music has always been a safe haven for me. Even when my mother didn’t understand, I knew I had something special. It’s true bliss to create something meaningful.”



Future Aspirations: From the Oracle to the World



Looking ahead, OÒSHÀ is confident in what he brings to the table—and where he’s headed:



“I expect to be one of the biggest acts from Africa in the nearest future. I’m the face of perseverance. There’s so much to come.”



With an album in the works and dreams of collaborating with the likes of Burna Boy, Wizkid, Rema, Tems, and Omah Lay, his goals align with the vision of a generation redefining African music.



Why ‘Salvation’ Matters



At its core, “Salvation” is not just a song—it’s a declaration. It announces OÒSHÀ’s arrival with clarity, conviction, and spiritual depth rarely seen in debut releases. For fans of Burna Boy’s introspection, Wizkid’s melodies, or Tems’ soulfulness, OÒSHÀ offers a fresh voice anchored in truth and guided by destiny.




Stream ‘Salvation’



Visit OÒSHÀ

Today, Nigerian rapper and lyrical architect Jason Nkanga releases “Pi,” his latest addition to a catalog defined by intelligence, energy, and lyrical sharpness. The track is a bold statement—complex, calculated, and creatively unbounded. Like the mathematical constant it’s named after, “Pi” challenges convention and stretches beyond limitations.







Jason has never been one to follow trends. With “Pi,” he presents not just a song, but a concept.



THE SOUND OF “PI”



“Pi” delivers sharp lyricism wrapped in a haunting, minimalist beat. Jason moves with intention, weaving through themes of ambition, knowledge, and personal philosophy. His flow mirrors the unpredictable yet calculated rhythm of the number itself—relentless, intelligent, and purposeful. The production leaves room for every word to land with force.









This isn’t casual listening. It’s crafted for those who listen to understand.



JASON NKANGA: INDEPENDENT BUT UNDENIABLE



Since his debut with Go Dumb in 2014, Jason Nkanga has remained a standout voice in African hip-hop. His acclaimed projects The Art of Rap and Redemption earned him respect as a thoughtful lyricist with global vision. Collaborations with names like PsychoYP, Blaqbonez, Mick Jenkins, and theMIND, alongside features in BBC, Hunger Magazine, and Okay Africa, have positioned him as a cultural voice in his own right.




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Jason Nkanga (@jasonnkanga_)




With “Pi,” Jason pushes further—continuing to define his sound and shape his legacy without compromise.



ARTIST STATEMENT ON “PI”



Jason describes his creative process with clarity and focus:



“It started like every song does—I cut off distractions, zoned in on the beats, and waited for the one that stuck. ‘Pi’ hit me because the concept felt limitless. Once I started writing, it flowed endlessly. I even researched some bars to make sure they were airtight—because when I rap, every word has to mean something.”







He adds, “If my team likes it, that’s a bonus. But even if they don’t, if I feel strongly about a track, it drops. That’s the kind of artist I am—I take risks because the music deserves that.”



THE BIGGER PICTURE



“Pi” represents more than just lyrical ability—it’s about longevity, vision, and impact. In a space often ruled by trends and algorithms, Jason continues to build a legacy rooted in quality, authenticity, and craft.



Whether you’re a lifelong fan or new to his sound, this is the perfect moment to step into his world.



OUT NOW ON ALL PLATFORMS



“Pi” proves that the mind is a powerful instrument—and Jason Nkanga is using his to shift the culture.




Stream Pi

At the stroke of midnight, Abuja’s most trusted creative sanctuary delivers a cultural gift to the world — FREQIE SPACE ALL STAR CYPHER is officially out now.







Marking one year of groundbreaking impact, Freqie Space has released this powerhouse collaboration as a musical tribute to the community it built. Founded by visionary artist Frequencie, Freqie Space has been instrumental in transforming Abuja’s creative pulse — hosting over 75% of original creative events in the city and serving as a launchpad for both new and seasoned talent.



The release of FREQIE SPACE ALL STAR CYPHER represents more than just a song drop — it is the result of months of collaboration, trust, and cultural synergy. Set for midnight on June 22, 2025, the Dannywon engineered track is being globally distributed and strategically marketed by RADARMusic, the music division of RADARCharts of REM powered by Soft Lifestyle Record. This marks a major milestone in the growing relationship between the two brands, who share a commitment to elevating independent African talent. The marketing rollout, cover art reveal, promotional media, and digital distribution campaign were all carefully coordinated by a shared team of creatives, making this cypher not just a track, but a statement of what’s possible when vision meets infrastructure.



MEET  THE ALL-STARS



Every artist on this record is a vital thread in Abuja’s cultural fabric — together, they create a sonic quilt of street soul, resilience, rhythm, and originality.



Frequencie







The founder of Freqie Space and a long-time innovator in the Nigerian music scene, Frequencie uses this cypher to bridge his mission with his music. His contribution ties everything together — both as a voice and as the visionary behind the platform being celebrated.



Shagba







A respected lyricist and performer, Shagba brings grit, wisdom, and emotional power to the track. With years of independent releases and a signature sound that resonates with real-life experience, he stands as one of Abuja’s most grounded and authentic voices.



Moefasa







Moefasa delivers a sharp, focused verse that reflects his journey as an artist rooted in truth. Known for his consistent growth and depth, he adds balance and intensity to the cypher.



Toocoldbaby







TC (fka Zaddytc) is a rising star who fuses melody, personal storytelling, and urban energy to create a sound uniquely his own. His performance on this cypher is smooth, reflective, and delivered with a cool that mirrors his name.



Uncle Wales







With a reputation for turning every mic into a moment, Uncle Wales adds a layer of energy and entertainment to the project. Known for his work as both a hypeman and artist, his performance brings the vibe full circle.



More Than A Song — It’s A Cultural Statement



The FREQIE SPACE ALL STAR CYPHER isn’t just a lyrical exhibition — it’s a love letter to Abuja’s underground, a lighthouse for creatives in search of community, and a bold declaration of independence and artistic freedom.



Set against the backdrop of The Bolingo Hotel Rooftop Lounge, Freqie Space has become a core destination for rising talent and cultural movements. This cypher not only celebrates its impact — it fuels the next wave.











Stream Now and Share the Energy



The FREQIE SPACE ALL STAR CYPHER is now available across all digital streaming platforms. Listen now, share your favorite moments, and celebrate the space that celebrates you.



Use the hashtag #FreqieSpaceAllStarCypher



Tag the artists and @radarcharts / @freqiespace



Join the anniversary celebration live on July 5th



Freqie Turns One. Abuja Rises With It.

Rising Afrobeat sensation Phylop is making headlines once again with the release of his latest single titled Olekuu — a soulful, streetwise anthem that blends classic Afrobeat rhythms with real-life storytelling. Released today across major streaming platforms, Olekuu marks a powerful return for the Ondo-bred singer/songwriter and continues to position him as one of the most promising new voices in Nigeria’s dynamic soundscape.







Phylop: The Afrobeat Voice of the Streets



Born Philip Ireyeri, Phylop’s journey into music began in the heart of Ondo State, where his raw passion for rhythm and lyrics quickly set him apart. With every release, he has refined his style — a rich blend of Afrobeat melodies, street poetry, and heartfelt delivery. After his breakout single Sabi Way featuring Harteez took off and resonated strongly with fans across the country, Phylop has consistently proven that his music is both soulful and socially conscious.




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by SABI BOI ❤️🐐 (@phylop__)




Olekuu: An Anthem for the Hustlers



With Olekuu, Phylop delivers more than just a song — he shares an experience. A sonic journal of survival and struggle, the track mirrors the hustle many young Nigerians face daily, navigating through hardship, hope, and self-belief. Rooted in personal reflection, Phylop said the creative process was inspired by the harsh realities of life in the trenches — yet it carries an undertone of resilience and strength.










“This one is for the streets,” Phylop says. “I wanted to remind every young man out there that their hustle is valid, their story is important, and they are not alone.”




Produced with a melodic Afrobeat base, layered with rhythmic percussion and a haunting vocal hook, Olekuu manages to be deeply emotional and yet radio-ready — a balance that showcases Phylop’s evolution as both a songwriter and performer.



More Than Music: A Cultural Moment



Beyond its sound, Olekuu carries a cultural message. It reflects a generation constantly fighting to break out of limitations — the dreams of the boy from Ondo, the city struggle, and the nation’s pulse. It’s the kind of record that feels like a diary entry but sounds like a national chant.







With a growing fan base, a distinctive voice, and a message that cuts through the noise, Phylop isn’t just dropping hits — he’s building a legacy.




Stream ‘Olekuu’

Beyond its sound, Olekuu carries a cultural message. It reflects a generation constantly fighting to break out of limitations — the dreams of the boy from Ondo, the city struggle, and the nation’s pulse. It’s the kind of record that feels like a diary entry but sounds like a national chant.

With a growing fan base, a distinctive voice, and a message that cuts through the noise, Phylop isn’t just dropping hits — he’s building a legacy.

Two rising voices. One heartfelt sound.



Fancey Dyce and Veeboiski, two of Nigeria’s most promising young talents, are joining forces for an emotionally rich collaboration titled “All For You,” set to be released on July 11th, 2025. 







The single serves as the official prelude to their forthcoming joint project, Beat of My Heart—a genre-blending musical journey centered around love, truth, and vulnerability.



“All For You” is more than just a song—it’s a love letter to that one person who holds the heart, inspires the verses, and anchors the soul. Drawing from their signature sounds—Fancey Dyce’s melodic Afro-fusion and Veeboiski’s streetwise Afrobeat grit—the duo delivers a track filled with raw emotion, smooth rhythms, and relatable lyricism that captures the intensity of sincere love and devotion.








“We wanted to create something timeless,” says Fancey Dyce. “This track is personal. It’s about expressing real emotions without fear.”





Veeboiski adds, “It’s for the one who stands by you when nobody else does. That kind of love deserves a song.”




With this release, the duo sets the tone for Beat of My Heart—a collaborative effort expected to showcase their artistic chemistry, vocal depth, and creative synergy in a way the industry hasn’t seen before.

Nigerian rising star SUBZIRO, born Collins Chisom Ugwuonah, has officially dropped his highly anticipated debut EP under Kucci World Records, and it’s already making serious noise.







Following the buzz generated by his breakout single “NI’ME OGBE”, SUBZIRO’s debut EP is now available on all major streaming platforms — delivering a gritty, passionate, and deeply personal introduction to one of Nigeria’s most compelling new voices.



A 7-Track Testament to Identity and Ambition



This project isn’t just a collection of songs — it’s a statement of intent. Across seven genre-blending tracks, SUBZIRO fuses Afrobeats, drill, and rap, weaving real-life stories with sharp lyricism and raw emotional energy. It’s street-born, culture-rich, and future-focused.









“This EP is my truth — it’s a reflection of where I’ve been and where I’m going. Every track holds a piece of my journey,” SUBZIRO shares.



From energetic bangers to introspective rhythms, each record delivers a unique perspective — painting a fuller picture of the man behind the music.



A Kucci World Records Breakout Star



Backed by Kucci World Records, a label committed to spotlighting bold, forward-thinking artists, SUBZIRO’s debut is not just a personal milestone — it’s a cultural moment. The partnership reflects a shared vision: to push the boundaries of African music and elevate voices that represent the streets with truth and style.







The EP arrives at a time when the world is paying closer attention to the raw, unfiltered voices coming out of Nigeria’s underground scene — and SUBZIRO stands at the center of this shift.

In the heart of Nigeria’s capital, Abuja, a fire has been steadily burning—fueled by rhythm, rooted in tradition, and refined by global sound. That fire has a name: Bennixx. An African artist and producer with a flair for fusion and a heart for heritage, Bennixx has emerged as one of the most dynamic voices in the Afrobeat and Afro-fusion landscape today.







Renowned for his vibrant productions and soulful lyricism, Bennixx seamlessly blends African rhythms with modern bounce, giving listeners a sound that feels both familiar and groundbreaking. Whether on stage or in the studio, he delivers every note with purpose, passion, and presence.



THE SOUND OF CULTURE



Bennixx’s artistry is more than just musical—it’s cultural storytelling. Drawing deeply from his Nigerian roots, he crafts music that reflects the rich textures of African life, from love and loss to unity, spirituality, and social change.



Each track is a canvas, painted with energetic beats, vibrant melodies, and emotionally resonant lyrics. What sets Bennixx apart is his ability to bridge the ancestral and the contemporary, creating a sound that echoes Africa’s history while carving a lane for its future.



THE PROJECT: SOUNDFYAR



With his new EP titled “Soundfyar,” Bennixx takes us on a genre-defying journey through the flames of emotion, culture, and evolution. But this isn’t just music—it’s a movement. It’s a statement.










“Creating Soundfyar was like translating emotion into frequency,” Bennixx shares.“Each track was born from a moment—sometimes loud and chaotic, other times soft and intimate.”




The body of work embodies both fire and calm—a sonic experience that balances explosive rhythm with introspective storytelling. From the first kick drum to the last fading harmony, Soundfyar captures a spectrum of human experience in six unforgettable tracks.



THE CREATIVE PROCESS



Bennixx’s creative process is rooted in intuition and authenticity. Before the beat, before the pen—there is feeling.




“My process started with feeling, always,” he says.“I’d sit with the vibe, let the melodies come naturally, then build around the emotion with lyrics that told real stories—mine, and those close to me.”




In Soundfyar, you’ll hear hints of Afro-Caribbean soul, the grit of dancehall, and the bounce of global pop—all held together by the warmth and richness of African instrumentation. Each sound was carefully designed to immerse, move, and ignite.




“Soundfyar isn’t just a name—it’s a statement. This is me lighting the path with sound.”




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Bennixx (@bennixx__)





THE IMPACT & WHAT’S NEXT



With Soundfyar, Bennixx plants his flag as a trailblazer of the next wave of African music. The EP speaks to listeners across generations and geographies, reflecting the universality of rhythm and the specificity of lived experience.



As the project continues to ripple through streaming platforms, clubs, and live performances, Bennixx remains committed to expanding the boundaries of Afrobeat—while staying grounded in the soul of Africa.



He’s not here to fit in. He’s here to set the pace—and light it up, one track at a time.

In the ever-evolving Nigerian music landscape, where Afrobeats and pop dominate the airwaves, a new wave of rap is beginning to assert itself—thoughtful, layered, and unapologetically introspective. At the forefront of this shift is D-44, a compelling rap duo made up of Advocate Tha Chronicle and White Da Poet. Their debut project, This Is D44, presents a raw and resonant exploration of personal identity, artistic purpose, and sonic innovation. It is a defining moment that invites listeners into a fresh, grounded vision of Nigerian hip-hop.







Origins and Creative Synergy



The story of D-44 began at Ahmadu Bello University (ABU), Zaria, where Advocate, hailing from Jalingo, and White Da Poet, from Ibadan, discovered a shared passion for lyricism and the cultural roots of hip-hop. What started as a mutual appreciation evolved into a partnership rooted in poetry, introspection, and a commitment to challenging the norms of Nigeria’s mainstream music ecosystem. Their synergy birthed D-44—a creative force intent on pushing boundaries without compromising authenticity.



A Manifesto in Motion



This Is D44 is not just an album—it is a declaration. Over the course of the project, Advocate Tha Chronicle and White Da Poet open the doors to their inner lives, tackling themes of growth, vulnerability, and self-awareness with remarkable clarity. Rather than leaning into performative bravado, the duo prioritizes substance, offering listeners a reflective and deeply human experience. Their words are poignant, their themes timely, and their commitment to truth unwavering.









In their own words: “This Is D44 is who we are in our most vulnerable state, in our happiest moments, and as we strive to be better persons.”



Each verse is delivered with purpose, each beat carefully chosen to underscore the emotional weight of the narrative. The result is a body of work that commands attention and rewards active listening.



Sonic Identity and Musical Direction



Musically, the project leans into alternative hip-hop, characterized by stripped-back beats, soulful samples, lo-fi textures, and Afrocentric rhythms. While the sound pays homage to legendary acts like Show Dem Camp, Mobb Deep, MI Abaga, Dagrin, and Wizkid, it retains a distinctive D-44 flavor—intimate, grounded, and immersive.




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Umar Muhammed White (@whitedapoet)




Every track contributes to a larger sonic and thematic arc. Rather than overproduced polish, the album embraces a raw, almost journal-like quality. This approach not only reinforces the personal nature of the project but also challenges prevailing trends in Nigeria’s commercial music scene.



The Collaborative Highlight: “Condoleezza” Featuring President Zik



A standout moment on the album is the track “Condoleezza,” featuring President Zik, also known as Prezzy. A respected figure in Nigeria’s underground music circuit, Zik brings both gravitas and finesse to the collaboration. His verse melds melodic cadence with philosophical reflections, enhancing the track’s emotional depth.




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by PREZZY 🇳🇬 (@presidentzik)




Zik’s role extends beyond the mic. As co-founder of the BHP collective and curator of the Urban Lifestyle Fest, his involvement symbolizes a bridge between past and present generations of alternative hip-hop. His feature on This Is D44 is not just musical—it’s cultural.



Cultural Impact and Broader Implications



What sets This Is D44 apart is its ability to transcend music. The project functions as:




A reclamation of narrative by artists working outside Lagos and other industry centers



A celebration of creative integrity in an era that often prizes conformity



A rallying cry for alternative voices in African hip-hop




Though it may not be engineered for radio spins or playlist placements, the album’s significance is undeniable. It reaffirms that Nigeria’s hip-hop scene is rich, alive, and evolving—especially in spaces that value substance over spectacle.







A Defining Moment for Nigerian Alt-Rap



This Is D44 firmly establishes Advocate Tha Chronicle and White Da Poet as thoughtful, intentional artists. They are not chasing trends—they are shaping the future. With this project, D-44 signals the emergence of a new voice in Nigerian hip-hop: bold, reflective, and uncompromising.



This debut is more than music—it is a moment. And if this is just the beginning, the future of alternative hip-hop in Nigeria looks more promising than ever.




Stream This Is D44

On June 27, Nigerian rapper Jason Nkanga will release his latest single, Pi—a cerebral and electrifying entry that continues his streak of genre-pushing hip-hop. Known for balancing razor-sharp lyricism with melodic experimentation, Jason stands out as one of the most consistent and creatively daring voices in African rap. 







Pi isn’t just a track—it’s a layered reflection of identity, intellect, and instinct woven into sound.



About the Artist: Jason Nkanga



Jason Nkanga first broke onto the scene with his 2014 debut Go Dumb. What followed was a steady rise fueled by lyrical intelligence and narrative depth. With standout projects like The Art of Rap (2018), a collaboration with Ghanaian rapper Jules Delø, and Redemption (2019) featuring Mick Jenkins, Blaqbonez, and theMIND, Jason positioned himself as both a student of the craft and an innovator within it.







His 2023 hit T-House Basement with PsychoYP cemented his presence, merging global drill influences with streetwise Nigerian flavor. In 2024, Jason returned with Real Talk and the One of One EP—an eclectic, collaborative effort featuring artists like MojoAF, Reeplay, and Tomi Obanure. With each release, Jason refines a sound that is equal parts intellectual and authentic, complex yet accessible.



The Meaning Behind ‘Pi’



Named after the mathematical constant π, Pi is both metaphor and mindset. Just as Pi is infinite and non-repeating, the song explores the limitless potential of creativity, thought, and personal evolution.




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Jason Nkanga (@jasonnkanga_)




Lyrically, Pi promises to deliver Jason’s signature rapid-fire delivery fused with philosophical reflections. The track draws from diverse sources—history, mathematics, culture, and the everyday grind—challenging listeners to engage beyond the surface.



Musically, expect a minimalist beat layered with deep bass and abstract sonic textures, creating a space where every word is amplified. It’s not just meant to be played—it’s meant to be decoded.



Inside the Creative Process



Jason approaches his work with precision and intentionality. Sharing insights into how Pi came together, he explains:



“I start by putting my phone on DND to avoid distractions while I’m in the studio, and I grab some snacks so I don’t have to get up and ruin the creative flow.”



He digs through numerous beats, searching for one that resonates. Once he finds it, writing begins—an intense, often uninterrupted session, where fact-checking mid-verse is standard practice.



“Sometimes I’m even researching while writing to make sure I get the facts 100% right.”



Jason then sends his draft through a trusted inner circle. Their feedback matters, but the final decision remains his:



“If they like it, I send it over for engineering. If they don’t, I bin it—but sometimes I’ll still send it over if I really like it, because at the end of the day, I get the final say.”



Recognition, Reach, and Cultural Footprint



As an independent artist, Jason Nkanga has achieved recognition that many signed acts still aspire to. His music has been featured on BBC platforms and in global campaigns with brands like Tommy Hilfiger. Media outlets such as Hunger Magazine, Notion Magazine, The Guardian Nigeria, and OkayAfrica have highlighted his voice and vision.



More than accolades, Jason has become a bridge-builder—connecting genres, cultures, and audiences. He isn’t chasing what’s popular. He’s constructing what’s next.



Why ‘Pi’ Matters Now



In an era where viral content often overshadows substance, Pi is a timely reminder of what thoughtful rap can be. Jason Nkanga continues to prove that hip-hop still has room for thinkers, strategists, and storytellers.



With Pi, Jason delivers a new kind of rap formula—where intellect meets instinct, and where drill is reimagined through depth and direction. As the June 27 release approaches, it’s clear that Jason isn’t just adding to the conversation—he’s rewriting the equation.

On June 27, Nigerian rapper Jason Nkanga will release his latest single, Pi—a cerebral and electrifying entry that continues his streak of genre-pushing hip-hop. Known for balancing razor-sharp lyricism with melodic experimentation, Jason stands out as one of the most consistent and creatively daring voices in African rap.

Pi isn’t just a track—it’s a layered reflection of identity, intellect, and instinct woven into sound.

About the Artist: Jason Nkanga

Jason Nkanga first broke onto the scene with his 2014 debut Go Dumb. What followed was a steady rise fueled by lyrical intelligence and narrative depth. With standout projects like The Art of Rap (2018), a collaboration with Ghanaian rapper Jules Delø, and Redemption (2019) featuring Mick Jenkins, Blaqbonez, and theMIND, Jason positioned himself as both a student of the craft and an innovator within it.

His 2023 hit T-House Basement with PsychoYP cemented his presence, merging global drill influences with streetwise Nigerian flavor. In 2024, Jason returned with Real Talk and the One of One EP—an eclectic, collaborative effort featuring artists like MojoAF, Reeplay, and Tomi Obanure. With each release, Jason refines a sound that is equal parts intellectual and authentic, complex yet accessible.

The Meaning Behind ‘Pi’

Named after the mathematical constant π, Pi is both metaphor and mindset. Just as Pi is infinite and non-repeating, the song explores the limitless potential of creativity, thought, and personal evolution.

Lyrically, Pi promises to deliver Jason’s signature rapid-fire delivery fused with philosophical reflections. The track draws from diverse sources—history, mathematics, culture, and the everyday grind—challenging listeners to engage beyond the surface.

Musically, expect a minimalist beat layered with deep bass and abstract sonic textures, creating a space where every word is amplified. It’s not just meant to be played—it’s meant to be decoded.

Inside the Creative Process

Jason approaches his work with precision and intentionality. Sharing insights into how Pi came together, he explains:

“I start by putting my phone on DND to avoid distractions while I’m in the studio, and I grab some snacks so I don’t have to get up and ruin the creative flow.”

He digs through numerous beats, searching for one that resonates. Once he finds it, writing begins—an intense, often uninterrupted session, where fact-checking mid-verse is standard practice.

“Sometimes I’m even researching while writing to make sure I get the facts 100% right.”

Jason then sends his draft through a trusted inner circle. Their feedback matters, but the final decision remains his:

“If they like it, I send it over for engineering. If they don’t, I bin it—but sometimes I’ll still send it over if I really like it, because at the end of the day, I get the final say.”

Recognition, Reach, and Cultural Footprint

As an independent artist, Jason Nkanga has achieved recognition that many signed acts still aspire to. His music has been featured on BBC platforms and in global campaigns with brands like Tommy Hilfiger. Media outlets such as Hunger Magazine, Notion Magazine, The Guardian Nigeria, and OkayAfrica have highlighted his voice and vision.

More than accolades, Jason has become a bridge-builder—connecting genres, cultures, and audiences. He isn’t chasing what’s popular. He’s constructing what’s next.

Why ‘Pi’ Matters Now

In an era where viral content often overshadows substance, Pi is a timely reminder of what thoughtful rap can be. Jason Nkanga continues to prove that hip-hop still has room for thinkers, strategists, and storytellers.

With Pi, Jason delivers a new kind of rap formula—where intellect meets instinct, and where drill is reimagined through depth and direction. As the June 27 release approaches, it’s clear that Jason isn’t just adding to the conversation—he’s rewriting the equation.

From the spirited streets of Hackney to the vibrant rhythms of Lagos, SamxCas — the British-Nigerian twin duo reshaping Afro Fusion — are back with a message wrapped in melody: “Better Days” are coming. The upcoming single, officially dropping June 27th, marks their most mature and emotionally charged release to date.







After building a steady following with standout tracks like Progress(feat. JeriQ), Ocean, Run Dis, and BAD (feat. HotKeed), SamxCas are poised to elevate their artistry with a single that reflects the evolution of not just their sound — but their souls.



WHO ARE SAMxCAS?



Born in Hackney. Rooted in Nigeria. Wired for Now.



SamxCas, born Samantha and Casilda Okan, are more than identical twins — they are identical visions moving in harmony. Rooted in storytelling, performance, and musical exploration, the London-born sisters have crafted a brand that blends melodic depth with visual elegance. From their early acting work in global productions to viral online content and head-turning fashion moments, every move they make speaks to a creative synergy most artists dream of.







But it’s music that centers them. Music that grounds them. And with every drop, they’re refining a sound that feels both deeply Afrocentric and uniquely SamxCas.



A New Era Begins



“Better Days” is a gentle storm — one part healing, one part hustle anthem. With silky harmonies riding over textured percussion and mellow strings, the twins channel a message of resilience, patience, and purpose. The production is fluid, fusing West African rhythms with UK alternative soul influences — a clear hallmark of their diasporic duality.




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by SAM X CAS ☆ (@samxcas_)





“We wrote ‘Better Days’ during a time when everything felt uncertain. It’s a reminder that light is always on the other side — for us, and for everyone listening.” — SamxCas




The song speaks not just to their fan base but to an entire generation navigating instability with hope in their hearts. It’s music for quiet nights, long drives, new beginnings — and for anyone who needs a gentle push forward.



Ready or Not?



With the global Afrobeat and Alté scenes rapidly expanding, SamxCas are carving out a signature sound within the Afro Fusion space — one that doesn’t rely on hype, but on honest emotion and sonic artistry. Their work isn’t tied to trends; it’s tied to truth.



Backed by a growing digital fanbase, their distribution deal with Dvpper Digital, and a clear visual aesthetic rooted in minimalism and bold femininity, “Better Days” represents a shift from potential to presence.



It’s the song you didn’t know you needed. And the song the culture deserves.

Emerging from Nigeria’s vibrant alternative music scene, Kida Oj returns with a dazzling new single titled Zodiac Sign—a genre-defying Afrodancehall track infused with rhythm, wit, and lyrical flair. 







Officially released on June 20, 2025, the song positions Kida Oj not only as a sonic innovator but also as a cultural bridge connecting Africa to the global Black diaspora through a humorous and heartfelt take on modern love and astrology.



About the Artist: Kida Oj



Born Ayomide Anota, Kida Oj has steadily carved out a niche for himself by blending Alté’s soulful introspection with Dancehall’s infectious energy. A proud figure in Abuja’s creative resurgence, his collaborative resume includes heavyweights like Zilla Oaks, Grammy-winning producer Phantom, and hitmaker Egar Boi.







More than his accolades, Kida Oj’s music reflects a broader mission: unifying Africans, Caribbeans, Black Americans, and diasporic communities through rhythm, storytelling, and shared cultural identity. His sound is marked by lyrical depth, genre fusion, and a deep understanding of the emotional textures that move listeners.



Zodiac Sign: A Playful Yet Poignant Story



At its heart, Zodiac Sign is more than just a feel-good anthem. It’s a cultural commentary wrapped in melody — a humorous, intimate take on how astrology influences modern romance.



In the artist’s own words:



“It’s a vibrant showcase of new-age dancehall music. I wanted it to feel nostalgic yet fresh — with piano chords, melodic vocals, and lyrics that speak to the complexities of dating woke women in this era. ‘Zodiac Sign’ starts off sweet and ends on a cheeky note, literally listing all the star signs like I’m trying to cover my bases.”









The track opens by celebrating “woke women” and quickly evolves into a tongue-in-cheek tale of romantic misadventures. In a playful twist, Kida confesses to lying about his star sign to win favor, creating an instantly relatable and catchy hook.



Lyrically, the song zooms in on a passionate yet complicated bond with an Aries woman—known for her boldness, independence, and sharp intuition. The outro, which calls out all twelve zodiac signs, wraps the track in inclusivity, giving everyone a moment in the spotlight.



A Future-Focused Fusion of Sound and Spirit



Zodiac Sign arrives at a cultural intersection where Black youth are embracing spirituality, identity, and authenticity. Kida Oj captures this zeitgeist perfectly by merging astrology with dancehall and blending humor with raw emotion. The result is a track that feels timely, personal, and globally resonant.




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by AYO🏆 (@popboy_kidaoj)




Whether you’re a Leo demanding attention, a Virgo analyzing the lyrics, or a Pisces feeling every note, this song offers a rhythm and a wink just for you.



Why It Matters: Bold, Relatable, and Ready to Travel



With Zodiac Sign, Kida Oj continues to distinguish himself in Nigeria’s new wave of music creators—bold in vision, rich in storytelling, and willing to take risks. As Alté and Afrodancehall continue to merge, this track stands as both a love letter to individuality and a showcase of genre-bending brilliance.




Stream Zodiac Sign

Who is Benvee?







Victor Sesugh Benjamin, better known by his stage name Benvee, is a Nigerian Afro singer, songwriter, stage performer, and brand ambassador steadily carving out a name for himself in the Nigerian music scene. Hailing from Kwande Local Government Area in Benue State, Benvee was born and raised in Kubwa, Abuja, where the rhythm of his surroundings helped shape the energy of his sound. He is not just a musician—he is a storyteller and a cultural voice of his generation, uniting melodies with meaning and passion with purpose.



Early Life & Background



Growing up in the capital city of Nigeria, Benvee completed both his primary and secondary education in Kubwa, a vibrant suburb of the Federal Capital Territory. Immersed in a cultural blend of sounds and street stories, it was only a matter of time before Benvee’s passion for music took center stage in his life. After years of writing, freestyling, and performing locally, he took the bold leap to become a full-time solo artist.



Career Launch & Breakthrough




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by RADARCharts by REM (@remradar)




Benvee officially launched his professional music career in 2017, but it wasn’t until 2021 that his talent started receiving widespread attention. In 2022, he dropped his first official single “God Ahbeg,” a raw and resonant anthem that quickly became a street favorite—not just in Kubwa but across the broader Abuja music community. The track stood out for its emotionally honest lyrics, catchy hooks, and Benvee’s unmistakable vocal delivery. It announced his arrival not just as a singer, but as a movement of sound and soul.



The EP: “HERE TO STAY”



Riding on the success and growing love from fans, Benvee released his debut Extended Play (EP) titled “HERE TO STAY.” The 7-track project was a bold artistic statement—a fusion of Afro rhythms, soul, street-hop, and introspective songwriting. The EP was produced, mixed, and mastered by top-tier Nigerian producers and engineers, giving it the professional polish that matched Benvee’s raw talent. 









Each track reflects different layers of his journey—from hustle to hope, from pain to pride. The title “HERE TO STAY” isn’t just a declaration—it’s a mission. It reflects the unwavering belief Benvee has in his craft, and a promise to fans that he’s not going anywhere.



Sound & Influence



Benvee’s sound is best described as Afro-centric with emotional depth, combining melodic Afrobeat with indigenous lyricism and honest storytelling. 







His style draws influence from everyday Nigerian life—its joys, struggles, spirituality, and resilience. With a compelling vocal tone and authentic delivery, he speaks directly to his listeners, especially the youth and streets that raised him.



Brand Collaborations & Representation



As a growing force in the entertainment space, Benvee has also served as a brand ambassador, leveraging his growing popularity to represent youth-centered brands and cultural initiatives. His image, confidence, and community roots make him a natural fit for collaborations, especially those targeting the rising Afro youth culture in Nigeria and beyond.



What’s Next?



Benvee’s journey is only just beginning. With more music, visuals, collaborations, and performances in the pipeline, fans can expect even more evolution from the young creative. His resilience, authenticity, and sonic identity mark him as one of Abuja’s brightest exports. He’s not just another name in the Afrobeat wave—he’s a voice of his people.



Benvee is officially On The RADAR.

INTRODUCING FISSTYJR







In a generation bursting with musical talent, one name is steadily climbing the radar in Nigeria’s Afrobeats landscape: FisstyJR. Born Abdulbasit on June 13th, 1999, this Port Harcourt native has found a new home in Abuja, where his sound continues to evolve, influence, and ignite a growing fanbase. With a fearless approach to fusion and a voice that cuts through with clarity and confidence, FisstyJR is fast becoming a name to know.



ROOTS & RISE



Hailing from the vibrant city of Port Harcourt, Rivers State, FisstyJR discovered his artistic calling early. By high school, he was already penning lyrics, vibing to classic rhythms, and performing with an energy that marked him out from his peers. What started as a hobby quickly grew into a passion—and now, a purposeful career.



His move to Abuja placed him right in the center of a buzzing creative scene, and he’s made it his playground for pushing boundaries and creating something new.



SOUND & STYLE



Crowned the “King of Afro New School”, FisstyJR doesn’t just make music—he builds sonic bridges between genres. His signature sound draws from:










Afro fusion



Afro house



Hip-hop



Reggae



Old school grooves




This melting pot of influences delivers music that’s both nostalgic and futuristic—crafted to make you feel, move, and think. Whether it’s a soulful hook, a danceable beat, or a reflective verse, there’s always depth behind his delivery.



MISSION & MESSAGE



FisstyJR’s artistry goes beyond vibes. At his core, he’s a storyteller, using music as a medium of inspiration and connection. For him, every song is a message, and every performance a moment to spark something deeper in his listeners.









He’s not just trying to top charts—he’s working to touch hearts, spread positivity, and leave a lasting legacy.



WHERE HE’S HEADED



With Abuja as his base and the world as his stage, FisstyJR is actively gearing up for his next big leap. From studio sessions to live appearances, every step is part of a bigger plan—to place Afro New School on the global map.







As more fans tune in and his name echoes beyond Nigeria’s borders, it’s clear: FisstyJR is not just an artist to watch—he’s an artist to remember.

Emerging from the vibrant music scene of Lagos, Nigeria, Jayslite is a singer-songwriter whose artistry seamlessly blends Afrobeat with alternative sounds, crafting a unique sonic identity that resonates deeply with listeners. His music is characterized by infectious rhythms, soulful melodies, and introspective lyrics that explore themes of love, life, and personal growth.







A Deep Connection to Roots



Born and raised in Nigeria, Jayslite’s profound connection to his cultural heritage is evident in his music. He draws inspiration from the rich tapestry of Nigerian musical traditions, infusing his songs with elements that reflect the country’s diverse sounds. This fusion creates a contemporary yet deeply rooted musical experience that honors his origins while appealing to a global audience.



Musical Style and Influences







Jayslite’s distinctive style is marked by a dynamic blend of Afrobeat and alternative genres. His smooth vocals are complemented by a rich array of instruments, creating an immersive and emotionally resonant soundscape. Through his music, he seeks to inspire, uplift, and empower listeners, envisioning his songs as sources of comfort and encouragement.



Notable Works and Recognition



One of Jayslite’s standout tracks, “Kpe Kpe,” has been highlighted for its infectious energy and uplifting message. The song embodies resilience and positivity, embracing the essence of Afro-fusion and showcasing his ability to create music that resonates with a wide audience. He currently released ‘Live it Up’ an amazing blend of reggae and good ryhtmn









Looking Ahead



As Jayslite continues to evolve as an artist, he remains committed to creating music that reflects his soul and connects with listeners on a profound level. With a vision to contribute positively to society through his art, he stands as a promising figure in the Afrobeat and alternative music scenes, poised to make a lasting impact both in Nigeria and beyond.



For those seeking music that combines heartfelt storytelling with captivating rhythms, Jayslite offers a refreshing and emotionally resonant experience that speaks to the heart and soul.

Emerging Nigerian artist TMJ has joined lyrical forces with streetwise rapper OG Mage on the hard-hitting new single “YAWA” — an emotionally charged protest song that strikes at the heart of Nigeria’s social and political struggles. 







Now available on all major streaming platforms, “YAWA” isn’t just music — it’s a movement, a message, and a mirror of our times.



A Song That Speaks for the People



“YAWA” opens with a haunting saxophone solo that immediately signals the gravity of the message to come. Over a soulful and melancholic Afrobeats instrumental, TMJ delivers raw, unfiltered vocals filled with emotion, honesty, and pain — speaking directly to the lived experiences of everyday Nigerians.









From street violence and poverty to corruption, disunity, and political betrayal, the song shines a spotlight on the systemic issues that continue to plague the country. OG Mage’s gritty verse injects a street perspective, amplifying the urgency of the track’s message and adding another layer of depth and authenticity.




“We can only rise if we stand together,” says TMJ — a bold declaration that runs as a core theme through the entire song.




A National Wake-Up Call



With lyrics like “A brother man killing a brother man, why?” and “Yawa don enter the matter”, the song doesn’t shy away from asking the hard questions. But rather than only highlight the pain, “YAWA” pushes for unity, awareness, and collective healing. It echoes the sentiments of a youth population yearning for change, both at home and across the diaspora.



This track is tailor-made for playlists and programs that focus on conscious music, Afrobeats with substance, and homegrown Nigerian talent. It also aligns powerfully with communities championing social justice, youth advocacy, and grassroots movements across Africa.



Lyrical Highlights



Here are a few standout lines from the powerful chorus:




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Samuel Ogaba (@ogmagegram)





“Yawa dey ooh



The thing wey I see, na the thing I want to talk ooh



People dem dey suffer, my people just dey suffer”




And from OG Mage’s verse:




“Naija is truly blessed, really nobody dey drag am



But oga at the top dey sell us out, pocket the raba”




Each line is delivered with intention, laying bare the raw emotional weight of Nigeria’s current state — while simultaneously stirring hope and resistance.




Stream ‘YAWA’

With the release of his bold new full-length project ‘You Make Me Feel’, Nigerian artist and producer Raytheboffin invites us into a realm where dance meets depth and rhythm meets raw emotion. Out via Outer South, this mixtape isn’t just a listening experience—it’s a movement. Spanning Afro-fusion, Jersey Club, Amapiano, and House, Ray builds an audio universe that’s as intimate as it is expansive.







Coming off a string of magnetic releases and clocking in over 700,000 streams, Raytheboffin’s evolution has never sounded so clear—or so fearless.



A COMING-OF-AGE IN SOUND



At its core, You Make Me Feel is about emotion in motion. Whether it’s heartbreak, ego, freedom, or release, Ray brings a refreshing honesty to every beat and every bar. The mixtape documents the tension between longing and liberation, using genre as a tool—not a box.









Each track is meticulously produced, layered with shimmering synths, off-kilter rhythms, and voice notes that blur the line between the personal and the performative. It’s club music with heart. Vulnerability with a side of bass.



STANDOUT TRACKS YOU NEED TO HEAR









 “what you think this is” ft. Ayüü



This track struts and stares all at once. Ray and Ayüü ride a gritty Amapiano bounce with effortless confidence, asking the listener (and maybe themselves): What exactly is this game we’re playing? It’s a swaggering moment of reflection—an anthem for uncertainty.



 “burn my shit” ft. Webmoms



This one hits like a digital breakup text sent through subwoofers. With frenetic Jersey Club drums, smoky synth layers, and glitchy production, “burn my shit” is pure catharsis. It’s the sound of letting go—and dancing while you do it.



“interplanetary” (Focus Track)



The heart of the project. “interplanetary” is your passport to the other side of the moon. Euphoric, hypnotic, and otherworldly, this track blends cosmic synths and clubby percussion into something spiritual. It’s both invitation and escape—Ray’s mission statement in a single track.



Cold Summer with Suté Iwar & Sinachi is a classic



COLLABORATIVE ENERGY AT ITS FINEST



From the soul-tinged vocal layers of Ayüü to the experimental fire of Webmoms, and the dynamic synergy with DAP The Contract, Tim Lyre, and Iver Rivers on previous releases, Ray continues to curate a creative circle that reflects his range and vision. These aren’t just features—they’re co-pilots on the journey.



BEYOND THE MUSIC: RAYTHEBOFFIN AS SONIC ARCHITECT



Raytheboffin doesn’t just make tracks—he builds sonic architecture. He uses space and silence like tools, balancing minimalism with maximal emotion. His work resonates with a generation navigating love, loneliness, and legacy, all in the glow of club lights and bedroom ceilings.







With each release, he cements his role not just as an artist, but as a cultural futurist—someone who sees the club as a church, the beat as a diary, and the mixtape as memoir.



WHY THIS PROJECT MATTERS



In an era of short attention spans and cookie-cutter drops, You Make Me Feel dares to be something more. It’s immersive, intentional, and infinitely replayable. It doesn’t chase virality—it creates gravity.



This is Raytheboffin’s leap. Not into mainstream complacency, but into artistic mastery.




Stream ‘you make me feel’

Rhia Bello is a Nigerian-British singer, songwriter, and creative visionary reshaping the sonic landscape of contemporary soul and alté music. With roots stretching from Lagos to London, her music is a fusion of cultures, emotions, and timeless narratives. She draws from a well of personal truth, offering listeners a sound that is both soothing and profound.







Emerging as a standout voice in the global alté and neo-soul movement, Rhia’s artistry is defined by vulnerability, introspection, and elegance. Inspired by iconic women like Sade, Tems, and Solange, she channels feminine power through subtlety and grace.



MUSIC & STYLE



Rhia’s music transcends genre constraints while remaining grounded in emotional storytelling. Her sound is built on a foundation of soulful melodies, ambient production, and rich lyrical content. Each track is a reflection of her identity, capturing the tension and harmony of navigating multiple worlds. She blends elements of R&B, Neo-Soul, Alté, and Afro influences with effortless fluidity. Her lyrics dive deep into themes of vulnerability, self-discovery, and spiritual growth, all while maintaining a sonic palette that is lush, atmospheric, and rhythmically subtle. 




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by R H I A  B 💫✨ (@rhia_bello)




LIVE PRESENCE



Rhia Bello’s live performances are immersive and soulful. Whether performing in a gallery space in London or an outdoor festival in Lagos, her shows are carefully crafted experiences that leave lasting impressions. Her stripped-down setups emphasize authenticity and voice, allowing her storytelling to take center stage.







Her performance style:



Intimate band arrangements that highlight the emotional core of each song Visual storytelling aligned with her brand—minimal, elegant, and Afrocentric Themes of healing, empowerment, and introspective discovery woven into her setlists



She has performed at showcases, cultural events, and creative sessions in cities like London, Lagos, and New York, building a reputation for delivering performances that are both grounded and transcendent.



BRAND & CREATIVE VISION



Rhia Bello represents more than just a sound—she embodies a creative movement. Her vision is rooted in self-expression, cultural pride, and the pursuit of artistic truth. As an advocate for women, the diaspora, and mental health, her work often extends beyond music and into collaborative projects with other creatives.









Core pillars of Rhia’s brand:



Artistry fused with advocacy, creating space for conversations around identity and wellness Aesthetic rooted in Afro-futurism and femininity, blending traditional elements with modern expression A multidisciplinary approach that includes partnerships with fashion designers, poets, and visual artists

Introducing a fresh, authentic voice to the Afrobeat landscape, County makes his official debut with the deeply personal and emotionally resonant single “64 Kids.” Now available on all streaming platforms, the track marks a defining first step for the UK-based Nigerian artist whose sound is rooted in both heritage and heart.









The Sound of Love and Memory



“64 Kids” blends the warm, infectious rhythm of Afrobeats with the smooth, expressive feel of Afro-Soul. Built on layered percussion, soft melodies, and reflective lyrics, the track captures the emotional journey of a young man navigating love — not only through words and feelings, but also through acts of care and generosity.




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by M A Z Z A  ⭐️ (@county_kuti)




Reminiscent of early ‘90s Nigerian love songs, “64 Kids” is nostalgic in tone, yet unmistakably modern in its delivery. It’s a refreshing take on romance, grounded in cultural context and elevated by County’s calm yet captivating vocal performance.



Inspired by True Life



For County, this isn’t just music — it’s memory. The song was born from real-life experiences and a desire to turn vulnerability into sound. “I wanted to make a song off what I really feel,” County shares. That authenticity pulses through every lyric, making “64 Kids” not just a track, but a conversation — a story shared with listeners who know what it means to love with intention.



A New Chapter in Afrobeat Storytelling



County’s artistry is defined by emotional depth, sincerity, and an unwavering connection to culture. Where much of today’s Afrobeats centers on energy and elevation, County offers intimacy and introspection — without losing the pulse that drives the genre.







With cultural roots in Lagos and creative growth in the UK, his debut offers a cross-cultural richness that positions him uniquely in the global Afrobeat movement. “64 Kids” is proof that romantic storytelling, when told with honesty, never goes out of style.




Stream ’64 Kids’

Ánesi’s upcoming single ALKEBULAN draws its name from a term embraced by Pan-African and Afrocentric movements as the ancient identity of Africa—Alkebulan, meaning “mother of mankind.” Though its historical use is debated, the symbolism it carries is powerful: a return to origins, pride, and legacy.







With ALKEBULAN, Ánesi channels this symbolism into sound—offering listeners a transcendent prelude that bridges ancestral memory with forward-thinking artistry.



A Sonic Interpretation of Identity



In this new release, Ánesi fuses African acapella with Afrobeats, R&B, rock, and experimental electronica. The result is a rich, genre-bending soundscape that feels both ceremonial and futuristic. Her layered harmonies rise like echoes of the past, while the production propels us into tomorrow.

County (real name Abdulazeez Adam Temidayo) is an emerging Afrobeat and Afro-Soul artist whose roots run deep in Lagos, Nigeria, and whose voice now echoes from the United Kingdom. With a musical style that blends African rhythms, heartfelt storytelling, and soulful vocal textures, County is setting the stage for a dynamic entry into the global music scene.







Now, he’s ready to debut his very first Afrobeats single — 64 Kids — a track that promises to tug at the heartstrings while keeping fans moving.



ABOUT THE SONG: “64 KIDS”



64 Kids isn’t just a love song — it’s a time capsule wrapped in rhythm. Channeling the energy of early 1990s Afrobeats, County takes listeners on an emotional journey, exploring what it means to love out loud — with feeling, with action, and yes, with money.








“It’s a classic love story. The kind where a young man doesn’t just say he loves you — he shows it,” says County. “I wanted to make a song off what I really feel. It’s my real life, my real emotion — but told in a way everyone can feel and vibe to.”




Built on warm percussion, lush harmonies, and catchy melodic phrasing, the song evokes a nostalgic Afro feel while remaining unmistakably modern.



CREATIVE PROCESS & INSPIRATION



The creative spark behind 64 Kids is rooted in true life experience. According to County, the song came from a space of reflection — moments lived, love expressed, and lessons learned. This isn’t just a studio-crafted story; it’s a diary entry wrapped in melody.




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by M A Z Z A  ⭐️ (@county_kuti)





“This was about turning my own reality into rhythm,” he explains. “Every line came from a place of honesty. I wanted it to feel like a conversation — like you’re right there with me in that moment.”




This authenticity is what sets County apart as a storyteller and sound architect.



REPRESENTING THE NEW SCHOOL



County is part of a new wave of African artists blending culture, emotion, and creativity, crossing continents while staying grounded in their heritage. His music represents not just a sound, but a movement of cultural fusion — where Lagos meets London, and personal stories become universal songs.



As an artist, County embodies class, charisma, and connection — the three Cs that are quickly becoming his signature.

Nigerian Afro-fusion artist Khalie—popularly known as Big Khalie—is back with another infectious banger titled Fatassi, just weeks after setting the tone for 2025 with his first single of the year, Friday. 







The rising star continues to deliver bold, feel-good music that connects with fans on the dancefloor and in the heart.



About Fatassi



Released last Friday, Fatassi dives into a sultry groove that fuses Afrobeat with funk-inspired undertones. Khalie’s smooth delivery and rhythmic cadence give life to a passionate confession as he expresses his desires to his lover. It’s a song that radiates sensual energy while keeping things light, vibrant, and irresistibly danceable.









The track showcases Khalie’s knack for balancing lyrical intimacy with rhythmic excellence. The production is rich with live-sounding instruments, catchy hooks, and a pulsating beat that instantly grabs attention—making Fatassi a strong contender for playlists and club rotations.



The Rise of Big Khalie



Adeyemo Khalil, professionally known as Khalie or Big Khalie, is making waves in the Afro-fusion scene with his consistent delivery of standout tracks. Hailing from Kwara State, Khalie’s music is a celebration of rhythm, emotion, and cultural storytelling. His recent hits like Steady Riddim (Move), Blessings (Shower), Friday, and now Fatassi have solidified his reputation as an artist to watch in 2025.







Big Khalie’s sound is uniquely his own—a rich fusion of Afrobeat, funk, and contemporary vibes, paired with heartfelt lyricism and high-energy performances. As he continues to expand his catalog, each new release deepens his musical identity and connects him with a growing audience across Nigeria and beyond.



What’s Next for Khalie?



With Fatassi following so closely behind Friday, fans are speculating that a larger body of work may be on the horizon. Whether it’s a full EP or a string of singles, one thing is certain—Big Khalie is not letting up in 2025.




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by BIGKHXLIE🌶🎼 (@bigkhxlie)




Stay tuned for more music, visuals, and surprises from one of Nigeria’s most dynamic emerging artists.




Stream ‘Fatassi’

Introduction: A Voice from the Trenches



In an era where rap often leans towards the glamorized, Sweat and Blood by Advocatee Tha Chronicle stands firmly in its own lane — grounded, introspective, and unshakably real. The track is a bold offering that blends lyrical depth with emotional weight, laying bare the struggles, sacrifices, and strength it takes to rise from humble beginnings.







Advocatee Tha Chronicle, one-half of the Nigerian rap duo D-44, steps into the spotlight with this solo record, carving out space for his personal testimony. More than just a song, Sweat and Blood is a poetic journal entry soaked in experience — the kind that can’t be bought or borrowed, only lived.



The Track: Pain, Passion, and Perseverance



On Sweat and Blood, Advocatee channels his personal experiences into potent lyricism. The production is minimalist yet immersive, allowing his voice to take center stage — a deliberate choice that underscores the weight of his message.









According to the artist, “We made this song out of the desire to represent our struggles and tell the stories of the pain that have defined our journeys.” This narrative forms the emotional backbone of the track — from moments of vulnerability to glimpses of unbreakable resolve.



It’s a song that speaks directly to anyone who has ever fought for their place in a world that doesn’t always listen. Whether it’s the grind of a student balancing school and survival, or the tension of holding onto a dream in the face of reality, Sweat and Blood finds the words many are unable to say.



D-44: Hip-Hop Brotherhood Rooted in Purpose



D-44 is the dynamic collaboration between Advocatee Tha Chronicle and White Da Poet, two visionary lyricists hailing from Jalingo and Ibadan respectively. The duo’s paths crossed at Ahmadu Bello University (ABU) Zaria, a meeting that sparked a shared mission: to use hip-hop as a vessel for truth, identity, and resilience.







Their music is a melting pot of sonic and cultural influences, paying homage to Nigerian and global icons alike — from the introspective calm of Show Dem Camp to the street-coded storytelling of Dagrin, the lyrical mastery of MI Abaga, the raw East Coast grit of Mobb Deep, and the global appeal of Wizkid. With each release, D-44 continues to challenge the status quo, offering music that is both thought-provoking and sonically compelling.



Lyrical Substance in a Melodic Frame



Advocatee’s performance is a masterclass in delivery. Every bar carries intention, shaped by a cadence that is both assertive and reflective. The beat — soulful, stripped-down, yet cinematic — leaves room for the lyrics to breathe, and for the listener to feel.









He doesn’t rely on flashy punchlines or viral hooks. Instead, the strength of the track lies in its sincerity. Each verse is layered with meaning, from tales of personal loss to the quiet triumphs that often go unseen. It’s a record that demands repeat listens, not just for enjoyment, but for understanding.



Final Thoughts: A Bold Testament of Grit and Growth



With Sweat and Blood, Advocatee Tha Chronicle proves that vulnerability is a strength — especially in hip-hop. The track is a reminder that music, at its core, is storytelling. And Advocatee’s story is far from over; in fact, it’s just beginning.



For listeners who appreciate rap with depth, poetry with pain, and verses that mean something — this is your next essential listen.




Stream Now

KING STUNNA’s “Fall Out” Is Out Now — And It’s Already Making Waves Across Borders




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by KING STUNNA (@iamkingstunna)




Since its release on May 8, 2025, KING STUNNA’s explosive new single “Fall Out” has been catching fire across Nigeria and beyond, racking up streams, sparking conversation, and reaffirming his place as one of Africa’s most compelling hip-hop voices. Gritty, raw, and unfiltered, the track isn’t just being heard—it’s being felt.



A Voice Born of the Streets, Built for the World



Emerging from Nigeria’s ever-evolving music landscape, KING STUNNA has long been recognized for his ability to fuse streetwise storytelling with global ambition. His unique blend of Pidgin and English, combined with bold lyricism and undeniable charisma, has already earned him chart placements in Nigeria, Malaysia, and Brunei. Now, “Fall Out” is pushing that reach even further.







The Making of a Moment: “Fall Out”



Produced by PapiGunzo, “Fall Out” hits hard from the first beat. The instrumental sparked something deep in STUNNA, triggering an instinctive creative process that unfolded quickly and without compromise.



“I wasn’t writing to impress anyone,” he shares. “I was documenting my energy, my city, my madness.”



From the freestyle hook to verses written in one emotionally charged sitting, every bar hits with purpose. KING STUNNA raps with an urgency that cuts through the noise—talking about dodging daily pressure, navigating relationships, and staying untouchable in the face of adversity. It’s the sound of someone with nothing to prove but everything to say.



A Raw Sound for Real Life



“Fall Out” isn’t polished for playlists—it’s sculpted from the grind. The production is hard-hitting and minimal, letting STUNNA’s voice carry the weight of each word. It’s hip-hop stripped of vanity and dressed in realness.









“No filters, no smoothing edges. I didn’t want it to sound polished—I wanted it to sound honest.”



Listeners have responded. The song is being shared in WhatsApp groups, reposted on TikTok, and featured on underground hip-hop playlists across continents. For those tuned into the global wave of street-rooted, lyrically rich African rap—this is a defining moment.



KING STUNNA’s Global Rise



With “Fall Out,” KING STUNNA cements his standing as a global contender in the next era of African hip-hop. His music isn’t just crossing borders—it’s breaking them. And as he continues to defy expectations, he’s taking the stories of his city, his hustle, and his truth along with him.



Stream “Fall Out” now and experience the raw power of a voice that won’t be ignored.



Listen Here: https://awal.ffm.to/fallout

In a defining moment for African music culture, Nigerian rapper and visionary artist TELMAN has officially been announced as the RADARMan—the flagship face of the RADARCharts Union and creative empire. This appointment not only solidifies his rising star status but also marks the beginning of a powerful synergy between artistic excellence and visionary enterprise.







A Movement, Not Just a Title



For those watching the evolution of Afrocentric hip-hop and global underground talent, TELMAN is no stranger. Born Chukwuemeka Rich Ifeanyi in Enugu State, Nigeria, TELMAN’s art has always stood at the intersection of purpose and raw poetic energy. His work is laced with cultural wisdom, street perspective, and spiritual undercurrents—an embodiment of the RADARCharts ethos: “To discover, support, and amplify the gems of the future.”









RADARCharts is more than just a music platform. It is a three-pronged cultural powerhouse—RADARCharts, RADARMusic, and REM (RADAR Entertainment Management)—focusing on storytelling, representation, and artist development. And at the center of it all now stands TELMAN, not just as a representative, but as the heartbeat of a movement.



“I Expect Greatness” — TELMAN on His New Era



In an exclusive quote following the announcement of his new management deal with RADARCharts, TELMAN shared:




“I expect greatness in teamwork. I love working with people or organisations that understand the vision and key in to it. So I expect greatness and nothing less. And my fans should expect the best from T.”








This isn’t just PR talk—it’s a reaffirmation of TELMAN’s creative clarity and commitment to purpose. From his early days of writing verses in his dorm room to releasing REBIRTH, a deeply spiritual and emotionally intelligent project, TELMAN has never strayed from being intentional about his path.



With this new partnership, TELMAN is no longer just navigating the industry—he’s helping define it.



Why TELMAN Is the Perfect RADARMan



RADARCharts needed a face who doesn’t just look like the future, but one who sounds, moves, and builds like the future. TELMAN checks every box:










Artistry: A blend of introspective lyricism, trap energy, and conscious narrative.

articles.body:
The Voice of the Future Emerges from Nigeria



In the ever-evolving landscape of global Hip-Hop, few artists carry both the grit and grace of a generational voice. 







Enter TELMAN — the official RADARMan of RADARCharts, a creative visionary who is about to shake the scene once again with his upcoming single, “BLACK N WHITE,” dropping on June 6th, 2025.



More Than Music: The Rise of a Movement



Born Chukwuemeka Rich Ifeanyi, TELMAN is not just another rapper. He is the front runner of the RADARCharts company and union — a symbolic torchbearer for a movement rooted in creativity, confidence, and cultural authenticity. His emergence signals not just a sonic evolution, but a shift in the entire creative economy of West Africa.







His artistry is shaped by faith, family, and fierce originality. Raised in Akpugo, Enugu State, Nigeria, TELMAN channels the introspective poise of Dave, the emotional texture of Drake, and the raw spirit of Nasty C, fusing melodic trap with poetic precision.



What to Expect from “BLACK N WHITE”



From the teasers and early listening sessions, “BLACK N WHITE” already feels like a declaration of independence. Produced by the genius Tytaan, the track is an autobiographical burst of energy, addressing jealousy, self-awareness, and personal growth.



Lyrically, it’s a punchline-heavy, emotionally reflective anthem that challenges conformity — “I don’t see myself in their midst black and white,” TELMAN raps, delivering a message that’s both personal and universal. It’s the kind of record that hits immediately, but also rewards deeper listens.







Self-Belief as a Weapon



TELMAN himself describes the track as a tribute to self-confidence and respect. Sparked by a real-life moment of being doubted, “BLACK N WHITE” is a response without retaliation — a step back instead of a swing. In his words, “when you’re so aware and confident in yourself, no one can really make you feel bad for being different.”



This is not just a song—it’s a statement. One that fits perfectly within the mission of RADARCharts to amplify undiscovered gems and foster global-scale storytelling through music.



From Campus Stories to Cultural Shifts



“BLACK N WHITE” has roots in university gossip, but blooms into a worldwide narrative. TELMAN’s creative process for this record was swift, yet intentional—built from experience, charged with emotion, and packaged in a sound that speaks volumes.







He’s not just giving us music. He’s giving us therapy, motivation, and a mirror.



What’s Next: The Vision



The release of “BLACK N WHITE” will be followed by a feature on TALK TO US Magazine, where TELMAN dives deeper into his journey, his mindset, and his goals. Expect exclusive insights and behind-the-scenes looks at how the RADARMan is shaping the future of African music, fashion, and visual storytelling.



As TELMAN puts it: “I’m not just chasing greatness—I’m designing it.”




Visit ‘TELMAN’

A Timely Anthem for a Troubled World



As the world trembles under the weight of systemic injustice, cultural decay, and silent suffering, one voice is rising from Abuja with clarity, conviction, and courage. 







Teeroy Tyobee, the inspirational musician and writer, is set to release “Wise Up”—a fearless Afrobeat anthem that addresses mental slavery, inequality, and the pressing need for collective consciousness. More than just music, this is a call to arms for a generation teetering between delusion and awakening.



Artist Spotlight: The Messenger Behind the Mic



Teeroy Tyobee is not your average Afrobeat artist. Born in Africa and based in Abuja, he is a storyteller, healer, and spiritual traveler, using music as a vessel for change. A devout member of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, Teeroy’s work is infused with faith and fire—deeply rooted in African consciousness yet reaching universal truth. An unwavering commitment to truth, transformation, and transcendence marks his artistic journey.







Inside the Message: What Is ‘Wise Up’ Really About?



“Wise Up” is more than a song—it’s a battle cry against the silent plague of mental slavery, which Teeroy describes as a more dangerous form of oppression than any physical chain. In his words:



“Until we abolish mental slavery, we are just preaching a gospel of false hopes and delusions.”




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by TeeRoy Tyobee (@teeroy_tyobee)




The song challenges listeners to examine the narratives that shape our identities, the thought patterns that keep us stuck, and the systems that benefit from our silence. It is both a warning and a torchlight—guiding people toward self-awareness, critical thinking, and collective emancipation.



Musical Composition: Afrobeat Meets Soulful Resistance



Drawing from the rhythmic pulse of Afrobeat and the emotional gravity of soul music, “Wise Up” is an immersive listening experience. Expect:




Layered percussion that roots the track in African tradition



Bold horns and urgent guitar riffs that mirror the energy of protest



A crescendo of instrumentation that reflects the rising tide of resistance and awakening




Teeroy’s vocal delivery is equal parts prophetic and poetic, oscillating between soft introspection and impassioned declaration.



Themes to Watch For:




Mental Slavery: The invisible chains that keep people bound despite physical freedom



Systemic Inequality: How social structures maintain oppression



Self-Liberation: The power of individual awareness and growth



Collective Action: Building a better future through unity and purpose




Mood & Atmosphere: Urgent, Soulful, Revolutionary



The emotional resonance of “Wise Up” lies in its duality. It is angry yet hopeful, critical yet compassionate, intellectual yet deeply spiritual. It invites listeners not only to feel—but to act.



Why This Matters Now: Nigeria, Africa, and the Global Pulse



In Nigeria and across Africa, communities are dealing with generational trauma, political unrest, and a youth culture caught between apathy and action. Globally, marginalized people continue to struggle under the weight of systemic injustice.



“Wise Up” arrives as a mirror and a megaphone—a reflection of the times and a bold call to change them.



Prepare to Wake Up



Teeroy Tyobee’s “Wise Up” isn’t just for music lovers—it’s for freedom fighters, thinkers, and dreamers ready to challenge the status quo. It’s the song you didn’t know you needed, dropping soon to shake up playlists and perspectives alike.



Stay ready. The revolution will be rhythmic.

Snowfella, the rising Igbo rapper known for blending street wisdom with haunting cinematic energy, is back with a powerful new freestyle titled “Aristotle”, dropping May 14. This isn’t just another track—it’s a philosophical deep-dive into the mind of a young man navigating pain, survival, and the search for meaning in chaos.







Hailing from the streets of Owerri, Snowfella’s style is unmistakable: raw, real, and laced with unfiltered emotion. His music is a gritty mirror reflecting life’s harshest truths, layered over haunting beats that stick with you long after the song ends. With “Aristotle (Freestyle)”, he steps further into the role of a street philosopher, offering bars soaked in introspection and truth.








“The title Aristotle came to me because I was in a headspace where I felt like a street philosopher,” Snowfella shares. “I wasn’t just rapping to rhyme—I was trying to make sense of chaos.”




Unlike many polished singles, Aristotle was recorded in one take, capturing the raw, unfiltered emotion that Snowfella is known for. No pen. No paper. Just a beat that unlocked a memory—and a mindset.



This freestyle is more than music—it’s a moment of clarity, a journal entry from someone who’s lived on the edge and come back with lessons wrapped in rhyme. Spitting in Igbo, Pidgin, and English, Snowfella’s words cut deep and carry weight.



Why You Should Pre-Save “Aristotle”




It’s a freestyle with depth—unfiltered, philosophical, and grounded in real-life pain.



If you’re a fan of conscious rap, dark visuals, or soul-stirring lyricism, this one’s for you.



It marks another chapter in Snowfella’s rise as a voice for the misunderstood.




Don’t miss this drop.Pre-save “Aristotle (Freestyle)” now and be among the first to hear Snowfella’s truth from the shadows.



📅 Release Date: May 14
