Daren FOB, an emerging force in Nigeria’s music scene, is set to release his highly anticipated EP, Enter: Vibe God. Known for his eclectic mix of Afrobeats and a variety of other genres, Daren’s music transcends the boundaries of typical African sounds, weaving together stories of love, loss, and personal growth. This powerful body of work, which features a collaboration with Project Arrow, paints a vivid picture of the complexities of modern relationships and the journey to self-discovery.







Born in Port-Harcourt but raised in Abuja, Daren FOB’s roots are as diverse as his sound. With a self-taught foundation in music and formal training at the prestigious Carnegie Institute, his influences are a blend of cultural sounds and global music icons. Drawing inspiration from the likes of Elton John, Asake, and Burna Boy, Daren has cultivated a musical identity that reflects his unique upbringing and the eclectic world he inhabits.



His notable achievements include a show at a stadium in Kaduna and opening for Asake in Abuja—marking Daren FOB as an artist to watch closely in the Nigerian music scene. But his rise is not solely attributed to his stage presence; his sound is what truly sets him apart. Combining soulful melodies, infectious rhythms, and raw, introspective lyrics, Daren creates an atmosphere where music becomes a therapeutic tool for listeners to connect with their own emotions.



The Creative Process Behind Enter: Vibe God



In Daren’s own words, Enter: Vibe God is more than just an album—it’s a personal diary, a story of growth through pain and redemption. “EVG unfolds the story of a young man who captivates a love interest, only to spiral into a toxic relationship that shatters his confidence. Seeking fulfilment, he ventures into increasingly high-stakes business dealings—until he reaches a breaking point and turns to God for guidance,” Daren explains. “This EP retells various stories from my life, fuelled by the lows of depression and the euphoria of love.”









The EP’s tracks range from the upbeat, groove-driven Lamba to the introspective Prayer for Life, where Daren’s vulnerability shines through. Turn Off the Lights, featuring Project Arrow, offers a smooth and captivating collaboration that shows Daren’s versatility as an artist, fusing genres with ease and inviting listeners into his reflective world.



What to Expect From Enter: Vibe God



Fans of Daren FOB will find that Enter: Vibe God is an emotional rollercoaster, full of highs and lows that capture the essence of love, life, and the struggles that come with it. Each track offers something unique, whether it’s the infectious rhythm of 9:30, the deep emotions in Angela’s Song, or the introspective tone of Involve. But at its core, this EP is about finding peace amidst chaos and seeking divine intervention when life’s storms feel too much to bear.



Enter: Vibe God is a testament to Daren FOB’s growth as an artist and as a person. His journey, shared with listeners, provides a mirror to the complexities of modern existence, filled with lessons on love, strength, and personal transformation.



Connect with Daren FOB:Stay up to date with Daren’s musical journey and upcoming shows by following him on social media and streaming his latest work on all platforms.




Listen to Enter: Vibe God

Rising Afro-fusion star Mamuzo is making major waves across the Nigerian capital, marking a triumphant moment in his artistic journey as his latest release, “Jazzman,” crosses 50,000 streams on all major platforms.









A blend of raw soul, storytelling, and vibrant instrumentation, Jazzman has proven to be more than just another record—it’s an anthem. With its infectious groove and Mamuzo’s smooth, melodic delivery, the track is resonating deeply not just with fans in Abuja but across Nigeria’s rapidly evolving soundscape.



From smoky open mics to buzzing clubs in Wuse, Garki, and Jabi, Mamuzo’s name is becoming synonymous with a new era of Nigerian sonic identity. “Abuja’s energy is different,” Mamuzo shares. “It’s a melting pot of cultures and sounds—and Jazzman is my love letter to that vibe.”







The single’s success reflects more than numbers. It’s a clear indication that the artist’s refined fusion of jazz, highlife, and modern Afrobeat is carving out a unique lane in the industry. With fans sharing Jazzman across TikTok and Instagram, Mamuzo’s audience is growing fast, and the buzz is only getting louder.



Supported by local tastemakers and radio personalities, and spotted performing live at key Abuja venues, Mamuzo is no longer just an underground gem—he’s stepping boldly into the spotlight.









As Jazzman continues to soar past streaming milestones, industry insiders are watching closely. Is Mamuzo Abuja’s next breakout star? All signs point to yes.



One thing is certain: Mamuzo isn’t just riding the wave—he’s becoming the tide.

On May 9, Afro-fusion artist OG Mage is set to drop “Faraway”, a deeply personal single that blends smooth melodies with raw, confessional rap. For fans of genre-defying African music, this release is more than just another drop — it’s a statement of resilience, emotion, and artistry.







The Sound of Vulnerability: What “Faraway” Means



In a world filled with distractions and noise, Faraway offers a moment of reflection. It speaks to the quiet battles we all face — the internal tug-of-war between seeking peace and dealing with life’s chaos.



Musically, the track weaves OG Mage’s soulful vocals with hypnotic Afrobeat rhythms, punctuated by rap verses that speak from the heart. It’s both soothing and intense — the kind of song you play late at night when the weight of the day begins to settle in.



Who Is OG Mage?



Samuel Ogaba, popularly known as OG Mage, has spent years honing a sound that bridges cultures and emotions. Starting out as the leader of the university rap collective IHN (In His Name) under WWJD, his early music was grounded in lyricism and spiritual conviction.



Processed with VSCO with m5pro preset



But things shifted in 2021 when a chance encounter with a music executive at the airport opened doors. That same year, he moved from Lagos to Abuja and dropped his debut EP Alter Ego — a project that signaled his arrival as a solo artist to watch.



Growth, Grit, and Global Perspective



Determined to refine his craft, OG Mage dedicated the next two years to vocal training, evolving beyond his rap roots and embracing melody-driven compositions. His commitment paid off during a writing camp in the UK, where he gained rare backstage access to Wizkid’s O2 Arena show, recorded Anthem Ready, and shot his first official video in Bournemouth.




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Samuel Ogaba (@ogmagegram)




In 2022, he joined Hennessy Artistry, collaborating with Manny Tseayo on Beggin’, one of the standout tracks on the Up to No Good compilation.



Momentum That Can’t Be Ignored



OG Mage’s breakout moment came with The Capital featuring Reeplay, a song that became an anthem in Abuja and boosted his profile across major radio stations. He kept the momentum going with Hot Boy and Head of State (featuring Geezyshore), the latter released on Nigeria’s Democracy Day and celebrated again with a music video on Independence Day.



His ability to weave cultural context into his releases — and perform them live alongside artists like Rema, Davido, Buju, and Odumodublvck — shows his increasing relevance in Nigeria’s evolving music landscape.



What Makes “Faraway” Different?



While OG Mage has always balanced confidence with consciousness, Faraway strips everything back. It’s not about bravado or status — it’s about the human condition. The lyrics reveal a man searching for calm amid the storm, reaching out to anyone who’s ever felt the same.



The track blends Afro-Fusion and Afro Hip-Hop, using the rhythm of the drums to echo the heart’s longing. It’s meditative, immersive, and powerfully relatable.



Final Thoughts: The Rise of a Cultural Bridge



OG Mage has become more than an artist — he’s a cultural bridge, connecting the rhythmic pulse of Afrobeats with the storytelling power of hip-hop. With Faraway, he opens a new chapter, one that deepens his message and widens his impact.



As the release date approaches, fans and newcomers alike are encouraged to pre-save the track and join OG Mage on this next leg of his journey.

articles.body:
Big Cali has officially entered a new era with the release of his hard-hitting single, “Grind” — a sonic testament to perseverance, passion, and the power of relentless ambition.







Backed by pulse-pounding production and a message carved from the raw truth of lived experience, “Grind” isn’t just a track — it’s a manifesto. A soundtrack for every underdog pushing through adversity, every visionary building quietly behind the scenes, and every soul who refuses to give up.



From street corners to corporate boardrooms, lecture halls to night shifts, “Grind” resonates with anyone chasing something greater than themselves. It speaks to those who’ve been doubted, dismissed, or worn thin by the weight of their journey — yet still find the strength to rise.









Cali’s delivery is nothing short of magnetic. His lyrics ring with authenticity, forged in the fire of personal trials and triumphs. This isn’t abstract inspiration — it’s real-life hustle distilled into bars that hit hard and stay with you. Setbacks, solitude, sacrifice, and small wins — Cali captures it all with sharp lyricism and unwavering conviction.




“You don’t need to have it all figured out,” Big Cali says.“You just need to keep grinding. Because for as long as you roll the dice… you’re going to get your 6. It’s only a matter of time.”




“Grind” is more than a song — it’s a mindset, a philosophy, a movement. It reminds listeners that while success isn’t promised, the effort is always worth it. In an era that often prioritizes shortcuts over stories, Cali’s message is refreshingly clear: Ambition + Action = Impact.



He urges the next generation — and anyone on their path — to remain relentless, intentional, and unshakably hungry. Because in the end, there’s still honor in the hustle.




Listen to “Grind”

articles.body:
Nigerian trap sensation Lakezzdope returns to the airwaves with a fiery new track, “Like I Care” — a bold fusion of tap-dancehall energy and raw lyrical attitude, featuring the debut of rising female talent, Niffy B.







Omoregie Lakezz Dennis, professionally known as Lakezzdope, has carved a reputation for being fearless with his sound. Born in Benin City and raised between Edo State and Lagos, Lakezzdope’s musical evolution has always leaned into the unexpected — blending gritty trap flows with afro-fusion grooves, reggae undertones, and now, a fresh tap-dancehall bounce that sets him apart in Nigeria’s ever-diversifying soundscape.









“Like I Care” is more than just a track — it’s a statement. Backed by skippy, rhythmic percussions and a hypnotic melody, Lakezzdope delivers effortlessly cool verses that carry a message of unapologetic self-worth and resilience. But what really elevates this single is Niffy B, who makes her music debut with poise, confidence, and a soulful hook that leaves a lasting impression. Her vocals bring a smooth contrast to Lakezzdope’s rugged cadence, offering a perfect balance of grit and grace.



Niffy B’s first appearance is already causing a stir, with fans praising her natural charisma and vocal tone. If Like I Care is anything to go by, she’s one to watch closely.







Since launching his solo career with the 2020 single “Su Mo Mi” and the genre-blending debut album Virus Shit in 2021, Lakezzdope has proven time and again that he’s not afraid to experiment. From the breakout success of “Bad Guys (Winning)” featuring DaBlixx Osha, to 2024’s emotive “Change” with Zilla Oaks, he’s stayed ahead of the curve — and this latest drop is no exception.



Released under his independent imprint Millzgvng Entertainment Limited, Like I Care adds another vibrant layer to the Lakezzdope legacy. It’s a perfect pre-summer anthem — one that’s bound to light up playlists, dancefloors, and digital streams alike.



Tap in, turn it up, and remember the name — Lakezzdope isn’t just making music; he’s building a movement. And with Niffy B now on the radar, that movement just got stronger.

articles.body:
In an era dominated by rapid gratification and fleeting trends, Nigerian Afro-soul artist Odenose offers a poignant reminder of the virtues of patience and resilience with her latest single, “Up and Down,” featuring the soulful tones of Cef Ashanta. This collaboration stands as a testament to the enduring human spirit, capturing the nuanced dance between hope and adversity.







A Melodic Tapestry of Life’s Ebbs and Flows



“Up and Down” transcends conventional musical boundaries, weaving together elements of Afrobeat rhythms and highlife grooves. Odenose’s evocative vocals narrate the universal story of life’s unpredictability:




“Up and down e go / Life no be straight line / Good thing e take time.”










Her lyrics serve as a gentle reminder that progress is seldom linear, and that growth often emerges from the most challenging experiences.



Cef Ashanta: A Custodian of African Musical Heritage



Joining Odenose on this track is Cef Ashanta, a Nigerian-born singer, songwriter, and multi-instrumentalist renowned for his commitment to preserving African musical traditions. Ashanta’s contribution to “Up and Down” is both grounding and enlightening:




“No be ginger dey cook beans eh / Everything get e time and e season eh.”








Ashanta is the pioneer of Genti music, a genre deeply rooted in Igbo native sounds and enriched with ogene instruments, highlife, Afrobeat, soul, reggae, and jazz influences. His dedication to cultural authenticity is evident in his previous works, such as the album Jide Ofor, which explores themes of spirituality, love, society, and responsibility .



Crafting Authenticity Through Sound



The production of “Up and Down” was a deliberate endeavor to capture the essence of waiting and introspection. Collaborating with producers Bkswithvibe and Ifektive, Odenose ensured that every beat and chord resonated with sincerity. She reflects:




“It had to be honest. It had to sound like how waiting feels.”




This meticulous approach results in a track that not only entertains but also offers solace to listeners navigating their own journeys.



Odenose: Amplifying Voices of the Unseen







Emerging as a vital voice in Nigeria’s Afro-soul scene, Odenose distinguishes herself through her vulnerability and commitment to storytelling. Her music resonates with those who find themselves in transitional phases, seeking affirmation and understanding.



Embracing the Journey



“Up and Down” is more than a song; it’s an anthem for those who continue to strive amidst uncertainty. In a world fixated on immediate success, Odenose and Cef Ashanta remind us of the beauty found in perseverance and the strength derived from embracing life’s fluctuations.




Stream ‘Up & Down’

Nigerian artist Phlexzywest is ready to make a powerful statement with his upcoming single, “No Emotions,” dropping on May 8, 2025. Known for his genre-blending sound and soul-stirring melodies, Phlexzywest takes a stark and honest turn with this track, confronting emotional fatigue with refreshing clarity.







About Phlexzywest



Phlexzywest is a Nigerian singer and songwriter with a mission to impact the global music scene through authentic storytelling and genre-defying sound. His journey began at the age of 15 as a church choir boy, where he first discovered the transformative power of music. Over the years, he has drawn influence from legends such as Bob Marley, Fela Kuti, Lucky Dube, Michael Jackson, Wyclef Jean, and Labrinth—each playing a part in shaping his dynamic sound.



Today, Phlexzywest is known for blending elements of Afrobeats, Dancehall, R&B, and Hip-hop, creating a style that feels both grounded and expansive. His ability to explore vulnerability, identity, and emotion through music has earned him a loyal following and growing industry recognition.







Behind the Song: “No Emotions”



“No Emotions” is a sharp, stripped-back reflection on love, detachment, and self-preservation. According to Phlexzywest, the inspiration for the song was born from emotional exhaustion. “I got tired of relationships and switched off emotions,” he shares—a sentiment that echoes throughout the track in its tone, lyricism, and delivery.



With minimalistic yet impactful production, the song leans into a more vulnerable space without losing its rhythmic edge. It’s not just a breakup anthem—it’s a declaration of self-awareness, a refusal to settle for one-sided love, and a signal of growth.



Why You Should Pre-Save “No Emotions”



In a time when music often leans into spectacle, “No Emotions” stands out for its quiet honesty. This is Phlexzywest at his most introspective—unfiltered, emotionally raw, and sonically bold. For fans of music that speaks to the heart while still moving the feet, this release is essential.



Pre-save “No Emotions” today and be the first to experience one of the most emotionally resonant drops of the season.

Nigerian hip-hop powerhouse KING STUNNA is set to unleash his boldest work yet with his new single, “Fall Out,” releasing on May 8, 2025. Gritty, honest, and untamed, the track captures everything fans have come to expect from the rising international force—and more.







KING STUNNA has steadily built his name as a fearless lyricist and charismatic performer whose music commands attention. With chart appearances in Nigeria, Malaysia, and Brunei, his cross-continental appeal is undeniable. Whether it’s his fluid transitions between English and Pidgin or his ability to merge street narratives with slick production, KING STUNNA stands out as a unique voice in today’s hip-hop landscape.



About KING STUNNA



Emerging from Nigeria’s dynamic music scene, KING STUNNA brings street-hardened wisdom, sharp lyrical prowess, and a relentless drive to every track. His music is deeply rooted in real-life experience—hustle, ambition, loyalty, survival—and his raw style reflects both vulnerability and strength. With a growing global fanbase and multiple successful releases under his belt, KING STUNNA is pushing African hip-hop to new heights.







Inside the Making of “Fall Out”



“Fall Out” is more than a single; it’s a statement. Produced by PapiGunzo, the beat immediately resonated with KING STUNNA, triggering a creative process that was instinctive and emotionally charged. He describes the moment as zoning out, with the instrumental perfectly matching his thoughts and emotions.




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by KING STUNNA (@iamkingstunna)





“I poured my life into every line,” he says. “No filters, no smoothing edges. I didn’t want it to sound polished—I wanted it to sound honest.”




This track wasn’t written to impress. It was made to tell the truth. From evading financial burdens throughout the week to navigating the complexities of his environment and relationships, KING STUNNA delivers every line with intention. The hook came through a freestyle, capturing the raw essence of the moment, while the verses were written in a single sitting—no polish, just pure honesty.



Why You Should Pre-Save “Fall Out”



“Fall Out” is a fearless blend of raw emotion and street energy. It’s KING STUNNA at his most candid, delivering a performance that’s both personal and universally relatable. For listeners who crave authenticity, hard bars, and storytelling that cuts deep, this release is essential.



Pre-save “Fall Out” today and be among the first to experience one of the most compelling drops of the year.

A bold, cinematic 2-pack featuring Vr1zz, Makama & Plvyboi Pluto, now streaming worldwide







The moment has arrived. Nigerian-born, genre-defying artist FeyoTheGenius has dropped When It’s Time For Action, a potent two-track release that cuts through the noise with surgical precision. Rooted in real-life experience and delivered with an unwavering sense of urgency, this release is more than a new chapter — it’s a statement of intent.



No gimmicks. No compromises. Just raw, fearless creativity.



A CROSSROADS OF SONIC POWER AND STRATEGY



FeyoTheGenius has long been known for blending street realism with forward-thinking sound design, and this drop pushes that reputation to new heights.









Track 1: “Time For Action” (feat. Vr1zz & Makama)



Opening with ominous textures and heavy-hitting percussion, “Time For Action” immediately establishes a sense of tension and resolve. Vr1zz brings a razor-sharp cadence that slices through the beat with confidence, while Makama injects a streetwise edge, grounding the track in lived experience. The chemistry between all three artists is undeniable — each voice reinforcing the other, building toward a larger narrative of loyalty, survival, and making your mark before the world tells you otherwise.



This is drill with a mission. Cinematic and militant, yet deeply personal.



Track 2: “I Lost My Feelings For You” (feat. Plvyboi Pluto)



In stark contrast, the second track explores the emotional fallout of ambition. Over moody synths and melancholic melodies, Plvyboi Pluto’s autotuned vocals drift like smoke — blurred, wounded, and cool to the touch. Feyo’s verses hit with clarity and reflection, addressing themes of detachment, heartbreak, and the emotional toll of building a legacy in a world that rarely gives back what it takes from you.



The result? A hauntingly beautiful flip side to the raw aggression of the opener.



MEET FEYOTHEGENIUS: PURPOSE IN EVERY BAR



Raised in Nigeria and now operating globally, FeyoTheGenius embodies a new generation of independent artists who refuse to be boxed in. Drawing inspiration from hip-hop, afrobeats, drill, alternative R&B, and cinematic soundscapes, Feyo is more than just a rapper or producer — he’s a storyteller, architect, and visionary.







With roots in street culture and an eye firmly fixed on global recognition, Feyo’s music speaks to anyone who’s had to fight to be heard, respected, and remembered.




“This drop is for the ones who know what it means to move with purpose. No more talking. It’s action time.” – FeyoTheGenius




FEATURED ARTISTS BRING THE HEAT




Vr1zz: Known for his unapologetic delivery and lyrical precision, Vr1zz is quickly becoming one of the most exciting new voices in the underground rap scene.



Makama: A fearless storyteller with gritty authenticity, Makama brings both heart and hard-earned wisdom to “Time For Action.”



Plvyboi Pluto: A melodic force who floats between rap and R&B, Pluto’s feature on “I Lost My Feelings For You” adds emotional depth and sonic contrast, making it one of the standout moments of the project.




MORE THAN A RELEASE — IT’S A RECKONING



When It’s Time For Action is the culmination of a year of growth, experimentation, and relentless grind. Following a string of strong singles and collaborations in 2024, this release marks a new phase in Feyo’s artistic evolution — one that’s self-assured, creatively fearless, and ready to challenge the norms of both Nigerian and global music spaces.



Feyo’s ability to walk the tightrope between vulnerability and defiance is what makes this project so powerful. It’s not just a soundtrack for the streets — it’s fuel for anyone chasing something bigger than themselves.



JOIN THE MOVEMENT



This isn’t just a vibe. It’s a movement in motion. And FeyoTheGenius is leading it with fire in his belly and vision in his mind.



Stream When It’s Time For Action now on all major platforms. Follow Feyo on social media for updates, visuals, and behind-the-scenes access to what’s next.




Stream Now




Independent. Unfiltered. Ready for war. Don’t just watch it happen — be a part of it.

In a world spinning ever faster toward instant gratification, Odenose invites us to slow down, breathe, and reconnect with something far more enduring: truth. Her new single, “Up and Down” featuring the rich, soulful tones of Cef Ashanta, isn’t just another song on the playlist — it’s a quiet revolution. It’s a song for the unseen, the almost-there, and the silent strivers among us.







Set for release on May 1st, 2025, “Up and Down” is a soul-stirring Afro-soul anthem that gracefully captures the bittersweet dance between hope and heartbreak. It tells Folake’s story — but in reality, it tells all of ours.



A Song That Speaks to the Struggle We Hide



Unlike tracks chasing viral moments, “Up and Down” is built for the quiet hours — the moments of doubt, the slow steps forward, the long nights wondering if it will all be worth it.Over lush layers of Afrobeat rhythms and highlife grooves, Odenose’s voice doesn’t just sing — it breathes life into shared experiences:




“Up and down e go / Life no be straight line / Good thing e take time.”




Her message is disarmingly simple: life doesn’t move in straight lines. In a culture obsessed with speed and success, Odenose reminds us that growth, healing, and fulfillment arrive in their own time.




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by 𝗢𝗗𝗘𝗡𝗢𝗦𝗘 (@odenosegram)




Cef Ashanta’s feature is a warm, grounding presence, delivering wisdom with a gentleness that soothes even the most restless hearts:




“No be ginger dey cook beans eh / Everything get e time and e season eh.”




Their collaboration feels less like a feature and more like two old friends, exchanging truths we often forget we need to hear.



The Creative Journey: Honesty Over Hype



The making of “Up and Down” was as intentional as its message. Odenose, alongside producers Bkswithvibe and Ifektive, crafted a soundscape that values patience and emotional weight over trends.Every drumbeat, every chord progression is placed with care, allowing the song — and the story within it — the space to breathe.




“It had to be honest,” Odenose shares. “It had to sound like how waiting feels.”




And it does. It’s an experience of being seen, in the quiet, in-between spaces of life.



Odenose: A Voice for Those Still Becoming



Emerging as one of Nigeria’s most vital new Afro-soul voices, Odenose weaves emotional storytelling with a rich tapestry of African sounds — from highlife and alté to classic Afrobeats and R&B.Her strength lies not just in her vocal prowess but in her vulnerability: a rare willingness to share the private struggles so many endure in silence.







Where others chase bangers for the moment, Odenose crafts songs for the journey.“Up and Down” stands tall among them — a quiet classic in the making, an anthem for every Folake who has whispered “God when?” into the night and kept moving anyway.



Why “Up and Down” Matters Right Now



In an era defined by curated perfection and the pressure to “arrive” quickly, “Up and Down” offers something radical: patience. Compassion. Solidarity.



It’s not a song of easy answers or manufactured hope — it’s a hand on the shoulder, a whisper in the dark:



Your time is still coming.Trust your path.Honor your pace.Believe.




“This song is for the people who are still becoming. For those who are still on the way. You’re not late. You’re just right on time.” — Odenose




“Up and Down” by Odenose featuring Cef Ashanta releases worldwide on May 1st, 2025. Prepare to feel seen.

When FeyoTheGenius speaks, the streets listen — and when he raps, the world watches.This April 29, the fast-rising Nigerian hip-hop innovator drops his latest statement piece: a high-voltage 2-pack project titled When It’s Time For Action.







With a reputation for pushing boundaries and an undeniable hunger that’s fueled his rapid ascent, FeyoTheGenius is making it clear: this is his moment.



Two Tracks, Two Different Energies, One Mission



On When It’s Time For Action, Feyo unleashes two powerful records that capture the tension, ambition, and mindset of an artist on the verge of something bigger.








“Time For Action” — featuring Vr1zz and Makama — is an anthem for anyone who knows that loyalty and survival are non-negotiable. It’s militant, aggressive, and cinematic, loaded with vivid storytelling and cold-blooded bravado.



“I Lost My Feelings For You” — featuring Plvyboi Pluto — flips the script with a more melodic but equally ruthless vibe. It’s about emotional detachment, moving forward, and putting success above sentimentality.




Together, they paint a complete picture of the hustler’s soul: one track for when the pressure’s on, one for when the feelings fade and the mission stays.







“Time For Action”: A Street Sermon for the Real Ones



The lead track wastes no time setting the tone.Opening with dark, cinematic production, Feyo fires off hard-hitting bars like:




“Told ’em do him like they did to Sonny Corleone / Still feeling the massacre like Nagasaki…”




It’s raw, it’s urgent, and it’s backed by serious firepower:Vr1zz brings sharp street wisdom in his multilingual verse, flipping between English and Hausa, while Makama rounds out the record with a verse soaked in paranoia and grit.

In a time when authenticity is the new currency, few artists wear their truth like armor the way TELMAN does.







Born Chukwuemeka Rich Ifeanyi in the quiet town of Akpugo, Enugu State, TELMAN’s journey is not just about beats and bars—it’s a narrative of rebirth. A rapper, songwriter, and creative visionary, TELMAN is rapidly emerging as one of Nigeria’s most introspective and emotionally resonant voices in Hip-Hop. His music is a powerful conversation between faith and struggle, ambition and identity—crafted with care, clarity, and soul.









Raised under the influence of his grandfather, Pastor Donatus Chukwuemeka, TELMAN’s foundation is spiritual, yet his sound is street-savvy. It’s a compelling fusion—Drill, Trap, Afrobeat, and classic Rap—laced with the kind of lyricism that cuts deep. Whether he’s unpacking generational trauma, exploring personal battles, or celebrating growth, TELMAN approaches every record with intention.









His latest body of work, “REBIRTH,” is more than a release—it’s a declaration. A creative and spiritual reset, the project signals a bold new phase in his evolution as an artist. With each track, TELMAN sheds old layers, inviting listeners into a raw, cinematic world of honesty and healing. It’s the type of album that doesn’t just entertain—it reminds you who you are.




“My music is where pain meets power. I’m not just telling stories — I’m making soundtracks for anyone who’s ever had to find themselves in the dark.” 



— TELMAN




Now signed to The RADAR Trinity (RADARCharts for marketing, RADARMusic for licensing & distribution, REM for management) taking the seat as the RADARMan, TELMAN is not just here to rap—he’s building a movement. One rooted in faith, fashion, and cultural fusion. He’s designed his lane, and he’s riding in it with fearless momentum.







With influences like Dave, Drake, and Nasty C, TELMAN doesn’t just borrow sounds—he translates them. For his generation. For Nigeria. For the world.



And the best part? He’s just getting started.




Checkout Telman’s official page

Lagos-bred rapper and genre-bending artist Kakes ON is back with a hard-hitting new release titled “FELELE,” a vibrant anthem that speaks to the heart of living free, wild, and unbothered. Known for his introspective storytelling and genre versatility, Kakes ON fuses Hip-Hop, Drill, and Alte elements on this track to deliver a sonic experience that’s both liberating and deeply infectious.







Following a steady stream of critically-acclaimed projects — from No Days Off (2019) to Moon Rave (2023) — Kakes ON continues to redefine his sound. With over 300K streams across all platforms and a TopNaija Music Award for Best Campus Music Artiste (2020) under his belt, the 27-year-old creative is proving once again why he’s a force in the evolving Nigerian music space.



What “FELELE” Is All About



“FELELE” is more than a track — it’s a mood, a mantra, and a movement. Translating to a carefree lifestyle, the song is built on infectious drill percussion and dark undertones, paired with raw lyricism that explores the beauty of letting go, embracing freedom, and living life on your own terms.









Kakes ON doesn’t just ride the beat — he commands it, weaving in his personal story and Lagos upbringing with sharp flows and expressive delivery. It’s a track that invites the listener to break free from societal expectations and bask in their own authenticity.



A Legacy in Motion



Since launching his career in 2018, Kakes ON has continued to evolve with every drop. His previous projects Before I Japa to the Moon and Moon Talk showcased his ability to balance vulnerability with confidence, while Moon Rave cemented his alter-ego as an unapologetic vibe-maker. “FELELE” is the continuation of that sonic exploration, one that feels bolder and more refined.




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by KAKES ON (@kakes_on)




Next up? 



The highly-anticipated track “One Dayy” — a motivational anthem produced by Ukrainian hitmaker TrapNinjaBoy, set to drop January 31st. Stay tuned.

Nigerian hip-hop is experiencing a renaissance, and at the heart of this lyrical revolution is Gneric, a fierce voice from Edo State whose conscious flows, poetic delivery, and fearless expression are rewriting the narrative for women in rap. On April 25, 2025, Gneric solidifies her rising star status with the release of her deeply personal new EP, I Found My Sound — a powerful four-track journey of introspection, resilience, and raw expression.







A Battle Rapper Turned Wordsmith of Emotion



Gneric’s roots lie in Nigeria’s underground battle rap circuit, where she earned her stripes exchanging bars with lyrical titans like Dabu The Gemini. But since her recorded music debut in 2023, she’s been more than just a skilled MC — she’s become a storyteller for a generation seeking truth. Her music reflects the echoes of her idols — Lauryn Hill, Erykah Badu, and Little Simz — yet it remains uniquely hers: filled with honest vulnerability, grit, and Nigerian soul.




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by GNeric (@gnericvibes)




In her own words, the making of I Found My Sound was “a rollercoaster of emotions,” a process in which each track mirrored the peaks and valleys of her personal evolution. From the effortless magic of “Road” — crafted during an impromptu studio session with Northern Nigeria’s lyrical titan ILLANOID — to the meditative, spoken-word driven “This Spot,” Gneric isn’t just making music. She’s making statements.




“Many people don’t understand why I combine spoken word with my music,” she reflects. “My background as a battle rapper has opened me up to new ways of expression. Battle rap is poetry to me.”




Cross-Cultural Chemistry: Ànesi & ILLANOID Add Fire



The project is further elevated by collaborations with two powerful artists:








ILLANOID, a Northern Nigerian rap icon and battle rap veteran whose pen is as sharp as his self-awareness. His gritty cadence on “Applaud” brings balance to Gneric’s introspection — fusing street wisdom with lyrical precision.



Ànesi, the Cameroonian-born, Nigerian-raised genre-bender, brings her Trapiano magic to the mix. Known for her haunting melodies and Billie Eilish-inspired emotional depth, Ànesi adds a rich layer of soul to the project’s sonic palette.




Gneric’s Mission: Expression Without Limits



“I want people to connect with me in diverse ways,” Gneric explains — and that intention is clear. Whether it’s the empowering bounce of “Applaud,” the energizing affirmations of “Activate,” or the contemplative mood of “This Spot,” I Found My Sound feels like a body of work that refuses to be boxed in.







More than an EP, it’s a declaration: of creative freedom, of identity, and of a Nigerian artist carving out her lane with fearless authenticity.



Stream ‘I Found My Sound’ starting April 25 on all platforms.Follow Gneric’s journey on Instagram, Twitter, and your favorite music blog — because Nigeria’s next lyrical powerhouse has officially arrived.

Buckwild Ken once again delivers a vibrant anthem that hits close to home and resonates far beyond borders. His latest drop, “Send Me Mo Mo,” featuring the sensational Maya Sh’Von transcends just a mood, it’s a cultural anthem.







From the very first beat, “Send Me Mo Mo” draws listeners into a rhythm that feels both nostalgic and refreshing—combining afrobeats,rap, diaspora influence, and feel-good storytelling. The lyrics? Relatable. The energy? Absolutely infectious.What sets this video apart is its intentional inclusivity. Featuring people from all walks of life, the video showcases a vibrant array of individuals, notably personalities in the diaspora,united by the joy of the music. Their spirited sing-alongs and carefree dance moves radiate authenticity, adding a layer of cross-cultural pride and success to the visual narrative.







Maya Sh’Von’s feature is magnetic. Her smooth, soulful vocals harmonize seamlessly with Buckwild Ken’s signature style, creating a sonic synergy that’s as vibely as it is groovy.



For the uninitiated, MoMo stands for Mobile Money — a popular and essential cashless transfer system widely used throughout Africa to send and receive funds via mobile phonesWhether you’re dancing in your kitchen, driving through the city, or hustling in a boardroom, this track feels like a universal call to joy.









Buckwild Ken continues to prove he’s more than an artist—he’s a storyteller, a connector, and a creative force. Buckwild Ken might just be on the brink of turning a viral hit into a commercial and cultural milestone.

In a world increasingly driven by trends and quick hits, some artists stand out by choosing to tell real stories — raw, unfiltered, and true. Nigerian-born, Lithuania-based artist Http//:riri is one such voice, and with his upcoming fifth studio album, Mother Tongue, he’s taking things to an entirely new level.







Scheduled for release this Friday, April 25th, Mother Tongue is more than just another project — it’s a reflection of identity, transformation, and the journey toward self-acceptance. Known for his genre-blending approach that fuses trap, hip-hop, afrobeats, R&B, and alternative sounds, Http//:riri delivers a deeply introspective body of work that is both sonically expansive and emotionally charged.



A Project Rooted in Authenticity



Over the years, Http//:riri has built a reputation for crafting music that feels personal and alive. His story began backstage at a concert — a life-altering moment that reignited his creative flame after years of poetry, instrument training, and cross-cultural exploration. With a strong DIY ethic, he continues to write, produce, record, and direct much of his work himself, making each project a fully immersive experience.







On Mother Tongue, he strips away the layers even further. For the first time, he delivers an album with zero features, putting his full lyrical, vocal, and emotional range on full display. It’s a bold move, but for an artist like Http//:riri, it’s the natural next step in a journey built on authenticity and independence.



Themes of Identity, Growth, and Resilience



Across 18 tracks — including titles like “Focus,” “Money on the Table,” “Alive!,” and “Blessings” — Http//:riri delves into the complex emotions tied to home, fatherhood, self-worth, and the courage to evolve. Every song feels like a journal entry, documenting not just where he is today, but everything it took to get here.








“There’s something sacred about reclaiming your voice,” Http//:riri says of the album. “Mother Tongue is about honoring where I came from, embracing where I am, and moving forward without apology.”

In a world where life often moves too fast and pressure builds quietly behind every smile, Boluké emerges with a song that feels like freedom. Her debut single, “Kolo”, is more than just a musical introduction — it’s a spiritual release wrapped in Afrobeat rhythms and infectious pop energy.







Released on March 21, 2025, “Kolo” marks the entrance of a dynamic triple-threat talent: Boluké Abiona — singer, songwriter, and dancer — who’s already proving she’s a force to be reckoned with.



A Sound That Speaks to the Soul



“Kolo,” a Yoruba slang word meaning “crazy,” takes that chaos and flips it on its head. It’s not about madness in the destructive sense — it’s about letting go, dancing through the pressure, and embracing emotional honesty. With a pulsing Afrobeat groove and Boluké’s soaring vocals, the track sweeps listeners into a moment of pure, liberating sound.









But behind that upbeat, high-energy production is a heartfelt message. “I was going through a phase,” Boluké reveals. “Adulthood can be overwhelming and mentally stressing. That word — Kolo — just came to me naturally. I crafted it into a kind of prayer, something that speaks to everyone feeling the weight of life.”



And that’s the beauty of Boluké’s music. It meets you where you are — tired, anxious, or just trying to stay afloat — and lifts you up with melody, movement, and meaning.



More Than a Song — It’s an Experience



Raised in an environment where music and dance were inseparable, Boluké doesn’t just perform — she embodies her art. Her vocals are drenched in emotion, her lyrics paint vivid realities, and her performances bring every word to life. “Kolo” is not just a single; it’s a full-body experience, an emotional detox for anyone in need of a release.







Whether you’re driving home late, dancing in your room, or simply trying to breathe through the chaos, Boluké’s “Kolo” is that song that says, you’re not alone — and yes, it’s okay to feel a little kolo sometimes.



🎧 Stream “KOLO” Now



Tap into Boluké’s sonic prayer and let the rhythm guide you back to yourself.




Listen to KOLO now

On Today’s episode we spoke to KEZIAH MALLAM, an original talent with her own sound called ‘Audio Therapy’. She’s really amazing, listen to TROUBLE and get what we mean. We trust you’d love it 







WHERE SHE COMES FROM



You’ve dubbed yourself “The Audio Therapist”—what sparked that identity, and how did your early environment influence it?




It came from me describing how my voice sounds and what I want my music to do for people and myself. Anyone who knows me knows my life has been hella eventful from a young age, so music and God have been my therapy through that. My voice has a slight whisper to it at times. Like air. You can hear it in harmonies and layering. That felt like therapy to me and some of my people when I first started. It still does. So Audio Therapy has been a movement of bringing peace & therapy to life’s craziness.




Growing up between cultures, how has being British-Nigerian shaped your voice and sound as an artist?




I’m very experimental(😂). I remember my first manager saying something like I just create whatever comes to my head and it’s so true. Growing up in South London, Garage, Drill, both UK & US R&B/Soul as well as other genres became a part of me. Now, moving to Abuja for high school in 2010 put me on a different sound. That became a part of me too. My music reflects how much my ear has been stretched. My beats can have the most unlikely sound pairings, then I’ll come and throw the softest R&B/ Soul vocal on top. I’m sonically free, and I love that. 








You spent a whole year releasing self-produced records monthly (in 2022). What did that chapter teach you about discipline and self-trust?




Man, it taught me that one of my greatest gifts in life is my ability to learn. It’s also taught me that the results of consistency are addictive (in a good way). I just grew to understand that the only thing stopping me was myself, and God has given me everything I need to succeed. I always say this. There’s no reason I should fail. God showed me in 2022 that this is just the beginning.




Who were the first artists or producers that made you believe music could be more than just entertainment?




Errrm, I think some of my friends are Osayuki, the producer duo Happyboy, my brother Beezyx, my sister RnB Princess, and my good friend UCEE. 




As someone who also crafts for other artists, what’s the most rewarding part of being behind the scenes in vocal production?




It’s hearing my ideas through the ears, tones, and pronunciations of others. There’s something beautiful about hearing/ seeing something you’ve created live through others. It’s like it multiples its life or further validates its existence. 








Your goal is to merge Afrocentric vibes with global sounds. What unique elements do you incorporate to achieve this fusion?




It’s the sounds. I try to evoke emotions with my music. When making a song, I try to experiment a lot with different sounds. I want my music to go beyond boundaries, so I infuse a lot of elements into the sound. At the end of the day, I want everybody to feel connected when they listen to my records, be it from the melodies, lyrics, drums, guitars, etc.




What’s a memory from your journey so far—on stage or in the studio—that affirmed you’re on the right path?




Felabration last year with my band. I did a live show every month, supported by my management, and at the start of the year, I told my band guys I wanted us to do Felabration that year. They believed in me from the start and said we’ll do it. We did it and we did amazing. I met with the Kutis, and my friend Nedo made it memorable. It just reminded me that God is only getting started with us. 










To everyone who’s supported you from the start—what’s one prayer or message you want to leave with them today?




May you never be scared to go for your dreams, and may God always bring people who wholeheartedly believe in you. But most importantly, may you be fully aware that God has already given you everything you need to succeed. All you have to do is move with what you have. In Jesus’ name, amen 




WHERE SHE’S GOING TO



Your new single “Trouble” with Tim Lyre is a vibe. What emotional space were you both trying to explore on this track?




Thank you. It was just a song articulating that fun, cheeky space you can be in with someone. Just enjoying that tension or whatever(😂) Like, you know you shouldn’t do it, so it makes it more tense. People say that space is more fun than the real thing, but I wouldn’t know lol










With “Audio Therapy” becoming more than a sound, what’s your big-picture dream for it as a movement or brand?




I want to tour. I’m seeing what Cleo Sol is doing. It feels like a healing tour for the audience and herself. I want to do that too. Tour the world with my band and have therapy sessions in stadiums and the biggest venues one day. I just want people to feel the hope God has given me, and I plan to do that throug

Tour the world with my band and have therapy sessions in stadiums and the biggest venues one day. I just want people to feel the hope God has given me, and I plan to do that through Audio Therapy.

In a world full of noise, how do you stay grounded while evolving creatively?

Always God, my bestie, and good family and friends. I live a simple life in my opinion(😂). My music, my Jesus, and my people. It reduces too much talk, and I pick my battles wisely. It allows me to have the peace of mind and space to make some of my best music. 

Are there any dream collaborators or producers you’re manifesting for future work?

My favourite artist, D’Angelo, is my number 1. All my people know that. In general, I’m just looking forward to working with whoever wants to make good music with me too, as long as we align.

Looking ahead, what message would you love to leave with your fans as you step into this next chapter of your journey?

Stick with me and we’ll figure it out together. It’s been a lot of growth since I started in 2021 and it only gets better, even without a clear plan at the beginning. We’ve got God, so we’ll keep figuring it out and evolving sonically and creating the stuff that means something.

The wait is over. Contra Banz, the hard-hitting Nigerian Hip-Hop and Afro-fusion sensation, has officially released his highly anticipated project, HITMAN ALL DAY EVERYDAY. 







Available now on all major streaming platforms, the project marks a powerful new chapter for the genre-blending artist known as Eruku Flows.



From the very first track, HITMAN ALL DAY EVERYDAY pulls no punches. It’s a gritty, high-energy ride through the mind of an artist who refuses to be boxed in. Contra Banz seamlessly fuses Drill, Afro-pop, and Dance with fearless lyricism and infectious rhythms, delivering a sound that’s as bold as it is addictive.









Following the success of his earlier works—Birth of a Hitman and Contrabanz EP—this latest project showcases Contra’s growth, hunger, and unrelenting drive. The title itself is a declaration of intent: this is a lifestyle, a movement, and a full-time hustle.




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Moses Oluwajuwonlo Samson (@contra_banz)




Now based in Lagos but repping his roots in Oyo State, Contra Banz is once again proving why he’s one of the most compelling voices in Nigeria’s new music wave. With HITMAN ALL DAY EVERYDAY, he’s not just releasing a project—he’s raising the bar.




Stream HADED

Emerging artist Keziah Mallam returns with her latest release, Trouble—a sultry, jazz-infused R&B track that marks an exciting new chapter in her sonic evolution. 







Following the success of her 2024 debut Floating, Keziah once again showcases her genre-blending artistry, inviting listeners into a lush, emotionally charged world shaped by timeless sounds and contemporary storytelling.



A Deep Dive into “Trouble”



From the very first note, Trouble makes its presence felt. A smoky trumpet intro sets the tone, drawing the listener into a sonic landscape where jazz, soul, and R&B converge effortlessly. Layered harmonies wrap around percussive rhythms, creating a rich backdrop for Keziah’s warm and expressive vocals. The production is deliberate yet fluid—each element working in harmony to create a listening experience that’s both intimate and cinematic.







Lyrical Exploration



At its heart, Trouble explores the playful, unpredictable side of romantic attraction. With clever lyricism and a flirtatious tone, Keziah walks the line between desire and restraint, capturing the thrill of emotional tension and the mischievous joy of giving into it. Her delivery is confident and smooth, laced with charm and subtle vulnerability, allowing the song’s themes to unfold naturally.









Collaborative Synergy with Tim Lyre



The addition of Tim Lyre on Trouble adds a compelling dynamic. Known for his fluid movement across genres, Tim complements Keziah’s sultry tone with seamless transitions between melodic harmonies and expressive rap verses. His presence heightens the track’s emotional complexity, bringing a bold, modern edge to the vintage-influenced production. The collaboration between the two artists feels organic and well-balanced, enhancing the song’s layered feel.




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Keziah Mallam🎋 (@keziahmallam)




Keziah Mallam: Redefining Soul with a Global Edge



Keziah Mallam is a multi-talented instrumentalist, singer and producer. Hailing from Kudana, Nigeria, but based in Croydon, South London. With an incredibly unique and timeless sound, seamlessly blending R&B, Funk, Jazz and Afro elements. She draws inspiration from Sade, Ange Stone and Cleo Sol and finds herself landing somewhere in between, with her own special take and flavour. Drawing inspiration from soul icons and contemporary voices alike, Keziah’s work reflects a deep understanding of musical tradition, filtered through her personal lens.



Artistic Evolution



Trouble marks a bold step forward in Keziah’s artistic evolution. While Floating introduced audiences to her soulful introspection, Trouble leans into experimentation with jazz and groove. The result is a track that not only reinforces her versatility but also hints at the direction her future releases might take. It’s daring, polished, and emotionally resonant—a true reflection of an artist coming into her own.







Outer South: A Platform for Pan-African Innovation



The single arrives via Outer South, a cross-continental creative hub and label dedicated to pushing boundaries and amplifying African voices. Operating between Johannesburg and London, the label has quickly become known for its support of forward-thinking artists working across Afro-fusion, R&B, and alternative sounds. Keziah’s work under their banner reflects a shared vision of innovation, authenticity, and global impact.



Final Thoughts



With Trouble, Keziah Mallam proves that she’s not just an artist to watch—she’s one to remember. The track’s seamless fusion of soulful vocals, jazz textures, and lyrical sophistication showcases a maturing talent with something real to say. As she continues to explore and redefine what modern soul can sound like, one thing is clear: Keziah isn’t just making music—she’s crafting a legacy.

With an incredibly unique and timeless sound, seamlessly blending R&B, Funk, Jazz and Afro elements. She draws inspiration from Sade, Ange Stone and Cleo Sol and finds herself landing somewhere in between, with her own special take and flavour. 
Drawing inspiration from soul icons and contemporary voices alike, Keziah’s work reflects a deep understanding of musical tradition, filtered through her personal lens.

Artistic Evolution

Trouble marks a bold step forward in Keziah’s artistic evolution. While Floating introduced audiences to her soulful introspection, Trouble leans into experimentation with jazz and groove. The result is a track that not only reinforces her versatility but also hints at the direction her future releases might take. It’s daring, polished, and emotionally resonant—a true reflection of an artist coming into her own.

Outer South: A Platform for Pan-African Innovation

The single arrives via Outer South, a cross-continental creative hub and label dedicated to pushing boundaries and amplifying African voices. Operating between Johannesburg and London, the label has quickly become known for its support of forward-thinking artists working across Afro-fusion, R&B, and alternative sounds. Keziah’s work under their banner reflects a shared vision of innovation, authenticity, and global impact.

Final Thoughts

With Trouble, Keziah Mallam proves that she’s not just an artist to watch—she’s one to remember. The track’s seamless fusion of soulful vocals, jazz textures, and lyrical sophistication showcases a maturing talent with something real to say. As she continues to explore and redefine what modern soul can sound like, one thing is clear: Keziah isn’t just making music—she’s crafting a legacy.

There’s something unforgettable about a song that lives rent-free in your head. That was the case with Anyafulugo’s “Chukwu Ekwena”—a track that reemerged in my subconscious like a sacred chant. It wasn’t until I replayed it that I fully realized: this man makes timeless music. The kind of sound that finds you, even in silence.







Today, as Anyafulugo celebrates his 30th birthday, he offers a deeply personal gift to his growing tribe: a surprise project titled 30. Dropped just months after his critically acclaimed debut album Psychotic or Iconic, this new EP signals a bold continuation of his Afro-Agwu sonic journey.



A Cultural Torchbearer from the East



Born Obumneme Mark-Anthony Osuchukwu, Anyafulugo hails from Abia State but grew up in the vibrant city of Onitsha—where his roots in art and activism began to flourish. Long before he stepped into the recording booth, many knew him for his potent written voice. His essays—featured on platforms like Linda Ikeji’s Blog and Instablog9ja—tackled cultural and social issues with raw honesty.



When he finally entered the studio in late 2023 at Voice of the East Studios in Enugu, it was nothing short of alchemy. His debut single “Chibuzo” was only his second recorded track—but it arrived like a manifesto. Singles like “Nwoke,” “Ngwo Ngwo,” and the standout “Vladimir” soon followed, further cementing his place as the pioneer of Afro-Agwu.



Afro-Agwu: A Genre and a Calling



For Anyafulugo, music isn’t just sound—it’s a spiritual invocation. Drawing deeply from his agwu (the ancestral deity of creativity), his lyrics blend streetwise bars with Igbo proverbs, hip-hop cadence, and ancestral energy. It’s music as education. As healing. As memory.







Tracks like “April 18” from Psychotic or Iconic reflect the emotional depth behind his pen, capturing his painful coming-of-age after the loss of his father at 18. His collaborative works—with artists like Nuno Zigi, Icah, Stoner Nwaigbo, and M’Joey—show that Afro-Agwu is no solo act. It’s a movement.



More Than Music: A Cultural Force



Anyafulugo’s pride in his heritage extends beyond the studio. His fashion choices—like his signature handwoven wool hat and Akpa-Agwu side bag—aren’t just stylistic; they’re statements. He wears his culture like armor, merging tradition and modernity with purpose.




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Anyafulugo Obumneme (@chief__anyafulugo)




His cultural footprint expands into literature as well. Alongside author Michael Chukwudera, he co-founded the Eagle Nest Book Club in Awka, a vibrant literary hub that birthed the Umuofia Arts and Book Festival. Whether through essays, events, or music, Anyafulugo is reshaping Igbo narratives with visionary passion.



‘30’: A Ritual in Sound



Released on April 7th—his 30th birthday—30 is more than just a collection of tracks. It’s a spiritual checkpoint. A sonic offering. Though the tracklist remains under wraps, fans can expect themes of introspection, ritual, and bold experimentation. Like his past work, this project promises to feel less like a playlist and more like an initiation.









In an industry often overrun by trends, Anyafulugo is defiantly original. Alongside rising Eastern acts like Jeriq, Aguero Banks, Hugo P, Stoner Nwaigbo, and Rord Kelly, he’s part of a new wave that’s redefining what it means to be Igbo and global. Legends like Phyno and Flavour may have paved the way, but artists like Anyafulugo are now carrying the torch into uncharted territory.



An Icon in the Making



In under a year, Anyafulugo has done what many artists spend decades chasing—crafted a distinctive sound, built a loyal community, and laid the foundation for a movement rooted in identity, spirituality, and fearless expression.



Whether through his music, his writing, or his public presence, the message remains the same:




“Music will save me.”




And in saving himself, he’s helping others find light, too.



As 30 enters the world today, it stands not just as a project, but as a rite of passage, a thank-you, a declaration, and maybe—just maybe—a prophecy.



Long live Afro-Agwu. Long live Anyafulugo.




Stream 30

Rising Afro-fusion and street-hop artist Jelo Matini continues to solidify his position as a fearless new voice in the music landscape with the release of his latest single, “Russia.” Crafted in collaboration with producer Dillions Beats, the track is more than just a song—it’s a rallying cry for ambition, perseverance, and unshakable belief in self.







Representing the bold spirit of Outside Babiez, Jelo Matini brings an unfiltered, hard-hitting perspective to his music, drawing from lived experience and turning hustle into high art. With previous releases like “Money Bop” capturing attention for their authenticity and gritty energy, “Russia” raises the bar even further—both in sound and message.



At its core, Russia is a self-motivational anthem—a sonic embodiment of resilience and the refusal to be boxed in. “It was created out of the will to do what I want and succeed at it, at all cost,” Matini explains. “I wanted to inspire the hopeless, to remind them that all hope isn’t lost. They have to stand up and fight for what they want—regardless.”









The record is laced with smooth melodies, layered flows, and hard-hitting street sensibilities, maintaining Matini’s signature style while tapping into deeper emotional and spiritual energy. The title Russia symbolically reflects the idea of facing adversity with strength, navigating life’s battlefield with strategy, and coming out stronger.



What sets Jelo Matini apart is not just his lyrical grit, but his commitment to using his voice as a vessel for truth. He isn’t chasing trends—he’s building a movement, one grounded in authenticity, ambition, and the determination to connect street narratives to the world stage.




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by JELO MATINI (@jelo_matini)




As he continues to evolve, “Russia” serves as both a powerful statement and a promise of what’s to come. With each release, Matini proves he’s not just another artist—he’s a force with purpose.




Stream Russia

Emerging with a fresh and authentic voice in the Nigerian music scene, Erima continues her ascent with the official release of “Mogbe Remix,” a captivating rework of her breakout single. Featuring the vibrant flair of Riskykid Intl, this remix breathes new life into an already celebrated track, offering listeners an elevated fusion of Afrobeat, R&B, and Afropop.







Known for her unique sonic identity and dynamic artistry, Erima has steadily built a reputation for creating music that is both emotionally resonant and rhythmically compelling. Her ability to effortlessly blend contemporary sounds with relatable storytelling has garnered a loyal and fast-growing fanbase, particularly in the capital city of Abuja, where her name is rapidly gaining prominence.









The original “Mogbe” was born from a moment of spontaneous creativity—a TikTok beat that sparked an emotional reaction and led to an immediate lyrical outpouring. That organic approach remains at the heart of the remix, but with an added layer of vibrancy thanks to Riskykid Intl’s contribution. His energetic performance complements Erima’s emotive delivery, creating a balanced and engaging duet that reintroduces the song in a fresh and compelling light.







The “Mogbe Remix” stands as a testament to Erima’s evolving artistry and her willingness to explore new dimensions of her sound. With its infectious rhythm, heartfelt lyrics, and polished production, the single is poised to further solidify her position as one of Nigeria’s most promising new acts.



As the track continues to gain traction, Erima proves that she is not just another voice in the crowd but a rising star with a story to tell and a sound that resonates.




Stream Mogbe Rmx

Emerging Nigerian talent Rozzz makes an unforgettable entrance with his debut single, “Things Fall Apart”—a soulful, genre-blending ballad that captures the emotional wreckage of love lost. 







Deeply introspective and gracefully melancholic, the track is a stunning showcase of vulnerability and artistry.



A Soundtrack for Broken Hearts



From its opening notes, “Things Fall Apart” sets a moody tone—wrapped in rich sonic textures and a slow-burning groove. The song doesn’t seek pity—it tells its story with clarity, pain, and poetic honesty. Rozzz’s voice floats between strength and softness, guiding listeners through the wreckage of a relationship with raw emotional gravity.



Pen Game Strong: Rozzz as a Storyteller



What makes Rozzz stand out isn’t just the music—it’s the songwriting. His lyrics feel like scenes from a well-shot film, turning heartbreak into an immersive experience. 







Drawing from influences like Ed Sheeran, Linkin Park, 2Face Idibia, and Asa, Rozzz seamlessly blends Afrosoul, R&B, and alternative energy into something truly his own.



More Than Just a Debut—Rozzz Has Been Putting in Work



Though “Things Fall Apart” marks his official solo debut, Rozzz isn’t new to the game. With a background in psychology and a strong pen, he’s written for major campaigns like Honda x Davido’s Billboard campaign, and worked alongside artists such as Lila Ike, Psycho YP, Ladipoe (on “Hallelujah”), and Tomi Owo.




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Rozzz (@s_rozzz)




Now, stepping into his own spotlight, Rozzz delivers a debut that feels both timely and timeless.



Final Thoughts



“Things Fall Apart” isn’t just a song—it’s a statement. It introduces Rozzz as a fearless new voice in Afrofusion—one that’s unafraid to sit with pain, process it, and turn it into something beautiful.



If this is the first chapter, we can’t wait to hear the rest.




Stream Now

The streets are buzzing and the energy is rising—Contra Banz, the genre-blending Nigerian artist known for his bold mix of Drill, Afro-pop, and Dance, is back with a vengeance. His upcoming project, HITMAN ALL DAY EVERYDAY, drops on April 11, and it’s set to be his most defining body of work yet.







Born Moses Oluwajuwonlo Samson, Contra Banz—popularly known as Eruku Flows—has been steadily carving out a space for himself in Nigeria’s ever-evolving music scene. From the raw lyrical intensity of his 2020 debut project Birth of a Hitman, to the genre-hopping brilliance of his Contrabanz EP, he has proven to be a sonic shapeshifter, unafraid to experiment and expand his creative universe.



With HITMAN ALL DAY EVERYDAY, Contra Banz is going full throttle. This isn’t just another tape—it’s a bold statement. It reflects his evolution as an artist, a celebration of hustle culture, and a reminder of why he’s a force to reckon with. The project promises aggressive energy, street-rooted storytelling, and beats that command movement—whether you’re in Lagos traffic or on global dance floors.







Now based in Lagos but rooted in Oyo State, Contra Banz continues to push the boundaries of Afro-fusion. His vibrant energy, unforgettable flows, and sharp lyricism make him one of the most exciting voices of the new wave.



Mark your calendars. April 11 isn’t just a release date—it’s a takeover. Whether you’re a day-one fan or just catching the Eruku Flows fever, HITMAN ALL DAY EVERYDAY is the moment you don’t want to miss.

On Today’s episode we spoke to RHAGETTI an amazing talent taking the mainstream approach to becoming a megastar with his new release ‘PROPANE’







WHERE HE COMES FROM



At what point did you realize that music was your true calling, and what inspired you to pursue it professionally?




At 5 years old, when I first saw a video of Michael Jackson’s “Smooth Criminal,” that automatically awakened the passion for music in me. Though I started off emulating his dance moves, I then progressed to singing. From there, my love for music kept growing, and people started identifying me as the music guy from my childhood days and urged me to take it seriously, and so I did.




Your music blends Afrobeats, R&B, Afro-Pop, Dancehall, and Reggae. Which artists or experiences shaped this eclectic style during your formative years?




Kanye West inspired how I make music. Albums like 808s & Heartbreak and Graduation shaped me creatively. People call it genres, but I call it avenues to make good music, so it doesn’t matter what genre it is—I tap from them as long as the final product is good music. I feel that’s the beauty of creativity, the fact that you’re free to explore these sounds and try out stuff. For me, this is my biggest strength. Musically, I’m an explorer, and I’ll put my touch on anything I explore. I feel that’s how I invent something new with the music. There are no boundaries for me.








Beginning your musical journey in 2015, what were some significant challenges you faced, and how did you navigate them?




I tell you one fact: a lot of mistakes were made. From the music to the business to the crew, it was a mess. The only thing solid from that time was the vision, which made me stay focused on the mission. I had to reevaluate stuff and learn from my mistakes. I wouldn’t be too hard on myself, though, because I was a rookie, very young and inexperienced. But those mistakes shaped who I am today, and looking back, it was a learning curve.




Reflecting on your career, which moments or achievements stand out as pivotal in your growth as an artist?




2021, when I dropped the Waveboy EP, marked a new era in my career. You see, I have two parts of my music career: 2015 to 2020 and 2021 to date. That EP was me overcoming my trials and tribulations with the music and reaffirming my intent with this music thing. Because I took a break before then and proceeded to work behind the scenes for other people while contemplating if I’d continue my solo career or not. Dropping that EP was like fighting off my demons and coming out on top, and most importantly, I was happy with myself creatively.




You’ve cited influences like Burna Boy, Kizz Daniel, Wizkid, and Davido. How have these artists impacted your musical direction?




Burna, for me, stands for hard work and resilience. I see a lot of myself in him, from the point where you can be super talented and have to break through rocks to gain recognition. Kizz Daniel, for me, is straight-up talent. Wizkid, for me, is vision. His talent is not up for debate, but what stands out to me is the vision; I feel he is ahead of his time. How he operates, you can tell the man has long-term goals, and he’s not living in the moment. Davido represents passion, and I admire Olamide a lot too. For me, I look at people doing great things, and I draw inspiration from their biggest strength.








Your goal is to merge Afrocentric vibes with global sounds. What unique elements do you incorporate to achieve this fusion?




It’s the sounds. I try to evoke emotions with my music. When making a song, I try to experiment a lot with different sounds. I want my music to go beyond boundaries, so I infuse a lot of elements into the sound. At the end of the day, I want everybody to feel connected when they listen to my records, be it from the melodies, lyrics, drums, guitars, etc.




WHERE HE’S GOING TO



Congratulations on the release of “Propane”. What inspired this track, and what message do you hope listeners take away from it?




Thank you very much. Propane is a record inspired by the current gender wars infiltrating our social media space. It seems men have issues with women, and women have issues with men. It’s chaos, lol. So I’m like, let’s bring love back. There are still good women out there, and there are good men who appreciate good women. So Propane is like an ode to an amazing woman who lights up your world like propane does.





        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by ʟᴀ ᴡᴀᴠᴇ 👽🛸 (@rhagetti)




How does “Propane” differ from your previous releases, and what does it signify about your evolution as an artist?




Propane is different. Propane is unique. And Propane is one of my best works yet. I’m on a mission to carve a niche for the brand Rhagetti through my music, and Propane is a huge step in that direction. I want to make music where people feel they know the artist, even if they just heard it for the first

The wait is over—OJ and Zee Flex have officially dropped their highly anticipated single, “I AM,” and it’s everything fans hoped for and more. A bold fusion of raw lyricism, rich storytelling, and genre-defying sound, this track is already making waves and proving why these two artists are a powerful duo to watch.







OJ, celebrated for his gritty bars and authentic flow, joins forces with Zee Flex, the genre-bending multi-talent from Kaduna, Nigeria. With a sound that weaves traditional African instruments into modern beats, and lyrics that explore themes of love, social justice, and self-empowerment, Zee Flex brings an unforgettable vibe to the track. Inspired by icons like Eminem, Kendrick Lamar, Gabzy, and even James Bond, his influence is unmistakable in this collaboration.



The Story Behind the Music



Born from a completely unplanned studio session, “I AM” came to life in a flash of creative synergy. What began as a laid-back hangout turned into an all-night studio lock-in the moment the beat hit. Both artists felt the magic instantly, and what followed was a spontaneous yet deeply intentional crafting of a record that speaks to identity, perseverance, and power.









From OJ’s piercing delivery to Zee Flex’s melodic edge and genre-blending finesse, “I AM” captures lightning in a bottle—showcasing both artists at their most expressive and fearless.



The Buzz Is Real



Social media is lit with excitement. Fans are calling “I AM” a statement piece—an anthem of self-awareness and defiance that reflects today’s cultural and musical moment. Early listeners are praising the chemistry between OJ and Zee Flex, and industry insiders are hailing the track as a standout in 2025’s hip-hop and Afro-fusion landscape.



Why This Release Stands Out



“I AM” isn’t just a collaboration—it’s a movement. It bridges cultures, sounds, and generations. It underscores OJ’s commitment to lyrical depth and authenticity, while highlighting Zee Flex’s ability to innovate and captivate across genres. The track holds its own among a new wave of music that’s emotionally honest, musically rich, and culturally resonant.



With no gimmicks, just pure talent and storytelling, this single marks a pivotal moment for both artists as they continue redefining what modern African music can be.

Ghana’s dynamic drill music scene is about to be electrified once more with the release of Saka, the latest single from the formidable group, SAVAGE 4. 







Set for release on April 4, 2025, this track promises to further cement their reputation for delivering raw energy and authentic narratives from the streets of Accra.Who is SAVAGE 4?SAVAGE 4 is an afro drill music group that has quickly gained recognition for their raw energy, gritty lyrics, and authentic portrayal of street life. Emerging from the vibrant music scene of Accra, the group has captured the hearts of fans both locally and internationally with their hard-hitting tracks and captivating performances. Their music reflects the realities of urban Ghana, blending powerful storytelling with electrifying beats that resonate deeply with listeners.







Emerging from Accra’s vibrant neighborhoods, SAVAGE 4 has rapidly ascended the ranks of Ghanaian drill artists. Their previous hits, such as Makaveli featuring Kwame Dabie and Badman Riddim with Tsuii Gang, have showcased their ability to blend gritty storytelling with compelling beats. Their unique style offers listeners an unfiltered glimpse into urban life, resonating with fans both locally and internationally.



Song Overview









Saka delves deep into themes of resilience and ambition. The track’s mood oscillates between introspective verses and anthemic choruses, capturing the essence of street survival and dreams of ascension. Standout lyrics reflect the group’s commitment to authenticity and their roots. The production, helmed by the talented AKB, is characterized by pulsating basslines and haunting melodies, creating a soundscape that’s both immersive and evocative.Cultural & Industry ImpactPositioned within the burgeoning Asakaa movement—a Ghanaian adaptation of drill music—Saka exemplifies the genre’s evolution in West Africa. SAVAGE 4’s contribution to this scene is significant, as they infuse local dialects and rhythms, distinguishing their sound from other drill interpretations globally. Their collaborations with artists like Kwame Dabie and Tsuii Gang further highlight their influence and commitment to elevating Ghanaian drill on the world stage.Audience & Reception



Anticipation for Saka has been building, with teasers on platforms like Instagram hinting at its imminent release. Fans have expressed excitement, eager to experience the group’s latest offering. Given SAVAGE 4’s track record and the song’s compelling narrative, Saka is poised for significant streaming success and potential viral moments, especially within communities passionate about drill music.




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by SAVAGE 4🦅 (@wethesavage4)




Saka is more than just a song; it’s a testament to SAVAGE 4’s artistry and their unwavering dedication to storytelling through music. Whether you’re navigating the bustling streets of Accra or seeking an authentic drill experience, this track is a must-listen. Mark your calendars for April 4, 2025, and get ready to immerse yourself in the raw, unfiltered energy of Saka. Share it with fellow music enthusiasts and stay connected with SAVAGE 4 as they continue to shape the future of Ghanaian drill.
