Tommy Pizzle hails from the vibrant streets of Ijebu Ode. He is quickly making waves in the Nigerian hip-hop scene. His approach to rap is raw and unapologetic. His genre is rooted in hard-hitting realism. He channels the energy of his surroundings into vivid storytelling. His lyrics are socially conscious.



Tommy Pizzle



The Journey from Ijoko Sango Ota



Emerging from the gritty streets of Ijoko Sango Ota, Tommy Pizzle’s journey into music is deeply intertwined with his environment. His raw and aggressive flow captures the complexities of life in the urban jungle. It offers listeners a front-row seat to real-life events. His flow highlights societal struggles and personal experiences. His music resonates with those who crave authenticity and transparency, creating a powerful connection with his audience.



The Sound of Truth



At the core of Tommy Pizzle’s artistry lies an unwavering commitment to truth. His lyrics tackle public problems, amplify the voices of the overlooked, and offer unfiltered commentary on the state of society. Tommy Pizzle’s resolute delivery isn’t just rap. It’s a call to action. He challenges listeners to rethink the status quo and pushes for meaningful conversations.









Amplifying the Voiceless



What sets Tommy Pizzle apart is his mission to represent the underrepresented. He speaks for those often silenced through his music. He shines a light on the struggles and triumphs of everyday life in Nigeria. Tommy Pizzle addresses systemic issues. He shares his personal story. He is determined to amplify the voices of the degraded. He inspires others to rise above their circumstances.



A Rising Star in Nigerian Hip-Hop



Tommy Pizzle’s fearless approach and powerful lyricism make him one of the most compelling voices to emerge from Ijebu Ode. He paints vivid pictures of life’s realities through rap. This ability has solidified his place as an artist to watch in the ever-evolving Nigerian music landscape.









As Tommy Pizzle continues his journey, his mission is to challenge the norms. Amplifying truth remains at the heart of his artistry. With his undeniable talent and authenticity, he’s poised to leave an indelible mark on Nigerian hip-hop and beyond.

Lagos is the bustling epicenter of Nigeria’s creative scene. It continues to birth groundbreaking talent. Manu3l is a name destined to resonate far beyond its borders. Manu3l is a multi-faceted artist. He seamlessly blends Alternative Rap and Drill with deeply rooted Nigerian influences. He is redefining the boundaries of storytelling in music.



Manu3l



A Journey into Rap



Manu3l began his journey into music during his early years. He drew inspiration from the golden era of rap between 2009 and 2011. At a young age, he wrote his first song in junior secondary school (JSS1). He was inspired by Kanye West’s hit “Black Skinhead.” His budding passion for hip-hop was fueled by an ever-expanding list of influences. These include Santan Dave, Stormzy, Kendrick Lamar, Eminem, NF, and early MI Abaga.









By 2015, Manu3l’s musical identity began to take a distinctive shape. He drew heavily from the UK rap scene. He seamlessly fused its raw edge with his Nigerian roots. This created a hybrid style that stands out in Lagos’ vibrant rap culture.



Music with Depth



Manu3l’s artistry transcends just rap. His music is a canvas on which he paints stories inspired by his environment and the world around him. His lyricism is a refreshing blend of emotional depth. It showcases thought-provoking themes and raw energy. He achieves this with minimal use of profanity. It is a testament to the influence of artists like NF. His sound reflects a wish to inspire and connect with audiences on a personal level.









More Than Music



What sets Manu3l apart is his multifaceted talent. Beyond music, he is an accomplished visual artist and designer, with a deep appreciation for creativity in all forms. This versatility gives his artistry a unique edge. It allows him to craft a distinct visual and auditory experience for his audience.



Looking Ahead



As one of Lagos’ emerging stars, Manu3l is a force to watch in the Nigerian rap scene. He weaves together UK Drill influences with Nigerian sounds. His personal storytelling positions him as a torchbearer for a new era of alternative rap. With every track, Manu3l invites listeners into his world—one filled with inspiration, authenticity, and undeniable talent.

In just four short months, Independence Jorji—better known as Ms. Jorji—has taken the music world by storm. Her journey is nothing short of extraordinary. She reached the top of RADARCharts. She is the first female artist to achieve this milestone on the platform’s new chart. With her debut single “Pami” leading the charge, Ms. Jorji is proving to be a trailblazer in the global Afrobeat and trap scene.







The African Bad Girl on Tour



Presently headlining her groundbreaking ABG (African Bad Girl) Tour across Africa, Ms. Jorji has electrified fans with her raw talent and magnetic stage presence. The tour has seen her dominate performances, engage in vibrant radio tours, and connect with fans in deeply personal ways. Her ability to light up university campuses and major venues alike is a testament to her versatility as a performer.







Ms. Jorji’s fanbase, affectionately known as “Jorjipets,” has grown exponentially with each performance. She keeps her audience captivated through social media. Her Instagram page offers behind-the-scenes glimpses of her tour life and music-making process.



The Birth of a Star



Born and raised in Nigeria, Ms. Jorji describes herself as someone who speaks her native language first. She speaks English last. This makes her art deeply rooted in her heritage. The most remarkable part of her story? She only discovered her talent for rap four months ago. “I didn’t even know I rap! Now that I’ve found my voice, I am here and ready,” she shared in an interview.







Her sound is a genre-bending blend of Afrobeat and trap. It creates a unique vibe. This vibe resonates with a new generation of music lovers. Tracks like “Shake It” and “Wassup” highlight her skill in merging fiery lyricism with head-nodding beats. This solidifies her as a force to be reckoned with.



Topping the RADARCharts



Ms. Jorji’s rise to the number one spot on RADARCharts is a historic achievement. Her chart-topping single “Pami,” a collaboration with Big Orch, has garnered thousands of streams across Spotify and other platforms. The track’s infectious rhythm and relatable lyrics make it a standout anthem of empowerment and celebration.







For RADARCharts, this moment is monumental as Ms. Jorji becomes the first female artist to top the new chart. Her success indicates a shift in the music industry. More African artists, especially women, are taking center stage on the global scene.



A Star in the Making



Ms. Jorji’s incredible journey is only just beginning. Her determination, talent, and authenticity set her apart in an industry that’s constantly evolving. The ABG Tour was successful. Her rapid rise on RADARCharts highlights her potential. She is positioned to become a global icon.



For now, Ms. Jorji is laser-focused on her craft, stating, “I’ve found my voice, and I’m here to stay.” Her story serves as a powerful reminder that sometimes, the greatest talents are discovered in the most unexpected moments.









As Ms. Jorji continues to blaze her trail, one thing is clear: this African Bad Girl is just getting started. Stay tuned for more chart-topping hits, electrifying performances, and the rise of a true music legend.

You’ve been active in music for over a decade. How has your upbringing in both Saskatoon and Zaria shaped your unique sound and artistic identity?



• 10 years deep in the game and honestly, I feel like I’m new to it every time. Growing up in Saskatoon, my mom was constantly recording specials on cassette for us, so that got me in contact with artists like Michael Jackson, Sade, Kriss Kross, etc. Seeing their artistry up close definitely had an impact on me. Zaria was more of a hip-hop center, and that allowed me to tap into Biggie, Jay-Z, Nas, etc. This gave me some sort of balance regarding the genres I felt comfortable drawing inspiration from.



Your music often touches on introspection and personal growth. What moments in your life have had the biggest influence on your lyrics and creative process?



• Growing up in an environment where I saw my brothers and their peers dabble in music and try to tell a story—our story—was definitely a turning point for me. At times, it felt like an obligation to carry on with the tradition and also for the fact that I was always taught to dream and believe that anything I wanted to do was possible.







One of my major influences was my childhood friend Aaron convincing me that I had the prospects and possessed relatability in the way I composed my music. All I needed to do was to take it seriously, and I haven’t looked back since then.



Your sound straddles hip-hop and R&B with a largely eclectic approach. How do you balance these genres to maintain your artistic authenticity?



• I really don’t give it much thought and basically allow the music to do all the talking. I never try to force anything when it comes to making music, and I believe there’s a song for every mood. So I like to approach making music like that.



The themes in your music—dedication, independence, and social commentary—resonate deeply. How do you ensure your message reaches and inspires your audience?



• I try to make sure the music is genuine, and I try to make sure it comes from the heart. I know that as human beings, we’re all going through the same shit (pardon my expletives). So I try to be a voice for the voiceless.



Over the years, how has your approach to creating music evolved, from your early demos in 2012 to your most recent releases in 2024?



• Not much has changed, to be honest. I started learning how to make proper songs by writing music with the collective BHP. We would sit down and analyze the type of music that needed to be made and how to go about it. Nowadays, it’s just more refined, and as I continue to write about my experiences, it makes it much easier to channel the right emotions and the right message.



What challenges have you faced while navigating the music industry, and how have they shaped your career today?



• I’m sure the challenges I’ve faced are general problems and are definitely not peculiar to me. Dishonesty, lack of transparency, envy, greed, jealousy—the list goes on and on. The truth is that they probably won’t end anytime soon, but experience is the best teacher, and these things will continue to help me make better-informed decisions along the way.



Looking back on your career so far, what project or milestone are you most proud of, and why?



• I’m proud of every single project because behind every project, there’s a mad story right there. I’m even proud of the ones I haven’t done yet because they’re going to play a role in my story.



As both an artist and a businessman, how do you manage the balance between creativity and the commercial aspects of your career?



• To be honest, it is no easy task, but the best ones have done it before me, so it’s easy to learn from their experiences and mistakes. I pattern myself in a way that I can balance proficiency in both aspects.



Independence is a recurring theme in your work. What does independence mean to you as an artist in the modern music industry?



• Independence means moving in a way that is true to you. There’s little or nothing that will make you compromise on what you set out to do initially. Independence means taking control of your narrative and allowing people to appreciate you for who you are and your uniqueness.

• More music that is both introspective and intriguing at the same time. My music will continue to tell the story of boys and girls like me who have strived to make something of themselves. My hope for my legacy is to be the first of many who will make it off their craft and personality. Consistency is the first step to building the legacy. Every other thing will follow after that.

Are there any specific artists or producers, locally or globally, that you would like to collaborate with to further expand your sound?

• I would really love to make some shit with Sarz. He has always been eclectic in his approach to making music. I would love to do some stuff within the South African rap scene as well—Emtee, A-Reece. I wish AKA was alive, man. That’s one collab that would’ve changed my life. RIP Supa Mega.

How do you hope to use your platform to inspire the next generation of artists, especially in the Nigerian music scene?

• Personally, I would love to inspire originality from artists who want to share their craft with the world. To embrace their authenticity and to be unapologetic with their sound and aesthetic.

GIDI Cypher: The Pulse of Lagos



The GIDI Cypher is presented and hosted by THE PLUG FROM THE STREET. It offers a raw and unfiltered lyrical exploration of life in Lagos. It also highlights the surge of the African youth. This cypher captures the realities of navigating chaos. It involves chasing dreams and thriving against all odds. These experiences unfold in one of Africa’s most vibrant cities.







Each artist brings their unique voice and story. They weave sharp wordplay, thought-provoking rhymes, and captivating flows. These elements reflect the grit, ambition, and unrelenting energy of Lagos life. GIDI Cypher isn’t just a showcase—it’s an anthem of resilience, creativity, and the spirit of a generation. It is powered by THE PLUG FROM THE STREET’s unwavering commitment to elevate young, dynamic voices.







The goals are clear:



• Discovering and Showcasing Talent: Traveling across states and universities, uncovering the most promising rap stars.



• Providing a Platform for Excellence: Creating cypher sessions where young artists unleash their lyrical and melodic talents.



• Amplifying Nigerian Music Globally: Building a platform that garners respect and attention from music labels, fans, and distributors worldwide.



• Celebrating Diversity: With plans to include other genres in the future, this project reflects the richness of African music.



Stars of THE PFTS CYPHER SERIES









Jxck Frost – The Ice King of Nigerian Rap 



Jxck Frost



A lyrical powerhouse, Jxck Frost blends Afro-infused hip-hop with clever wordplay, multi-syllabic rhymes, and storytelling. Inspired by legends like J.Cole, Eminem, MI, and Olamide, he’s on a mission to put African rap on the global stage. Jxck Frost’s unique ability to fuse raw energy with catchy hooks makes him a name to watch.



Enzzy Boi – Afrobeat’s Voice of Resilience



Enzzy boi



Known for his melodic approach and heartfelt storytelling, Enzzy Boi brings his personal struggles to life through music. Tracks like Far Away delve into themes of depression. They also explore hope. His Guinness World Record achievement proves his relentless drive. With hits like Jaga Jaga and Groove, Enzzy Boi is carving a path of success. He balances his music career with his education.



Fozter – Nigeria’s Lyrical Beast



Fozter 



With countless accolades under his belt, Fozter is a force to reckon with in the Nigerian rap scene. From Hennessy VS Class to Boomplay’s Pass The Mic, he has consistently proven his mettle. Fozter secured collaborations with legends like Tech N9ne and MI Abaga. His raw energy and precision make him an undeniable star of the cypher series.



Astrumm – The Eastern Lyricist



Astrumm



Born to shine, Astrumm brings intricate lyricism and magnetic flows to the table. With inspiration from icons like Nicki Minaj, Tupac, and Fela Kuti, Astrumm’s sound blends international appeal with African roots. Her viral Shutdown cover and freestyle prowess have positioned her as a rising star with a voice that demands attention.



Tommy Pizzle – The Urban Chronicler



Tommy Pizzle



Emerging from Ijoko Sango Ota, Tommy Pizzle delivers hard-hitting narratives about life, societal issues, and personal struggles. With his unapologetically raw style, he challenges the norm, amplifying voices that often go unheard. Tommy Pizzle represents the spirit of authenticity, making him a perfect fit for the PFTS Cypher Series.



Vwore: The Technical Wordsmith



VWORE fka Propaganda Grey



Formerly known as Propaganda Grey, Vwore is a lyrical craftsman and a dedicated student of the art form, hailing from Delta State. His journey into hip-hop began after being inspired by the Disney film Let It Shine, where he realized his dream of making music on a grand scale.



Drawing influences from icons like Kendrick Lamar, Drake, Odumodublvck, M.I Abaga, and most notably, Lil Wayne, Vwore’s style is marked by intricate wordplay, sharp delivery, and an unmistakable passion for storytelling.



Manu3l: The Storytelling Visionary



Manu3l



Manu3l is a multifaceted rapper whose journey into music began with the influence of the dynamic 2009-2011 rap scene. He wrote his first song as a Junior Secondary School student, drawing inspiration from Kanye West’s iconic track “Black.” By 2015, Manu3l started weaving elements of the UK rap scene into his craft, blending it seamlessly with his Nigerian roots to create a unique and captivating sound.



His influences include Santan Dave, Stormzy, Kendrick Lamar, Eminem, NF (whose minimal use of cuss words inspired Manu3l’s lyrical approach), and the legendary M.I Abaga during his early days.



Why THE PFTS CYPHER SERIES is a Game Changer



The PFTS Cypher Series is more than a music project—it’s a movement. It’s about:



• Creating opportunities for underrepresented voices.



• Building a community of rap enthusiasts who support emerging talent.



• Establishing a global platform that highlights Nigerian artistry.

In a world where photography is both an art and a medium of storytelling, Yanga Visuals has emerged as a name synonymous with innovation, creativity, and excellence. Kingsley Ndubuisi Ebere, popularly known as Yanga Visuals, is a self-taught photographer and creative director who has become a beacon of inspiration in Nigeria’s creative industry. Based in Abuja and hailing from Ebonyi State, Yanga Visuals’ work is a masterful fusion of artistic vision and technical brilliance.







The Visionary Behind the Lens



Yanga Visuals is not just a photographer; he is a storyteller, using his camera to weave narratives that resonate deeply with his audience. His unique style seamlessly blends creative portraiture, high-fashion editorial storytelling, commercial photography, and traditional art, creating images that are as bold and vibrant as they are emotive.



Each photograph by Yanga Visuals is a celebration of vibrant colors, striking compositions, and evocative styling. His ability to integrate elements of contemporary and traditional art into his work sets him apart in the highly competitive photography scene. Whether it’s a dynamic fashion shoot, a commercial campaign, or an intimate portrait, Yanga Visuals brings an unmatched level of creativity and professionalism to every project.



A Portfolio of Excellence: Notable Projects



Yanga Visuals’ portfolio is a testament to his artistic versatility and expertise. Here are some of his most popular and groundbreaking projects:




MEN’S RANGEThis fitness campaign is a burst of energy and inspiration. With visuals that ignite motivation, MEN’S RANGE is the perfect fit for fitness magazines and brands looking to captivate their audience.



FÀÁJÌ EXPRESSA celebration of Nigeria’s vibrant fashion and social culture, this project captures the essence of Nigeria’s celebratory spirit with bold colors, dynamic poses, and cultural depth.



THIS IS FASHIONA high-fashion editorial masterpiece, this project blends edgy aesthetics with urban backdrops, redefining the boundaries of fashion photography.



ANDI-KANA project that exemplifies the power of visual storytelling. ANDI-KAN is a compelling editorial portrait series that captivates with its depth and emotion.



THIAGO THE EYE



TERMS & CONDITIONS



PHONE CONVERSATIONS








Balancing Creativity and Professionalism



What makes Yanga Visuals stand out in the crowded photography landscape is his ability to balance boundless creativity with unmatched professionalism. His works are not only visually stunning but also deeply evocative, making them ideal for editorial spreads, advertising campaigns, and personal portraits. Yanga Visuals understands the importance of storytelling in every frame, making his photographs not just images but experiences.



Pushing Boundaries in Nigerian Photography



With a commitment to pushing boundaries, Yanga Visuals has carved a niche for himself as a dynamic and forward-thinking photographer. His bold approach to composition, use of vibrant colors, and meticulous attention to detail have earned him recognition as one of the most innovative photographers in the Nigerian creative industry.



What’s Next for Yanga Visuals?



As Yanga Visuals continues to expand his artistic horizons, audiences can expect even more groundbreaking projects that challenge norms and redefine modern photography. Whether he’s capturing the vibrancy of Nigerian culture or producing stunning fashion campaigns, Yanga Visuals’ work promises to inspire and captivate for years to come.



Stay connected with Yanga Visuals on his journey to reshape the future of photography, one frame at a time.



Instagram

Dear RADARCommunity,



As we step into 2025, RADARCharts is thrilled to announce our official return to full operations on Monday, ushering in a transformative era for our brand and community. We’ve been working tirelessly to bring upgrades and innovations that will not only elevate the RADAR experience but also solidify our position as the hub for creative talent and groundbreaking artistry.



This new chapter is about coming back stronger, sharper, and more impactful than ever.



What’s New in RADAR 2025?



Official brand logo



Spotlight for Artists and Photographers



We’re amplifying our efforts to provide visibility for creatives. RADARCharts will spotlight emerging and established artists, as well as photographers, offering them a dedicated platform to share their work and gain recognition.



Exclusive Articles for RADARArtists



Stay informed and inspired! Our curated articles will provide insights, resources, and strategies for artists to navigate the ever-evolving creative industry. Whether it’s tips on branding, release strategies, or personal growth, we’ve got you covered.



Introducing the Brand-New RADAR Website & Store



Say hello to www.radarcharts.net!



Our new website is your one-stop hub for all things RADAR. From discovering talent to engaging with our content, this platform will be the core of our operations moving forward.



In addition, we’re proud to introduce the RADARStore, a marketplace designed specifically for artists. Here, you can easily book tools, assets, and services to enhance your releases and artistic projects. Whether you need promotional materials, cover art, or event assets, the RADARStore is built to support your creative journey.



Rebranding Talk To Us Magazine: A New Voice for 2025



As part of RADARCharts’ commitment to continuous innovation, Talk To Us Magazine is undergoing a major rebranding to better serve and engage our creative community. With fresh ideas, upgraded designs, and interactive content, the magazine is set to become a centerpiece of the RADAR experience.



Tap to visit magazine 



RADARDiscovery: Growing Our Playlist Forums



The RADARDiscovery initiative remains at the heart of our mission, and we’re committed to expanding its reach. Through RADARDiscovery, we continue to provide a space for undiscovered talents to thrive, while enhancing our playlist forums.



This year, expect new playlists that reflect the incredible growth within our community. These playlists will showcase the diversity, innovation, and passion that define RADAR artists and ensure their voices reach broader audiences.



Celebrating the RADARCommunity



We’ve achieved so much together, and it’s time to highlight those unforgettable moments. Through features, highlights, and throwbacks, we’ll celebrate the milestones that have shaped the RADARCommunity.



ON THE RADAR: The Campus Tour







Our ON THE RADAR event tag, which launched the pioneer set of 2024, returns bigger and better! As we prioritize these trailblazing creatives, we’re embarking on a campus tour in 2025, bringing the RADAR experience to students and young talents across the country. Get ready to discover the next wave of creators on the rise!



Rebranding for the New Era



We’ve reimagined our brand templates to reflect our upgraded identity. The new look aligns with our website, ensuring a cohesive and distinct aesthetic for RADARCharts in 2025.



New Charts Coming Soon



Our updated charts will celebrate the best of RADAR’s pioneer artists from 2024, while spotlighting new talents. Expect more comprehensive and dynamic rankings as we continue to showcase excellence.



Introducing RADARCyphers



In collaboration with Royal Empire Management, RADARCyphers will feature thrilling musical showcases, spotlighting our top-tier artists and fostering collaboration within the RADAR community. This new initiative promises to be a breeding ground for creative synergy and groundbreaking performances.



Tap to view profile



RADAR Tradition, Bigger Dreams



While we embrace innovation, we remain rooted in our traditions. The RADARDiscovery and playlist forums are pillars of our mission to foster growth and discovery. This year, we’re not just continuing these traditions; we’re scaling them to new heights, ensuring every artist has the opportunity to shine.



Thank You for Being a Part of RADARCharts



As we embark on this exciting journey, we want to thank you for your unwavering support and belief in our mission. RADARCharts is more than just a platform—it’s a community, a movement, and a vision for the future of art and creativity.



We can’t wait to share 2025 with you. Together, let’s make it the most remarkable year yet.



Stay creative,



The RADARCharts Team



Visit us: www.radarcharts.net



Follow us for updates!

The new year brings a fresh chapter for Nigerian Afro-fusion star Big Khalie, formerly known as Khalie, as he steps into 2025 with a powerful rebrand, an exciting new single titled Friday, and the announcement of his independent music brand and label, Pepper Music.







Big Khalie: The Next Evolution of an Afro-Fusion Star



Born Adeyemo Khalil and raised in Kwara State, Big Khalie has made a lasting mark in the Afro-fusion scene. Known for his unique blend of infectious rhythms and vibrant melodies, he has captivated audiences with hits like Steady Riddim (Move) and Blessings (Shower).



Now managed by Royal Empire Management, Big Khalie’s transformation marks a new era in his career. The rebrand reflects his ambition to scale new heights while staying true to his roots. His signature tag, “Pepper,” embodies his bold, flavorful artistry and now takes center stage as the inspiration behind his independent music brand and label, Pepper Music.







Introducing Pepper FC



Pepper isn’t just a name—it’s a movement. As his own music brand and independent label, Pepper Music represents Big Khalie’s commitment to creative freedom and artistic authenticity. By running his own label, Big Khalie is taking full control of his music journey, building a legacy on his own terms, and creating opportunities for himself and emerging talents in the Afro-fusion space.



“Pepper Music is more than a brand; it’s a family, a lifestyle, and a platform to showcase bold, innovative music,” says Big Khalie. “It’s about doing things my way and sharing that vision with the world.”



New Single: ‘Friday’



To kick off this exciting new era, Big Khalie is set to release Friday, a track that perfectly captures the carefree, celebratory spirit of the weekend. With Afro-fusion vibes and soulful highlife energy, Friday is a vibrant anthem for anyone looking to unwind and dance their worries away.

“Friday is all about living in the moment, celebrating the little joys, and starting the weekend with good vibes,” shares Big Khalie. “It’s the perfect soundtrack for anyone who loves to vibe and enjoy life.”

With Friday set to drop soon, Big Khalie is setting the tone for an ambitious year ahead. Through Pepper Music, he plans to release more groundbreaking music, collaborate with rising stars, and solidify his place as a leader in the Afro-fusion space.



His rebrand, independent label, and upcoming projects signal that Big Khalie is ready to dominate 2025 with his signature blend of bold artistry and entrepreneurial spirit.

British-Nigerian rap sensation AnaYor is gearing up to kick off 2025 with a bang! His highly anticipated single, Cole Palmer, is set to release on January 10th, drawing inspiration from Chelsea’s rising star whose composure and brilliance on the pitch perfectly mirror AnaYor’s icy, hard-hitting lyricism.







AnaYor: A Future Star of Rap



With a sound that fuses British rap precision with electrifying Nigerian energy, AnaYor has quickly established himself as a force to be reckoned with. Based in Abuja, AnaYor’s music takes listeners on a journey of self-discovery, tackling issues like mental health, addiction, family, and growing up as a black man in the UK.







In just three releases, AnaYor has amassed close to 40,000 streams on Spotify, gaining recognition from top broadcast companies like SoundCity FM, Cool FM, Max FM, and Beat FM. With his genre-defying flows and out-of-the-box style, AnaYor is primed to dominate the rap scene.



‘Cole Palmer’: Bars as Cold as Ice



Inspired by the calm, calculated brilliance of Chelsea midfielder Cole Palmer, AnaYor’s upcoming single embodies unshakable confidence and precision. Just like Palmer controls the game on the pitch, AnaYor commands the mic with sharp bars, sleek delivery, and storytelling that hits hard.



“Cole Palmer is more than just a song; it’s about staying cool under pressure, making every move count, and playing to win,” AnaYor shares. “It’s my way of showing how football and music connect—both are about rhythm, strategy, and heart.”



Packed with punchlines as cold as the January weather, Cole Palmer promises to be the anthem you didn’t know you needed to start the year right.



Don’t Miss the Drop!



Mark your calendars for January 10th and pre-save Cole Palmer today to be among the first to experience AnaYor’s coldest bars yet. This track isn’t just a nod to a football icon—it’s a statement of intent from one of rap’s brightest rising stars.



🎧 Pre-Save ‘Cole Palmer’ Now!



AnaYor is ready to bring the heat (and the ice) this year. Get ready for Cole Palmer—a track as calculated as a game-winning assist and as powerful as a last-minute goal.

In the ever-evolving world of photography, some artists stand out not just for their technical skill but for their ability to tell compelling stories through the lens. Etim Essang, popularly known as Etim Shooter, is one such creative force. Based in Abuja, Nigeria, Etim has made a name for himself as a visual storyteller whose work captures the soul of Nigerian culture, fashion, and landscapes with stunning vibrancy and emotional depth.







A Visionary Behind the Camera



Born with an innate passion for art and storytelling, Etim Shooter has turned his camera into a tool for exploration and expression. His imagery, rich in color and cultural authenticity, reflects the intricate tapestry of Nigerian life. Whether it’s a bustling Lagos street, a serene rural landscape, or the bold aesthetics of modern fashion, Etim’s photographs tell stories that transcend the frame.



Etim’s dedication to his craft is evident in the precision and care with which he approaches each project. His work strikes a perfect balance between technical mastery and creative instinct, resulting in visuals that resonate deeply with audiences.



Signature Projects



Etim Shooter’s portfolio boasts several standout projects that showcase his versatility and creative genius. Some of his most celebrated works include:




FÀÁJÌ EXPRESS: A vivid celebration of Nigeria’s vibrant nightlife and social scene, this project captures the energy, colors, and cultural essence of the country’s celebratory spirit.



Predator



This is Fashion: A high-concept fashion series that pushes boundaries and redefines the intersection of culture and couture.



Mania



Vanity

The Essence of Etim Shooter’s Work



What sets Etim Shooter apart is his ability to infuse every frame with meaning. His images do more than capture moments—they evoke emotions, provoke thought, and celebrate the human experience. By focusing on the nuances of Nigerian culture and the diversity of its people, Etim creates a visual dialogue that bridges the past, present, and future.



The Road Ahead



As one of the leading voices in Nigerian photography, Etim Shooter continues to push creative boundaries. With each project, he redefines what it means to be a visual storyteller in a rapidly changing world. His dedication to his craft, coupled with an unrelenting passion for cultural representation, ensures that his work will remain impactful and timeless.



Follow the Journey



Etim Shooter’s artistry is a testament to the power of photography as a medium for storytelling and cultural preservation. As he continues to explore new themes and perspectives, his work promises to inspire and captivate audiences both in Nigeria and beyond.



Keep up with Etim Shooter on his journey as he paints vivid stories through his lens, one frame at a time.

The Afrobeat scene continues to flourish, and one artist making a name for himself is Twyze. Born in 2002 in Makurdi, Benue State, Nigeria, and now based in Lagos, Twyze is an exciting new voice in the industry. With his infectious rhythms, soulful melodies, and relatable lyrics, he is steadily capturing the hearts of music lovers across the continent.







Rooted in Culture, Inspired by Legends



Growing up in Makurdi, Twyze was immersed in the rich cultural heritage of Benue State. From an early age, he developed a passion for music, drawing inspiration from Afrobeat icons like Fela Kuti, King Sunny Adé, and Ebenezer Obey. These influences helped shape his artistry, giving his sound a timeless quality that blends the best of traditional Afrobeat with contemporary elements.



Finding His Voice in Lagos



In 2023, Twyze relocated to Lagos, the epicenter of Nigeria’s vibrant music scene. The move was pivotal, allowing him to connect with industry professionals, explore new sounds, and refine his craft. Living in Lagos has brought an eclectic edge to his music, combining his Benue roots with the city’s dynamic energy.









Twyze’s sound reflects this fusion—an intoxicating blend of Afrobeat traditions and modern Afro-fusion vibes. This duality is the foundation of his music, allowing him to resonate with listeners across diverse backgrounds and generations.



An Afrobeat Trailblazer in the Making



Since making the leap to Lagos, Twyze has released a series of critically acclaimed singles that have garnered millions of streams. Known for his high-energy live performances and magnetic stage presence, Twyze has built a reputation as an artist who delivers more than just music—he creates an experience.



His music dives deep into themes of love, social issues, and personal growth, offering a soundtrack to life’s highs and lows. It’s this ability to connect with his audience on an emotional level that sets Twyze apart as one of Afrobeat’s brightest rising stars.



A Celebration of His Roots



Despite his growing success, Twyze remains grounded in his cultural heritage, proudly representing his Benue roots. His music serves as a bridge between his upbringing in Makurdi and his current journey in Lagos, celebrating the diversity and unity of Nigerian culture.



Looking Ahead



Twyze’s journey is just beginning, but his impact is already undeniable. As he continues to push the boundaries of Afrobeat, he’s poised to take his music to a global audience. With his distinctive sound, unwavering dedication, and Lagos as his creative hub, Twyze is well on his way to becoming one of the genre’s most influential voices.



Discover the magic of Twyze now and join him on his journey as he redefines the Afrobeat soundscape. With his talent and passion, the sky is truly the limit for this Lagos-based rising star.

Every once in a while, an artist emerges who not only captures the sound of the times but also redefines it. Straight out of Nigeria, Kólá The Ryder (Olakorede Kolawole) is one such talent. With a vibrant mix of Afrofusion and Alté, Kólá’s music is a sonic adventure, combining soulful storytelling with Afro-psychedelic melodies that leave listeners both inspired and entranced.







The Sound and Spirit of Kólá The Ryder



Kólá The Ryder’s music is a rich tapestry of influences, blending traditional African rhythms with modern experimental sounds. His dynamic vocals seamlessly shift between English, Yoruba, and Nigerian Pidgin, reflecting his cultural heritage and his versatility as an artist. Whether delivering introspective verses or infectious hooks, Kólá’s sound radiates originality and authenticity.









His debut single, “Rosa”, introduced the world to his unique style. The track’s hypnotic beats and heartfelt lyrics resonated with fans far and wide, cementing his place as a promising force in the Afrofusion scene. Critics praised “Rosa” for its ability to fuse relatable storytelling with genre-defying production, setting Kólá apart from his peers.



The Mind Behind the Music



Kólá’s artistry is as much about innovation as it is about emotion. With a Master’s degree in Intellectual Property Law, he approaches music creation with a deep understanding of originality and creative ownership. This academic background informs his ability to think outside the box, crafting songs that are not just compelling but also deeply meaningful.









For Kólá, music isn’t just a passion; it’s a vehicle for connection. His lyrics often explore themes of love, identity, and the complexities of modern life, creating an emotional resonance that draws listeners into his world.



What’s Next: The Evolution of Kólá The Ryder



As the buzz surrounding “Rosa” continues to grow, Kólá is gearing up to release his next single, “Mia”. This track promises to be another step forward in his musical evolution, showcasing his ever-expanding range and ability to push creative boundaries. Fans can expect a blend of introspection, rhythm, and innovation that has become synonymous with Kólá’s artistry.







Speaking about his upcoming release, Kólá shared, “‘Mia’ is about embracing the journey, no matter how unpredictable it gets. It’s a reminder that growth happens in the in-between moments, and that’s where the magic lies.”



Why You Should Pay Attention



Kólá The Ryder is more than just a rising artist—he’s a storyteller, a boundary-pusher, and a voice for a generation seeking new ways to connect with their roots while embracing the future. As he continues to carve his niche in the global Afrofusion and Alté landscape, one thing is clear: Kólá The Ryder is an artist you don’t want to miss.



Keep your ears open and your playlists ready—“Mia” is just the beginning of an exciting journey for this Nigerian powerhouse.

In the dynamic world of visual arts, few names stand out as boldly as Emmanuel “Renle” Lucky, or simply Ren. A self-taught photographer and visual arts director from Edo State, Renle is a creative force who seamlessly blends art, culture, and individuality into his work. With his lens capturing the vibrant essence of Nigeria’s urban landscapes and its people, Renle is quickly establishing himself as a pioneer in the field.







A Journey Rooted in Passion



Renle’s path to photography was not conventional, but it was fueled by an unwavering passion for art. Growing up in Edo State and later navigating the bustling creative hubs of Lagos, Abuja, and North Central Nigeria, Renle cultivated his craft organically, guided by his love for visual arts, music, and basketball.



As a retrophile and aesthete, he has a unique talent for finding profound beauty in the everyday—proving that even the seemingly mundane holds artistic potential. “Nothing that truly exists can be called ‘ordinary,’” Renle says, a philosophy that permeates every frame he captures.



Challenging the Status Quo



Renle’s work challenges the traditional norms of Nigerian photography, where technical “cleanliness” often overshadows artistic expression. For him, the focus lies in the interplay of colors, moods, and storytelling. His bold approach has made him a trailblazer, pushing boundaries and reshaping visual narratives. “My goal is to redefine how we see and create in Nigeria. I want to be the King of Visual Creatives,” he shares.

In the vibrant music scene of Abuja, Nigeria, one name is making waves with her unique sound and profound storytelling: Lyna Verse. A dynamic artist and composer, Lyna Verse has captured hearts with her ability to blend creativity, cultural identity, and deeply personal narratives into her Afrobeat sound.







A Rising Star with a Story to Tell



Lyna Verse’s music is more than just entertainment—it’s an invitation to step into her world. Drawing from her background and personal experiences, she crafts songs that reflect her journey, exploring themes of resilience, identity, and the human experience. Whether performing on stage or collaborating with fellow artists, her work resonates deeply, offering listeners an authentic and refreshing perspective.









Her passion for composing catchy yet meaningful songs has earned her recognition from music blogs and industry insiders. With each release, Lyna Verse pushes the boundaries of Afrobeat, blending it with innovative elements to create a sound that’s entirely her own.



Music with a Mission



At the core of Lyna Verse’s artistry is her mission to inspire and provoke thought. She uses her music as a platform for storytelling, addressing challenges and celebrating triumphs in ways that connect with audiences on a personal level. Her work is a testament to the power of art to spark conversations and drive meaningful change.







A Force to Watch



As she continues to grow, Lyna Verse is solidifying her place as one of Abuja’s most exciting musical talents. Her dedication to her craft, combined with her unique ability to fuse creativity with cultural expression, makes her a force to be reckoned with in the Afrobeat scene.









For fans of music that moves the soul and challenges the mind, Lyna Verse is an artist to watch. Stay tuned for her upcoming projects as she continues to redefine what it means to be an Afrobeat storyteller.

Meet Kanayo Victor Uwajeh, better known by his stage name, AnaYor—a fast-rising British-Nigerian rapper who is redefining rap with his unique blend of British style and Nigerian vibrancy. Based in Abuja, Nigeria, AnaYor has carved out a niche with his innovative flows and genre-bending rap style, creating music that transcends boundaries and resonates deeply with listeners.







The AnaYor Sound



AnaYor’s music is not just rap; it’s an experience. His ability to fuse live sounds with gripping lyricism takes listeners on a profound journey of discovery. Through his tracks, he shares deeply personal stories, touching on themes of mental health, addiction, family, and his experiences growing up as a black male in the UK. These raw, emotional narratives are delivered with a style that is undeniably his own—energetic yet reflective, bold yet relatable.









AnaYor’s ability to merge British influences with Nigerian energy forms the backbone of his distinctive sound. Each song is a testament to his versatility and creativity, solidifying his place as one of the most exciting emerging artists in the rap scene.



Making Waves



In just three months, AnaYor has amassed close to 40,000 streams on Spotify across three releases—a remarkable feat for an independent artist on the rise. His music has received widespread support from major broadcast platforms like SoundCity FM, Cool FM, Max FM, and Beat FM in Abuja, signaling his readiness to dominate the industry’s soundscape.









His latest release, “Higher” is a standout track that exemplifies AnaYor’s growth as an artist. With its infectious beats and introspective lyrics, the song has quickly become a fan favorite, showcasing his potential to create hits that resonate on a global scale.



A Star on the Rise



AnaYor isn’t just an artist; he’s a storyteller and a trailblazer. By fearlessly addressing personal struggles and societal issues through his music, he’s creating a space for honest conversations and genuine connections with his audience. His journey from the UK to Nigeria and his ability to infuse these cultural influences into his sound makes him a beacon of innovation in the rap scene.



The Future of Rap



With his unique style, compelling stories, and growing fanbase, AnaYor is undoubtedly one of the future stars of rap. His ability to combine British rap sensibilities with Nigerian energy positions him as a global force to be reckoned with. As he continues to evolve and share his journey through music, AnaYor is a name that music lovers should keep on their radar.







The world better get ready because AnaYor is here to take rap to new heights—and he’s just getting started.

In a world where music is constantly evolving, few artists manage to carve out a genre uniquely their own. Enter Anyafulugo, an Igbo artist whose creation of Afro-Agwu—a genre that masterfully blends traditional Nigerian music with contemporary production—sets him apart as a trailblazer in the industry.







Celebrating Cultural Heritage Through Afro-Agwu



Afro-Agwu, a genre deeply rooted in Anyafulugo’s Igbo heritage, derives its name from the Igbo spiritual concept of “Agwu,” often associated with creativity, wisdom, and a connection to ancestral roots. With this genre, Anyafulugo doesn’t just make music—he crafts an auditory experience that bridges the old and the new. Each track is a celebration of Nigeria’s diverse musical traditions, enriched with modern production techniques to create a sound that is both nostalgic and innovative.









The Global Appeal of Anyafulugo’s Sound



What makes Anyafulugo truly remarkable is his ability to make Afro-Agwu resonate with audiences far beyond Nigeria’s borders. By seamlessly blending the rhythmic and melodic richness of traditional African music with contemporary global trends, he creates a soundscape that feels both familiar and fresh. His work fosters a deeper appreciation for African music worldwide, positioning him as a cultural ambassador who bridges gaps and connects diverse audiences through his art.









A Commitment to Innovation



As an artist, Anyafulugo is defined by his relentless pursuit of originality and his commitment to pushing boundaries. His music is not confined to one style or audience; instead, it is a constantly evolving reflection of his journey and the stories he wants to tell. Through Afro-Agwu, Anyafulugo explores new sonic territories while staying true to his cultural roots, making every song a testament to his creativity and passion for his craft.



Making an Impact on the Modern Music Scene



Anyafulugo’s contribution to the rich tapestry of modern African music cannot be overstated. He stands out not just as a musician but as a visionary who understands the importance of preserving cultural heritage while embracing progress. His work inspires other artists to explore their own roots and innovate, ensuring that African music continues to thrive on the global stage.







What’s Next for Anyafulugo?



With Afro-Agwu as his platform, Anyafulugo’s journey is just beginning. As he continues to release music that captivates listeners and sparks conversations, he is solidifying his place as one of the most exciting and original voices in modern African music. Fans can look forward to more groundbreaking releases and projects that further expand the reach and influence of Afro-Agwu.



Why You Should Pay Attention to Anyafulugo



Anyafulugo isn’t just an artist; he’s a storyteller, a cultural advocate, and a pioneer. His music transcends borders, bringing people together through a shared appreciation for creativity and heritage. If you’re looking for a fresh sound that honors the past while embracing the future, Anyafulugo is the artist to watch.

Emerging from the vibrant music scene of Owerri, Imo State, ICAH is carving a unique space for herself as an independent artist. Blending elements of soul, soft R&B, and alternative music, her sound is a rich tapestry of emotional depth and captivating storytelling. With each note, ICAH invites listeners to experience her world, one filled with vulnerability, creativity, and authenticity.







A Bold Introduction



ICAH’s debut into the music world came through her two-pack single, ICAH (Me & Enough)—a project that showcases her raw emotion and boundless creativity. Each track in the release tells a personal story, underscored by soulful melodies and lyrics that linger long after the song ends. With this debut, ICAH not only introduced her artistry but also set the tone for what listeners can expect: music that resonates deeply.









A Blend of Genres and Emotions



What makes ICAH stand out is her ability to fuse genres seamlessly. Her sound, a mix of soul and soft R&B with touches of alternative flair, creates an emotional experience that feels both contemporary and timeless. Each song is a reflection of her inner world, making her music deeply personal yet universally relatable. This ability to connect on a profound level is what sets her apart from the crowd.



Building Momentum



Although she’s only released two tracks with a feature by Anyafulugo (Ngwo Ngwo) so far, ICAH is already gaining recognition in the music scene. Her growing audience is a testament to her talent and the way her music speaks directly to listeners’ hearts. With every release, she continues to push the boundaries of music, driven by her passion for authentic expression and meaningful connections.



        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by ICAH👽💡🕊️🤞🏾 (@the_icah)
//www.instagram.com/embed.js



The Journey Ahead



For ICAH, music isn’t just a form of entertainment; it’s a way to communicate, heal, and inspire. As she steadily builds her presence, she’s proving that her artistry has no limits. With her unique sound and dedication to storytelling, ICAH is undoubtedly a name to watch in the ever-evolving landscape of soul and R&B.







Whether you’re drawn to her heartfelt lyrics, her soothing melodies, or her ability to blend genres effortlessly, ICAH’s music offers something special for every listener. As she continues to grow and explore new dimensions of her artistry, one thing is certain—ICAH is here to stay.



Keep an ear out for ICAH as she makes her mark on the music world, one soulful note at a time.

•RADARCharts promised to bring the best talents to you and today we have Anyafulugo. Your genre, Afro-Agwu, blends traditional Igbo music with modern beats. What was the inspiration behind creating such a unique fusion?The inspiration is Agwu—the head of creativity. It’s an infinite energy, “Agwu Agwu,” that drives the sound and soul of this fusion.



•Your music speaks about identity and cultural pride. How do you balance honoring your roots while staying relevant in the global music scene?The nucleus of every creative expression is culture. There’s always a backdrop of culture in art, and the Igbo culture is rich and flamboyant enough to hold a significant place on the global stage.



•You’ve experienced fast growth in a short period. What do you believe has been the key to your rapid success?My Igbo name, “Obumneme,” loosely translates to “Is it my doing?” To that, I’d say no—there are forces propelling this ship. But at the same time, I’ll give myself credit for the groundwork I’ve done in the past. It’s like calling in favors from far and wide.



•In your opinion, what role does the Agwu spirit play in your creative process and the sound of Afro-Agwu?Agwu is the premise of my creativity. Since childhood, my dreams have always had background music, and I often wake up with melodies in my mouth. While some people sleep-talk, I used to sleep-sing. Now, I’m simply bringing those melodies from that plane of existence into this one.



•What has been the most difficult part of your journey as an artist, and how did you overcome it?I have a memory problem—I don’t dwell on battles I’ve fought because, once I win, I’m already onto the next challenge.

• Hello Ronehi, welcome to a special edition of TALK WITH US by RADARCharts, we are so happy to have you with us. So, let’s know you officially, what’s your real name?Ronehi Omofuma



• How long have you been a sound engineer?I’ve been an engineer for about 3ish years now.



• Your songs are always featured with Mojo AF, is he your alter-ego?Lol, no, he’s not my alter-ego. He’s my bro. Omo, I get jams with other artists too.



• What is your biggest music project?It would probably be between I Know You Miss Me and a project Tim Lyre has been working on for about two years now.



• What was the startup journey like?It was hard, but I wasn’t alone. I had my safe space to create and work on myself for the most part. I just kept to myself and my guys and tried to grow.



• How do you react to challenges and setbacks in your line of work?I take regular breaks from whatever project I’m working on so I can always come back with fresher ears and a different perspective on things in general. Setbacks are bound to happen; I soldier on.



• Who are the artists you’d love to work with in the future?Davido, Kah-Lo, Tems, Wizkid, Easyscope, Berlioz, Jourden, ScHoolboy-Q, Blaqbonez—Omo, e plenty, to be honest.



• What does it entail for an artist to work with Ronehi?Talk to Adam from Outer South.

articles.body:
Once again, we are back with another special episode of our magazine, featuring our very own RADAR artist, Blazehenshaw. Nice to have you here, champion.



• Can you please tell us your real name?Thank you for having me. My real name is Edem-ita Richard Henshaw.



• SYLOM is your debut project, and it’s already generating a lot of buzz. What inspired the concept behind this EP, and what message do you hope to convey to your listeners?First of all, SYLOM stands for “Shine Your Light On Me.” With this project, I’m trying to let the world know that it’s time to shine forth their light on me, giving me their ears and letting them into my world through my sound. The message I want to convey is that it’s my time to be heard, and I hope to inspire others to find and share their light as well.



• Each track on SYLOM seems to explore different themes and emotions. Can you walk us through the creative process behind one of your favorite tracks and how it reflects your personal journey?My favorite track on the project is “Normally.” It tells a story of how we all wish life could be a bed of roses for us.But, as much as we want things to go our way, we have to understand that God has the final say. This track reflects the ups and downs of life and the acceptance that, despite our best efforts, some things are beyond our control. It’s a personal reminder to stay grounded and trust the process.



• The project titled, “SYLOM (Shine Your Light On Me),” carries a powerful message of hope and resilience. What does this song mean to you personally, and how do you hope it will resonate with your audience?SYLOM holds a deep personal meaning for me. As I mentioned earlier, it’s about shining your light, but more than that, it’s about deriving strength, hope, confidence, and perseverance. I want my audience to feel empowered when they listen to this project—to know that no matter what they’re going through, they have the strength within them to overcome it. It’s a call to keep pushing forward, even in the face of adversity.



• Your music blends Afrobeat, R&B, and Afro-fusion in a unique way. How do these genres influence your sound, and what challenges did you face in merging these styles together on this EP?I like to think of my sound as Afro Folklore because I’m a storyteller at heart. Each genre I incorporate—whether it’s Afrobeat, R&B, or Afro-fusion—adds a different layer to the story I’m telling. There’s always something to talk about, so for me, there weren’t any challenges in merging these styles together. It felt natural because each genre brings its own flavor, and I love blending them to create something new and compelling.



• As a rising artist, how do you see SYLOM contributing to your growth and identity in the music industry? What impact do you hope it will have on your career and on Afrobeat music?My sound has evolved over the years, and SYLOM is my first body of work. It took me three years to put these pieces together, and it represents a new dimension for me and my fans. I believe SYLOM will push me to where I belong in the industry and open more doors for future projects. I hope it also contributes to the Afrobeat genre by bringing a fresh perspective, showing that there are still many stories to be told within this music.



• You’ve mentioned that SYLOM is not just an EP but a narrative journey. How did your personal experiences shape the storytelling aspect of this project, and how do you hope listeners will connect with it on a deeper level?My personal experiences are the foundation of SYLOM. Every track is a chapter in my life—my thoughts, my struggles, my victories. I wanted to create something that wasn’t just a collection of songs but a story that listeners could follow and relate to. I hope that by sharing my journey, others will find parts of their own story in it, and connect with the emotions and messages on a deeper level.



• With SYLOM set to be one of the most anticipated releases of 2024, what’s next for Blazehenshaw? Are there any upcoming projects or collaborations that fans should be excited about?There’s a lot coming after SYLOM. I’m really looking forward to my concert at the end of the year, which I think will be a great way to bring this project to life on stage. I’m also working on my next album, which is already in the works. Fans can definitely expect more music, more stories, and more growth from me. I’m excited about what’s to come, and I hope everyone will join me on this journey.

Welcome to another exciting episode of TALK TO US.Today, we have the honor of hosting an iconic voice from the East, a name that resonates with fans all over the world—Hugo P. Hugo, it’s a true privilege to have you here with us today. To start, could you please share with us your biological name?



• What is your real name?My name is Edwin Prince MMESOMACHUKWU.



• How long have you been an artist?I’ve been an artist for 7 years.



• Hugo, your music has touched the hearts of many and left an indelible mark on the industry. Could you tell us what initially drove your passion for music?I’ve always had a passion for music since childhood. I used to write songs and participate in rap battles in school. After Phyno’s breakthrough, it inspired me to take my music to the next level and record an actual song in the studio.



• As you rose to prominence in your career, I’m sure you faced numerous challenges, both financially and in terms of public perception. How did you manage your finances and handle the backlashes that inevitably came your way during your journey to success?I’ve kept pushing forward despite the challenges. I don’t let obstacles hold me back, and I believe hard times are opportunities for growth and learning. I’ve learned to embrace those lessons and use them to fuel my determination and resilience.



• Have you had the opportunity to engage in any international collaborations during your career? If so, could you tell us about your experiences and what you learned from them?I haven’t had the opportunity yet, but I’m eagerly looking forward to collaborating with international artists and producers in the future. I’m excited to learn from their perspectives, share my own creative vision, and create something special that resonates with a global audience.



• Every artist encounters moments of doubt and adversity in their career. Can you share with us a specific experience that made you contemplate quitting music, and how did you overcome it to continue pursuing your passion?While I haven’t personally faced a moment where I wanted to quit music, I understand that many artists do struggle with self-doubt and adversity. For me, music is an intrinsic part of who I am, and the joy it brings me and others is what drives me forward. I’ve been fortunate to have a strong support system and an unwavering passion that motivates me to keep creating and pushing boundaries. Music is my purpose, and I can’t imagine a life without it.



• Looking back at your impressive catalogue of work, do you have a favorite track that holds a special place in your heart? Additionally, could you share with us your favorite collaboration or feature that you’ve been a part of and why it stands out to you?Yes, my track with Phyno holds a special place in my heart because it was a dream come true to work with someone I admire and who has inspired me so much. Similarly, my collaboration with Zoro is also very dear to me. I’m forever grateful to have had the opportunity to work with my heroes, and I cherish the experience and lessons learned from them. The energy and creativity we shared in the studio was incredible, and I believe our combined passion and talent resulted in something truly special.

EESKAY EESKAY… Let’s do this, let’s do this again.Nice to have you on today’s special celebrity episode of TALK WITH US. Let’s get to know you officially.



• What’s your real name?My real name is Ishaq Baba Bello.



• Most people hear your name and think you adapted it from the popular weed (SK). What’s the inspiration behind your stage name?The inspiration behind my name was actually taken from somebody else’s initiative. I was called Skiddy, but a friend of mine advised I should drop the IDDY and just keep SK. So, we got SK. I decided to add 2 E’s (EE) to it because it represented my brand—Double Energy. It caught on, and everyone loved it.



• We know how long you’ve been pushing your career. Do you feel frustrated at any point?(Deep sigh) Not really. I mean, life is a journey. As long as I’m learning, I’m fine.



• How can you define your music style and its relation to your fanbase?Hmm… My music style? I think I just come up with more of the energy, whether it’s in a calm way or a hard way. I deliver music that keeps the audience wondering, what’s next?



• Let’s discuss Robo Skeng. That song seems to have some of the hardest bars in the country right now. What was the creative process like?The creative process of Robo Skeng was mainly from adapting Lagos Boys by Olamide. I was like, I’d love to do a Robo Skeng after getting my new haircut. That’s how it was, basically—just vibes.



• Before you write music, what are those warm-up routines you use?I write music. That’s one of the things I try to tap into—thinking about what I’ve been through and where I wanna see myself. Then I (uhm) roll another one. You get me? (laughs).



• The year seems to be steaming for your arrival since the release of Bad Character Remix. Do you think it’s breakthrough time?Breakthrough already came, but there’s no such thing as too much breakthrough. So, we keep it going. Sure man, we’re here to stay.



• If you were to meet a die-hard fan, what would be your advice to him?Hmm, if I were to meet a die-hard fan, my advice would be… go with the energy. If you’re supporting me, make sure you’re supporting yourself too. It’s different ways. You can get carried away with another artist you love, but you should show that love to yourself too. Fans are more precious when it’s fun and mutual energy. Keep supporting, bro, I need you.

I decided to add 2 E’s (EE) to it because it represented my brand—Double Energy. It caught on, and everyone loved it.

• We know how long you’ve been pushing your career. Do you feel frustrated at any point?

(Deep sigh) Not really. I mean, life is a journey. As long as I’m learning, I’m fine.

• How can you define your music style and its relation to your fanbase?

Hmm… My music style? I think I just come up with more of the energy, whether it’s in a calm way or a hard way. I deliver music that keeps the audience wondering, what’s next?

• Let’s discuss Robo Skeng. That song seems to have some of the hardest bars in the country right now. What was the creative process like?

The creative process of Robo Skeng was mainly from adapting Lagos Boys by Olamide. I was like, I’d love to do a Robo Skeng after getting my new haircut. That’s how it was, basically—just vibes.

• Before you write music, what are those warm-up routines you use?

I write music. That’s one of the things I try to tap into—thinking about what I’ve been through and where I wanna see myself. Then I (uhm) roll another one. You get me? (laughs).

• The year seems to be steaming for your arrival since the release of Bad Character Remix. Do you think it’s breakthrough time?

Breakthrough already came, but there’s no such thing as too much breakthrough. So, we keep it going. Sure man, we’re here to stay.

• If you were to meet a die-hard fan, what would be your advice to him?

Hmm, if I were to meet a die-hard fan, my advice would be… go with the energy. If you’re supporting me, make sure you’re supporting yourself too. It’s different ways. You can get carried away with another artist you love, but you should show that love to yourself too. Fans are more precious when it’s fun and mutual energy. Keep supporting, bro, I need you.

“2024 is the promised year for the underground RADAR. If you have a wonderful talent, show the world.”



Today, we have someone proudly raising the flag for the Gen-Z generation, all the way from Bauchi—Danziko. It’s great to have you in our community!



• Could you tell us your real name?Thank you for having me. My real name is Bolarinwa Daniel Oladeji.



• When did you officially start your music career?I started my music career officially in 2022.



• What motivated you to pursue a career in music?My passion for music and my family. I owe them a better life.



• What was your experience like before starting your music journey? Did you have any doubts about your talent?Yeah, I had so many doubts. So many people discouraged me, many didn’t believe in me. I was told hurtful words, but I never gave up. Funny enough, many of those people are my fans now.



• Let’s talk about your song “Kilimanjaro.” Is it dedicated to someone special?Nah, it’s not dedicated to anyone. I made that song out of the thoughts in my head—I’d call it an imaginary song. I made it out of imaginations, lol.



• We noticed that you featured RADARrtist and LandLord on “Kilimanjaro.” How did that collaboration come about?Yeah, Asound is a wonderful person. We met at a show in Jos (IMF Festival) hosted by some of the greats in the music industry—MI Abaga, Ice Prince Zamani, and Jesse Jagz. Asound graced the show, and I loved his performance. We linked up and made one of the best songs in the country right now.



• How has the song been received so far?Kilimanjaro is doing madness!!! In less than a month, for someone like me who doesn’t have a fan base, Kilimanjaro hit over 4k+ streams on all platforms. It’s called Grace—Grace of God and the reward of good music. I love to give myself my flowers. I put in a lot of work. Special thanks to everyone that made Kilimanjaro a success.



• If you could share a message with your potential fans out there, what would it be?We’re going to be the biggest geng in the world soon. I call them Geng Zee (it’s a purple home). Purple is the new black.

articles.body:
• Hello everyone, and welcome to another episode of TALK TO US. Today we have a RADARArtist in our midst, currently part of our TOP25 charts, Obuduboi. We’re glad to have you here! What’s your real name?I was born Athanasius Chukwuagozie Unimke, and I’m glad to be doing this with y’all too. It shows I’m starting to gain some recognition in the industry—thank God!



• How long have you been in the music scene?I recorded my first song ever in 2017, but I’d say I started doing music full-time last year, 2023, when I released my first music project as an artist. Yeah, I dropped my first EP last year as an intro or opener, lol.



• Your stage name ‘Obuduboi’ sparks a lot of curiosity. What’s the inspiration behind it?I started with the name Duke Chagzy (from my name Chukwuagozie), but I had to change it because people barely know about Obudu, where I come from. So it’s like me being patriotic. I know I’m certainly gonna blow up someday, and when it happens, I’ll be putting my city on the map again with that, you know.



• Given that you rep your hood so much, is the energy reciprocated?Yeah, although I’d say I still need to do some sort of gig or concert in my hometown because I guess there are some unbelievers that need to be converted. But the ones who know me fwm heavily, you know what I mean, right?



• Your previous release ‘Halle’ remains one of our most iconic discovered tracks. What motivated the lyrics?Halle is a song about triumph over hardships and tribulations as a young hustler trying to make ends meet on the streets of Nigeria. I had to collaborate with my niggas with a similar mindset to make that great jam. I’m sure it’s definitely gonna get bigger than it is currently. I’m glad the song made it to your charts, and that’s just the beginning of the exploits Halle will do—put a bet on it, man.



• Seeing that you’ve been in the music scene for a while, does it get frustrating at a point waiting for the breakout?Nah, I’m good. Well, I’m human, yeah, and some experiences make you feel like, damn, these people don’t recognize me yet. But it’s fine. Give them a year or two, and I bet the narrative will be way different. I know what I do behind the scenes, and my God won’t let me down either. He’s got my back, and I’m doing good. It’s just a matter of time till I get to where I’m headed.



• How have you managed to deal with all the backlash and neglect shown toward you as an upcoming artist?I just let it slide, man, with the mindset that they don’t see my potential yet. I believe that when they’re done sleeping on me, they’ll all apologize for how they treated me on the come-up. So for now, anyone can say or do anything they want, and it won’t faze me. It’s just a mere distraction from where I’m headed, and I’ve learned how to shut distractions up and increase my focus. You feel me?



• After hearing ‘Halle’ and longing for more, we’re sure the audience is wondering: What’s cooking next for Obuduboi?I can’t say everything here, man, but I’m definitely coming with more good music, more professional collaborations, and great visuals too. Y’all should just know that I’m working so hard behind the scenes. Although I do get some limitations, that’s not gonna stop me either. Whatever it is would only delay what I’ve got for y’all, but it’s coming… Watch out!

• On today’s episode, we are looking at the birth of a whole new grime squad, a fantastic 4—Savage 4. Welcome to TALK WITH US by RADARCharts. We are so happy to have you with us. What are your names and where do you come from?We’re Simeon Kalas, OG Wan, and 09 Burdac… and we’re from Tema, Ghana.



• I’m sure our audience will want to know how the creation of the Quad Team came about.SAVAGE 4 was formed in secondary school, actually! We all found ourselves in the same department at a random time. After showcasing our talents to the school, that was the moment we decided to form the group!



• Let’s talk about synchronizing sounds. Did you guys work on a sound system, or were each of you drillers before the link-up?We were all solo artists before we met! We were experimenting with different sounds and dropping freestyles in various genres. When we finally met, we became drillers.



• How has the journey been so far?The journey has been one hell of a rollercoaster! So many naysayers and doubters… but we keep pushing each and every day! Brick by brick, we’ll get to the top.



• Your new release seems to be making some waves. What are the next steps?Yeah, BADMAN RIDDIM is a really crazy record, and it’s doing its best! As for what’s next, you’ll have to stick around to find out because what we’ve got coming is dangerous!



• Let’s talk funding and management. How have you guys managed that so far?We’re doing this whole music thing independently—no management, no label. Everything is us… at least for now!



• If you guys were to make a BADMAN RIDDIM remix, who would be the feature?A BADMAN RIDDIM remix? Hmm… definitely ODUMODUBLVCK and Skillibeng.



• Given the opportunity to say something to your potential fans, what’s the word?We love each and every one of you supporting our music, and we won’t stop giving you the best we can! SAVAGE 4 to the world!



        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by SAVAGE 4🦅 (@wethesavage4)

• We have a real traveler here, all the way from Cameroon. Nice to have you on today’s episode of TALK WITH US, Vherse… let’s know you officially. What’s your real name?My birth name is Ndi Graham Nyincho.



• What inspired the name Vherse?The name Vherse, I can’t really explain what inspired it, but I’m working to build what makes the name.



• How long have you been an artist?Professionally since 2023, but I’ve always been a music person. I first recorded in 2019 and have been doing freestyles since then.



• You seem to have a record on your hands (first African artist to top the chart outside Nigeria). Did your Top Chart position come as a shock, or did you see that track going places?Well, I believed I put out a good song, so I wouldn’t say I was shocked. Instead, I count it as a blessing to be recognized.



• Your RADARCharts-topping track, ‘Aye,’ seems to have a lot of emotions attached to it. What’s the song about, and what was its creative process?‘Aye’ is a very personal song. It depicts my struggles, goals, and the motivation I need to stay focused on my journey.



As for the creative process, I wrote and recorded ‘Aye’ on my phone using the BandLab app before it ever made its way to the studio.



• How can you describe the journey of coming up and keeping up in Cameroon?My journey has been nothing short of God’s grace, I must say. There have been ups and downs—very challenging times—but I keep trusting.



• Have you ever had a reason to stop music? If so, how did you survive that?It could only be a wild natural thought on some days, but I haven’t had a concrete reason to stop.



• Who do you wish to work with in the future?It’s a long list, but I’ll name a few: Jovi, Omah Lay, Victony, Burna Boy, Wizkid, Libianca, and it goes on.

• Welcome to “Talk with Us” by RADARCharts, where we embark on a new-age journey of awakening with the SAPA RIDDIM crooner, BlaqRose. It’s a pleasure to have you here. Could you share with us your real name?Peter Attah



• Our audience would love to know when you officially began your music career professionally.Well, I started voicing and recording in 2017 and released my first song in 2018. Trust me, those are lost files now, lol.



• We’ve observed a backtrack, or perhaps a step back, from the style you developed earlier in your career, particularly from your school days. Could you elaborate on what led to this change?Let’s just say everything dawned on me when I got into the university. At that point, I realized this wasn’t what I truly wanted to study. So, I told myself, “Let’s just get this done with, but know this now—if you ever want to put food on your table (career-wise), it just has to be music.” And bam! In November 2019, I decided to pursue it fully.



• Regarding your fans, how did those who truly love your music react to your recent change in direction?I received messages and check-ins, especially when I stopped posting or texting. I tried to communicate through song covers, letting them know I’m still here and that music is important to me, despite the challenges. Pretending everything was okay wasn’t easy, but I appreciate those who stood by me. Now, I’m focused on patching things up, moving forward, and not losing myself again.



• Reflecting on your early days as a student artist, what was it like navigating the challenges, especially considering the unique environment of Veritas University, which is akin to a boarding school with its own set of obstacles?A big shoutout to Veritas University—that place can either shape or break you depending on your choices. Back in 2019, with about 200 students, it was crucial to either grow with the population or struggle as it increased. I chose growth, even though I knew only a few people initially.My focus was on building connections and relationships, not seeking praise. Although I’ve encountered people who fabricated stories about meeting me, I stayed true to myself. The journey of self-discovery there has been both challenging and rewarding.



• Your awakening process—what was the thought? What was that call you had that made you realize you were backwards?Having faith in God always paves the way. Despite the emotional weight of my journey, I stayed focused and didn’t dwell on obstacles. It’s crucial to find sources of encouragement and motivation while staying true to yourself.



• Now that you’re ready to take the stand, what are you expecting? Any special projects or features?I hope listeners focus more on my lyrics rather than just the beat or melody. Once my connection with my audience is strong, I’ll release my songs, ensuring the timing is right for maximum impact.



• Given the opportunity to say something to your potential fans, what’s the word?Zumzy Brown made me realize there’s a different world out here. It might be tough, but when you know what you want, you don’t stop until you get there. Also, never grow wings until you reach the top; that way, if you fall, you won’t have to use the stairs anymore.



“Don’t judge me now; cross-reference when I start getting everything I’ve worked for.” I promise you haven’t seen my kind before—I’m way different.



My name, BlaqRose, isn’t just a name. It’s a coin—head and tail. It’s an experience of rise and fall. It represents my life, love, and hate.
