• Welcome to “Talk with Us” by RADARCharts, where we embark on a new-age journey of awakening with the SAPA RIDDIM crooner, BlaqRose. It’s a pleasure to have you here. Could you share with us your real name?

Peter Attah

• Our audience would love to know when you officially began your music career professionally.

Well, I started voicing and recording in 2017 and released my first song in 2018. Trust me, those are lost files now, lol.

• We’ve observed a backtrack, or perhaps a step back, from the style you developed earlier in your career, particularly from your school days. Could you elaborate on what led to this change?

Let’s just say everything dawned on me when I got into the university. At that point, I realized this wasn’t what I truly wanted to study.
So, I told myself, “Let’s just get this done with, but know this now—if you ever want to put food on your table (career-wise), it just has to be music.” And bam! In November 2019, I decided to pursue it fully.

• Regarding your fans, how did those who truly love your music react to your recent change in direction?

I received messages and check-ins, especially when I stopped posting or texting. I tried to communicate through song covers, letting them know I’m still here and that music is important to me, despite the challenges. Pretending everything was okay wasn’t easy, but I appreciate those who stood by me. Now, I’m focused on patching things up, moving forward, and not losing myself again.

• Reflecting on your early days as a student artist, what was it like navigating the challenges, especially considering the unique environment of Veritas University, which is akin to a boarding school with its own set of obstacles?

A big shoutout to Veritas University—that place can either shape or break you depending on your choices. Back in 2019, with about 200 students, it was crucial to either grow with the population or struggle as it increased. I chose growth, even though I knew only a few people initially.
My focus was on building connections and relationships, not seeking praise. Although I’ve encountered people who fabricated stories about meeting me, I stayed true to myself. The journey of self-discovery there has been both challenging and rewarding.

• Your awakening process—what was the thought? What was that call you had that made you realize you were backwards?

Having faith in God always paves the way. Despite the emotional weight of my journey, I stayed focused and didn’t dwell on obstacles. It’s crucial to find sources of encouragement and motivation while staying true to yourself.

• Now that you’re ready to take the stand, what are you expecting? Any special projects or features?

I hope listeners focus more on my lyrics rather than just the beat or melody. Once my connection with my audience is strong, I’ll release my songs, ensuring the timing is right for maximum impact.

• Given the opportunity to say something to your potential fans, what’s the word?

Zumzy Brown made me realize there’s a different world out here. It might be tough, but when you know what you want, you don’t stop until you get there. Also, never grow wings until you reach the top; that way, if you fall, you won’t have to use the stairs anymore.

“Don’t judge me now; cross-reference when I start getting everything I’ve worked for.” I promise you haven’t seen my kind before—I’m way different.

My name, BlaqRose, isn’t just a name. It’s a coin—head and tail. It’s an experience of rise and fall. It represents my life, love, and hate.

• Hello Mannie, nice to have you on today’s special episode of TALK WITH US… let’s know you officially. What’s your real name?My government name is Tseayo Emmanuella Nguavese.



• What’s the inspiration behind your stage name?Mannie is short for Emmanuel, and it’s usually spelled with a “Y,” so I added “IE” to give it my own flare. I was just Mannie until a conversation with Felix Shyne inspired me to add my surname to it. It made sense to me, hence “Mannie Tseayo.”



• How long have you been into music?I was born into the choir, recorded my first song when I was 8 thanks to my uncle Paul (PIP CLASSIC), and I’ve been writing and recording ever since.



• Given your status as a female rapper, it comes with a lot of backlash. How have you coped with that?I try not to pay attention to things like backlash and instead focus on further honing my craft.



• Have you ever been intimidated in the field before?Nervous? Yes, I’ve been. Intimidated? Nah (lol).



• Let’s talk family. We know the expectations of a girl child. How were you able to stand out with your career?Luckily, the only expectations I pay attention to are the ones I carve out for myself.



• What’s your drive and mentorship process?My existence is my drive.



• Who do you wish to work with in the future?Tems, Blaqbonez, Bloody Civ, Nicki Minaj, Burna Boy, Kendrick Lamar… The list goes on, honestly, because I look forward to working with as many people as I can.

• Hello OG Mage, nice to have you on today’s special celebrity episode of TALK WITH US… let’s know you officially, what’s your real name?Samuel Ede Ogaba.



• What’s the inspiration behind your stage name?Mage means “Sorcerer,” that’s why they call me the lyrical sorcerer. I chose this because back in uni, I was called a magician because I had many talents. The “OG” comes from my last name, OGaba, but it also stands for Original Gangster.



• How long have you been into music?Technically, since 2009. Professionally, since 2021.



• How can you define your music style and its relation to your fanbase?All three of my alter egos have distinct sounds: Afrobeat, Hip-Hop/Rap, and Pop. I fuse these sounds together to create music. My fanbase is made up of people who love good music, meaningful messages, and me as a person. My music tells personal stories and gives insight into my life. This connection is what binds me to my fanbase.



• If you weren’t into music, what would have been your career path?I already walk in two worlds. I am both a Software Engineer and an Artist.



• Facts show you started your musical career abroad. Would you say you have a better fanbase there than here in Nigeria?I’d say those facts aren’t exactly true. I started my career in Abuja in 2021. By some divine intervention, I crossed paths with very strategic industry people, which helped me gain some traction in the UK at the start of my career. I wouldn’t even say I have a fanbase abroad yet—I’m still working on that.



• Here’s a tricky one: If you have a release you want to drop so badly but don’t have the proper finance for marketing, what would you do?I’d craft a less capital-intensive release plan. Content is key, and these days, that’s what really sells. My joy comes from making music and sharing it with people who enjoy it. Even with limited resources, I’d still have that.



• Who do you wish to work with in the future?Oh, that list is very long. I keep an actual list, and it’s ever-growing. But even outside of that list, I meet new artists all the time, and we make magic. The list just helps keep me grounded.

• Hello Tripster, nice to have you on today’s episode of TALK WITH US… let’s know you officially, what’s your real name?My name is Princewill Eniola Adams.



• What inspired the name Tripster?The name Tripster actually has two origins. One, “TRIP” is an acronym for “Till I Rest In Peace.” Then the name evolved to “Tripster” when I discovered a part of me that has a jester personality. So yeah, The Tripster.



• How long have you been a cinematographer?I’ve been a cinematographer for 4 years and counting now.



• What motivated your craft?My music. My music is actually what motivated me to start learning how to make videos because I didn’t want to be at the mercy of someone who only wanted to execute what they felt was best for me, rather than what I wanted.



• What project cemented your name in the industry?Hmm, thinking about it, I can’t place a finger on one specific project. It was more of a culmination of several projects I worked on during that particular period.



• How can you describe the journey coming up?The journey hasn’t been easy at all—dealing with users, terrible clients, and not to mention the days when it feels like nothing is working out. But by the grace of God, and knowing how much I’ve sacrificed for this, I know I can’t afford to lose.



• What do you have to tell your colleagues coming up?Message to my colleagues: Your passion for whatever you are doing isn’t determined by the good days when everything is going smoothly. It’s determined by your resilience through the bad days, even when things look like shit.



• Who do you wish to work with in the future?Travis Scott and Rema.



        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Trip (@tripssterr)

• Hello Oosha, nice to have you on today’s episode of Talk To Us. Let’s know you officially, what’s your name?My name is Adegoke Habeeb.



• What inspired the name Oosha?The name “OOSHA” (Oracle) was inspired by my journey through life, which has mostly been rough, and how I’ve managed to keep my head above water through it all with the help of the creator. It also represents the power to create music, a gift I believe I received from the supreme. It’s more like a self-realization thing.



• How long have you been into music?I’ve been making music officially since 2015 when I was known as Bucho DeGo, with my first official single, Faaji Repete.



• It seems you’ve had a lot of experience in the field, who’s your mentor?I’ve admired and been inspired by many different sounds growing up, ranging from Dancehall, R&B, Reggae, and Highlife music. However, I’ve never been mentored by anyone specifically. Only God!



• How have you managed to push your music so far?I’ve been pushing my music independently since I got out of my first deal in 2017. With the help of a few good people, God has been good to me, and I’ve been blessed with friends who are always ready to show up when I need them. My debut album OOSHATIDE is currently being distributed by CNC Distro.



• Your latest project, OOSHATIDE, has a lot of crazy vibes on it. What was the creative process?OOSHATIDE is a project meant to show people what I’ve been working on. I make music not just for myself but for everyone who cares to listen. The songs on the project are special. I’ve been able to craft these undeniable melodies by myself, with some help from the producers involved. I also recorded it myself through the entire process, so it’s really undiluted.



• Have you ever had a reason to stop music?I’ve had bad days when I doubted the possibility of being noticed, but I’ve never really thought about giving up. Music has been a safe haven for me, so when things look rough, I resort to it. It has always been a blessing. My mother has tried to talk me out of it, but she never really understood its value, especially when there was no money coming in. The feeling of creating something meaningful and positive is true bliss.



• Who do you wish to work with in the future?I would love to work with Burna Boy, Rema, Wizkid, Tems (though I’ve had the opportunity to create with her), Omah Lay, and many others.

• Hello Hvntar, nice to have you on today’s episode of Talk To Us. Let’s know you officially, what’s your biological name?My name is Peter Oche.



• What inspired the name Hvntar?There was a popular story of a legendary hunter back in my hometown that we were told as children. I really loved the story, so much that I would beg my granddad to tell it to me every chance I got. As a result, everyone started calling me “Hunter,” which eventually became my nickname. As I grew older, when I needed to rebrand my musical career, it just felt right. I also like that the name is provocative.



• How long have you been into music?Professionally, I’ve been in music for 6 years now.



• Wonderful! Checking your biography, we can see you tried pushing your career from a difficult entertainment community like Makurdi. How did you cope with that?I wasn’t in Makurdi for long; the major push started when I was at the University of Ibadan.



• Nice. How was that for you? What’s the struggle like?Oh well, it definitely has its highs and lows. One thing for me is that I try to enjoy every bit of the process. So I’d say, it was a good learning experience.



• How do you connect with your fans through your music?Building a loyal fanbase creates a community of supporters who will help spread the music. So, I consistently try to come up with ideas on how to build a community, one fan at a time, to walk the journey with me as I grow. A few ways I do this are through social media platforms, live performances to connect face-to-face with the fans, online communities/groups, collaborations with other creatives, etc. This has helped me over the years to stay connected and in touch with my fans.



• Have you had the chance to work with a celebrity artist before?I served as a backup singer for the legendary 2Baba, with whom I, along with a boy band team, did a song. He’s the only celebrity artist I’ve worked with so far. There are plans in the pipeline for more to come soon, of course.



• (Amazing!) Who would you love to work with in the future?I have a long list of local and international stars I’d love to work with. But at the back of my mind right now, I’d say Ayra Starr and Bnxn (formerly Buju). I think we can create some magic together.



        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Hvntar (@thehvntar)
//www.instagram.com/embed.js

• Hello Industry Messiah, that’s a mighty name, Chief. Welcome to Talk With Us brought to you by RadarCharts. We want to know you. What’s your real name?Hello guys, I’m really happy to be here. I’m proud of the system. My name is Tarzaa Anzenge Gerald Caesar of REM, in short, Cza of REM.



• You’re called the Industry Messiah, how did you come about that name?Uhmm, nothing serious. It’s just an entity reflecting on my parent brand, Royal Empire Management (REM). It’s a system that I, myself, control, and it’s been a good deed for upcoming talents, helping them achieve their growth and passion. That’s what led to the claim of Industry Messiah.



• So, what do you do? What’s your professional career?Officially, I call myself an entertainment enthusiast and talent manager. But my services stand as one for all, all for one, as long as respect and transparency are in place.



• Your bio says you’ve been in the business since 2019. How has that been so far?Well, off the record, it’s actually been since 2017, as that’s when I started my kick-off learning process. It hasn’t been easy, though—ups and downs, happy times, and really depressing times (lol). But the passion will help you see the future and who you want to be. Nothing good comes easy. If you don’t dare, you won’t grind. Zero evidence.



• So, in your line of business, who do you admire and look up to?Personally, it’s Olamide and Don Jazzy. I respect Olamide because he’s an artist who has conquered the managerial conquest perfectly while keeping his own superstar status and career intact.



• Who are the artists you’ve managed so far?On the record, I’ll rate based on their popularity and quality. Currently, I’m managing (in assistance of my brand) Choo, Cutda (formerly Spaceryde), Late Zumzy Brown’s posthumous work, co-managing EASTSIDEALIEN, Asound, and acting as an agent for Khalie. I’ve also managed BlaqRose, Adthekvng, Dxnzel, Ghandi, ZaddyTC, Uzzi King, among others.



• Asides management, what else do you do?I’m an A&R, project manager, and event planner. I’ve based my life and career so far in entertainment. Let’s eat where we’re happy. Life is meant to be fun.



• What’s your advice to artists who would rely on intellect?Simple. Make good music, hire an A&R (you can’t build your career now without one), get a unique brand, identify with your brand, and connect with your audience. That’s the trick.

• Hello dear, can we know HybridTrips? What’s your real name and your story? Where are you from? Tribe? Student? (If yes, where?)I am Bakare Ololade Micheal, the oldest son in a family of six from Ogun State. I began my musical journey at a young age, excelling in drumming, and was influenced by my church upbringing. I officially delved into music production in 2010 at Soundtime Studios in Kaduna, where I gained valuable experience that molded my musical beliefs and refined my skills. Music is like a spouse to me, holding immense significance in my life due to my deep passion for it. Though I have completed my studies in Sociology at the Federal University Oye Ekiti, I like to see myself as a lifelong learner.



• What inspired the name HybridTrips?The name HybridTrips reflects my versatility across various roles in the recording industry. I’m involved as a music producer, sound engineer, writer, A&R, singer, and creative director. Due to this diverse skill set, my friends affectionately refer to me as “Hybrid,” and I added “Trips” to the name to signify my trippy vibes.



• What track signifies your pioneer production work?Honestly, I think there are two:




Highest Student by Mojo AF & Masiano



For You by Mannie Tseayo & HybridTrips




• Who are the artists you aspire to work with in the future?I aspire to work with Kanye West, Skepta, Burna Boy, Zkid, J Hus, FirstKlaz, and Odumodublvck.



• Finally, what are the requirements an artist must meet when working with you?




The artist has to understand the music business to an extent.



Their publishing should be sorted out.



They should have a detailed plan on how we will promote the song from pre-release to post-release.




        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by DROP IT AHGAIN 🦅 (@hybridtrips)

•So happy to have you with us BoyLiam. According to your artist profile, you’ve mentioned growing up in a Christian household with various musical influences. How did those early experiences shape the sound we hear in your music today?Most of the songs my parents played at home had amazing melodies that made you feel things deeply. That’s what I try to recreate in my music—intentional sounds meant to evoke emotions and make listeners feel good.



•Winning a music competition in Benin Republic was a turning point for you in 2019. How did that experience impact your confidence and direction as a professional artist?It gave me so much confidence in my craft and voice because, naturally, I’m a shy person. That’s one of the reasons I don’t participate in most competitions. However, that win gave me newfound confidence in my voice, and I’ve been riding that wave ever since.



•When working on your latest project, Ecstasy, what does your creative process look like? Do you start with lyrics, a melody, or a beat first?I like to start with a theme. Do I want to talk about love, life, struggles, or something else? Once I figure out the theme, I dive into the melodies. My melodies are designed to make you feel whatever I’m feeling at the moment, making them relatable and nostalgic. Lyrics come last because they require more time. I want to express myself poetically but in a way that’s easy for listeners to connect with and remember.



•Your voice has been described as nostalgic and comforting. Was this a conscious direction for your music, or did it naturally evolve that way over time?It wasn’t conscious at all. I’m a big consumer of music, especially older records. My parents played a lot of old gospel songs, and my bus driver always had old rap, R&B, and Afrobeat records on. So I naturally draw melodies and inspiration from those experiences.



•The Nigerian music industry is highly competitive. What have been the biggest challenges you’ve faced so far, and how have you managed to overcome them?One big issue for me, which I’m still working on, is creating content for the music. I’ve been spending more time on TikTok and Instagram, and with the help of my manager and friends, I’m gradually improving at putting more content out.



•How do you think you’ve grown musically and personally since your debut in 2019? What lessons have shaped your evolution as an artist?I’ve grown a lot because the Nigerian music industry has pushed me out of my comfort zone. It’s made me better lyrically, improved my branding, and enhanced every other aspect of my artistry. Being in the same room with so many talented artists has taught me to prioritize learning over proving how good I am. This approach has helped me identify my weaknesses and work on them.



•You’ve worked solo so far, but if you could collaborate with any artist, locally or internationally, who would it be, and why?I have a long list of amazing people I’d love to work with. One person who stands out is Wande Coal, mainly because of my admiration for him. I feel like Wande made Nigerians appreciate vocalists more, and he’s one of the artists who shaped what we now call “Afropop.”



•Where do you see yourself as an artist in the next five years? What legacy do you hope to leave in the Afrobeats space?I hope to be at the top of my game, creating beautiful and evergreen songs. I want to be one of the major influences in songwriting. I believe I have a gift with words, and I want to use it to preach the gospel of love in a way that resonates across all age groups and races.



•In a fast-paced music world where trends come and go, how do you ensure that you stay true to your sound while still remaining relevant?I remind myself that the greats before me stayed relevant because they made music out of love, not just for trends. They had a message and made sure to pass it on, even if it meant waiting longer for recognition. That’s the mindset I try to emulate.



•What advice would you give to younger artists who are trying to make it in the music industry, especially in a genre as vibrant and dynamic as Afrobeats?The best advice I ever got from a mentor was to stay true to myself and find my sound. Identity is crucial; it transcends into everything we do as creatives. So my advice is this: find yourself, and then be yourself. •We welcome another superstar from the southern part of Nigeria, Godskidx. Can You Kindly Tell Us Your Biological Name?My name is Godswill Edewor.



•Your Debut Single “Many Men” Made an Impact in 2023. How Did It Influence Your Career and Approach to Music?“Many Men” was actually my first song. I did that track with my bro, Blaqdakid. We had this idea of doing a song together, so we went to the studio and put our ideas together. That’s how we created “Many Men.” It had a great impact and showed me what was possible when you collaborate and put effort into your art.



•How Did Your Collaboration With Lyta on “SORRY” Come About, and What Was It Like Working Together?“Sorry” was originally a full song I had completed. Then, I thought about featuring someone on it, and Lyta came to mind. I reached out to see if I could get him on the track, and God was kind enough to make it happen. He was available, we met, and that’s how we did the song together. It was fun working with Lyta. He’s a very nice, calm person, and I enjoyed the experience.



•“SORRY” Explores Themes of Vulnerability and Regret. What Inspired This Track, and How Do These Themes Connect With Your Own Experiences?“Sorry” came to mind after I went through a breakup—what we call ‘chopping breakfast’ (laughs). After writing “Broken,” I thought about what it would be like to apologize for everything that happened, even though I was no longer in the relationship. So, I put all those feelings together and wrote “Sorry.”



•Can You Walk Us Through the Creative Process Behind “SORRY,” From Songwriting to Production?Writing “Sorry” was all about reflecting on my past relationship. I thought about the things I did that weren’t right and decided to say sorry for them all. The production was amazing, done by Mikaba, who really helped bring the song to life.



•The Production of “SORRY” Blends Afrobeat With Contemporary Sounds. How Involved Were You in Shaping Its Sound?Musically, I love experimenting with different sounds, but Afrobeat is a favorite of mine. I was definitely involved in shaping the sound, working closely with the producer to get it just right.



•How Has Your Sound Evolved Since “God Design” and “Broken”? What’s Driving Your Music Now?If you listen to “God Design” and compare it with my current songs, you’ll notice a lot of differences, from production to the recording process. Everything is different now, and I love the way my sound has evolved. “Broken” and “Sorry” reflect the inspiration I get from things happening in my life and around me. That’s what drives my music at the moment.



•What Can Fans Expect From You in 2024? Are There Any Upcoming Projects or Collaborations You’re Excited About?My fans can expect more good music from me. I plan to drop a new song before the year ends, and yes, I might release a new single soon. For now, there aren’t any new collaborations in the works, but I’m focusing on delivering great music.

Wilfred Uchenna Ibeagwa, better known by his stage name Snowfella, continues to solidify his place as a force to reckon with in the Afro-Hip-Hop scene. The Imo State native has dropped his latest single, ‘Pontius Pilate,’ a track that dives deep into themes of betrayal, moral dilemmas, and resilience. This release comes hot on the heels of his widely acclaimed collaboration with Yng Ryme on ‘Mendez & Boss,’ which showcased Snowfella’s ability to hold his own alongside heavy hitters in the rap game.







A Bold Evolution



Snowfella’s rise in the music industry began with his debut project, “Blood and Sweat EP,” in 2023, a body of work that introduced audiences to his unique blend of Afrobeat rhythms and sharp lyrical prowess. Over time, he has honed a sound that resonates deeply with fans who crave authenticity and storytelling in their music. ‘Pontius Pilate’ sees Snowfella delve even deeper into his creative well, offering a layered narrative set against a hard-hitting, yet melodic, Afrobeat-inspired instrumental.



The Story Behind ‘Pontius Pilate’



In ‘Pontius Pilate,’ Snowfella uses the metaphor of the biblical figure to explore themes of betrayal and moral compromise. The track’s raw lyrics and emotive delivery reflect the weight of making tough decisions while navigating a world where loyalty is often fleeting. “This song is about standing firm in your truth, even when the odds are stacked against you,” Snowfella explained in a recent interview. His ability to weave such heavy themes into a track that remains sonically captivating is a testament to his artistic growth.









Building Momentum with ‘Mendez & Boss’



Fans and critics alike are still buzzing from Snowfella’s collaboration with Yng Ryme on ‘Mendez & Boss,’ a high-energy anthem that perfectly blended the duo’s dynamic flows and lyrical depth. The track not only reaffirmed Snowfella’s position as one of Afro-Hip-Hop’s most promising voices but also hinted at his versatility as an artist who can seamlessly move between introspective narratives and braggadocious bangers.



What’s Next for Snowfella?



With ‘Pontius Pilate,’ Snowfella is gearing up for what promises to be a monumental phase in his career. This latest release is rumored to be part of a larger project, though the artist has remained tight-lipped about details. One thing is certain: Snowfella’s trajectory is on a steep upward climb, and ‘Pontius Pilate’ is a clear marker of his ambition and talent.







For fans of Afro-Hip-Hop and lovers of music that speaks to the soul, Snowfella’s latest offering is a must-listen. Stay tuned for more from this rising star as he continues to push boundaries and elevate the genre to new heights.

The Nigerian Afro Beats and Afro Alte sensation, Yng Ryme, is kicking off 2025 with a bang. After the success of his collaboration with Snowfella on the explosive track Mendez & Boss, the Owerri-born artist is set to make waves once again with his upcoming single, Swirl. This highly anticipated release marks the beginning of a new chapter in Yng Ryme’s ever-evolving musical journey.







A Glimpse into Yng Ryme’s Roots



Born Chidera Chimamkpa Smart, Yng Ryme’s artistry is deeply rooted in his rich Nigerian heritage and the vibrant culture of Owerri, Imo State. His innovative approach to blending Afro Beats with Afro Alte has consistently pushed boundaries, earning him a growing fanbase and recognition across the Nigerian music scene and beyond.



Yng Ryme first captured attention with his debut EP, Climax, in 2022, a project that showcased his ability to craft emotive lyrics and infectious melodies. Following this, his breakout single Want It solidified his reputation as a versatile artist unafraid to explore new sonic territories.



From ‘Joromi’ to ‘Swirl’: A Trail of Growth



2024 was a transformative year for Yng Ryme, with the release of his debut project Joromi, a record that resonated deeply with fans and critics alike. The project cemented his place in the Afro Beats and Afro Alte genres, blending traditional Nigerian sounds with a modern, experimental edge.







Yng Ryme’s collaboration with Snowfella on Mendez & Boss further expanded his artistic range. The track, a fusion of hard-hitting beats and lyrical ingenuity, served as a prelude to what fans can expect from his forthcoming work.



The Magic of ‘Swirl’



Now, Yng Ryme is ready to introduce Swirl, a single that promises to define his 2025 era. This track is a perfect blend of his signature Afro Alte sound and fresh experimental elements, reflecting his commitment to innovation and artistic growth. Swirl is expected to captivate listeners with its irresistible groove and relatable storytelling, making it a standout release in his discography.







Speaking about the inspiration behind Swirl, Yng Ryme shared, “This song is about navigating life’s twists and turns, finding beauty in the chaos, and staying true to yourself no matter what comes your way.”



What’s Next for Yng Ryme?



With Swirl, Yng Ryme is not just dropping another single—he’s setting the tone for what promises to be a groundbreaking year. Fans can anticipate more music, bold collaborations, and a deeper dive into the vibrant soundscapes that have made him one of the most exciting voices in contemporary Nigerian music.



As Yng Ryme continues to push boundaries and redefine Afro Alte, Swirl is a testament to his unwavering commitment to growth and creativity. Mark your calendars—this is one track you won’t want to miss.



Stay tuned for the release of Swirl and follow Yng Ryme’s journey as he takes 2025 by storm!

Today, we celebrate the remarkable growth and achievements of the esteemed beat king, Dawie. It is a pleasure to have you with us. Congratulations on your recent successes.



• Could you please introduce yourself to our audience by sharing your full name?Okay, my names are Noiki David, popularly known as Dawie (Dawieonthis1).



• How long have you been working as a music producer?For a very long time.



• Your catalog is truly a collection of exceptional sounds. How have you managed to establish connections with these artists?Honestly, I just go with what I feel, to be honest. I let the music speak to me, and I also try to be the best version of myself I can be, honestly.



• Many producers face challenges in getting their beats to well-known artists, and some even encounter issues of exploitation. Do you have any advice for them?Honestly, I think it’s just for you to be informed but also know how to apply the information you have.Creatives just need to know that this thing is a career/profession, and in order to have longevity, you need to create sustainability. Money is an important factor in it.So, in creating those career opportunities, also try to secure the bag. That doesn’t mean you should overprice yourself out of the market, but know your worth—that’s the important thing.



• Let’s talk about your 2024 catalog. You’ve been consistently making waves with collaborations with artists like Damo, Zyno, and Hyce. Did you envision reaching this level of success this year?Honestly, 2024 has been a surprising year. In a good way, but all I can say is that everything is happening in God’s time. I have just been grinding and leaving the rest to God—He’s the one that determines all.



• People often say you can feel it when you create a hit. Can you describe that sensation?|Honestly, that can be true but also dicey because it boils down to what you define a hit as. I personally think a hit is more than numbers—it’s more in the music and what it does to you, the listener.



• Have there been moments in your career when you felt frustrated and considered quitting?Frustration? Yes… a lot of times. But the thing is, whenever it happens, I just smile, and I remember why I started and the things that fuel my inspiration. Honestly, I go back to my God—that’s the best place to draw strength from, and He never disappoints, yunno.



• Finally, how can an artist collaborate with you, Dawie?I’m very open to collaborating. Just shoot me a DM. Trust me, if you wanna really get me gingered, just drop me the right melody—I’m gone!

Today, we celebrate the remarkable growth and achievements of the esteemed beat king, Dawie. It is a pleasure to have you with us. Congratulations on your recent successes.

• Could you please introduce yourself to our audience by sharing your full name?

Okay, my names are Noiki David, popularly known as Dawie (Dawieonthis1).

• How long have you been working as a music producer?

For a very long time.

• Your catalog is truly a collection of exceptional sounds. How have you managed to establish connections with these artists?

Honestly, I just go with what I feel, to be honest. I let the music speak to me, and I also try to be the best version of myself I can be, honestly.

• Many producers face challenges in getting their beats to well-known artists, and some even encounter issues of exploitation. Do you have any advice for them?

Honestly, I think it’s just for you to be informed but also know how to apply the information you have.Creatives just need to know that this thing is a career/profession, and in order to have longevity, you need to create sustainability. Money is an important factor in it.
So, in creating those career opportunities, also try to secure the bag. That doesn’t mean you should overprice yourself out of the market, but know your worth—that’s the important thing.

• Let’s talk about your 2024 catalog. You’ve been consistently making waves with collaborations with artists like Damo, Zyno, and Hyce. Did you envision reaching this level of success this year?

Honestly, 2024 has been a surprising year. In a good way, but all I can say is that everything is happening in God’s time. I have just been grinding and leaving the rest to God—He’s the one that determines all.

• People often say you can feel it when you create a hit. Can you describe that sensation?|

Honestly, that can be true but also dicey because it boils down to what you define a hit as. I personally think a hit is more than numbers—it’s more in the music and what it does to you, the listener.

• Have there been moments in your career when you felt frustrated and considered quitting?

Frustration? Yes… a lot of times. But the thing is, whenever it happens, I just smile, and I remember why I started and the things that fuel my inspiration. Honestly, I go back to my God—that’s the best place to draw strength from, and He never disappoints, yunno.

• Finally, how can an artist collaborate with you, Dawie?

I’m very open to collaborating. Just shoot me a DM. Trust me, if you wanna really get me gingered, just drop me the right melody—I’m gone!

• While preparing for this episode, we got hooked on Connected; it told a story of endurance. What’s the backstory to the track?Connected is actually a very special track to me. Fun fact: I was just showing a producer friend of mine (Juju Beats) how to do a reverse 808 on FL Studio, and right after I showed him how to do it from scratch, he suggested I make it into a whole beat because the 808s were fire by themselves already. So, I started building on that and making the beat, and the moment I got the chords, I knew this was going to be it. The rest is history, as they say.



• We saw your production credit on Ice Prince’s Fire & Ice project. How did that link-up come about?That has actually been a major highlight of my year. I met Ice Prince late in 2022. I was invited to a session at his crib to produce. We made a couple of records that night, but it wasn’t until early 2023 when he personally called me back to work on his project. We were locked in for over 8 months, just recording and making amazing music. Ice is my big OG and friend.



• A very curious question, champ: with the kind of music and craft, we are surprised you gained more popularity this year. What was the challenge?To me, I just believe God’s timing is simply the best. We’ve been putting in work, and I’m glad to see it’s getting recognized.



• When are we expecting that Ice Prince feature?Say less. Me and Big Bro got bangers for days. My next single will feature him.



• How do you go about feature requests from other artists?The only criterion now is if I vibe with your sound, especially if you’re doing Hip-Hop because I love Hip-Hop.



• Any projects in progress?Yes, I will be dropping my debut mixtape Candy Dreams in a month. It’s expected to have at least 15 tracks.



• If you are given the chance to say a few words to your potential fans, what would you say?Stay true to yourself and your craft. Always dream big, and remember, Candy Dreams is coming!

Today, we have the pleasure of hearing from a promising voice from the rising sun, one of the most promising artists from the eastern part of the country, Rhatti. Thank you for accepting our invitation. Can you kindly tell our audience your real name?My names are Armstrong Chukwuebuka Arize.



• How long have you been an artist?I’ve been an artist for over 7 years now, recording professionally.



• We see that you have a wonderful track record. How has the journey to fame been?It’s been a roller coaster with so much work to do ahead…and we keep pushing.



• Looking at your growth so far, what’s the craziest experience you’ll never forget?The craziest experience I wouldn’t forget was raising funds to pay for studio time and my recording services as an undergraduate without any consistent source of income. Losing my dad during my early days was another tough part of the journey.



• Have you ever had a reason to quit?No, never. I’ve taken breaks to find myself and create balance, but quitting has never been an option.



• What’s a career move you made that you almost regret?No regrets, just lessons learned—and learning never ends.



• Let’s talk about what’s coming next for Rhatti. Firstly, what’s your message for your fans? Are there any amazing features your audience should look forward to?To my fans, I really want to apologize for the delayed project release. I truly appreciate my day ones who’ve been with me through thick and thin and are still rooting for me.



• How can an artist get the opportunity to feature or collaborate with you?Not just artists—promoters, brands, and companies interested in working with me can book me directly through my social media pages or email.

MAN OF THE HOUR, nice to have you on today’s episode of TALK WITH US. EASTSIDEALIEN, let’s get to know you officially. What’s your real name?My real name is Udegbunam Richmond Chiemezie.



• The name EASTSIDEALIEN is unique, and your intro tag “Tryna get it done” is even more unique. What does it mean exactly? What inspired that phrase?It’s like a mantra for me—a motivational statement. It’s about staying focused and achieving greatness no matter what. The world needs to see what we’re made of.



• Your rap lines always come with a strong message. Can you tell us about your creative process?Honestly, it’s all about reflecting on my life, my experiences, and the things I’ve been through. Having good energy around me helps too—it keeps me grounded and fuels my grind.



• Let’s dive into your project, AREA 51. How did the name come about?AREA 51, as we all know, is linked to UFOs and alien mysteries. I felt it aligned perfectly with my stage name, EASTSIDEALIEN. It’s like my sound is an invasion—something fresh and different in the industry.



• How has the public received this project so far?The love has been real. People are vibing with it, but you know how it is—the grind never stops. I’m expecting bigger things to come from this, God willing.



• We noticed there aren’t any features on this project, unlike your previous work. Was that intentional?Yes, it was intentional. I actually planned to feature my brother on one track, but since this project was a reintroduction of EASTSIDEALIEN as a brand, I had to keep it solo. That doesn’t mean my VTB family wasn’t with me throughout—they always got my back.



• What are some of the goals you hope to achieve with this project?Breakout season! This project is designed to capture hearts across the nation and beyond. With God on my side, we’re making it happen.



• If AREA 51 turns out to be your breakthrough project, what’s your next move?The next step is to go even bigger—taking on larger stages and collaborations. The feature with JeriQ was just the beginning. Soon, we’ll be vibing with the big boys in the game. My fans are my backbone, so keep streaming and spreading the word. We rise together—one for all, all for one.

We often hear about producers having an artist as an alter ego or symbiosis. Who’s that artist for you?For now, I haven’t figured out that artist yet, but very, very soon.

Coming from a community where music is not really seen as a career, how did you cope?You just need to put in the work and prove that you can actually make a good career with music. In summary, “Show Workings.”

What does it entail for an artist to work with KingGeorge?You just have to be good and know exactly what you want. With that, the session will be very, very smooth.

• Were you certain you’d come this far in the industry, coming from a city where breakouts are not as frequent as usual?I’m a positive person, so I always try to stay positive in everything I do.

• Ever had a moment in your career where you felt like giving up?I’ve always been positive, even when things weren’t going so great.



• We know the music industry has its ups and downs. How have you managed to keep going to this point?Shout out to the real ones around me—my team, fans, and family. They keep me going.



• What does it entail for an artist to work with IceBeatzz?To work with Icebeatzz, you’ve gotta be LiT!

• Hello King Kiing Lu, welcome to a special edition of TALK WITH US by RADARCharts. We are so happy to have you with us. So, let’s know you officially. What’s your real name?My name is Lucas Emodi.



• You seem to possess the Larry Gaga, DJ Khaled style of music. What’s the motive behind that?Well, after pursuing a music career in 2005, I saw the need to help other artists grow. After acquiring the business knowledge, I decided to be an enthusiast. We need to make and protect good music.



• Looking back at your past musical career, do you think you’d have been a breakout by now?Maybe yes, maybe no. The industry isn’t a ground where you define your blow time. You move with the wave. A child who started music tomorrow can become a great star over someone who started 20-30 years ago. It’s all time and chance.



• Let’s discuss the Exec lifestyle. How has the journey been so far as a music exec, seeing you’ve worked with major music labels before?It’s been great, actually. Having the experience of being an artist/producer, combined with talent management and executive roles, creates a career blend of success. We thank God for His grace and blessings.



• People (especially artists) always ask questions about how to get themselves in the sight of all these big labels. What’s your professional advice?It’s all about putting yourself out there. The big fishes are watching, and most of them are fans you don’t even know. Don’t let them down. Show them the shine in you. Show them why you’re worth their investment—both funds and expertise. Keep up with the steeze.



• How do you go about curating artists for your projects?Music is all about having good networks. I get the best beats done and call on talents that fit perfectly into the vision of the project.



• What are we expecting next from Kiing Lu?The tag, “When you’re up! You’re up!” is the motto. Expect more militancy.



• What’s your professional advice for upcoming artists out there on their journey to stardom?If you believe in yourself, never give up. Just believe—that’s all that matters. That’s the lead.



• What motivated your profession as a producer and sound engineer?God will forever take the glory. I couldn’t have imagined things this way. I thought I was going to study nuclear engineering.



• What was the startup like? How did you keep up with financing and rejection by other artists?It’s a testimony and a humbling experience—starting from one step to thousands and millions of steps and more. Little beginnings should not be despised. God aided and provided for us through friends and partners who believed in and supported the process, even financially.

articles.bodyHtml:
•Hello King Afroselecta BBK, welcome to a special edition of TALK WITH US by RADARCharts. We are so happy to have you with us. So, let’s know you officially. What’s your real name?

lol, “David” is the first name, though.

•We have to ask, what does BBK stand for?

BBK is an abbreviation for the family name. It means “father of children.”

•What motivated your profession as a producer and sound engineer?

God will forever take the glory. I couldn’t have imagined things this way. I thought I was going to study nuclear engineering.

•What was the startup like? How did you keep up with financing and rejection by other artists?

It is a testimony and a humbling experience, starting from one step to thousands and millions of steps and more. Little beginnings should not be despised. God aided and provided for us through friends and partners who believed in and supported the process, even financially.

Rejection is not easy for any human being, but there are situations or scenarios where you will learn that it’s nothing personal from other artists. We tend to gravitate towards who is known or popular.
Once you learn not to take things personally and realize nobody is obligated to know you, it helps set your mind to work more on your craft and promote your work and yourself more.

•What career path would you have chosen aside from music production?

Football. I thought at some point I was going to play soccer!

•We heard you have a brother who sings too (Laxy BBK). Have you been part of his creative process?

Yes, I am his executive producer and I help manage him.

•What’s the biggest music project you’ve worked on?

Every music project is big for me! When I post, it’s me displaying my work and CV. It’s a testimony and testament to what God does and did for me.


•What does it entail for an artist to work with Afroselecta BBK?

Working with any and every artist is a privilege. But these days, there’s a price (monetary level), and it keeps going up!

Last Sunday, December 22nd, the ON THE RADAR Concert lit up the stunning Mojito Lounge Rooftop in Abuja with a powerful fusion of music, art, and Afrobeat culture. Presented by RADARCharts in partnership with Freqie Space and The Scene, this Black & White Afrobeat celebration proved to be an unforgettable evening of collective artistry and innovation.







The event was headlined by the incredible Ms. Jorji (African Bad Girl), who captivated the audience with her dynamic energy and commanding stage presence. She set the tone for the night, showcasing her unwavering support for female creatives and inspiring others to take bold steps in the industry.



Performances That Ignited the StageThe concert featured a star-studded lineup of talented artists, each bringing their unique sound and charisma to the stage. Performances by Mannie Tseayo, ASTROKULTURE, Twyze, Bolaryn, Anayor, Wichyskills, Lit Vybz, Vj Skinny, Strange Village, Danziko, Kakes ON, Henggz, Uzzi King, Chillzworldwild, Aj Daviis, MaczyFire, Eightyeightwonder, Teeroy Tyobee, and Chipio The Spirit (known as the Class of set’24)kept the crowd on their feet all night long.









From Afro-fusion rhythms to vibrant rap flows and dynamic live bands, every artist brought their A-game, creating an electric atmosphere that resonated with the 1,500+ attendees. Each performance reflected the raw passion and creativity of a new generation of artists ready to elevate the Nigerian music scene to unprecedented heights.



A Hub for Networking and InspirationThe Mojito Lounge Rooftop provided the perfect setting for artists, fans, and industry leaders to connect and network. From engaging conversations at the media lounge powered by The Scene to immersive art installations curated by Freqie Space, the event wasn’t just a concert—it was a cultural hub where ideas, stories, and creative visions flowed freely.



What’s Next?Building on the success of the ON THE RADAR Concert, RADARCharts is already planning the next edition, with even bigger collaborations and groundbreaking concepts. This event solidified RADAR’s commitment to fostering creativity, celebrating diversity, and connecting artists and fans in ways that inspire and transform.



Stay tuned for more exciting updates as we prepare to take ON THE RADAR to the next level. This is just the beginning of an extraordinary journey.



For more information and to stay updated on upcoming events, follow us on our platforms. Together, let’s keep pushing the culture forward!

As 2024 draws to a close, Nigerian music sensation Lit Vybz is leaving no stone unturned in making his presence felt. The Middle Belt-born artist, known for his captivating blend of rap, melody, and storytelling, has taken his artistry to the airwaves with an electrifying radio tour across Abuja’s top stations. From Hot FM to Kiss FM, Raypower FM, and Rhythm FM, Lit Vybz is ending the year with a bang, sharing his journey, music, and vision with listeners far and wide.







The Abuja Radio Tour: Lit Vybz On Air



Throughout December, Lit Vybz has been gracing the studios of Abuja’s leading radio stations, captivating audiences with his charisma and undeniable talent. Each stop on the tour offered fans and listeners a deeper insight into his musical journey, his inspirations, and what drives him to create songs that resonate with so many.



During his appearances, Lit Vybz delved into his background, sharing stories about his Christian military upbringing and how he turned life’s challenges into a source of artistic inspiration. Tracks like his breakout single and recent releases have been hot topics, with hosts and fans alike eager to discuss the creative process behind his hits.



From exclusive freestyle sessions to live renditions of his songs, the radio tour has showcased Lit Vybz’s versatility as an artist and performer. Abuja fans have been particularly thrilled to hear about his plans for 2025 and his commitment to elevating Nigerian music on a global scale.



Celebrating Success with ON THE RADAR



Adding to the excitement, Lit Vybz is wrapping up the year by joining the prestigious ON THE RADAR platform. Known for spotlighting emerging talents across various genres, ON THE RADAR is a significant milestone in Lit Vybz’s career, marking him as one of the year’s standout artists.









This collaboration underscores his growing influence in the music scene, providing a platform to connect with fans and industry players alike. With a dynamic performance and heartfelt reflections, Lit Vybz used the opportunity to celebrate his wins in 2024 while setting the tone for an even bigger year ahead.



2024: A Year to Remember



This year has been monumental for Lit Vybz. From expanding his audience through live performances to gaining recognition for his ability to blend genres and tell compelling stories, he has proven that he’s a force to be reckoned with in the Nigerian music scene.







As fans tune in to his interviews and celebrate his milestones, the message is clear: Lit Vybz is just getting started. With his unique sound, authentic storytelling, and tireless dedication, the future holds even greater things for this multifaceted artist.



Looking Ahead



Lit Vybz’s Abuja radio tour and ON THE RADAR feature are the perfect capstones to a phenomenal year. As we gear up for 2025, fans can expect even more music, collaborations, and groundbreaking performances from this rising star.







Stay connected with Lit Vybz by following him on all social media platforms and streaming his latest releases. This is just the beginning of a journey that promises to reshape the future of Nigerian music.

Port Harcourt’s rising star, Badt Soma, is turning heads in the Afro-fusion scene with his latest project, UP I COME. This dynamic body of work captures his journey, struggles, and triumphs, wrapped in a soundscape that blends Afrobeat, Hip-Hop, and Trap. With raw emotion and magnetic charisma, Badt Soma cements his place as a powerful voice in the music industry.







A Journey Through Badt Soma’s World



UP I COME isn’t just an album—it’s an experience. Each track takes listeners on a journey through Badt Soma’s life, offering a glimpse into his ambitions and challenges. From the anthemic opener “Issues” to the hauntingly vulnerable “Unholy,” Soma’s artistry shines through. His storytelling is laced with authenticity, a trait that makes him instantly relatable to his growing fanbase.



The project strikes a perfect balance between introspection and celebration, capturing the duality of Badt Soma’s rise. Whether you’re vibing to the infectious hooks or dissecting his thought-provoking lyrics, UP I COME has something for everyone.



Track Highlights









1. Issues



UP I COME kicks off with “Issues,” a deeply personal track that showcases Soma’s introspection and lyrical depth. The raw energy of the song immediately sets the tone for what’s to come, drawing listeners into his world.



2. Envious



On “Envious,” Badt Soma channels his frustrations and triumphs over jealousy and competition. The track’s Afrobeat-inspired rhythm pairs seamlessly with his impassioned delivery, making it a standout anthem for overcoming adversity.



3. Mad For You (feat. Peng Boy)



“Mad For You” introduces a playful yet emotionally charged vibe. Featuring Peng Boy, the collaboration is a perfect blend of Soma’s soulful style and Peng Boy’s dynamic energy. It’s a surefire hit for fans of Afro-fusion love anthems.



4. Unholy



The album closes with “Unholy,” a bold, haunting track that delves into themes of temptation and redemption. The intense Trap influences and gripping lyricism ensure this song lingers in listeners’ minds long after the music stops.



Badt Soma: The Afro-Fusion Sensation



Born as Amos Emmanuel Chigozirim, Badt Soma is a Port Harcourt native who has been captivating audiences with his infectious rhythms and soulful delivery. A graduate of Rivers State University, Soma’s journey in music reflects a blend of traditional African sounds with modern influences. His energetic stage presence and innovative approach have quickly earned him a loyal following.







With UP I COME, Badt Soma solidifies his reputation as an artist who can seamlessly merge cultural authenticity with contemporary trends.



Why UP I COME Deserves a Spot on Your Playlist



Badt Soma’s latest project is a testament to his growth and vision. It’s not just about catchy beats; it’s about telling a story, connecting with audiences, and leaving a mark. The album’s themes of resilience, love, and ambition are universal, resonating deeply with listeners from all walks of life.



If you’re a fan of Afrobeat, Trap, or any genre in between, UP I COME is a must-listen. Badt Soma’s authentic storytelling and genre-blending sound are proof that he’s not just on the rise—he’s here to stay.



Stream UP I COME



Get ready to immerse yourself in the world of Badt Soma. Stream UP I COME on all major platforms and join the movement as he continues to make waves in the global music scene.

In a world where music serves as both an escape and a connection, TeeRoy Tyobee has once again delivered a masterpiece that resonates deeply with listeners. His latest single, One for the Road, is an Afro-fusion gem that effortlessly blends soulful melodies with infectious rhythms, cementing his place as one of Nigeria’s most promising voices in contemporary music.







Released to critical acclaim, One for the Road is more than just a song—it’s a story. With smooth vocals and heartfelt lyrics, TeeRoy takes us on a reflective journey about life, perseverance, and savoring the moments that matter most. The track’s vibrant production underscores its emotional depth, creating a soundscape that is both timeless and refreshingly modern.



A Rising Star With a Unique Voice



TeeRoy Tyobee has been steadily carving a niche for himself in the music industry. Known for his authentic sound and lyrical depth, TeeRoy draws inspiration from his roots in Kwande, Benue State, Nigeria. His previous works, such as the fan-favorite Better Man, have established him as a storyteller who effortlessly combines Afrobeat, soul, and pop elements to create music that transcends borders.







Speaking about the release, TeeRoy shared, “Music is a universal language, and I want my songs to heal, inspire, and connect with people on a deeper level. One for the Road is my way of reminding everyone to cherish the journey and celebrate life’s moments, big or small.”



The Sonic Appeal of One for the Road



The production of One for the Road is a testament to TeeRoy’s commitment to quality and innovation. The song opens with a mellow yet captivating instrumental, quickly building into a dynamic Afrobeat rhythm complemented by TeeRoy’s velvety voice. The chorus is irresistibly catchy, making it an anthem for anyone who loves good vibes and great music.









Whether you’re on a late-night drive, reflecting on your own journey, or vibing with friends, this song is bound to become a playlist staple.



Where to Listen



One for the Road is now available on all major streaming platforms, including Spotify, Apple Music, and Audiomack. Fans are already raving about the track, with many calling it TeeRoy’s most mature and impactful release to date.



What’s Next for TeeRoy Tyobee?



As TeeRoy continues to evolve as an artist, fans can expect even more groundbreaking music from him in the near future. With his unique ability to blend heartfelt storytelling with infectious rhythms, TeeRoy is undoubtedly on the path to becoming a global sensation.



Final Thoughts



TeeRoy Tyobee’s One for the Road is a must-listen for anyone who appreciates music with meaning and soul. It’s not just a song; it’s an experience—a celebration of life, love, and everything in between.

His previous works, such as the fan-favorite Better Man, have established him as a storyteller who effortlessly combines Afrobeat, soul, and pop elements to create music that transcends borders.

Speaking about the release, TeeRoy shared, “Music is a universal language, and I want my songs to heal, inspire, and connect with people on a deeper level. One for the Road is my way of reminding everyone to cherish the journey and celebrate life’s moments, big or small.”

The Sonic Appeal of One for the Road

The production of One for the Road is a testament to TeeRoy’s commitment to quality and innovation. The song opens with a mellow yet captivating instrumental, quickly building into a dynamic Afrobeat rhythm complemented by TeeRoy’s velvety voice. The chorus is irresistibly catchy, making it an anthem for anyone who loves good vibes and great music.

Whether you’re on a late-night drive, reflecting on your own journey, or vibing with friends, this song is bound to become a playlist staple.

Where to Listen

One for the Road is now available on all major streaming platforms, including Spotify, Apple Music, and Audiomack. Fans are already raving about the track, with many calling it TeeRoy’s most mature and impactful release to date.

What’s Next for TeeRoy Tyobee?

As TeeRoy continues to evolve as an artist, fans can expect even more groundbreaking music from him in the near future. With his unique ability to blend heartfelt storytelling with infectious rhythms, TeeRoy is undoubtedly on the path to becoming a global sensation.

Final Thoughts

TeeRoy Tyobee’s One for the Road is a must-listen for anyone who appreciates music with meaning and soul. It’s not just a song; it’s an experience—a celebration of life, love, and everything in between.

Singer-songwriter Oladeji Solomon Adisa, popularly known as Kashamadupe Kst, has unveiled his latest single, Journey, a heartfelt anthem celebrating resilience, self-belief, and personal growth. This release marks another milestone in the artist’s evolving career, showcasing his signature sound and storytelling prowess.







A Musical Journey Rooted in Experience



Born and raised in Jos, with ties to Oyo State and Bauchi, Kashamadupe’s artistry is a reflection of his rich cultural background and life experiences. Drawing inspiration from Nigerian music legends such as Lagbaja, Ebenezer Obey, and Beautiful Nubia, Kashamadupe’s sound blends Afrocentric rhythms with contemporary vibes.



Kashamadupe is no stranger to pushing boundaries in music. Tracks like Zambezi and Para have already established his reputation for delivering music that is both meaningful and memorable. With Journey, he continues to evolve as an artist while staying true to the values and stories.



The Message Behind “Journey”



Kashamadupe describes Journey as more than just a song—it’s a movement. “Journey is a powerful expression of the unwavering belief in oneself and one’s dreams,” he shares. “Inspired by the struggles and triumphs of my own journey, this track is a testament to the unrelenting drive that fuels our passions and creativity.”









The single is built on an infectious beat, uplifting melodies, and lyrics that speak directly to the soul. It captures the essence of perseverance, offering listeners a reminder that challenges can be overcome with determination and faith.



A Testament to Artistic Growth



Having worked with renowned producers like SicaTunezz and Ezikel Phoenix, Kashamadupe continues to grow as a versatile and innovative artist. Journey stands as a reflection of his experiences, blending traditional influences with modern sounds to create something truly unique.



Join the Movement



Be part of Kashamadupe’s inspiring story by streaming ‘Journey‘ today: 



With its captivating sound and empowering message, Journey is set to become an anthem for anyone pursuing their dreams against all odds. This single reaffirms Kashamadupe KS’s place as a rising force in the Nigerian music industry.

Lagos-born record producer and songwriter 28Mojo is redefining the soundscape of Nigerian music with his latest project, “Alte Messiah Vol 1.” A pioneer of “Alte-Pop” – a unique blend of Alte-Fusion and Afro-Pop – Mojo continues to break creative boundaries with his visionary approach to music.







A Glimpse into 28Mojo’s Journey



From a background of struggle and solitude, 28Mojo has emerged as a force in the Nigerian music industry, proving that consistency and hard work can pave the way for greatness. His debut project, “Isolated,” explored themes of peace and self-acceptance, while his sophomore release, “Diaries of an Introvert,” celebrated the freedom of living on one’s own terms. Now, with “Alte Messiah Vol 1,” Mojo invites listeners on a transformative journey that intertwines raw emotions, rich storytelling, and genre-defying soundscapes.









A Creative Process Rooted in Growth



In Mojo’s words, “I gradually produced this project; one of the songs I made a few years back. But I recently decided it was time to release music, so I compiled them all. This project is the beginning of a new brand for me.”



“Alte Messiah Vol 1” represents not just a collection of tracks but a personal evolution. Mojo draws inspiration from the beauty of nature and the complexity of the human experience, channeling these influences into music that stirs emotions and sparks imagination.



Pioneering a New Wave



28Mojo has solidified his reputation as an “Afro-Crooner” and a master of sounds and rhythms. Using nothing but a PC as his creative tool, he crafts melodies that feel like stories – journeys into the heart of what it means to be human.







With “Alte Messiah Vol 1,” Mojo invites his listeners to experience music in its purest form, blending Alte-Pop with profound storytelling to create something truly groundbreaking.



Why You Should Listen



For fans of boundary-pushing music and innovative sounds, “Alte Messiah Vol 1” is a must-listen. It’s a testament to Mojo’s growth as an artist and his dedication to bringing something fresh to the global music stage.



“Alte Messiah Vol 1” is more than an album – it’s a movement, a manifesto, and a celebration of individuality and creativity. Dive into the world of 28Mojo and prepare to be mesmerized.







Follow 28Mojo on his musical journey, and experience the rise of the Alte Messiah.

Nigerian music powerhouses Lit Vybz and VJ Skinny have teamed up to release “Problem”, an Afro-Drill masterpiece that blends hard-hitting beats with heartfelt storytelling. Released December, the track is a testament to the artists’ ability to channel themes of struggle, resilience, and hope into a captivating soundscape.







A Sonic Exploration of Strength



“Problem” combines the infectious rhythms of Afrobeat with the bold, gritty energy of Drill, creating a sound that is both fresh and reflective. The track opens with haunting melodies and powerful percussion, setting the stage for Lit Vybz’s smooth, introspective verses and VJ Skinny’s raw, melodic delivery. Together, the duo crafts a compelling narrative of triumph over adversity, making “Problem” an anthem for perseverance.









Lit Vybz showcases his lyrical prowess with lines that speak to overcoming challenges, while VJ Skinny complements this with his emotive and relatable performance. Their synergy results in a track that is as inspiring as it is enjoyable, resonating with anyone facing life’s hurdles.



Meet the Visionaries Behind the Track







Lit Vybz



Born Kwen Joshua in Nigeria’s Middle Belt, Lit Vybz has been redefining Nigerian music since his breakout in 2015. Known for his unique fusion of rap, Afrobeat, and melodic storytelling, he draws from his personal experiences and cultural heritage to create music that transcends genres. With a career spanning nearly a decade, Lit Vybz continues to evolve, solidifying his reputation as one of Nigeria’s most versatile artists.



VJ Skinny



Peter Luis Onuh, better known as VJ Skinny, is a multi-talented artist from Benue State. A graduate of Theatre Arts from the University of Abuja, VJ Skinny’s music is a reflection of his personality, environment, and emotions. Influenced by the diverse sounds of his upbringing in Makurdi, he has developed a catalog that includes hits like “Benefit Boy”, “Secure the Bag”, and “Hey God”. With his ability to fuse raw emotion with rhythmic versatility, VJ Skinny has become a standout figure in the industry.



Why You Need “Problem” on Your Playlist



More than just a song, “Problem” is a movement—a call to rise above life’s obstacles and embrace hope. Whether you’re a fan of Afrobeat, Drill, or music that tells a story, this track offers a unique blend of rhythm and meaning. Lit Vybz and VJ Skinny prove that music can both inspire and entertain, delivering a track that will resonate deeply with listeners.



Listen here

GANDE IS BREAKING BOUNDARIES WITH “INSTA BABE”
articles.body: Gande Senamin Samuel, professionally known as Gande, is not interested in making music that simply sounds good and disappears. The young Nigerian artist from Benue State, Makurdi, and raised in Abuja has always approached music as a way to connect with people. His songs draw from life, relationships and everyday experiences, giving listeners stories they can recognize, laugh about and ultimately connect with. Now, with his first single of the year, “INSTA BABE,” Gande is pushing that approach into a more playful and unconventional territory. The song tells the story of a connection that begins where many modern relationships now begin: Instagram. Gande meets a girl on the platform, but getting her attention isn’t exactly easy. At first, she plays hard to get and appears completely uninterested. As the story develops, however, things begin to change — particularly after Gande starts sending her money. Eventually, despite living in different states, the two are able to meet through the connection they built online. But the real twist comes with a gift. She gets Gande a pair of Calvin Klein boxers, and suddenly, in the playful logic of the song, that gift becomes her justification for wanting to have some control over him. “All because say she buy me Calvin Klein boxersThe kele she say she get right to steady off am” And Gande doesn’t stop there. The story continues with another designer reference: “All because say she buy me Tommy HilfigerThe kele she say she get right to steady commot am” It is this combination of humour, everyday relationship dynamics and contemporary social-media culture that gives “INSTA BABE” its identity. Rather than presenting a polished fantasy of romance, Gande turns a familiar modern experience into music — the Instagram connection, the long-distance link-up, the mixed signals, the spending and even the unexpected power dynamics that can come with affection and gifts. The result is a song that feels deliberately unfiltered. A New Side of Gande “INSTA BABE” also represents something bigger in Gande’s artistic journey. Known for creating music that reflects life experiences while aiming to uplift and inspire his audience, Gande has been developing a sound that blends different genres rather than being restricted by one musical formula. That willingness to experiment is becoming an important part of his identity. With “INSTA BABE,” he isn’t trying to tell the biggest story in the world. He’s taking a small, almost comedic experience and turning it into something listeners can immediately picture. That is where Gande’s strength lies: making personal experiences feel universal. The story could easily belong to someone scrolling through Instagram late at night, meeting someone from another state, trying to get their attention, eventually meeting them in person and discovering that the relationship comes with its own unexpected rules. Gande simply turned the experience into a song. Breaking Boundaries For Gande, breaking boundaries isn’t necessarily about abandoning everything that came before. It is about giving himself permission to explore more. “INSTA BABE” demonstrates an artist willing to step outside a conventional narrative, embrace humour and personality, and allow real-life experiences to shape his music. It also gives listeners another reason to pay attention. Behind the playful story is an artist with a clear ambition: to build a lasting relationship with his audience, stay true to himself and continue creating music that makes people feel something. As Gande continues to grow, his evolution may ultimately become one of the most interesting parts of his story. From Benue to Abuja, from Instagram conversations to real-life connections, and now from personal experiences to music, Gande is carving out his own space. “INSTA BABE” is more than his first single of the year. It is another glimpse into an artist discovering just how far he can take his sound, his stories and his imagination. And if this is Gande breaking boundaries, there’s no telling where he goes next. Gande — “INSTA BABE” is out now.

articles.title: ONE VOICE: Kingx Vibe Beat Calls on Nigerians to Unite Through Music, Spoken Word and a Shared Message of Hope
articles.body: Nigerian music producer, musician and choir director Kingx Vibe Beat (Ezi Chukwu Wina) has announced the launch of ONE VOICE, a non-profit creative initiative calling on Nigerians from all walks of life to come together and express a collective message of hope, unity, prayer, awareness and positive change through music and spoken word. Created against the backdrop of the many challenges facing the country, ONE VOICE seeks to provide a platform where Nigerians can use their voices and creativity to speak against killings, kidnappings, insecurity, violence, division and other issues affecting communities across the nation. At its core, the initiative is built around a simple belief: Nigeria needs to hear its people speak as one. Unlike a conventional music project, ONE VOICE is not a commercial release, beat sale or promotional campaign. The initiative is completely non-profit and is not designed to promote Kingx Vibe Beat as an individual. Instead, its focus is on creating a collective platform where Nigerians can contribute their talents, experiences and messages toward a larger national conversation. “The vision is simple: to bring Nigerians together through one voice.” A Platform for Every Nigerian ONE VOICE is intentionally open to everyone. Singers, rappers, choir members, worship leaders, spoken-word artists, instrumentalists, content creators and anyone with a meaningful message for Nigeria are invited to participate. The initiative recognizes that music has historically served as more than entertainment. It has been a vehicle for protest, reflection, prayer, storytelling, healing and social consciousness. ONE VOICE seeks to channel that power toward a collective expression of what Nigerians hope for their country. Whether through a song, verse, prayer, performance, instrumental contribution or spoken message, participants are encouraged to add their voices to the movement. From the Church to Music Production The initiative is being led by Kingx Vibe Beat, born Ezi Chukwu Wina, a Nigerian music producer, musician and choir director based in Lagos. Kingx’s musical journey began in church, where he developed his abilities as a singer, instrumentalist and music director. His early experiences in the church environment helped shape his understanding of music not only as a form of entertainment, but also as a tool for expression, connection and inspiration. He later transitioned into music production, continuing to develop his craft through hands-on experience, collaborations and continuous learning. Known for his passion for creativity, faith and musical excellence, Kingx Vibe Beat has continued to explore ways of creating meaningful music that connects with people. ONE VOICE represents an extension of that philosophy — moving beyond individual artistry to create space for a collective Nigerian expression. More Than a Song ONE VOICE is ultimately about participation. It is an invitation for Nigerians to look beyond individual differences and contribute to a shared message about the country they want to see. At a time when conversations around insecurity, violence, division and the safety of communities continue to shape national discourse, the initiative aims to use creative expression as a peaceful means of raising awareness and encouraging unity. The project also carries an underlying message of hope: despite the challenges confronting the nation, Nigerians still have the ability to speak, create, pray, encourage one another and imagine a better future. ONE VOICE is that invitation. A call to the singer. A call to the rapper. A call to the choir. A call to the spoken-word artist. A call to the instrumentalist. A call to the creator. And a call to every Nigerian who has something to say. One country. Different voices. One message. ONE VOICE. God bless Nigeria. 🇳🇬

The initiative is being led by Kingx Vibe Beat, born Ezi Chukwu Wina, a Nigerian music producer, musician and choir director based in Lagos.

Kingx’s musical journey began in church, where he developed his abilities as a singer, instrumentalist and music director. His early experiences in the church environment helped shape his understanding of music not only as a form of entertainment, but also as a tool for expression, connection and inspiration.

He later transitioned into music production, continuing to develop his craft through hands-on experience, collaborations and continuous learning.

Known for his passion for creativity, faith and musical excellence, Kingx Vibe Beat has continued to explore ways of creating meaningful music that connects with people. ONE VOICE represents an extension of that philosophy — moving beyond individual artistry to create space for a collective Nigerian expression.

More Than a Song

ONE VOICE is ultimately about participation.

It is an invitation for Nigerians to look beyond individual differences and contribute to a shared message about the country they want to see.

At a time when conversations around insecurity, violence, division and the safety of communities continue to shape national discourse, the initiative aims to use creative expression as a peaceful means of raising awareness and encouraging unity.

The project also carries an underlying message of hope: despite the challenges confronting the nation, Nigerians still have the ability to speak, create, pray, encourage one another and imagine a better future.

ONE VOICE is that invitation.

A call to the singer.

A call to the rapper.

A call to the choir.

A call to the spoken-word artist.

A call to the instrumentalist.

A call to the creator.

And a call to every Nigerian who has something to say.

One country. Different voices. One message. ONE VOICE.

God bless Nigeria. 🇳🇬

articles.title: RHIA BELLO INVITES EVERYONE TO CELEBRATE, CONNECT AND “DRINK UP”
