articles.title: BIYO CIN CERA ENTERS A NEW ERA WITH “BOILING POINT,” AN EP ABOUT PRESSURE, IDENTITY AND TRANSFORMATION
articles.body: Alternative pop and R&B artist Biyo Cin Cera has officially released her highly anticipated EP, “Boiling Point,” introducing a deeply personal body of work shaped by pressure, resilience, transformation, and self-discovery. Built around the emotional intensity of reaching a breaking point, “Boiling Point” examines what happens when the weight of expectations, ambition, identity, and personal experiences becomes impossible to ignore. Rather than treating pressure solely as something destructive, Biyo Cin Cera uses the project to explore its transformative power. Across the EP, atmospheric soundscapes, intimate songwriting, and alternative pop and R&B influences create an immersive environment where vulnerability becomes a source of strength. At the centre of “Boiling Point” is a question that extends beyond the artist herself: What happens when everything you have carried finally reaches its limit? For Biyo Cin Cera, that moment becomes an opportunity for self-discovery. The project explores the tension between who people are, who they are expected to become, and the courage required to choose authenticity. Through emotionally driven storytelling, the Lagos-based artist turns those internal conflicts into a broader narrative about growth, ambition, resilience, and becoming. Speaking about the project, Biyo Cin Cera explains: “Boiling Point is about the moment where everything builds up you have to decide what you’re going to become. It’s about turning pressure into power.” That idea serves as the emotional core of the EP. “Boiling Point” does not simply document pressure; it examines what can emerge from it. With her alternative approach to pop and R&B, Biyo Cin Cera continues to develop a distinct artistic identity within Africa’s evolving music landscape. Her work is rooted in emotive storytelling and experimental sound, while creating an immersive world around themes of identity, resilience, love, and personal growth. “Boiling Point” therefore arrives as more than a collection of songs. It represents a defining chapter in Biyo Cin Cera’s artistic evolution — one where vulnerability, experimentation, and authenticity become central to the story. For an artist navigating the space between expectation and self-definition, the EP captures a moment of transformation: the point where pressure reaches its peak and the decision is no longer whether to change, but what to become. “Boiling Point” by Biyo Cin Cera is out now.

articles.title: BHADBOI DELA: BUILDING HIS OWN SOUND, ONE RECORD AT A TIME
articles.body: In an industry increasingly defined by constant movement and rapidly evolving sounds, BhadBoi dela is taking his own route to the spotlight. Born Nwogo Mandela, the emerging Nigerian recording artist traces his roots to Delta State, Nigeria, but his musical journey has been deeply shaped by Lagos. Driven by an early love for music and a desire to pursue it professionally, he moved to Lagos at a young age and was raised around the rural suburbs of Surulere. It is from that environment that much of his creative perspective has developed. His music draws from his surroundings, personal experiences and aspirations, translating the realities of his journey into records designed to connect through energy and emotion. For an artist still building his catalogue and audience, BhadBoi dela is already demonstrating a clear ambition: to develop a sound that can move beyond his immediate environment and establish him as a distinctive voice within Nigeria’s next generation of artists. THE JOURNEY BEHIND THE MUSIC For BhadBoi dela, music is more than simply a career choice. Creative Culture’s August 2026 profile presents his relationship with music as deeply personal, describing songwriting and recording as a means through which he expresses emotion, tells stories and connects with other people. The publication also highlights his belief in music’s ability to inspire and bring people together. (cculture.com.ng) That perspective gives context to the artist behind the records. His journey from Delta State to Lagos is itself part of the story. Growing up in Surulere exposed him to the energy, culture and everyday experiences of one of Lagos’ most recognizable communities. Those surroundings have become part of the foundation from which he continues to develop his artistic identity. Rather than presenting a distant version of himself through his music, BhadBoi dela is gradually building his catalogue around the experiences and ambitions that have accompanied his journey. FINDING THE BHADBOI DELA SOUND BhadBoi dela’s emerging sound is defined by energy, movement and an unmistakable desire to create records that resonate. His music sits within the contemporary Nigerian Afrobeat space while embracing a more energetic, rave-influenced direction. This is particularly apparent in his latest body of work, where rhythm and momentum play an important role in shaping the listening experience. That developing identity is important for an emerging artist. At a time when artists can easily become absorbed into the sounds dominating the market, creating a recognizable musical personality becomes one of the most important steps toward longevity. BhadBoi dela appears to be approaching that process through experimentation, consistency and a willingness to continue refining his sound. Creative Culture similarly describes him as an independent artist still climbing, using the challenges of the journey as motivation to improve his craft and deepen his understanding of the music industry. (cculture.com.ng) “SHOKOTO”: THE ENERGY STARTS HERE One of the clearest introductions to BhadBoi dela’s current musical direction is “Shokoto.” The record serves as an energetic showcase of the sound he is developing and has become an important part of the rollout surrounding his latest project. Creative Culture identified “SHOKOTO” as the lead single giving listeners an early glimpse into the energy, confidence and musical direction of ROCKSTAR Vol. 1. (cculture.com.ng) Its inclusion on the final EP is also confirmed by Qobuz, which lists “Shokoto” as the project’s second track. (Qobuz) For BhadBoi dela, the record represents more than another release. It functions as an introduction to the sonic world he is currently creating—one built around movement, confidence and high-energy Afrobeat. ROCKSTAR VOL. 1: A NEW CHAPTER On 20 August 2026, BhadBoi dela officially released ROCKSTAR Vol. 1, a four-track project that marks a significant step forward in his artistic development. The EP features: Abitoshaker Shokoto Aboki High Qobuz lists the project as a four-track Afrobeat release with a total runtime of approximately 11 minutes, with BhadBoi dela credited as the main artist and Mandela Nwogo credited as composer/lyricist across the tracks. (Qobuz) The compact format allows the project to function as a focused introduction to his current artistic direction rather than an attempt to say everything at once. Creative Culture described the EP as an important chapter in his artistic evolution and a statement that he is ready to take his artistry to another level. (cculture.com.ng) For an emerging artist, that positioning matters. ROCKSTAR Vol. 1 gives BhadBoi dela a defined body of work around which he can continue building his audience, live identity and musical catalogue. BEYOND LAGOS Although Lagos remains an important part of BhadBoi dela’s story, his ambitions extend considerably further. He is not approaching music with the intention of remaining confined to one city or one audience. His stated vision is global: to create music that can travel across borders, reach international listeners and eventually place him on major stages and festivals around the world. Creative Culture’s profile emphasizes this ambition, describing his dream of reaching audiences across continents and creating songs capable of living beyond temporary trends. (cculture.com.ng) That aspiration reflects a broader reality within Nigerian music. Nigerian artists are increasingly building careers that operate simultaneously within local and international markets, and emerging artists are entering the ecosystem with global audiences already in mind. BhadBoi dela wants to be part of that movement—not simply as another participant, but as an artist with his own story and sound to contribute. THE INDEPENDENT ARTIST’S CLIMB The path from emerging artist to established name is rarely straightforward. For independent musicians, the challenge extends beyond making good records. There is the continuous work of developing a sound, building an audience, understanding the business, maintaining consistency and finding opportunities to turn individual releases into a sustainable career. BhadBoi dela is currently navigating that stage. Creative Culture describes this period of his career as a climb marked by uncertainty, difficult decisions and the realities of independent artistry. Rather than presenting those challenges as setbacks, the artist views them as part of the process of becoming better. (cculture.com.ng) That mindset could prove important as his career develops. The strongest artist stories are rarely built around a single release. They are built through accumulation—one song, one project, one performance, one connection and one lesson at a time. CHASING GREATNESS At the center of BhadBoi dela’s story is ambition. He wants to grow. He wants his music to travel. He wants to connect with people who recognize something of themselves in his experiences. And ultimately, he wants to build a career that leaves a lasting mark. His philosophy is straightforward: keep moving. Creative Culture’s feature captures this through his emphasis on confronting fear rather than allowing it to determine the limits of his ambitions. (cculture.com.ng) That mentality is particularly relevant at this stage of his career. BhadBoi dela is not presented as an artist who has already reached the destination; he is an artist actively building toward it. And that is what makes his current chapter worth watching. WHY BHADBOI DELA IS AN ARTIST TO WATCH BhadBoi dela is still early in his journey, but the foundations are becoming clearer. He has a personal story rooted in Delta State and Lagos. He has developed a connection between his surroundings and his music. He is experimenting with an energetic Afrobeat direction. He has released a project with a defined sonic identity. And, perhaps most importantly, he has a clear ambition for where he wants the music to take him. With “Shokoto” providing a high-energy entry point and ROCKSTAR Vol. 1 establishing his latest chapter, BhadBoi dela now has an opportunity to turn momentum into sustained growth. The next phase will be about what comes after the introduction: expanding his catalogue, strengthening his identity, reaching new listeners and demonstrating how far the sound he is building can travel. For now, one thing is clear: BhadBoi dela is no longer simply chasing a dream. He is building the soundtrack to it. And with ROCKSTAR Vol. 1 now out in the world, the next chapter has officially begun.

articles.title: JustOne Sukay Emerges as a Distinctive New Voice in Abuja’s Music Scene
articles.body: Abuja’s increasingly dynamic music ecosystem continues to attract artists with distinctive perspectives, compelling stories and creative identities that challenge conventional boundaries. Among the emerging talents steadily carving out a unique space within the capital’s creative community is JustOne Sukay, known professionally as “The Rapitect.” A Nigerian rapper, singer and songwriter, JustOne Sukay approaches music through a multidisciplinary lens shaped by architecture, football, business, design and lived experience. Originally from Cross River State and influenced by his formative years in Calabar and experiences across different environments, Sukay has developed an artistic perspective that extends beyond the traditional boundaries of music. His latest single, “GENIUS,” produced by Gruzzmahn, offers a compelling introduction to that perspective. Drawing from Afro and Drill influences, the record is driven by assertive lyricism and a message centred on self-belief, ambition, resilience and personal determination. Rather than allowing circumstances or external expectations to define his trajectory, Sukay uses the song to reinforce a central idea: potential must be recognised, developed and ultimately expressed. That philosophy is reflected in the identity he has created for himself as The Rapitect. With an MSc in Architecture, Sukay views music through a similar principle of construction. Architecture demands vision, structure, precision and an understanding of how individual elements come together to form something greater. His songwriting follows a comparable approach, using words to construct ideas, emotions and narratives while giving each record its own identity and architecture. This perspective has contributed to his emergence as an independent artist associated with what he describes as “lyrically conscious” music—work that prioritises substance, perspective and intentional storytelling alongside sound. “GENIUS” marks another chapter in that progression. More than a standalone release, the record represents Sukay’s continued effort to establish a clearly defined artistic lane—one built around individuality rather than conformity. His interests outside music further reinforce that multidimensional identity. His background in architecture, combined with his interests in business, construction, design and football, gives him a broad creative vocabulary through which he interprets both his career and the world around him. As JustOne Sukay continues developing his catalogue and expanding his creative footprint within Abuja and beyond, The Rapitect is building more than a music career—he is constructing a creative blueprint of his own. And if “GENIUS” is an indication of what lies ahead, the blueprint is only beginning to take shape.

articles.title: EMIWIZZY CELEBRATES LIFE, PROGRESS AND THE JOURNEY ON NEW SINGLE “HAPPY DAY” FEATURING DAVID ACEKEYZ
articles.body: Nigerian Afro-pop artist Emiwizzy officially enters a new chapter today with the release of his latest single, “Happy Day,” featuring Nigerian producer and artist David Acekeyz. Available now across major streaming platforms, “Happy Day” arrives as a vibrant celebration of life, progress and the moments that make the journey meaningful. The release follows Emiwizzy’s 2026 record “OK OK OK” and introduces a lighter, more celebratory dimension to the artist’s evolving sound. Born Chukwuemelie Agagbo and originally from Anambra State, Emiwizzy grew up in Abuja, where his relationship with music began at an early age. His musical foundation was formed in the church choir, where he played drums at the Catholic Church of the Assumption in Asokoro. That rhythmic foundation has remained evident in an artistry built around energetic records and high-impact live performances. Emiwizzy officially began his recording career in 2017, releasing his debut single “King” before following it with the EMIWIZZY TO THE WORLD EP. Over the years, he has continued to build his catalogue through singles and collaborations, including “Control,” “Banger (Remix),” “Abj Boy” featuring Magnito, “Jaiye,” “ACTIVE,” and “OK OK OK.” His growing profile was recognised in 2022 when he received the Artist of the Year award at Capital Prom in Abuja, marking a notable milestone in his emergence within Nigeria’s Afro-pop space. Musically, Emiwizzy operates within a vibrant fusion of traditional African rhythm, contemporary pop and Amapiano-influenced production. His music is designed around catchy melodies, rhythmic energy and a performance-first identity — qualities that have increasingly become part of his artistic signature. “Happy Day” extends that identity through a collaboration with David Acekeyz, creating a meeting point between Emiwizzy’s vocal and songwriting approach and Acekeyz’s production sensibilities. The record arrives at a particularly important point in Emiwizzy’s career. With Cosco Entertainment behind his current chapter and Front Logik Distro working with him as brand consultant, the artist is positioning himself for wider collaborations, stronger visual direction and a sound capable of connecting with audiences beyond Nigeria. His audience has also continued to develop. Emiwizzy’s latest EPK records more than 36,800 combined streams and plays across Audiomack and Spotify, with more than 620 combined followers across both platforms. But “Happy Day” is ultimately less about statistics and more about a feeling. It is a record built around the simple idea of recognising the good moments — celebrating progress while remaining conscious of the road that made those moments possible. For an artist whose stated ambition is to achieve global recognition, touch lives and contribute to positive change through music, “Happy Day” represents another deliberate step toward that bigger picture. With a growing catalogue, an increasingly defined sound and a renewed focus on global reach, Emiwizzy is using “Happy Day” to remind listeners that sometimes the journey itself is worth celebrating. “Happy Day” by Emiwizzy featuring David Acekeyz is out now on all major streaming platforms. Stream Now

articles.title: EMIWIZZY SET TO BRING A NEW ENERGY WITH “HAPPY DAY” FEATURING DAVID ACEKEYZ
articles.body: Nigerian Afro-pop artist Emiwizzy is preparing to usher listeners into a brighter chapter with his forthcoming single, “Happy Day,” featuring Nigerian producer and artist David Acekeyz. The record is scheduled for release on August 14, 2026, across major streaming platforms. Coming shortly after his 2026 release “OK OK OK,” “Happy Day” finds Emiwizzy exploring a more celebratory and accessible side of his artistry. At its core, the song is built around appreciation — for life, progress, personal growth and the moments that make the journey worthwhile. For Emiwizzy, whose real name is Chukwuemelie Agagbo, music has always been closely connected to rhythm and performance. Born in Anambra State and raised in Abuja, his musical foundation was shaped in the church choir, where he played drums at the Catholic Church of the Assumption in Asokoro, Abuja. That early relationship with rhythm continues to influence the energetic character of his music and live performances. His professional journey began in 2017 with the release of his debut single, “King,” followed by the EMIWIZZY TO THE WORLD EP. Since then, he has steadily expanded his catalogue with releases including “Control,” “Banger (Remix),” “Abj Boy,” “Jaiye,” “ACTIVE,” and his latest project, “OK OK OK.” That progression earned Emiwizzy a significant early career milestone in 2022, when he was named Artist of the Year at Capital Prom in Abuja, recognition that reinforced his position among Nigeria’s emerging Afro-pop talents. Now signed to Cosco Entertainment and working with Front Logik Distro as brand consultant, Emiwizzy is entering a phase defined by sharper positioning, broader collaborations and an ambition to take his sound beyond familiar territory. His musical identity sits at the intersection of traditional African rhythms, contemporary pop and Amapiano-leaning production — a combination that has become central to his evolving sound. “Happy Day” adds another dimension to that evolution. The collaboration with David Acekeyz brings together Emiwizzy’s vocal and songwriting approach with Acekeyz’s production sensibilities. The result is positioned as a record that can live comfortably within everyday listening while carrying the energy and rhythm associated with Nigeria’s contemporary Afrobeats and Afro-pop landscape. The release also arrives as Emiwizzy continues to build an independent audience around his music. His current EPK records 36.8K+ combined streams and plays across Audiomack and Spotify, alongside 620+ combined followers across the two platforms. Those numbers represent more than accumulated plays; they reflect an artist steadily building the foundation for his next stage. With “Happy Day,” Emiwizzy appears less interested in simply adding another song to his catalogue and more focused on defining the feeling surrounding his next era — one rooted in movement, optimism and celebration. As the release date approaches, “Happy Day” stands as an invitation to pause, appreciate the journey and celebrate the progress already made. Presave Now

articles.title: Artist Spotlight: Melly Hypa
articles.body: The Rise of an Authentic Voice in Nigeria’s New Wave In Nigeria’s rapidly evolving music landscape, where countless artists compete for attention, Melly Hypa is quietly carving out a lane defined by authenticity, consistency, and emotional honesty. Emerging from the streets of Dei-Dei, Abuja, his story is one of resilience rather than overnight success—a journey built on persistence, lived experience, and an unwavering commitment to artistic growth. Rather than relying on viral moments, Melly Hypa has steadily expanded his catalog since 2021, developing a sound that blends hip-hop, Afrobeats, and melodic rap into music that feels deeply personal while remaining accessible to contemporary listeners. His growing body of work reflects an artist documenting his evolution one release at a time. Growing Up in Dei-Dei Born in Abuja, Nigeria, Melly Hypa spent his formative years in Dei-Dei, one of the capital city’s most demanding environments. Growing up amid economic hardship and limited opportunities exposed him to realities that many young Nigerians face daily. Instead of allowing those experiences to define him negatively, he transformed them into creative fuel. Music became more than entertainment—it became an outlet for reflection, self-expression, and ambition. Those early experiences continue to shape both his songwriting and artistic identity, giving his records a grounded perspective that resonates with listeners who appreciate authenticity over image. Crafting a Signature Sound Melly Hypa occupies a unique space between hip-hop, Afrobeats, and melodic rap, combining atmospheric production with reflective lyricism. His music explores themes of personal growth, street survival, ambition, relationships, self-belief, and emotional vulnerability, creating songs that balance introspection with contemporary Afro-urban energy. Rather than chasing whichever sound dominates playlists, Melly Hypa allows his music to evolve naturally alongside his life experiences. His records often carry a late-night, reflective atmosphere, blending melodic vocals with conversational rap flows. As both a songwriter and vocalist, he remains actively involved in shaping the creative direction of his music, collaborating closely with producers to ensure every record reflects his artistic vision. Building Momentum Through Consistency Melly Hypa officially began building his catalog with “Yee!” in 2021 before gradually expanding his audience through a steady stream of independent releases. His discography has since grown to include “Opor,” “Silence,” “Since 010” featuring Lapizy, “6Am,” “Stay Mute / Psychosis” with FBI SZN, “Good Life,” “Commit (Diamond),” “Gaddmn,” “Lol,” “Faraway” featuring Larry Omorr, and “Frightened & Fighting.” Each release represents another chapter in his artistic journey, showcasing his commitment to consistency rather than chasing overnight success. Collaborations That Expand His Reach Collaboration has become an important part of Melly Hypa’s artistic development. Throughout his career, he has worked alongside emerging artists including FBI SZN, Lapizy, and Larry Omorr, strengthening his presence within Nigeria’s independent music ecosystem while expanding his creative range. Behind the scenes, he has collaborated with respected producers including Telvie, Miickel, and Nantee, each contributing new textures to his evolving sound. These partnerships have helped him refine his musical identity without sacrificing the authenticity that defines his work. Powered by Independent Distribution An important component of Melly Hypa’s career has been his long-standing relationship with Jozbrain Media, which has distributed his music across major digital streaming platforms. Through independent distribution, his catalog has become accessible to listeners around the world, allowing him to steadily expand his audience while maintaining complete creative independence. Taking the Stage While still in the early stages of his career, Melly Hypa has begun translating his digital momentum into live performances. A defining milestone came in 2025, when he performed during the Ayo Maff Show at the legendary Fela Shrine in Lagos, one of Nigeria’s most culturally significant live music venues. Performing on such a respected stage represented an important step in his career, demonstrating his growing confidence as a live performer while introducing his music to a wider audience. Growing Beyond the Numbers Although Melly Hypa has yet to secure major industry awards or national chart placements, his progress reflects the steady growth of an independent artist committed to building a lasting career. His music is available across major streaming platforms, where listeners continue to discover an expanding catalog that reflects years of dedication and artistic development. Rather than relying on a single breakout hit, he has built momentum through consistency, quality releases, and an authentic connection with his audience. His digital presence continues to grow through streaming platforms, YouTube, and social media, where he shares new music, visuals, and insights into his creative journey. An Artist Focused on Longevity At the heart of Melly Hypa’s music lies a simple philosophy: your environment does not determine your destination. His records document growth rather than perfection, capturing moments of uncertainty, ambition, confidence, perseverance, and self-discovery while allowing listeners to follow both his personal and artistic evolution. This commitment to authenticity continues to distinguish him in a crowded music landscape where genuine storytelling remains one of the most valuable qualities an artist can possess. Looking Ahead Melly Hypa represents a new generation of Nigerian artists building sustainable careers through consistency, collaboration, and creative independence. From Abuja to an expanding international streaming audience, his journey reflects an artist who continues to evolve with every release while remaining true to the experiences that shaped him. With an increasingly diverse catalog, respected production collaborations, growing live performance experience, and a clear artistic identity, Melly Hypa is positioning himself as one of Abuja’s promising voices within Nigeria’s new wave of hip-hop and Afro-fusion talent. As his sound continues to mature and his audience expands, he stands as an artist whose greatest achievements may still be ahead.

articles.title: TulaPRO Doubles Down on His Lifestyle With BADBOY II
articles.body: TulaPRO isn’t interested in creating a character—he’s presenting himself exactly as he is. The six-track EP arrives as his most personal and self-driven body of work to date, built on lived experiences, unapologetic confidence, and complete creative independence. Blending Afro-fusion, Afrobeats, and Alté influences, BADBOY II captures the highs, risks, relationships, ambition, and mindset that define TulaPRO’s world. Rather than fictionalizing his experiences, every record serves as another page from his own story. “This project comes straight from my own life and lifestyle,” TulaPRO explains. “I’m not writing stories for other people—this is what I’ve actually lived through.” That authenticity becomes the foundation of the entire project. Whether listeners connect with the hustle, the nightlife, the production, or simply the energy, BADBOY II offers multiple entry points while remaining true to one consistent identity. Living Life on His Own Terms At its core, BADBOY II is built around independence. Across the project, TulaPRO embraces a mindset focused on ambition, financial freedom, and refusing to let outside opinions dictate his direction. The title itself reflects an attitude rather than just an image—a willingness to accept both the rewards and consequences of living without compromise. Opening record “P Star” immediately establishes the project’s mentality, centering on limitless ambition and the relentless pursuit of bigger goals. Instead of celebrating comfort, the record suggests that success only creates a hunger for more. That energy continues on “2026,” where spending, earning, and reloading become part of an endless cycle of chasing the next opportunity. On “Feeling Me,” the project shifts into relationship territory, offering an honest account of modern dating dynamics through TulaPRO’s own perspective. Rather than dressing the story up, he delivers it with the same blunt honesty that defines the rest of the EP. The nightlife takes center stage on “Cok Party,” a club-ready record inspired by one of the artist’s real-life encounters. Equal parts charismatic and unpredictable, the song reinforces the carefree confidence that runs throughout the project. One of the EP’s defining moments arrives with “SNM (She No Mind),” featuring Killerverse. Built around a true story, the collaboration recounts an unforgettable encounter that both artists experienced firsthand. The chemistry between the two gives the record an added level of authenticity, making it one of the standout moments on the project. Closing the EP is “BMS (Badman Settings),” a record that feels less like a song and more like TulaPRO’s personal manifesto. Looking back on years of betting on himself, the track celebrates resilience, self-belief, and staying committed to the grind regardless of the obstacles. A Fully Independent Creative Vision One of the biggest achievements behind BADBOY II isn’t just the music—it’s how it was made. With the exception of the opening track, TulaPRO personally wrote, produced, mixed, and mastered the entire project himself. That level of creative ownership allows the EP to feel cohesive from beginning to end, with every sonic decision reflecting his own artistic instincts rather than outside influence. While BADBOY II pushes his sound into new territory, it never loses the identity that has defined his music from the beginning. Real Stories. Real Lifestyle. For TulaPRO, BADBOY II isn’t about creating fantasy. It’s about documenting reality. The money.The nightlife.The relationships.The wins.The lessons.The mindset. Every record contributes to a larger picture of an artist determined to live on his own terms, regardless of public opinion. Listeners looking for polished storytelling will find honesty. Listeners looking for infectious production will find carefully crafted records. And listeners simply looking for music that captures confidence, ambition, and lifestyle without pretending to be something else will likely find themselves returning to this project. Final Thoughts BADBOY II represents an important step forward for TulaPRO—not because it reinvents who he is, but because it refines it. Raw.Personal.Independent. The project doesn’t ask for permission or approval. It simply invites listeners into TulaPRO’s world and lets the music speak for itself. Now Streaming on All Major Digital Platforms.

articles.title: FeyoTheGenius Embraces the Night on His Most Personal Project Yet: NOCTURNE
articles.body: With the release of NOCTURNE, FeyoTheGenius invites listeners into a world where darkness isn’t something to escape—it’s a place to reflect, create and evolve. Available today on all major streaming platforms, the four-track EP marks a defining chapter in the artist’s journey, showcasing years of artistic growth, sonic experimentation and complete creative independence. Entirely self-produced, NOCTURNE is more than a collection of songs. It is a carefully constructed listening experience built on immersive basslines, atmospheric synth textures and cinematic transitions that blur the line between music and storytelling. Every moment feels intentional, revealing an artist who has taken the time to refine not only his sound but also his identity. At its core, NOCTURNE represents honesty. Rather than chasing trends, FeyoTheGenius leans into vulnerability, allowing the music to speak through emotion, atmosphere and meticulous production. The result is a project that feels intimate while remaining expansive—equally suited for solitary late-night listening and repeated front-to-back sessions. The title itself perfectly reflects the mood of the project. Traditionally associated with the night, a nocturne evokes introspection, calm and mystery. FeyoTheGenius transforms those qualities into a modern Afro-inspired sonic landscape, creating an experience that rewards listeners who appreciate detail, ambience and authentic expression. What makes this release even more significant is the level of creative ownership behind it. By producing the entire EP himself, FeyoTheGenius demonstrates a commitment to developing a signature sound without compromise. articles.title: CREATIVE SPOTLIGHT: The Visionaries Behind AfroCamp — Young Sudan, Makama & The Tripster
articles.body: In every thriving creative ecosystem, there are individuals whose ideas transcend their own disciplines—artists who don’t simply make music, direct films or design visuals, but shape the culture around them. Across Nigeria’s Federal Capital Territory, three such creatives are steadily redefining what it means to build from the underground. Young Sudan, Makama and The Tripster have emerged as distinct voices in music, film and visual arts, yet together they form the creative heartbeat of AfroCamp, one of Abuja’s fastest-growing multidisciplinary creative collectives. Rather than following conventional paths, each creative brings a unique perspective to the movement. One is reconnecting audiences with African heritage through Afro-fusion and cultural storytelling. Another is dismantling genre boundaries to redefine Nigeria’s alternative music landscape. The third is transforming ideas into immersive visual worlds that have become synonymous with Abuja’s evolving creative identity. Together, they represent a generation proving that collaboration—not competition—is the foundation of lasting cultural impact. Guided by AfroCamp’s philosophy of “Culture First. Community Always. Creativity Without Borders,” these creatives are building more than individual careers. They are contributing to a movement where music, film, fashion, design and cultural expression exist within one shared ecosystem. As AfroCamp continues to expand its influence, these three visionaries are helping redefine the future of independent creativity in Northern Nigeria and beyond. Young Sudan — The Cultural Architect Every movement begins with a vision, and for AfroCamp, that vision belongs to Young Sudan. Founder of AfroCamp and one of Abuja’s most promising Afro-fusion artists, Young Sudan has built his artistic identity around reconnecting modern audiences with African culture through music. Formerly known as Basky, his evolution into Young Sudan reflects a deeper commitment to exploring heritage, identity and purpose through creative expression. His sound blends Afro-fusion, folk influences and traditional African elements into a style that feels both contemporary and deeply rooted in culture. His ambitions extend beyond music. Through documentary filmmaking, visual storytelling and cultural initiatives, Young Sudan has consistently demonstrated a desire to create conversations that celebrate African identity while challenging conventional narratives. Whether in the studio or behind larger creative concepts, his work reflects a belief that art should educate, preserve and inspire as much as it entertains. As the founder of AfroCamp, his greatest contribution may be the environment he has created for others. Rather than building a platform centered solely on himself, he has cultivated a creative ecosystem where artists, filmmakers, designers and innovators are encouraged to collaborate, experiment and grow together. Makama — The Alternative Revolutionary If Young Sudan represents AfroCamp’s cultural philosophy, Makama embodies its fearless spirit of experimentation. Among the most compelling voices emerging from Nigeria’s alternative music movement, Makama has earned recognition for creating music that refuses easy categorization. His artistry seamlessly blends alternative hip-hop, melodic trap, rage rap, indie rock, electronic influences and contemporary African sounds into an identity that is both emotionally raw and creatively ambitious. Since his earliest releases, Makama has steadily developed a reputation for pushing creative boundaries through unconventional production, immersive storytelling and a striking visual identity. His music challenges listeners to embrace vulnerability, individuality and artistic freedom while celebrating the cultural richness of Northern Nigeria through a modern lens. His rise reflects a broader shift taking place across African music, where artists are increasingly rejecting rigid genre definitions in favour of authentic self-expression. Within AfroCamp, Makama represents the collective’s willingness to embrace innovation without sacrificing identity, making him one of the movement’s defining creative voices. The Tripster — The World Builder Creativity rarely exists within a single discipline, and The Tripster exemplifies that philosophy. As a multidisciplinary artist and Creative Director, he works across film, music, fashion, visual arts and spatial design, creating immersive experiences where surrealism and reality coexist. Every project he undertakes is driven by a distinctive artistic language that blends cinematic storytelling with bold conceptual thinking, allowing him to transform ideas into visually unforgettable experiences. Beyond directing and creative consultancy, The Tripster has become an important figure within Abuja’s underground creative community through his commitment to building platforms that empower independent artists. His work consistently demonstrates that imagination and vision—not budgets or expensive equipment—are the true foundations of exceptional creativity. Within AfroCamp, his ability to translate concepts into compelling visual narratives gives the collective much of its cinematic identity, helping shape a creative movement that values artistry in every medium. Three Creatives. One Movement. Although their creative journeys differ, Young Sudan, Makama and The Tripster are united by a shared belief that culture should always come before commercial expectation. Young Sudan is building a platform that reconnects audiences with African identity. Makama is reshaping the future of Nigeria’s alternative music through fearless experimentation. The Tripster is redefining visual storytelling by creating worlds that challenge conventional creative expression. Individually, they are innovators. Together, they represent a collective vision that is transforming Abuja’s independent creative landscape. Their collaboration through AfroCamp demonstrates the power of multidisciplinary creativity, where musicians, filmmakers, designers and storytellers work together to build something greater than individual success. It is a movement grounded in authenticity, community and cultural preservation—one that continues to inspire a new generation of African creators. The RADARCharts by REM Perspective RADARCharts by REM proudly recognizes Young Sudan, Makama and The Tripster as three of the most exciting creatives shaping the future of Abuja’s underground scene. Their individual journeys highlight the diversity of talent emerging from the capital, while their collective work through AfroCamp reflects a bold vision for the future of African creativity. As AfroCamp continues to evolve, these three visionaries stand as living proof that the strongest creative movements are built not around a single star, but around a community of artists united by purpose, originality and an unwavering commitment to pushing culture forward.

articles.title: AfroCamp: The Creative Collective Rewriting Abuja’s Underground Culture
articles.body: In every generation, a movement emerges that reshapes the creative landscape from the ground up. Across Nigeria’s Federal Capital Territory, that movement is rapidly becoming AfroCamp—a multidisciplinary creative collective that is redefining collaboration, cultural expression, and artistic development within the capital’s thriving underground scene. Fully endorsed by RADARCharts by REM, AfroCamp stands as one of the most exciting creative ecosystems currently emerging from Abuja, bringing together musicians, filmmakers, designers, photographers, producers, storytellers, visual artists and innovators under one unified vision. Rather than following the traditional blueprint of a record label or creative agency, AfroCamp has positioned itself as a movement built around community, culture and long-term creative ownership. Founded by Ibrahim Haruna, professionally known as Young Sudan, AfroCamp is steadily becoming a central force in connecting the city’s independent creatives, creating a new culture where collaboration outweighs competition and authentic African storytelling remains at the heart of every project. More Than A Collective AfroCamp exists to bridge multiple creative disciplines into one ecosystem where music, film, fashion, design, heritage and technology coexist naturally. Its philosophy challenges the fragmented approach often seen within independent creative communities, replacing it with a model where every creator contributes to a larger cultural narrative. The collective believes Africa’s future influence on global culture will not be built through imitation, but through originality rooted in authentic identity. This vision is reflected throughout every aspect of AfroCamp’s work—from artist development and visual storytelling to documentary production, creative direction and community-driven experiences. Building The Future Of African Creativity At its core, AfroCamp seeks to become Africa’s leading independent creative ecosystem by empowering creators to preserve their heritage while producing work capable of resonating on the global stage. Its mission extends beyond entertainment. The collective is actively committed to: Building a sustainable creative home for African talent. Developing original music, films and documentaries. Preserving and reinterpreting African cultural heritage. Creating international opportunities for African creatives. Developing intellectual property that originates from Africa and travels worldwide. This holistic approach positions AfroCamp not simply as a creative brand, but as a cultural institution in the making. A New Energy Driving Abuja’s Underground Scene Abuja’s independent music and creative community has experienced remarkable growth over recent years, but AfroCamp represents something distinctly different. Instead of building around individual success stories, the collective is fostering an environment where entire creative disciplines evolve together. Musicians collaborate with filmmakers. Designers influence visual identity. Producers exchange ideas with photographers. Storytellers shape projects that extend beyond music into wider cultural conversations. The result is an ecosystem where creative excellence becomes a shared pursuit rather than an isolated achievement. This collaborative model is rapidly strengthening the unity of Abuja’s underground scene, creating opportunities for emerging voices while encouraging a culture built on mutual support and artistic innovation. Current Initiatives Leading The Movement AfroCamp’s expanding portfolio already reflects the ambition behind its vision. articles.title: EF MOON: The Fearless Afro-Fusion Visionary Building a World Beyond Genres
articles.body: Nigeria’s music landscape has entered a period of remarkable creative expansion. Alongside the global success of Afrobeats, a new generation of artists is reshaping the conversation through experimentation, emotional depth, and a willingness to challenge convention. Among the most compelling voices in this movement is EF Moon, a Lagos-based artist whose work sits at the intersection of Afro-fusion, alternative music, and deeply personal storytelling. What distinguishes EF Moon is not only his sound, but the clarity of his artistic intent. He is building a body of work that values honesty over formula and identity over imitation. In doing so, he has positioned himself as an artist whose appeal extends beyond genre boundaries and into the broader cultural conversation about what contemporary African music can become. Origins and Early Journey Born Elijah Friday, EF Moon’s artistic identity is rooted in family, heritage, and self-definition. The name “Moon” traces back to “Ochu,” an Igala name given to him by his grandfather. Over time, that name has evolved into more than a stage identity; it has become a symbol of direction, reflection, and purpose. Although his roots are in Cross River State, EF Moon’s creative development has been shaped in Lagos, where the pace of the city and the diversity of its music scene have provided fertile ground for experimentation. His early exposure to a wide range of sounds helped form an artistic sensibility that does not recognize rigid boundaries. Instead, he draws from Afrobeats, rock, trap, and alternative influences to create music that feels both contemporary and deeply personal. His visual identity reinforces that sense of intention. The moon tattoo on his forehead is not merely a stylistic choice; it is a declaration of presence. It reflects an artist who understands the importance of image as part of storytelling and who is unafraid to present himself with complete conviction. From the outset, EF Moon has approached his career not as a search for approval, but as a process of building an artistic world that is unmistakably his own. Crafting a Distinct Sound EF Moon’s music resists easy classification, and that resistance is central to its appeal. His work draws from Afro-fusion, alternative pop, trap, rock, and indigenous sonic textures, yet it never feels like a simple combination of influences. Instead, he uses those elements to construct songs that are emotionally layered and sonically adventurous. His records often move between intensity and restraint, confidence and vulnerability. That dynamic gives his music a cinematic quality, allowing listeners to experience not just melodies and rhythms, but mood, tension, and release. Rather than relying on predictable structures, EF Moon leans into experimentation, using arrangement and storytelling to create songs that linger long after they end. The themes he explores are equally deliberate. Love, resilience, self-reflection, emotional healing, and personal growth recur throughout his catalogue, giving his work a sense of continuity and depth. These are not abstract ideas presented for effect; they are lived experiences translated into music with precision and sincerity. In a musical environment where novelty can sometimes overshadow substance, EF Moon stands out for his ability to make experimentation feel purposeful. His sound is not designed to fit neatly into existing categories. It is designed to reflect the complexity of the world he inhabits. Milestones and Career Growth EF Moon’s rise has been gradual, but it has been marked by steady momentum and increasing recognition. As an independent artist, he has built his audience through consistency, originality, and a growing catalogue of songs that resonate with listeners seeking something beyond the mainstream. Tracks such as I Knoww, Cheat on Me, Investing, and Ehosa have played an important role in introducing his artistry to a wider audience. Each record contributes to a broader narrative about an artist refining his voice while remaining committed to authenticity. Among them, I Knoww has emerged as a particularly defining release, capturing the emotional balance that characterizes much of his work. It is a song that speaks to love, optimism, resilience, and self-awareness without sacrificing artistic edge. His debut album, MOON 1, released on June 4, 2026, marks a significant milestone in that journey. More than a collection of songs, the project functions as a formal introduction to his creative universe. Across the album, EF Moon explores identity, ambition, relationships, fear, and transformation with a level of focus that suggests an artist thinking beyond individual releases and toward a lasting body of work. MOON 1 is best understood as a statement of artistic direction. It signals that EF Moon is not simply participating in the current wave of alternative African music; he is actively helping define its contours. Cultural Impact and Vision EF Moon’s significance extends beyond his discography. At a time when many young artists are searching for ways to express individuality without losing cultural connection, he offers a compelling model of how both can coexist. His work encourages emotional openness, creative independence, and a refusal to dilute identity for the sake of convenience. That message resonates strongly with listeners who see music not only as entertainment, but as a space for recognition and self-understanding. EF Moon’s audience is drawn to the sense that his songs are made with intention and lived experience. He does not present perfection; he presents perspective. That distinction gives his work a rare kind of credibility. Visually and sonically, he is building more than a brand. He is shaping an artistic environment in which originality is not treated as a risk, but as a necessity. In that sense, his vision aligns with a broader cultural shift among African creatives who are expanding the possibilities of what contemporary music can communicate. Why This Artist Matters Now Nigeria’s music industry is evolving rapidly. While Afrobeats remains the country’s most visible global export, the appetite for alternative, experimental, and genre-fluid music continues to grow. Audiences are increasingly receptive to artists who bring new textures, new narratives, and new emotional registers to the conversation. EF Moon arrives at precisely this moment. His ability to merge Afrobeats with rock, trap, and alternative influences places him among a generation of artists redefining the sonic identity of Nigerian music. More importantly, his work reflects a broader cultural demand for authenticity. Listeners are no longer satisfied with technical polish alone; they want perspective, vulnerability, and a sense of artistic purpose. That is where EF Moon’s relevance becomes especially clear. He represents the rise of independent artistry, the expansion of Nigeria’s alternative scene, and the growing global interest in African music that is unafraid to experiment. His career suggests that the next chapter of the continent’s musical story will be shaped not only by scale and commercial success, but by originality and depth.

articles.title: ARTIST SPOTLIGHT: KEASUNGS -The Independent Storyteller Turning Nigeria’s Everyday Realities Into Viral Anthems
articles.body: In an era where virality often arrives before artistry, Anthony Ekene Obiechie—professionally known as Keasungs—has managed to merge both worlds. The Nigerian singer, songwriter, and producer has spent more than two decades refining his craft, quietly building a career rooted in authenticity before emerging as one of the most intriguing voices connecting digital culture with traditional storytelling. Whether through viral social sounds, infectious melodies, or songs that dissect family dynamics and relationships, Keasungs has demonstrated an unusual ability to transform ordinary experiences into culturally resonant moments. Origins and Early Journey Born in Lagos and raised in Ibusa, Delta State, Keasungs’ relationship with music began long before social media turned sounds into trends. Influenced by R&B and hip-hop, he started writing songs in 2003 and expanded into music production three years later, developing into a multifaceted creative capable of shaping every aspect of his records. His early musical experiences in Delta State alongside friends provided a strong foundation, but his relocation to Lagos in 2005 marked a defining chapter in his artistic journey. The move represented more than a change of environment—it was a commitment to pursuing music professionally and finding larger creative opportunities. Years later, the emergence of digital streaming fundamentally changed his outlook. By 2015, Keasungs had embraced the possibilities of independent distribution, recognizing that artists could build meaningful careers outside traditional label systems. Crafting a Unique Sound Keasungs occupies an interesting space within contemporary Nigerian music. His sound pulls from Afro-fusion, highlife, dancehall, R&B, and street-inspired storytelling, allowing him to move fluidly between genres while maintaining a recognizable identity. What separates him from many emerging artists is his reliance on narrative. His records often stem from real-life experiences, observations, and conversations happening around him. Songs like My Papa Na Ashawo, Nkpigamy, and Na Woman Finish My Papa explore themes of relationships, accountability, family dynamics, and human behavior through humour and social commentary. Rather than creating music solely for entertainment, Keasungs uses storytelling as a cultural mirror. His songs invite listeners to laugh, reflect, and engage in conversations about societal norms and personal choices. Milestones and Career Growth The artist’s digital breakthrough came in 2022 when several of his sounds and catchphrases gained traction across social media platforms, introducing his work to wider audiences and establishing him as a creator capable of generating viral moments. That same year brought an international milestone when his Afro-Dancehall cover of Ku Lo Sa secured a sync placement with Savage X Fenty, Rihanna’s globally recognised fashion and entertainment brand. The achievement highlighted his versatility as both an artist and producer while exposing his music to audiences beyond Nigeria. His momentum accelerated in 2026 with the release of highlife-inspired songs including Nkpigamy and My Papa Na Ashawo. The records gained substantial engagement online, supported by celebrities and user-generated content across social platforms. The success of these releases positioned Keasungs among the emerging independent voices benefitting from Nigeria’s rapidly expanding digital music ecosystem, where streaming and social media continue to create new pathways for artist discovery. Cultural Impact and Vision At the heart of Keasungs’ artistry is a commitment to honest storytelling. His music frequently tackles situations many Nigerians recognize but rarely discuss openly, giving his records a strong sense of relatability and cultural relevance. By blending humour with commentary, he creates songs that function as both entertainment and conversation starters. In a music industry increasingly driven by short attention spans, his ability to craft narratives that resonate beyond the first listen has become one of his defining strengths. His journey also reflects the rise of a new class of independent African creators—artists who understand production, distribution, branding, and digital engagement as interconnected parts of modern music careers. Why This Artist Matters Now Nigeria’s music industry is experiencing unprecedented growth, with local listeners embracing homegrown sounds and streaming numbers continuing to rise across multiple genres. Keasungs represents this evolution. He stands at the intersection of traditional storytelling, internet culture, and independent innovation. His success demonstrates that emerging artists no longer need to follow conventional industry pathways to create impact. As Afrobeats and African music continue expanding globally, voices like Keasungs offer something increasingly important: stories rooted in local realities yet capable of resonating with audiences far beyond their place of origin.

articles.title: ARTIST SPOTLIGHT: MAKAMA – The Architect of Nigeria’s Alternative Future
articles.body: From Abuja’s Underground to the Edge of Innovation In an era where algorithms often dictate creativity and trends move faster than culture can process them, MAKAMA exists in a lane entirely his own. The Abuja-based artist, producer, and sonic innovator has spent years quietly building a body of work that refuses easy categorization. While much of Nigeria’s music industry continues to revolve around commercial formulas, MAKAMA has chosen a different path—one rooted in experimentation, authenticity, and artistic freedom. Born Festus Udegbe and formerly known as Smvllz, MAKAMA represents a generation of creators redefining what Nigerian music can sound like. His music lives at the intersection of alternative rap, trap, house music, punk energy, and indigenous Northern Nigerian influences, creating a sound that feels simultaneously futuristic and deeply connected to home. For listeners searching for music beyond convention, MAKAMA has become one of the underground’s most compelling voices. Building a Sound Without Borders Every great artist possesses a defining characteristic. For MAKAMA, it is his refusal to operate within boundaries. His music doesn’t simply blend genres—it dismantles them. Across his catalog, psychedelic textures collide with hard-hitting percussion. Atmospheric melodies coexist with razor-sharp lyricism. Traditional Hausa influences merge seamlessly with global alternative sounds. The result is a musical identity that feels both unfamiliar and immediately recognizable. There is a certain unpredictability to a MAKAMA record. One moment you’re immersed in hypnotic melodies; the next, you’re pulled into intricate flows layered over experimental production that challenges expectations while remaining deeply engaging. This ability to balance innovation with accessibility has become one of his defining strengths. The Producer’s Mindset While many artists rely on producers to shape their sound, MAKAMA approaches music from a different perspective—he is both the architect and the artist. Long before audiences discovered him as a performer, he was developing his craft behind the boards, studying sound design, arrangement, and the emotional power of production. That producer’s mindset is evident throughout his work. Every drum pattern feels intentional. Every texture serves a purpose. Every transition contributes to a larger narrative. His production credits further reinforce his reputation as one of Abuja’s most creative musical minds. From co-producing projects like No Angels with paln to collaborating on MMXXII alongside Zilla Oaks, MAKAMA has consistently demonstrated an ability to elevate both his own artistry and the work of those around him. In many ways, he represents a new model of Nigerian musician—one who understands every layer of the creative process. The Power of Collaboration Great underground movements are rarely built alone. Throughout his career, MAKAMA has cultivated meaningful creative relationships with some of Abuja’s most exciting talents, including Zilla Oaks, BrisB, Blue7ame, and paln. Rather than treating collaboration as a marketing strategy, MAKAMA approaches it as creative chemistry. His collaborative records reveal an artist deeply invested in pushing ideas forward, creating spaces where different influences can coexist and evolve naturally. This spirit of community has helped shape a thriving ecosystem of alternative artists emerging from Abuja—an ecosystem MAKAMA continues to play a significant role in developing. A Voice for the Alternative Generation Nigeria’s music industry has never been more globally visible. Yet beyond the charts, a new movement is emerging—one driven by artists determined to tell their stories on their own terms. MAKAMA stands among the most exciting representatives of this generation. His music speaks to listeners who embrace individuality, who value experimentation, and who understand that culture moves forward when artists are willing to take risks. Whether through the haunting atmosphere of Northern Saints, the infectious energy of Drip, or the expansive sonic landscapes of his self-titled project, MAKAMA consistently demonstrates a commitment to growth and artistic evolution. He is not interested in following trends. He is interested in creating them. Beyond Music What ultimately separates MAKAMA from many of his contemporaries is vision. His work extends beyond songs and projects. It reflects a broader philosophy centered around creativity, self-expression, and cultural exploration. Each release feels less like a standalone record and more like a chapter in an unfolding story—one that continues to challenge expectations while expanding the possibilities of alternative African music. As global audiences increasingly look toward Africa for the next wave of cultural innovation, artists like MAKAMA are proving that the future of the continent’s music scene will not be defined by a single sound. It will be defined by fearless creators willing to imagine new ones. The Verdict MAKAMA is not merely an artist to watch. He is an artist helping shape the future. With a producer’s precision, a visionary’s imagination, and an unwavering commitment to authenticity, he continues to carve out a space that belongs entirely to him. In a world obsessed with fitting into categories, MAKAMA’s greatest achievement may be that he has created one of his own. And he’s only getting started.

articles.title: GyC Embraces Self-Worth and Confidence on Inspiring New Single “Worth”
articles.body: GyC Returns With A Message That Matters Nigerian multi-talented entertainer GyC is back with a brand-new release titled “Worth,” a song that places self-belief, confidence, and personal value at the center of its message. Known for his versatility across Afrobeat, Afropop, Highlife, Dancehall, and R&B, GyC once again showcases his ability to blend meaningful storytelling with infectious African rhythms. On “Worth,” the Lagos-based artist creates a record that speaks directly to dreamers, hustlers, and anyone navigating life’s challenges while striving to recognize their true value. At a time when conversations around self-esteem, identity, and personal growth continue to resonate globally, “Worth” arrives as both a musical statement and an empowering reminder that every individual possesses unique purpose and potential. A Decade Of Excellence Reflected In Every Note Born Fortune Kingsley, GyC has spent more than a decade building a reputation as one of Nigeria’s most dynamic entertainers. Since launching his professional music career in 2010, he has evolved into a respected singer, songwriter, producer, and actor whose contributions extend beyond the recording studio. His journey has been marked by notable achievements, including winning FME Singer of the Year and FME Producer of the Year, while also earning international recognition through multiple prestigious awards celebrating his talents as a producer, songwriter, and performer. Beyond his individual success, GyC has collaborated with industry heavyweights including 2Baba, Ice Prince, 9ice, Falz, and DJ Neptune, helping shape contemporary African music through both songwriting and production. The Sound And Message Behind “Worth” “Worth” captures the essence of GyC’s artistic identity — authentic storytelling delivered through vibrant African sounds. The record combines melodic Afro-fusion influences with uplifting lyricism, creating a listening experience that is both reflective and inspiring. Rather than focusing solely on external success, the song encourages listeners to recognize their intrinsic value, trust their journey, and remain confident despite obstacles. This balance between relatable messaging and commercial appeal has become a defining feature of GyC’s catalog, allowing his music to connect with audiences across different cultures and generations. Building Community Through Music While GyC’s achievements on stage are impressive, his impact extends far beyond performance venues. As the founder of the annual GyC Street Carnival in Lagos, he has demonstrated a commitment to community development, cultural celebration, and fan engagement. The free-entry entertainment event serves as a platform that unites music lovers while creating opportunities for connection and celebration. That same spirit of empowerment and community can be felt throughout “Worth,” reinforcing GyC’s belief that music should inspire, uplift, and create positive impact. A Global Vision For African Excellence Having performed across countries including South Africa, Kenya, Ghana, Mozambique, Ivory Coast, and Benin Republic, GyC continues to represent African creativity on an international scale. His performances alongside major stars such as Wizkid, Flavour, Phyno, Mayorkun, Kizz Daniel, Olamide, and 2Baba have further cemented his reputation as an entertainer capable of commanding major stages. With “Worth,” GyC continues that upward trajectory, delivering a record that reflects both his artistic maturity and his commitment to creating music with lasting value. Final Thoughts “Worth” is more than just another release. It is a statement of purpose from an artist whose career has been defined by consistency, creativity, and excellence. As GyC continues expanding his influence across Africa and beyond, this latest single stands as a reminder of the power of self-belief and the importance of recognizing one’s value. For listeners seeking motivation wrapped in infectious Afro-fusion sounds, “Worth” offers a timely and memorable soundtrack. “Worth” is now available on all major streaming platforms.

articles.title: Hillz Turns Aspirations Into Reality on Inspiring New Single “Dream”
articles.body: The Nigerian Afro-Fusion singer-songwriter delivers a heartfelt anthem about ambition, resilience, and believing in possibilities. As artists continue to use music as a vehicle for personal expression and inspiration, Nigerian Afro-Fusion talent Hillz returns with a powerful new release that speaks directly to dreamers, believers, and individuals pursuing purpose. Her latest single, “Dream,” arrives as an uplifting reflection on ambition, perseverance, and the courage required to pursue one’s vision despite uncertainty. A Voice Rooted in Authentic Experiences Since emerging onto the Nigerian music scene, Hillz has consistently built her artistry around authenticity, emotional honesty, and meaningful storytelling. The Cross River-born singer-songwriter has become known for blending Afrobeat, Dancehall, and Afro-Fusion influences into records that connect deeply with everyday experiences. Her music often explores themes of growth, resilience, self-discovery, and overcoming obstacles—qualities that have continued to shape her identity as an artist. With “Dream,” Hillz expands on those foundations, delivering a record that feels both deeply personal and universally relatable. The Soundtrack for Dream Chasers At its heart, “Dream” is an anthem for anyone determined to turn aspirations into reality. The song reflects on the journey between vision and achievement, acknowledging both the challenges and the unwavering belief required to keep moving forward. Through her expressive vocal delivery, Hillz paints a picture of hope in the face of adversity, reminding listeners that every accomplishment begins as a dream. The record carries an empowering message about trusting the process, embracing growth, and remaining committed to one’s purpose regardless of setbacks. Rather than focusing solely on success, “Dream” celebrates the courage it takes to keep believing when the destination still feels far away. A Rich Afro-Fusion Experience Musically, “Dream” showcases Hillz’s ability to merge soulful melodies with contemporary Afro-Fusion production. The record combines infectious rhythms, warm instrumentation, and emotionally resonant songwriting to create an atmosphere that feels both reflective and uplifting. The balance between introspective lyricism and engaging musicality allows the song to resonate across different audiences. Whether listeners are navigating personal challenges, pursuing career goals, or simply searching for motivation, “Dream” provides a soundtrack for perseverance and optimism. Continuing an Artistic Evolution Following previous releases that explored self-discovery and authenticity, Hillz continues to demonstrate growth as both a songwriter and performer. Each release reveals greater confidence in her artistic identity while maintaining the emotional depth that has become a defining characteristic of her music. “Dream” reflects an artist who understands the power of storytelling and uses her platform to inspire meaningful conversations about hope, ambition, and personal development. As her catalogue continues to evolve, Hillz remains committed to creating music that not only entertains but also encourages listeners to believe in themselves and their journeys. Positioning Herself Among Afro-Fusion’s Emerging Voices Nigeria’s music industry continues to produce a new generation of artists who are redefining contemporary African music through innovation and authenticity. Hillz stands among these emerging voices, bringing a unique perspective shaped by her experiences, influences, and commitment to honest storytelling. With “Dream,” she further strengthens her position as an artist capable of creating records that resonate emotionally while maintaining broad commercial appeal. The single serves as another important chapter in her journey—one that highlights her growth, vision, and potential to leave a lasting impact on the Afro-Fusion landscape.

articles.title: KING TEDI’S JUST RUN IT IS THE SOUNDTRACK OF MOTION, AMBITION, AND A NEW AFRO-TRAP GENERATION
articles.body: Nigeria’s music scene continues to evolve beyond familiar boundaries, with a new wave of artists redefining what African music can sound like. Among them is King Tedi, a rising voice emerging from Abuja’s rapidly expanding alternative and underground music culture. With the release of his latest EP, Just Run It, King Tedi isn’t simply adding another project to the growing catalogue of Nigerian music. He’s introducing listeners to a mindset, a philosophy, and a creative identity that reflects the experiences of a generation navigating ambition, pressure, self-belief, and constant evolution. At a time when artists are often pushed to choose between rap and Afrobeats, melody and lyricism, local identity and global influence, King Tedi chooses none of those limitations. Instead, he embraces all of them. The result is a sound he proudly describes as “Hybrid.” The Rise Of A Hybrid Artist Born Daniel Terver Iorfa in Benue State and currently based in Abuja, King Tedi’s journey into music began long before studio sessions and official releases. What started in 2014 as freestyles and personal expression gradually transformed into a deeper creative pursuit. By 2018, he had begun recording seriously, driven not by commercial expectations but by a genuine desire to understand himself through music. That foundation remains visible throughout his artistry today. Influenced by global icons such as Drake and Playboi Carti alongside African superstars Wizkid and Burna Boy, King Tedi has developed a style that feels culturally grounded while maintaining international appeal. His records move effortlessly between melodic hooks, trap-inspired production, reflective storytelling, and lifestyle-driven energy. It’s a balance that mirrors the reality of many young Africans today—caught between dreams and responsibilities, celebration and sacrifice, confidence and uncertainty. Just Run It: More Than A Title At its core, Just Run It is built around a simple but powerful idea: movement. The project captures an artist stepping fully into his identity while refusing to wait for validation or permission. Throughout the EP, listeners encounter different sides of King Tedi’s world, each track representing another chapter in a larger journey of growth and self-definition. There are moments of confidence and youthful freedom. Records like “Puff Pass” and “Bad Girl (Sit Down Pon It)” embrace nightlife culture, social energy, and the unapologetic enjoyment of success. These tracks deliver the project’s most infectious moments, pairing vibrant Afro-inspired bounce with modern trap aesthetics. Yet beneath the surface lies a more reflective narrative. On “SOML (Story Of My Life),” King Tedi shifts from celebration to introspection, offering a closer look into the mindset behind the music. Themes of perseverance, self-awareness, and personal growth emerge, creating some of the project’s most emotionally resonant moments. Elsewhere, “Problem” confronts the realities of ambition. The track acknowledges struggle, financial pressure, and the relentless pursuit of a better future—a reality that resonates deeply with young creatives and entrepreneurs across Africa. Meanwhile, “Soft Work” serves as a declaration of discipline and self-reliance. It is a reminder that consistency, focus, and belief in oneself often matter more than external approval. Together, these records create a project that feels less like a collection of songs and more like a reflection of a mindset in motion. Abuja’s Alternative Scene Is Growing Fast For years, conversations about Nigeria’s music industry have largely centered around Lagos. However, cities like Abuja are increasingly producing artists who are reshaping the national conversation through experimentation and originality. The Federal Capital Territory’s youth culture has become a breeding ground for creatives unafraid to challenge conventions, blending genres, aesthetics, and influences into entirely new forms of expression. King Tedi represents this movement perfectly. His music carries the confidence of contemporary Afrobeats while embracing the rebellious energy of modern rap culture. The result feels connected to global trends without losing touch with local realities. As Abuja’s alternative music ecosystem continues to grow, artists like King Tedi are proving that innovation is not restricted by geography. Instead, it thrives wherever ambitious creatives are willing to build something authentic. Running Toward The Future Perhaps the most compelling aspect of Just Run It is its honesty. Behind the energetic production, catchy hooks, and lifestyle narratives lies a project deeply rooted in personal evolution. It acknowledges setbacks, embraces growth, and champions the idea that success is not something handed out—it is something pursued relentlessly. For the Hybrids, the dreamers balancing multiple realities, the creators navigating uncertainty, and the young people determined to define success on their own terms, King Tedi’s message is clear: Keep moving. Keep building. Keep believing. And most importantly, just run it.

Together, these records create a project that feels less like a collection of songs and more like a reflection of a mindset in motion.

Abuja’s Alternative Scene Is Growing Fast

For years, conversations about Nigeria’s music industry have largely centered around Lagos. However, cities like Abuja are increasingly producing artists who are reshaping the national conversation through experimentation and originality.

The Federal Capital Territory’s youth culture has become a breeding ground for creatives unafraid to challenge conventions, blending genres, aesthetics, and influences into entirely new forms of expression.

King Tedi represents this movement perfectly.

His music carries the confidence of contemporary Afrobeats while embracing the rebellious energy of modern rap culture. The result feels connected to global trends without losing touch with local realities.

As Abuja’s alternative music ecosystem continues to grow, artists like King Tedi are proving that innovation is not restricted by geography. Instead, it thrives wherever ambitious creatives are willing to build something authentic.

Running Toward The Future

Perhaps the most compelling aspect of Just Run It is its honesty.

Behind the energetic production, catchy hooks, and lifestyle narratives lies a project deeply rooted in personal evolution. It acknowledges setbacks, embraces growth, and champions the idea that success is not something handed out—it is something pursued relentlessly.

For the Hybrids, the dreamers balancing multiple realities, the creators navigating uncertainty, and the young people determined to define success on their own terms, King Tedi’s message is clear:

Keep moving.

Keep building.

Keep believing.

And most importantly, just run it.
